title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
應天府鄉試錄序
皇上嗣登寶位之七年是爲萬曆
己卯天下復當大比士屆期
應天府府尹臣武卿府丞臣
自脩職在提調以例
請
上命中允臣啓愚侍讀臣萬化往
===
典試事先是禮官數條議科
指大抵以正文體端士習爲
務而其要在愼簡校錄者旣
荷
綸俞令四方行之矣玆復申飭所
司奉揚祗事視昔加嚴臣乃
惕然思曰士習之漸於風靡
punctuated:
應天府鄉試錄序
皇上嗣登寶位之七年，是爲萬曆己卯，天下復當大比士。屆期，應天府府尹臣武卿、府丞臣自脩，職在提調，以例請。上命中允臣啓愚、侍讀臣萬化往典試事。先是，禮官數條議科指，大抵以正文體、端士習爲務，而其要在愼簡校錄者，旣荷綸俞，令四方行之矣；玆復申飭所司，奉揚祗事，視昔加嚴。臣乃惕然思曰：士習之漸於風靡，
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Yingtian Prefectural Provincial Examination

In the seventh year after His Majesty succeeded to the imperial throne, which is the jimao year of the Wanli era (1579), the empire was once again due for the triennial recruitment examination of scholars. When the time arrived, the Prefect of Yingtian Prefecture, Your Servant Wu Qing 武卿, and the Vice Prefect, Your Servant Zixiu 自脩, whose duties were those of Proctor, submitted a request in accordance with precedent. His Majesty commanded the Secretariat Companion of the Heir Apparent, Your Servant Qiyu 啓愚 [Gao Qiyu 高啓愚], and the Hanlin Academician Reader-in-waiting, Your Servant Wanhua 萬化 [Luo Wanhua 羅萬化], to go and take charge of the examination affairs. Prior to this, officials of the Ministry of Rites had submitted several itemized deliberations on examination guidelines; in general, they took rectifying literary style and making upright the habits of scholars as the priority, while the crux of the matter lay in carefully selecting those who evaluate and record the essays. Having already received the imperial endorsement, these measures were ordered to be implemented throughout the realm; now the responsible authorities were again admonished to uphold, propagate, and reverently attend to the matter with even greater strictness than in the past. Your Servant thereupon reflected with trepidation, saying to himself: The gradual slide of scholars' habits into fashionable decadence,…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
文體之競於俗尚猶江河之
流愈趨愈變也乃所以正之
端之者皆將於舉者求多焉
斯不已重乎脫有不能稱
明詔謂
任使何矧臣學術淺薄才至不
肖而濫竽茲役寔惴惴乎有
===
餘懼矣已復念以人事
君人臣之大義儻藉是勉竭其愚
或得一二士足以樹尺寸於
他日則臣銜報
高厚之私庶可萬一少圖塞又得
不踊躍奮厲思所自効乎比
至其地維時府臣飭具旣備
punctuated: 文體之競於俗尚，猶江河之流，愈趨愈變也。乃所以正之端之者，皆將於舉者求多焉，斯不已重乎？脫有不能稱明詔，謂任使何？矧臣學術淺薄，才至不肖，而濫竽茲役，寔惴惴乎有餘懼矣。已復念以人事君，人臣之大義，儻藉是勉竭其愚，或得一二士足以樹尺寸於他日，則臣銜報高厚之私，庶可萬一少圖塞，又得不踊躍奮厲，思所自効乎？比至其地，維時府臣飭具旣備，
translation_en: … and the competition of literary styles after popular fashion, are like the flow of rivers and streams: the further they course, the more they change. Yet the means to rectify and straighten them will all be demanded in large measure from those who select the candidates—is this responsibility not weighty indeed? Should we fail to live up to the enlightened edict, what could we say to justify our commission? How much more so since my own learning is shallow and my talent utterly unworthy; occupying a place in this assignment beyond my deserts, I am truly filled with trembling and lingering dread. Yet on further reflection, to serve the Sovereign by recommending men of talent is the highest duty of a minister. If by means of this task I exert my humble utmost and perhaps obtain one or two scholars capable of achieving some small measure of merit in days to come, then my private desire to repay Your Majesty's heaven-high and earth-deep grace might in some tiny fraction be fulfilled—how, then, could I not leap with enthusiasm and rouse myself to think of how to render service? When we arrived at the place, at that time the prefectural officials had already made all the necessary preparations,…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
而御史臣應訓臣一鯤暨臣
楊際熙臣張友舜相與申約
東議防閑內外唯謹乃進諸
曹六館及先後提學御史臣
郭莊臣李學詩臣李時成所
選士凡四千六百有奇三試
之而與同考官推官臣邦儒
===
教諭臣士弘臣善臣稑臣曰
仁臣萃臣來鳳臣三省訓導
臣茂魁臣世美臣然胥誓胥
戒窮日夜肆力校閱拔儁者
百三十五人並錄其文以
獻遵
制也臣因諗諸衆曰自昔人才之
punctuated: 而御史臣應訓、臣一鯤，暨臣楊際熙、臣張友舜，相與申約東、議防閑，內外唯謹。乃進諸曹、六館及先後提學御史臣郭莊、臣李學詩、臣李時成所選士，凡四千六百有奇，三試之。而與同考官推官臣邦儒、教諭臣士弘、臣善、臣稑、臣曰仁、臣萃、臣來鳳、臣三省，訓導臣茂魁、臣世美、臣然，胥誓胥戒，窮日夜肆力校閱，拔儁者百三十五人，並錄其文以獻，遵制也。臣因諗諸衆曰：自昔人才之
translation_en: … and the Censors, Your servants Yingxun 應訓 and Yikun 一鯤, as well as Your servants Yang Jixi 楊際熙 and Zhang Youshun 張友舜, together reiterated the regulations and deliberated on security precautions, maintaining strict vigilance both inside and outside the compound. Thereupon, we admitted the scholars selected from the various government agencies, the Six Halls of the Directorate of Education, and by the successive Education-intendant Censors, Your servants Guo Zhuang 郭莊, Li Xueshi 李學詩, and Li Shicheng 李時成—numbering more than four thousand six hundred in all—and examined them in three sessions. Together with the Associate Examiners—the Prefectural Judge, Your servant Bangru 邦儒; the Confucian Instructors, Your servants Shihong 士弘, Shan 善, Lu 稑, Yueren 曰仁, Cui 萃, Laifeng 來鳳, and Sanxing 三省; and the Assistant Instructors, Your servants Maokui 茂魁, Shimei 世美, and Ran 然—we bound ourselves by oaths and mutual admonitions, working day and night to grade and review the papers with all our strength. We selected one hundred and thirty-five outstanding men and recorded their essays to present to the throne, in compliance with the imperial statutes. Your servant therefore addressed the assembled officials and graduates, saying: "Since antiquity, the…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
生縏由地之所鍾迨其出而
昌國也則獨盛于休明熙洽
之日我
聖祖甫入金陵即建禮賢館徵青
田劉基輩與論經史治道旣
定鼎廿餘載
覩奎壁間黑祲消滅乃
===
慶文運之當興蓋在
肇造初而
國家億萬載儒術之隆文明之
熾囿可預卜矣
列聖代作振新文教益紹明而光
大之肆我
皇上亶
punctuated: 生，縏由地之所鍾；迨其出而昌國也，則獨盛于休明熙洽之日。我聖祖甫入金陵，即建禮賢館，徵青田劉基輩，與論經史治道。旣定鼎廿餘載，覩奎壁間黑祲消滅，乃慶文運之當興。蓋在肇造初，而國家億萬載儒術之隆、文明之熾，囿可預卜矣。列聖代作，振新文教，益紹明而光大之。肆我皇上亶
translation_en: …birth always depends on the spiritual Concentration of the land; yet when they emerge to bring prosperity to the state, they flourish uniquely in times of auspicious brightness and harmonious peace. As soon as Our Sacred Ancestor [Emperor Taizu] entered Jinling [Nanjing], he immediately established the Hall for Honoring the Worthy (Lixian guan) and summoned Liu Ji (劉基) of Qingtian and his peers to discuss the Classics, Histories, and the way of governance with them. Over twenty years after establishing the dynastic capital, observing that the dark ominous vapors between the Kui and Bi constellations [associated with literature] had vanished, he rejoiced that the fortune of letters was bound to rise. Indeed, at the very beginning of the dynasty's founding, the flourishing of Confucian learning and the splendor of civilizing culture for hundreds of millions of years of our State could already be foretold! Successive Sacred Emperors arose generation after generation, renewing and invigorating civil teaching, further continuing, illuminating, and magnifying it. Thus Our Emperor today truly…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
濬哲之資履
君師之位
聖德天縱
帝學日新七載于玆
道化殷流內寧外謐而尤夙夜
孜孜籲俊登彥用丕隆治理
士伏巖穴者卽遐陬萬里外
罔不思見其才美以幸際
===
聖明矧都人士身躡禮賢之地仰
奎壁之輝而
鎬京辟廱之化又得躬被其盛
意必有卓然名世者感奮興
起于其閒而無從覯之也玆
得縱觀諸士所爲文言卽人
punctuated: 濬哲之資，履君師之位，聖德天縱，帝學日新。七載于玆，道化殷流，內寧外謐，而尤夙夜孜孜，籲俊登彥，用丕隆治理。士伏巖穴者，卽遐陬萬里外，罔不思見其才美，以幸際聖明。矧都人士身躡禮賢之地，仰奎壁之輝，而鎬京辟廱之化，又得躬被其盛。意必有卓然名世者，感奮興起于其閒，而無從覯之也。玆得縱觀諸士所爲文，言卽人
translation_en: …endowed with profound wisdom, occupies the position of both ruler and teacher. His Sacred Virtue is heaven-bestowed, and His Imperial Learning is daily renewed. For seven years now, the transforming influence of the Way has flowed abundantly, bringing peace within and tranquility without. Yet all the more, day and night, He tirelessly calls forth men of outstanding talent and promotes the worthy, thereby greatly exalting good governance. Even scholars hidden away in mountain caves, in distant corners ten thousand li away, without exception long to display their fine talents, counting themselves fortunate to encounter an era of sacred enlightenment. How much more so the scholars of the capital region, who themselves tread a land where the worthy are honored, look up to the radiance of the Kui and Bi constellations, and personally receive the flourishing transformative influence of the Imperial University in the ancestral capital [Nanjing]! I had thought that there must surely be preeminent men of the age who, moved and inspired, have risen up among them, though I had no way of meeting them. Now, having been able to thoroughly examine the essays composed by the candidates—although their words…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
人殊類皆抒性靈之眞闡皇
王之緒而辨晢理道敷邑化
猷弗以奇衺險僻相衒貿文
不幾近於正乎而緣是以覘
諸士之習若握贄以徵禮采
言以貢俗臣亦可據而知其
弗頗也顧臣於此則猶悚意
===
大懼焉何也蓋臣之盱衡擊
節於諸士者文也諸士異日
之標著於行業者則質而不
徒以其文也文非不可行遠
而每忌其太盛文太盛則質
易漓而世道人心攸繫之矣
昔者帝王質文相變以濟天
punctuated: 人殊，類皆抒性靈之眞，闡皇王之緒，而辨晢理道、敷邑化猷，弗以奇衺險僻相衒貿，文不幾近於正乎？而緣是以覘諸士之習，若握贄以徵禮、采言以貢俗，臣亦可據而知其弗頗也。顧臣於此，則猶悚意大懼焉，何也？蓋臣之盱衡擊節於諸士者，文也；諸士異日之標著於行業者，則質而不徒以其文也。文非不可行遠，而每忌其太盛；文太盛則質易漓，而世道人心攸繫之矣。昔者帝王質文相變以濟天
translation_en: … differs from person to person, in general they all express the truth of their innate spirit and expound the heritage of the sovereigns and kings; they clearly analyze principle and the Way, and set forth plans for transforming governance [? 敷邑化猷, likely a misprint for 敷陳化猷], without vying to peddle strange,heterodox, obscure, or eccentric expressions. Does their writing not come close to orthodoxy? And if on this basis one observes the habits of the scholars—just like holding up ritual gifts to verify propriety or collecting folk sayings to present popular customs—your servant can also rely on this to know that they are not biased. Yet at this juncture, your servant still feels anxious and deeply fearful. Why is this? Because what makes your servant raise his brows and beat time in admiration of the scholars is their literary refinement (wen); whereas what the scholars will distinguish themselves by in their conduct and achievements in future days is their substantial character (zhi), and not merely their literary refinement. It is not that literary refinement cannot carry far, but one must always beware of its becoming too exuberant; when literary refinement is too exuberant, substance easily wears thin, and the state of the world and human hearts are bound up with this. In antiquity, emperors and kings alternated between substance and refinement in order to succor the…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
下質敝則佐之以文文敝則
復之以質蓋爲世道人心計
者然也乃其潛移默運之機
則自求賢加之意焉耳我
朝設科之始唯以文質相稱爲
諭故其時最稱得人自是以後人
文漸以宣朗而敦厚純朴之
風不能不隨時而少變令
===
天子纂圖立極日嘉惠四方士嘗
廣厲學官者在
功令一切崇雅黜浮期得眞才
需實效毅然欲挽斯世之文
而盡歸于質
聖意所嚮指蓋可仰窺矣玆諸士
punctuated: 下：質敝則佐之以文，文敝則復之以質，蓋爲世道人心計者然也。乃其潛移默運之機，則自求賢加之意焉耳。我朝設科之始，唯以文質相稱爲諭，故其時最稱得人。自是以後，人文漸以宣朗，而敦厚純朴之風，不能不隨時而少變。令天子纂圖立極，日嘉惠四方士，嘗廣厲學官，者在功令，一切崇雅黜浮，期得眞才，需實效，毅然欲挽斯世之文，而盡歸于質。聖意所嚮指，蓋可仰窺矣。玆諸士
translation_en: … the empire: when substance declined, they supplemented it with literary refinement, and when refinement declined, they restored it with substance. This was done out of concern for the state of the world and the hearts of the people. Yet the subtle mechanism by which this unseen transformation was effected lay simply in paying special heed to how worthy men were sought. When our dynasty first established the examination system, its edicts instructed only that refinement and substance should be held in balance, and thus that era was most renowned for obtaining capable men. From that time onward, cultural refinement gradually grew more brilliant and expressive, while the ethos of magnanimity and simple purity could not help but change somewhat with the times. Now the Son of Heaven [actually 今, though printed 令], having succeeded to the throne and established the supreme standard, daily bestows his gracious favor upon scholars of the four quarters. He has broadly encouraged the officials of the schools, setting this down in the examination regulations: in all things exalting what is clásico and proper while rejecting superficiality, hoping to obtain true talent and looking for practical results, resolutely seeking to turn back the literary floridity of the present age and bring it wholly back to substance. The direction toward which His Sacred Intention points may thus be reverently glimpsed. Now, these scholars …

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
應里選而來業已考言見收
于舉者行且續食赴
公車用備
主上驅使果能振衣彈冠力脩其
行業以見于世而不至庸違
先資之言斯爲質與文稱庶
幾哉不負
===
今日之所求固臣之願也其或
情奪於聲利而志眩於紛華
將在璞者琱出蒙者汨而蠻
悅雖工第以弁髦視之耳於
上意則奚當焉此臣之懼所以諗
諗無已也臣又聞之龍噓致
雲雷震起蟄是故正鵠表中
punctuated: 應里選而來，業已考言，見收于舉者，行且續食赴公車，用備主上驅使。果能振衣彈冠，力脩其行業以見于世，而不至庸違先資之言，斯爲質與文稱，庶幾哉不負今日之所求，固臣之願也。其或情奪於聲利，而志眩於紛華，將在璞者琱，出蒙者汨，而鞶悅雖工，第以弁髦視之耳，於上意則奚當焉？此臣之懼，所以諗諗無已也。臣又聞之：龍噓致雲，雷震起蟄。是故正鵠表中，
translation_en: …who have come in response to the local selection have already had their words examined and been accepted among the provincial graduates. Soon they will receive travel provisions and proceed to the Public Carriage Office to hold themselves in readiness for the Sovereign's employment. If they can indeed shake out their robes and dust off their caps, striving to cultivate their conduct and achievements so as to manifest themselves in the world without turning their backs on the words they offered as their initial pledge, then their substance and literary refinement will match. In this way they will nearly avoid betraying what is sought of them today—and this is truly your servant's wish. If, however, their passions are carried away by fame and profit and their ambitions dazzled by ostentatious splendor, then what was uncarved jade will be chiseled away and what emerged from youthful innocence will be muddied; and though their embroidered belt-pendants and kerchiefs [i.e., ornate writings] be skillfully wrought, they will be treated merely as cast-off caps once the goal is reached. How could that correspond to the Sovereign's intention? This is what your servant fears, and why I cannot cease from offering earnest counsel. Your servant has also heard that when the dragon breathes, it summons clouds, and when thunder crashes, it rouses hibernating creatures. Therefore, when the target is set up in the center…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
兩耦決拾枹鼓當壘三軍奮
臂誠捷於所從也昔董仲舒
啓武帝以損周之文用夏之
忠夫忠則進乎質而渾然者
也董生當射策初尚未識帝
之意爲何如而惓惓以此說
進則其用世之畧固可知已
爾諸士抱經術負賢良視董
生當不少遜也矧
===
上以質求蓋旣示之以
意而循不以質應之耶矧諸士被
化首善振奮而起旣有徵於其
文顧不能副之以質耶臣固
信諸士之必不如是而臣之
punctuated: 兩耦決拾；枹鼓當壘，三軍奮臂，誠捷於所從也。昔董仲舒啓武帝，以損周之文、用夏之忠。夫忠則進乎質而渾然者也。董生當射策初，尚未識帝之意爲何如，而惓惓以此說進，則其用世之畧固可知已。爾諸士抱經術、負賢良，視董生當不少遜也。矧上以質求，蓋旣示之以意，而循不以質應之耶？矧諸士被化首善，振奮而起，旣有徵於其文，顧不能副之以質耶？臣固信諸士之必不如是，而臣之
translation_en: … the two pairs of archers put on their thumb-rings and bracers; when the drumstick and drum face the ramparts, the three armies raise their arms in ardor—truly, how swift they are to follow what leads them! In former times, Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒 advised Emperor Wu 武帝 to diminish the cultural refinement of the Zhou and employ the loyal devotion of the Xia. Now, loyal devotion approaches unadorned substance and is whole and uncarved. When Master Dong first answered the policy questions, he did not yet know what the Emperor's intentions were, yet he earnestly presented this counsel; from this, his strategy for serving the world can indeed be known. You scholars embrace classical learning and possess worthiness and goodness; compared to Master Dong, you surely do not fall short in the least. How much more so when His Majesty seeks unadorned substance and has already shown you his intention—could you still [?] fail to respond to him with substance? And how much more so when you scholars, having received the transformative influence of the premier place of moral cultivation, have roused yourselves and risen up—having already given proof of it in your literary compositions, could you yet be unable to match it with true substance? Your servant firmly believes that you scholars will certainly not be like this, and that your servant's…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
懼亦自量其終可釋也詩不
云乎王國克生維周之楨又
云行歸于周萬民所望夫士
幸生王國而且能周其行以
爲民望俾後之按是錄而稱
願然曰其良士其良士則司
校錄者之與諸士不均有無
窮之聞哉
===
右春坊右中允兼翰林院編
修高啓愚謹序
punctuated:
懼亦自量其終可釋也。《詩》不云乎：「王國克生，維周之楨。」又云：「行歸于周，萬民所望。」夫士幸生王國，而且能周其行以爲民望，俾後之按是錄而稱願然曰：「其良士！其良士！」則司校錄者之與諸士，不均有無窮之聞哉！
右春坊右中允兼翰林院編修高啓愚謹序。
translation_en:
…fear, I also reckon, may in the end be dispelled. Does not the Book of Odes (Shi) say: "The royal state is able to bring them forth; they are the pillars of Zhou"? And does it not also say: "In conduct they are faultless [or: return to Zhou], the ones to whom the myriad people look in hope"? Now, scholars have the good fortune to be born in the royal state, and if they are moreover able to make their conduct complete so as to become the hope of the people—causing those in later times who examine this record to praise them admiringly, saying, "What fine scholars! What fine scholars!"—then will not those in charge of assessing and compiling the record, along with all of you scholars, equally enjoy boundless renown?

Respectfully prefaced by Gao Qiyu 高啓愚, Right Companion of the Right Secretariat of the Heir Apparent and concurrently Junior Compiler in the Hanlin Academy.

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
舜亦以命禹
凡事豫則立不豫則廢言前定則不跲事
前定則不困行前定則不疚道前定則
不窮在下位不獲乎上民不可得而治
矣獲乎上有道不信乎朋友不獲乎上
矣信乎朋友有道不順乎親不信乎朋
友矣順乎親有道反諸身不誠不順乎
親矣誠身有道不明乎善不誠乎身矣
===
惻隱之心仁之端也羞惡之心義之端也
辭讓之心禮之端也是非之心智之端
也人之有是四端也猶其有四體也
易
象曰火在天上大有君子以遏惡揚善順
天休命
柔在內而剛得中
初六藉用白茅无咎子曰苟錯諸地而可
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

舜亦以命禹。
凡事豫則立，不豫則廢。言前定則不跲，事前定則不困，行前定則不疚，道前定則不窮。在下位不獲乎上，民不可得而治矣；獲乎上有道，不信乎朋友，不獲乎上矣；信乎朋友有道，不順乎親，不信乎朋友矣；順乎親有道，反諸身不誠，不順乎親矣；誠身有道，不明乎善，不誠乎身矣。
惻隱之心，仁之端也；羞惡之心，義之端也；辭讓之心，禮之端也；是非之心，智之端也。人之有是四端也，猶其有四體也。

易

象曰：火在天上，大有；君子以遏惡揚善，順天休命。
柔在內而剛得中。
初六，藉用白茅，无咎。子曰：「苟錯諸地而可…
translation_en:
First Session

The Four Books

"Shun also used these words to charge Yu."

"In all things, success depends on previous preparation, and without such preparation there is sure to be failure. If what is to be spoken be previously determined, there will be no stumbling. If affairs be previously determined, there will be no difficulty with them. If one's actions have been previously determined, there will be no sorrow in connection with them. If principles of conduct have been previously determined, the practice of them will be inexhaustible. When those in inferior positions do not obtain the confidence of their superiors, they cannot succeed in governing the people. There is a way to obtain the confidence of one's superiors: if one is not trusted by one's friends, one will not obtain the confidence of one's superiors. There is a way to be trusted by one's friends: if one is not obedient to one's parents, one will not be trusted by one's friends. There is a way to be obedient to one's parents: if on examining oneself one finds that one is not sincere, one will not be obedient to one's parents. There is a way to attain sincerity in oneself: if one does not understand what is good, one will not attain sincerity in oneself."

"The feeling of commiseration is the sprout of benevolence; the feeling of shame and dislike is the sprout of righteousness; the feeling of modesty and complaisance is the sprout of propriety; and the feeling of approving and disapproving is the sprout of wisdom. Men have these four sprouts just as they have their four limbs."

Classic of Changes (Yi)

"The Image says: Fire above heaven—Great Possession (Dayou). Thus the superior man represses evil and promotes good, in obedience to the beneficent mandate of Heaven."

"The yielding is within, and the firm occupies the central position."

"Six at the beginning: For an underlay one uses white rushes; there is no blame. The Master said: 'If one simply places it on the ground, that would be…'"

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
矣藉之用茅何咎之有愼之至也夫茅
之爲物薄而用可重也愼斯術也以往
其无所失矣
立人之道曰仁與義
書
禹曰都帝愼乃在位帝曰俞
惟王不邇聲色不殖貨利德懋懋官功懋
懋賞用人惟己改過不吝克寛克仁彰
信兆民
===
曰皇極之敷言是彝是訓于帝其訓凡厥
庶民極之敷言是訓是行以近天子之
光曰天子作民父母以爲天下王
文王卑服即康功田功徽柔懿恭懷保小
民惠鮮鰥寡自朝至于日中昃不遑暇
食用咸和萬民文王不敢盤于遊田以
庶邦惟正之供
詩
騏騮是中騧驪是驂
punctuated:
矣，藉之用茅，何咎之有？愼之至也。夫茅之爲物薄，而用可重也。愼斯術也以往，其无所失矣。
立人之道，曰仁與義。
《書》
禹曰：「都！帝，愼乃在位。」帝曰：「俞。」
惟王不邇聲色，不殖貨利。德懋懋官，功懋懋賞。用人惟己，改過不吝。克寛克仁，彰信兆民。
曰：皇極之敷言，是彝是訓，于帝其訓。凡厥庶民，極之敷言，是訓是行，以近天子之光，曰：「天子作民父母，以爲天下王。」
文王卑服，即康功田功。徽柔懿恭，懷保小民，惠鮮鰥寡。自朝至于日中昃，不遑暇食，用咸和萬民。文王不敢盤于遊田，以庶邦惟正之供。
《詩》
騏騮是中，騧驪是驂。
translation_en:
… yet if one spreads white cogongrass beneath it, what blame could there be? This is the utmost of caution. Now cogongrass as a thing is trifling, yet its use can be weighty. If one goes forward cautiously practicing this art, one will suffer no loss.”
“To establish the Way of man, they called it benevolence and righteousness.”

Book of Documents (Shu)
“Yu said, ‘Oh! Sovereign, be cautious on your throne.’ The Sovereign said, ‘Yes.’”
“The king did not approach sensual music and women, nor did he amass goods and profit. Where virtue was great, he greatly bestowed office; where merit was great, he greatly bestowed reward. He employed others as if their abilities were his own, and corrected his faults without reluctance. Capable of寬generosity and benevolence, he manifested trustworthiness to the millions of people.”
“Saying: This broad declaration of the August Ultimate is the constant norm, is the instruction; it is the instruction of the Supreme Ruler. All of the multitudinous common people, taking this broad declaration of the Ultimate as their instruction and putting it into practice, thereby draw near to the glory of the Son of Heaven, saying, ‘The Son of Heaven acts as father and mother to the people, and so becomes king of all under heaven.’”
“King Wen dressed humbly and devoted himself to the work of pacification and the work of agriculture. Admirable in his gentleness and piękny in his reverence, he cherished and protected the common people, and showed kindness to widows and widowers. From morning until midday and the sun’s decline, he had no leisure to eat, thereby bringing harmony to all the myriad people. King Wen did not dare to indulge in pleasure excursions and hunting, and received from the various states only the regular tribute.”

Book of Odes (Shi)
“The dappled bays and red horses with black manes are the inside pair; the yellow horses with black mouths and the pure blacks are the outside trace horses.”

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
彼交匪紓天子所予樂只君子天子命之
樂只君子福祿申之
瑟彼玉瓚黄流在中豈弟君子福祿攸降
鳶飛戾天魚躍于淵豈弟君子遐不作
人
嗟嗟臣工敬爾在公王釐爾成來咨來茹
春秋
三月鄭伯使宛來歸祊〔隱公八年〕
夏六月公會齊侯宋公陳侯鄭伯同盟于
幽〔莊公二十有七年〕六月公會宋公陳
侯衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯晉趙盾癸酉同
===
盟于新城〔文公十有四年〕
冬十月公會晉侯宋公衛侯鄭伯曹伯莒
子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子同圍齊
〔襄公十有八年〕公至自伐齊〔襄公十有
九年〕
宋公陳侯衛侯曹伯會晉師于棐林伐鄭
〔宣公元年〕公會晉師于瓦〔定公八年〕
punctuated:
彼交匪紓，天子所予。樂只君子，天子命之；樂只君子，福祿申之。
瑟彼玉瓚，黄流在中。豈弟君子，福祿攸降。鳶飛戾天，魚躍于淵。豈弟君子，遐不作人？
嗟嗟臣工，敬爾在公。王釐爾成，來咨來茹。

春秋
三月，鄭伯使宛來歸祊〔隱公八年〕；
夏六月，公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、鄭伯同盟于幽〔莊公二十有七年〕；六月，公會宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯、晉趙盾，癸酉，同盟于新城〔文公十有四年〕；
冬十月，公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、鄭伯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子同圍齊〔襄公十有八年〕；公至自伐齊〔襄公十有九年〕；
宋公、陳侯、衛侯、曹伯會晉師于棐林，伐鄭〔宣公元年〕；公會晉師于瓦〔定公八年〕。

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
禮記
大臣法小臣廉
是故清明象天廣大象地終始象四時周
還象風雨五色成文而不亂八風從律
而不姦百度得數而有常小大相成終
始相生倡和清濁迭相爲經
其親也慤其行也趨趨以數
孔子曰安上治民莫善於禮此之謂也
第貳塲
===
論
人主恭已於上
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢舉賢良方正直言極諫之士詔〔建元元年〕
擬唐以房玄齡杜如晦爲僕射誥〔貞觀三年〕
擬輔臣恭撰
進
punctuated:
《禮記》：
大臣法，小臣廉。
是故清明象天，廣大象地，終始象四時，周還象風雨；五色成文而不亂，八風從律而不姦，百度得數而有常；小大相成，終始相生，倡和清濁，迭相爲經。
其親也慤，其行也趨趨以數。
孔子曰：「安上治民，莫善於禮。」此之謂也。

第貳塲

論：
人主恭已於上。

詔、誥、表〔內科一道〕：
擬漢舉賢良方正直言極諫之士詔〔建元元年〕。
擬唐以房玄齡、杜如晦爲僕射誥〔貞觀三年〕。
擬輔臣恭撰進……
translation_en:
Record of Rites (Liji):
"The great ministers observe the laws; the lesser ministers are incorruptible."
"Therefore, in its brightness and purity it resembles Heaven; in its vastness and greatness it resembles Earth; in its endings and beginnings it resembles the four seasons; in its revolutions and turnings it resembles the wind and rain. Like the five colors, it forms a pattern without confusion; like the eight winds, it follows the pitch-pipes without irregularity; in its hundred standards, it attains proper measure and maintains constancy. Small and great complete one another; ending and beginning give rise to one another; leading and responding, clear and turbid tones alternate with one another as warp and准则 (standards)."
"In their personal conduct they are sincere and unadorned; in their walking they move with quick, short steps."
"Confucius said: 'For securing the rulers above and governing the people, nothing is better than ritual propriety.' This is what is meant."

Second Session

Discourse:
"The ruler holds himself in reverent composure above."

Edicts (zhao), Mandates (gao), and Memorials (biao) [select one to answer]:

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
雝肅殿箴表
判語五條
官員襲廕
舶商匿貨
御賜衣物
行宮營門
詐爲制書
第叄場
策五道
===
問祀典莫大乎
郊自昔帝王皆隆之乃禮家之指則犂然殊云
主合祀者本虞書肆類之文主分祀者
宗周禮司樂之制孰爲得歟漢氏而降
分合之議紛如不一所會通用者孰多歟
尊祖祀天之禮有奉始祖者有奉受命
之君者有天帝各配者有祖宗竝配者
將何所折衷乎洪惟我
太祖高皇帝初定天下即建
punctuated:
雝肅殿箴表

判語五條：
官員襲廕；
舶商匿貨；
御賜衣物；
行宮營門；
詐爲制書。

第叄場

策五道

問：祀典莫大乎郊，自昔帝王皆隆之，乃禮家之指則犂然殊云。主合祀者本《虞書》肆類之文，主分祀者宗《周禮》司樂之制，孰爲得歟？漢氏而降，分合之議紛如不一，所會通用者孰多歟？尊祖祀天之禮，有奉始祖者，有奉受命之君者，有天帝各配者，有祖宗竝配者，將何所折衷乎？洪惟我太祖高皇帝初定天下，即建

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
南北郊分祀
天地後乃改而合祀
列聖祇循百六十餘年至
世宗肅皇帝又改而分祀當時議禮之臣固壹
以周禮爲準果盡符合否
國家自
仁廟而後皆奉
太祖及
文皇帝配
===
天而嘉靖間始獨以
太祖配有其舉之一朝而更又何所見歟我
皇上寅御大寶肇舉
郊禋輔臣恭
進圖說典章沿革考據明悉至欲復
合祀
竝配之舊眞善體
世宗之心以光
太祖之定制
punctuated: 南北郊，分祀天地，後乃改而合祀。列聖祇循百六十餘年，至世宗肅皇帝又改而分祀。當時議禮之臣，固壹以《周禮》爲準，果盡符合否？國家自仁廟而後，皆奉太祖及文皇帝配天，而嘉靖間始獨以太祖配。有其舉之，一朝而更，又何所見歟？我皇上寅御大寶，肇舉郊禋，輔臣恭進《圖說》，典章沿革，考據明悉。至欲復合祀、竝配之舊，眞善體世宗之心，以光太祖之定制。
translation_en: … the Northern and Southern Suburbs, offering separate sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, and later changed this to a combined sacrifice. The successive sacred emperors reverently followed this for more than one hundred and sixty years, until Emperor Shizong Su (the Jiajing Emperor) again changed it to separate sacrifices. The ministers who deliberated on the rites at that time certainly took the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) exclusively as their standard, but did it truly conform in every respect? In our dynasty, from the time of the Renmiao (the Hongxi Emperor) onward, both Taizu (the Hongwu Emperor) and Emperor Wen (the Yongle Emperor) were reverently presented as coadjutors to Heaven; yet during the Jiajing reign, for the first time Taizu alone was made coadjutor. Once such a rite had been established, upon what insight was it suddenly altered in a single morning? When Our Majesty reverently ascended the great throne and first performed the suburban sacrifice, the Grand Secretaries respectfully submitted the Illustrated Explanations (Tushuo), in which the historical evolution of the institutions and statutes was investigated and substantiated with clarity and thoroughness. As for the desire to restore the former practice of combined sacrifice and joint coadjutors, this truly comprehends well the mind of Shizong so as to glorify the established institution of Taizu. …

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
上業已欣然嘉納有待而行矣然飭鉅典者貴
協于衆稽贊禮者不厭其詳諸士有能
博研經義參酌古今以佐
大議之萬一固
子
廟堂所樂聞也願相與懋明之其母曰以俟君
問治曆明時自古重之三代以前職在太
史顧其詳不可得聞已漢初法制疎闊
於是不愛祿爵益廣徵募言象數之士
寖寖衆矣歷代以還其法屢變而其說
亦逾精載在史冊甚具也可得聞其槩
與我
國家
大統曆采諸授時行之二百餘年司候靡爽蓋
法制之善卓邁百王矣曩正嘉間交食
分秒雖稍有不符然視前代之先後天
者相去甚遠更定曆元之議無庸陳已
頃者星官失職訛舛易常則有大駭聽
punctuated:
上業已欣然嘉納，有待而行矣。然飭鉅典者貴協于衆，稽贊禮者不厭其詳。諸士有能博研經義，參酌古今，以佐大議之萬一，固廟堂所樂聞也。願相與懋明之，其母曰「以俟君子」。

問：「治曆明時」，自古重之。三代以前，職在太史，顧其詳不可得聞已。漢初法制疎闊，於是不愛祿爵，益廣徵募，言象數之士寖寖衆矣。歷代以還，其法屢變，而其說亦逾精，載在史冊，甚具也，可得聞其槩與？我國家《大統曆》采諸《授時》，行之二百餘年，司候靡爽，蓋法制之善，卓邁百王矣。曩正、嘉間，交食分秒雖稍有不符，然視前代之先後天者，相去甚遠，更定曆元之議無庸陳已。頃者，星官失職，訛舛易常，則有大駭聽
translation_en:
… His Majesty has already gladly approved and accepted it, and is only awaiting the right moment to put it into practice. Yet those who put great state ceremonies in order value harmonizing with the views of the multitude, and those who investigate and assist in ritual matters never tire of thoroughness in detail. If among you scholars there are those capable of broadly researching the meanings of the Classics and weighing the ancient and modern so as to contribute even one ten-thousandth to the Great Deliberation, the court would certainly be delighted to hear it. Let us strive together to elucidate this; do not say [母, read 毋], "Let us leave that to awaited gentlemen."

Question: "Ordering the calendar and clarifying the seasons" has been esteemed since antiquity. Before the Three Dynasties, this duty rested with the Grand Scribe (taishi), though the details can no longer be known. At the beginning of the Han dynasty, the calendrical system was rough and imprecise; thereupon, the court did not begrudge emoluments and noble ranks, ever more broadly summoning and recruiting experts, and scholars who spoke of celestial phenomena and mathematical harmonics gradually grew numerous. Down through successive dynasties, the methods repeatedly changed and the theories grew ever more refined; they are recorded very fully in the historical annals—may we hear a general outline of them? Our dynasty's Great Concordance Calendar (Datong li) was adapted from the Season-Granting Calendar (Shoushi li); it has been in use for over two hundred years without error in the observation of astronomical signs, for the excellence of its system truly surpasses that of a hundred kings. Formerly, during the Zhengde (1506–1521) and Jiajing (1522–1566) eras, although the predicted fractions and seconds of eclipses showed slight discrepancies, compared to the calendars of previous dynasties that ran ahead of or behind the heavens, the difference was vast, so there is no need to put forward proposals for resetting the calendrical epoch. Recently, however, the astronomical officials have been derelict in their duties, and their errors and discrepancies have departed from the norm, to the point that there have been occurrences that greatly shocked the ears and …

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
覩者夫獨是莫曉獨非莫知此古人所
以論律曆也今之司其事者將無狃於
是說與萬一訛舛有甚於斯者可漫爾
不爲之計與夫法久則翫翫則必飭諸
士試陳所以振飭之術詳著于篇俟執
事者採焉
問學莫大乎與人同善夫與人同善斯兼
善矣舜自耕稼以至帝天下皆用此道
也而孟氏乃曰窮則獨善達則兼善窮
===
與達果二施歟伯夷柳下惠所遭遇不
可謂達矣乃其風能使百世興起焉要
非止於獨善者孟氏顧猶少之而願學
孔子其所以異者安在孔子生春秋寧
削跡絕糧而不忍於忘世洙泗之濱羣
弟子蓋三千焉其汲汲於兼善如此豈
顧不安於窮歟伊尹身任天下之重謂
之兼善宜也廼顏子終身陋巷耳孟氏
至稱其賢與禹稷竝其所以同者又安
punctuated:
覩者。夫「獨是莫曉，獨非莫知」，此古人所以論律曆也。今之司其事者，將無狃於是說與？萬一訛舛有甚於斯者，可漫爾不爲之計與？夫法久則翫，翫則必飭。諸士試陳所以振飭之術，詳著于篇，俟執事者採焉。
問：學莫大乎與人同善。夫與人同善，斯兼善矣。舜自耕稼以至帝天下，皆用此道也。而孟氏乃曰：「窮則獨善，達則兼善。」窮與達果二施歟？伯夷、柳下惠所遭遇，不可謂達矣，乃其風能使百世興起焉，要非止於獨善者；孟氏顧猶少之，而願學孔子，其所以異者安在？孔子生春秋，寧削跡絕糧而不忍於忘世，洙泗之濱，羣弟子蓋三千焉，其汲汲於兼善如此，豈顧不安於窮歟？伊尹身任天下之重，謂之兼善宜也；廼顏子終身陋巷耳，孟氏至稱其賢與禹、稷竝，其所以同者又安
translation_en:
…what is heard and seen. Now, "even if you alone are right, no one will understand it; even if you alone are wrong, no one will know it"—this was how the ancients discussed pitch-pipes and the calendar. Could it be that those in charge of the matter today have grown complacent because of this saying? If by some chance the errors and discrepancies become even worse than this, can we carelessly fail to make plans for it? When a system endures for a long time, people grow negligent of it; when they grow negligent, it must be rectified. Gentlemen, try to set forth the arts by which it may be roused and rectified, writing them out in detail in your essays, to await selection by those in charge of affairs.

Question: In learning, nothing is greater than sharing goodness with others. Now, to share goodness with others is to perfect the whole world as well. From the time he plowed and sowed until he ruled all under Heaven as emperor, Shun 舜 employed this Way throughout. Yet Mencius (Mengshi 孟氏) said: "In obscurity, a man perfects his own person; in prominence, he perfects the whole world as well." Are obscurity and prominence truly two different applications of the Way? What Bo Yi 伯夷 and Liuxia Hui 柳下惠 encountered in life could hardly be called prominence; yet their moral example was able to inspire people for a hundred generations—in short, they did not stop at merely perfecting their own persons. Still, Mencius thought them narrow and wished instead to learn from Confucius (Kongzi 孔子). Wherein lies the difference between them? Confucius was born in the Spring and Autumn period; he would rather have his footprints erased and his provisions cut off than bear to forget the world. Along the banks of the Zhu 洙 and Si 泗 rivers, his assembled disciples numbered some three thousand. When he was so tirelessly devoted to perfecting the whole world, could it be that he was not content with obscurity? Yi Yin 伊尹 personally took the heavy burden of all under Heaven upon himself, so it is fitting to call him one who perfected the whole world. Yet Master Yan (Yanzi 顏子) lived out his entire life in a mean alley, and still Mencius praised his worthiness and ranked him alongside Yu 禹 and Ji 稷. Wherein, then, lies their similarity…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
在楊氏爲我以忘世爲高而孟氏斥之
猶易辨也墨翟之名至與孔子並稱彼
其說主於兼相愛交相利則與兼善又
何以異且當其時異端之說紛紛矣孟
氏顧不此之攻而唯楊墨之深闢抑又
何歟夫學術之辨不明則趨嚮不正似
是之防有不得不嚴者爾諸士皆以兼
善來也幸相與殫其說主司將以是徵
所養焉
===
問今用人之要以治郡邑在吏以靖疆圉
在將昔人傳循吏者惟曰經術潤飾乃
謀置帥者必先禮樂詩書無亦以士之
明經爲國家用而用莫急於茲二者歟
而或謂人之材情運量固有不能盡同
焉則又安所爲倚也試即漢世數人相
與評之立學成都者齊魯比風平盜渤
海者刀劍易俗子視密人者下詔褒名
德理中年者按掾推異斯皆明經吏也
punctuated:
在？楊氏「爲我」，以忘世爲高，而孟氏斥之，猶易辨也。墨翟之名，至與孔子並稱，彼其說主於兼相愛、交相利，則與「兼善」又何以異？且當其時，異端之說紛紛矣，孟氏顧不此之攻，而唯楊、墨之深闢，抑又何歟？夫學術之辨不明，則趨嚮不正，似是之防，有不得不嚴者。爾諸士皆以兼善來也，幸相與殫其說，主司將以是徵所養焉。

問：今用人之要，以治郡邑在吏，以靖疆圉在將。昔人傳循吏者，惟曰「經術潤飾」；乃謀置帥者，必先「禮樂詩書」。無亦以士之明經爲國家用，而用莫急於茲二者歟？而或謂人之材情運量，固有不能盡同焉，則又安所爲倚也？試即漢世數人相與評之：立學成都者，齊、魯比風；平盜渤海者，刀劍易俗；子視密人者，下詔褒名；德理中年者，按掾推異：斯皆明經吏也，
translation_en:
… Wherein does that lie? Master Yang’s (Yang Zhu 楊朱) principle of “for oneself” regarded forgetting the world as lofty, and when Master Meng (Mencius 孟子) rejected him, that was still easy to distinguish. Yet the name of Mo Di 墨翟 came to be paired on an equal footing with Confucius; his doctrine centered on mutual universal love and reciprocal benefit—how then does that differ from “bringing goodness to all the world together”? Moreover, at that time, heterodox doctrines were arising in profusion; why did Master Meng not attack those others, instead reserves his deepest refutation solely for Yang and Mo? Truly, if distinctions in scholarly learning are not made clear, then one’s orientation cannot be rectified, and the defenses against what is speciously similar must of necessity be strict. All of you scholars have come here aspiring to bring goodness to all the world together. Pray set forth your explanations in full, and the examiners will thereby gauge what you have cultivated.

Question: Today, the crux of employing men lies with civil officials for governing commanderies and districts, and with generals for pacifying the frontiers. When men of the past wrote biographies ofupright officials, they spoke simply of “adorning administration with classical scholarship”; and those who took counsel on appointing a commander-in-chief inevitably put “Rites, Music, the Odes, and the Documents” first. Is this not because scholars who understand the Classics are of service to the state, and no service is more urgent than these two? Yet some say that men’s talents, dispositions, and capacities cannot be entirely identical—on what, then, can one rely? Let us evaluate together several men of the Han dynasty: he who established schools in Chengdu (Wen Weng 文翁), until its customs rivaled those of Qi and Lu; he who pacified bandits in Bohai (Gong Sui 龔遂), transforming habits so that swords and knives were traded for farm tools; he who treated the people of Mi County as his children (Zhuo Mao 卓茂), earning an imperial edict praising his name; and he who governed Zhongmou through virtue (Lu Gong 魯恭), whose inspecting subalterns commended his extraordinary administration—all of these were civil officials who understood the Classics, …

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
而以斮篇虎穴爲能者何亦與之並其
稱歟矯制徵兵者郅支授首持節傳諭
者莎車就戮大樹著號者立破赤眉北
道可主者卒降劇虜斯皆明經將也他
若拔於亡卒人奴者亦赫然成功何歟
我
朝設文武科羅天下俊傑而又參之以貢舉
之途騎射之技宜其得人斌斌盛矣而
緩急之際猶未盡適於用者其故何也
===
夫天下未嘗無才計
國家每進之士不啻什伯漢世乃事業聲稱
則少遜焉豈責實者容有未至歟今欲
吏咸加理將不失職以共成清寧悠遠
之治則何道而可
閩水之大而爲中國患者莫如河則治河
之役宜急今日之務也乃往往屈羣策
卒未聞以一奇見者何哉昔者禹抑洪
水用又諸夏詩書所稱於今爲烈焉其
punctuated:
而以斮篇虎穴爲能者，何亦與之並其稱歟？矯制徵兵者，郅支授首；持節傳諭者，莎車就戮；大樹著號者，立破赤眉；北道可主者，卒降劇虜：斯皆明經將也。他若拔於亡卒、人奴者，亦赫然成功，何歟？我朝設文武科，羅天下俊傑，而又參之以貢舉之途、騎射之技，宜其得人斌斌盛矣；而緩急之際，猶未盡適於用者，其故何也？夫天下未嘗無才，計國家每進之士，不啻什伯漢世，乃事業聲稱則少遜焉，豈責實者容有未至歟？今欲吏咸加理，將不失職，以共成清寧悠遠之治，則何道而可？

閩水之大而爲中國患者，莫如河，則治河之役，宜急今日之務也；乃往往屈羣策，卒未聞以一奇見者，何哉？昔者禹抑洪水，用又諸夏，《詩》《書》所稱，於今爲烈焉。其
translation_en:
…Yet why are those whose capability lay in hacking bamboo slips [to investigate hidden crimes] or entering the tiger's lair [to eradicate powerful villains] also praised alongside them? He who forged an imperial decree to levy troops took the head of Zhizhi; he who held the imperial credentials to proclaim an edict put Yarkand (Suoju) to the sword; he who became known as the "Big Tree General" immediately routed the Red Eyebrows; and he who could serve as host of the northern road ultimately forced fierce bandits to surrender—all of these were generals well-versed in the Classics. Yet why is it that others, such as those promoted from among deserters or household slaves, also achieved illustrious success? Our Dynasty has established civil and military examinations to gather theoutstanding talents of the empire, and further supplemented them with the avenues of tribute recommendation and the skills of horsemanship and archery. Rightly, the men obtained should be refined and flourishing in abundance; yet in times of crisis and urgency, why are they still not entirely suited for practical use? Now, the world is never without talent. Counting the scholars advanced by the State at each turn, they are more than ten or a hundred times those of the Han era, yet their achievements and reputations are somewhat inferior. Could it be that our demand for practical substance has not yet gone far enough? If today we wish for all civil officials to govern well and all generals not to fail in their duties, so as to jointly achieve a pure, tranquil, and enduring rule, by what way can this be accomplished?

Question: Among the great rivers that pose a threat to the Central Plain, none compares to the Yellow River; thus, the task of controlling the River should be an urgent priority among today's affairs. Yet why is it that although it frequently exhausts the collective strategies of the court, in the end we never hear of a single extraordinary insight being put forward? In antiquity, Yu suppressed the floodwaters and thereby brought order to the Chinese states; what is praised in the Classic of Poetry (Shi) and Classic of History (Shu) remains illustrious to this day. Its…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
故法可參綜而行之歟嗣後議者紛紛
總之不離塞與不塞兩說將技止此矣
抑或有一道而見偶未之及歟河自�until
礫既徙惟西京受害特甚當文武盛時
則力主於塞其效蓋有可覩者豈塞猶
愈於不塞歟夫法與時宜利因勢導揆
今時勢謀於塞不塞間而用之果孰爲
便歟比歲河決不治致厪
上慮特爲置督府使董其事唯是
===
聖德格
天百靈效職業已漸底于績矣然思患貴防於
初作事當善其後乃議者或謂黃河之
故道宜復或謂宜別開一河以備非常
是歟否歟茲欲於斯二者外別求所謂
萬全長策爲
國計民生永賴之也則將安出歟往代嘗博
徵能浚治者莫有應書執事者羞之爾
諸士抱業而來寧無有概於中耶其各
punctuated: 故法可參綜而行之歟？嗣後議者紛紛，總之不離塞與不塞兩說，將技止此矣，抑或有一道而見偶未之及歟？河自until礫既徙，惟西京受害特甚，當文、武盛時，則力主於塞，其效蓋有可覩者，豈塞猶愈於不塞歟？夫法與時宜，利因勢導，揆今時勢，謀於塞不塞間而用之，果孰爲便歟？比歲河決不治，致厪上慮，特爲置督府，使董其事，唯是聖德格天，百靈效職，業已漸底于績矣。然思患貴防於初，作事當善其後，乃議者或謂黃河之故道宜復，或謂宜別開一河以備非常，是歟？否歟？茲欲於斯二者外，別求所謂萬全長策，爲國計民生永賴之也，則將安出歟？往代嘗博徵能浚治者，莫有應書，執事者羞之。爾諸士抱業而來，寧無有概於中耶？其各
translation_en: …Can his former methods be consulted, synthesized, and put into practice? Thereafter, discussants offered a profusion of views, which in sum never departed from the two theories of blocking or not blocking the river. Does the art of river control stop here, or is there another way that their insight happened not to reach? After the Yellow River shifted course from礫 [Suoli?], the Western Capital (Xijing) suffered especially severe harm. During the flourishing eras of Emperors Wen and Wu of Han, policy strongly favored blocking the breaches, and its effectiveness could indeed be seen. Could it be that blocking is after all superior to not blocking? Now, methods should suit the times, and benefits are guided according to the configuration of circumstances. Judging by present times and circumstances, if we deliberate between blocking and not blocking and put one into use, which would truly be more advantageous? In recent years, the breaches of the Yellow River went uncontained, causing anxiety to His Majesty, who specially established a Supreme Commander's office to direct the affair. Only because His Sacred Virtue reached Heaven and the hundred spirits performed their duties has the work already gradually been brought to accomplishment. Yet in anticipating calamities, it is crucial to guard against them at the outset, and in undertaking affairs, one must ensure a good aftermath. Now some discussants say that the old course of the Yellow River ought to be restored, while others say that another channel ought to be opened separately to prepare for extraordinary emergencies. Are these views right or wrong? If we now wish, beyond these two options, to seek out a so-called completely secure, long-term strategy upon which the state finances and the people's livelihood may eternally rely, from whence shall it come? In former dynasties, when wide calls were made for men capable of dredging and controlling the river, no one responded to the summons, to the shame of those in charge of affairs. You gentlemen have come bearing your learning—could you have no deeply held views within? Let each of you…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text: 裁所見以對
punctuated: 裁所見以對。
translation_en: …tailor your views and present them in response.

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
中式舉人一百三十五名
第一名陸大成　太倉州學生　易
第二名石崑玉　湖廣蕲州黄梅縣人監生　詩
第三名甯瑞鯉　廣德州學生　書
第四名史懋文　金壇縣學附學生　春秋

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
舜亦以命禹
陸大成
同考試官訓導郭　批〔精瑩溫粹振雅還醇之作〕
同考試官訓導張　批〔闡明道統宛然虞廷之授受〕
同考試官教諭范　批〔莊嚴典雅迥異塵氛〕
考試官侍讀羅　批〔純正莊雅〕
考試官右中允高　批〔明實爾雅〕
===
虞聖之傳心以其所受者授之而已蓋帝王之
道本於心也則於授受之際惡容有異哉且夫
帝王相承之序有治統焉有道統焉由堯舜而
後禹蓋得其統矣彼繼舜而有天下者禹也爲
天下而得禹者舜也治之所在舜旣以堯之授
者授諸禹而寄聖神以立極道之所在舜亦以
堯之命者命諸禹而率彝訓以傳心原曆數而
揭執中之旨堯之肇開于舜者然也玆於禹命
之而協帝者因爲祗承之則語執中而嚴永終
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

「舜亦以命禹。」

陸大成
同考試官訓導郭　批〔精瑩溫粹，振雅還醇之作。〕
同考試官訓導張　批〔闡明道統，宛然虞廷之授受。〕
同考試官教諭范　批〔莊嚴典雅，迥異塵氛。〕
考試官侍讀羅　批〔純正莊雅。〕
考試官右中允高　批〔明實爾雅。〕

虞聖之傳心，以其所受者授之而已。蓋帝王之道本於心也，則於授受之際，惡容有異哉？且夫帝王相承之序，有治統焉，有道統焉。由堯、舜而後，禹蓋得其統矣。彼繼舜而有天下者，禹也；爲天下而得禹者，舜也。治之所在，舜旣以堯之授者授諸禹，而寄聖神以立極；道之所在，舜亦以堯之命者命諸禹，而率彝訓以傳心。原曆數而揭執中之旨，堯之肇開于舜者然也，玆於禹命之，而協帝者因爲祗承之則；語執中而嚴永終

First Session

The Four Books

Lu Dacheng 陸大成
Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Guo 郭, comments: [A refined,lustrous, gentle, and pure piece; a work that revives elegance and returns to purity.]
Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Zhang 張, comments: [It elucidates the transmission of the Way, vividly evoking the giving and receiving at the court of Yu (Shun).]
Associate Examiner, Instructor Fan 范, comments: [Solemn, dignified, classic, and elegant, far removed from worldly dust.]
Examiner, Academician Reader-in-Waiting Luo 羅, comments: [Pure, orthodox, solemn, and elegant.]
Examiner, Right Companion to the Heir Apparent Gao 高, comments: [Clear, substantial, and refined.]

When the Sage of Yu (Shun) transmitted the mind, he simply conferred upon another that which he himself had received. For the Way of emperors and kings is rooted in the mind; at the moment of giving and receiving, how could there be any difference? Moreover, in the sequence of succession among emperors and kings, there is the lineage of governance (zhitong) and the lineage of the Way (daotong). After Yao and Shun, it was Yu who obtained this lineage. He who succeeded Shun and possessed All under Heaven was Yu; he who found Yu for the sake of All under Heaven was Shun. Where governance resided, Shun already conferred upon Yu what Yao had conferred upon him, entrusting the sagely and divine one to establish the supreme standard. Where the Way resided, Shun likewise charged Yu with what Yao had charged him, following the constant instructions to transmit the mind. Tracing the calendar-calculated destiny of Heaven and holding up the doctrine of holding fast to the Mean—such was what Yao first opened up to Shun; now he charged Yu with it, so that what brought harmony with the Sovereign became the rule to be reverently received. Speaking of holding fast to the Mean and sternly issuing the warning about ending forever…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
之戒舜之首聞於堯者然也玆命禹以之而進
虞者因爲啓夏之謨上奉神明之依天意固有
攸歸矣乃命以祈天之本不過卽放勳之咨者
一叮嚀焉道雖始於堯而其傳固在舜也下撫
有衆之戴人心固有攸屬矣乃命以安人之要
不過卽文祖之受者一重申焉道雖託之禹而
其責實在舜也是非不能易也帝王大經大法
本於是堯可語舜舜不可語禹乎亦非不敢加
也天下萬事萬物原於是舜可紹堯禹不可紹
舜乎由是禹起而光大之千聖相傳之法不亦
===
衍於無窮哉吁此三聖相授而守一道也與嘗
論中者天命也執其中者天心也命同則心同
而舜益以微危精一云者何哉堯舜心與天一
而克勤克儉不矜不伐非人道幾希間乎乃精
一交致蓋執焉者事也故曰禹見而知之至是
而禹亦堯舜矣亦天矣誰謂入聖域而未優
凡事豫則立不豫則廢言前定則不跲事
前定則不困行前定則不疚道前定則
punctuated:
之戒，舜之首聞於堯者然也；玆命禹以之，而進虞者，因爲啓夏之謨。上奉神明之依，天意固有攸歸矣；乃命以祈天之本，不過卽放勳之咨者一叮嚀焉，道雖始於堯，而其傳固在舜也。下撫有衆之戴，人心固有攸屬矣；乃命以安人之要，不過卽文祖之受者一重申焉，道雖託之禹，而其責實在舜也。是非不能易也，帝王大經大法本於是，堯可語舜，舜不可語禹乎？亦非不敢加也，天下萬事萬物原於是，舜可紹堯，禹不可紹舜乎？由是禹起而光大之，千聖相傳之法，不亦衍於無窮哉？吁！此三聖相授而守一道也與！嘗論中者，天命也；執其中者，天心也。命同則心同，而舜益以「微危精一」云者，何哉？堯、舜心與天一，而克勤克儉，不矜不伐，非人道幾希間乎？乃精一交致，蓋執焉者事也。故曰「禹見而知之」，至是而禹亦堯、舜矣，亦天矣，誰謂入聖域而未優？
「凡事豫則立，不豫則廢。言前定則不跲，事前定則不困，行前定則不疚，道前定則
translation_en:
… [Speaking of Holding Fast the Mean and strictly enforcing the warning that the Mandate] might end forever—this was what Shun first heard from Yao; here he charged Yu with it, so that what had been offered as counsel to Yu [Shun] thereby became the plan for inaugurating the Xia dynasty. Above, in upholding the reliance of the spirits, the will of Heaven indeed had a place to which it turned; yet in charging him with the fundamental way of praying to Heaven, Shun did no more than earnestly reiterate the counsel once given by Fangxun [Yao]. Although the Way began with Yao, its transmission indeed rested with Shun. Below, in soothing the allegiance of the multitude, the hearts of the people indeed had someone to whom they belonged; yet in charging him with the essential means of bringing peace to the people, Shun did no more than reaffirm what had been received in the Temple of the Cultured Ancestor. Although the Way was entrusted to Yu, the responsibility for it truly lay with Shun.

This was not because he was unable to alter it: the great norms and great laws of emperors and kings are rooted in this—if Yao could speak of it to Shun, could Shun not speak of it to Yu? Nor was it because he dared not add to it: all the myriad affairs and myriad things under Heaven originate in this—if Shun could continue Yao, could Yu not continue Shun? From this, Yu arose and gloriously magnified it; was not the method transmitted from one sage to another across a thousand generations thus extended endlessly? Alas! Was this not how the three sages handed it down to one another while guarding a single Way?

I have observed that the Mean is the Mandate of Heaven, and to hold fast that Mean is the Mind of Heaven. Since the Mandate is the same, the Mind is the same; why then did Shun add the words about being "subtle and perilous, refined and single-minded"? The minds of Yao and Shun were one with Heaven, yet Yu's being able to be diligent and frugal, and neither boastful nor self-praising—was this not within that slight distinction pertaining to the way of man? Thus, to apply both refinement and single-mindedness mutually was the practical work of holding fast to it. Therefore it is said, "Yu saw it and knew it." Reaching this point, Yu too was Yao and Shun, and too was Heaven; who would say that he entered the realm of the sages and yet was not fully accomplished?

"In all things, if there is prior preparation, they will succeed; without prior preparation, they will fail. If words are determined beforehand, there will be no stumbling; if affairs are determined beforehand, there will be no distress; if conduct is determined beforehand, there will be no remorse; if the Way is determined beforehand, it will…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
不窮在下位不獲乎上民不可得而治
矣獲乎上有道不信乎朋友不獲乎上
矣信乎朋友有道不順乎親不信乎朋
友矣順乎親有道反諸身不誠不順乎
親矣誠身有道不明乎善不誠乎身矣
甯瑞鯉

同考試官教諭潘　批〔體裁純正而詞復典雅可式〕

===

中庸究言事之當豫而益推明其意焉夫豫之
於事也尚矣由言事行道及在下位推之而事
之當豫不益明乎中庸若曰天下無常事事吾心
有常誠亦存乎豫而已何則自達道達德以至
九經之屬凡事也凡誠之所行也唯勿二勿三
素豫吾內則事以有本而立有不爲爲斯成矣
使一時一事襲取於外則事以無本而廢有不
動動斯僨矣何以明其然也出身加民之謂言
punctuated:
不窮。在下位不獲乎上，民不可得而治矣；獲乎上有道，不信乎朋友，不獲乎上矣；信乎朋友有道，不順乎親，不信乎朋友矣；順乎親有道，反諸身不誠，不順乎親矣；誠身有道，不明乎善，不誠乎身矣。

甯瑞鯉

同考試官教諭潘　批〔體裁純正，而詞復典雅可式。〕
考試官侍讀羅　批〔明順。〕

《中庸》究言事之當豫，而益推明其意焉。夫豫之於事也尚矣，由言、事、行、道及在下位推之，而事之當豫不益明乎？《中庸》若曰：天下無常事，事吾心有常誠，亦存乎豫而已。何則？自達道、達德以至九經之屬，凡事也，凡誠之所行也。唯勿二勿三，素豫吾內，則事以有本而立，有不爲，爲斯成矣；使一時一事，襲取於外，則事以無本而廢，有不動，動斯僨矣。何以明其然也？出身加民之謂言，
translation_en:
…will not be exhausted. If those in subordinate positions do not win the confidence of their superiors, the common people cannot be governed. There is a way to win the confidence of one's superiors: if one is not trusted by one's friends, one will not win the confidence of one's superiors. There is a way to be trusted by one's friends: if one is not obedient to one's parents, one will not be trusted by one's friends. There is a way to be obedient to one's parents: if upon examining oneself one is not sincere, one will not be obedient to one's parents. There is a way to make oneself sincere: if one does not understand what is good, one will not make oneself sincere."

Ning Ruili 甯瑞鯉
Associate Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Li 李 comments: "Concise and polished; those who are merely thorough [?] cannot attain this."
Associate Examiner, Instructor Pan 潘 comments: "The form and style are pure and correct, and the diction is moreover classically elegant and worthy of serving as a model."
Examiner, Academician Reader-in-waiting (shidu) Luo 羅 comments: "Clear and smooth."
Examiner, Right Companion to the Heir Apparent (you zhongyun) Gao 高 comments: "The meaning of prior preparation is well developed."

The Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) thoroughly discusses how affairs ought to be prepared for beforehand, and further extends and clarifies this meaning. Indeed, prior preparation in affairs is of the highest importance! Extending the principle through words, affairs, conduct, the Way, and occupying a subordinate position, does it not become even clearer that affairs ought to be prepared for beforehand? It is as if the Doctrine of the Mean were saying: There are no constant affairs in the world, yet in handling affairs [?], our minds possess a constant sincerity—and this too lies simply in prior preparation. Why is this so? From the universal ways (dadao) and universal virtues (dade) down to the nine standard rules (jiujing) and the like, all are affairs, and all are that through which sincerity is put into practice. Only when, without duplicity or wavering, we habitually prepare beforehand within ourselves, will affairs be established through having a root; there may be things we do not undertake, but whatever we undertake is thereby accomplished. If, at a given moment or in a given affair, we merely seize upon it externally, then affairs will fail through lacking a root; there may be times we do not act, but whenever we act, they are thereby ruined. How can we make clear that this is so? That which issues from one's person and reaches the people is called "words,"…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
而措諸天下者事也必前定焉則言無不順而
事以時舉也不然跲且困隨之矣發邇見遠之
謂行而率諸吾性者道也必前定焉則行無不
慊而道以時出也不然疚且窮隨之矣斯非獨
居上然也至在下位未嘗不欲治其民者然能
治民未嘗不先獲乎上者以獲上道在信友非
信而譽命弗逺矣以信友道在順親非順而志
行弗孚矣順親之道誠身其本也不誠未有能
順者也誠身之道明善其要也不明未有能誠
===
者也蓋自治民而推極於身則無不豫必誠身
而達順於治斯無不立下位且然況凡事耶信
乎誠而不豫猶爲無誠而道德九經悉妄也已
豫之義大矣哉而君人者可以思矣抑此聖學
也文之緝凞武之敬義胥此焉在故當其時道
德純明而周官之法度燦然大備無廢而不立
者矣不然雖周禮具文耳而豫可弗講耶豫之
何如曰明善誠身無上下一也
惻隱之心仁之端也羞惡之心義之端也
punctuated:
而措諸天下者，事也。必前定焉，則言無不順，而事以時舉也；不然，跲且困隨之矣。發邇見遠之謂行，而率諸吾性者，道也。必前定焉，則行無不慊，而道以時出也；不然，疚且窮隨之矣。斯非獨居上然也。至在下位，未嘗不欲治其民者，然能治民，未嘗不先獲乎上者。以獲上，道在信友，非信而譽命弗逺矣；以信友，道在順親，非順而志行弗孚矣。順親之道，誠身其本也，不誠未有能順者也；誠身之道，明善其要也，不明未有能誠者也。蓋自治民而推極於身，則無不豫；必誠身而達順於治，斯無不立。下位且然，況凡事耶？信乎誠而不豫，猶爲無誠，而道德九經悉妄也已。豫之義大矣哉，而君人者可以思矣！抑此聖學也，文之緝凞、武之敬義，胥此焉在。故當其時，道德純明，而周官之法度燦然大備，無廢而不立者矣。不然，雖周禮具文耳，而豫可弗講耶？豫之何如？曰：明善誠身，無上下一也。
「惻隱之心，仁之端也；羞惡之心，義之端也；
translation_en:
… and what is put into practice throughout the realm is called affairs. Only when they are determined beforehand will words never fail to be smooth and affairs be carried out in timely fashion; otherwise, stumbling and distress will follow. What issues forth nearby and becomes visible afar is called conduct, and what follows from our nature is the Way. Only when they are determined beforehand will conduct never fail to be satisfactory and the Way be manifested in timely fashion; otherwise, remorse and exhaustion will follow. This is not true of those in high position alone. Even those in subordinate positions never fail to desire to govern their people well, yet to be able to govern the people, they must first win the confidence of their superiors. To win the confidence of superiors, the way lies in being trusted by friends; without trust, one's reputation and mandate will not reach far. To be trusted by friends, the way lies in being obedient to parents; without obedience, one's intentions and conduct will not inspire confidence. As for the way of being obedient to parents, making oneself sincere is its root; without sincerity, no one has ever been able to be obedient. As for the way of making oneself sincere, understanding the good is its essential point; without understanding, no one has ever been able to be sincere. Thus, when one traces the governance of the people all the way back to one's own person, there is nothing that is not prepared beforehand; only when one makes oneself sincere and extends that smoothly to governance will there be nothing that is not established. If this is true even for those in subordinate positions, how much more so for all affairs in general! Truly, sincerity without prior preparation is tantamount to having no sincerity at all, and the universal Way, universal virtues, and the Nine Standard Rules would all be in vain. Great indeed is the meaning of preparation beforehand, and rulers of men may well reflect upon it! Moreover, this is the learning of the sages. The "continuous bright敬" of King Wen and the "reverence and righteousness" of King Wu both reside herein. Therefore, in their time, the Way and its virtue were pure and illustrious, and the laws and institutions of the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan) were brilliantly and grandly complete, with nothing neglected or unestablished. Otherwise, even the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) would have been mere empty text—so how could one fail to study preparation beforehand? And how does one prepare beforehand? I say: by understanding the good and making oneself sincere, which is one and the same for both superior and inferior alike.

"The feeling of commiseration is the sprout of humaneness; the feeling of shame and dislike is the sprout of righteousness; …"

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
辭讓之心禮之端也是非之心智之端
也人之有是四端也猶其有四體也
閻士選
同考試官教諭曾　批〔精切明瑩誦之豁然〕

大賢論良心原其各出於性明其必有於人夫
性乃心之理而情則性之用也此良心之所以
必有也與孟子意謂人得天地之心心妙性情
===
之德是心也何以人而皆有也蓋不忍之心出
之卽惻隱而若羞惡若辭讓若是非皆是心之
所發也不忍之心斂之卽仁而曰義曰禮曰智
皆是心之所存也愛心感而惻隱生乃仁之露
其端也羞惡之萌於有耻則爲義之端矣敬心
感而辭讓著乃禮之呈其端也是非之形於有
別則爲智之端矣有是情悉根是性得之非自
外也有是性斯顯是情主之常在中也然則人
之有是四端也非卽其有四體乎吾知所存乎
punctuated:
辭讓之心，禮之端也；是非之心，智之端也。人之有是四端也，猶其有四體也。」

閻士選

同考試官教諭曾批：〔精切明瑩，誦之豁然。〕
考試官侍讀羅批：〔體認真切。〕
考試官右中允高批：〔縝密整雅。〕

大賢論良心，原其各出於性，明其必有於人。夫性乃心之理，而情則性之用也，此良心之所以必有也與？孟子意謂：人得天地之心，心妙性情之德，是心也，何以人而皆有也？蓋不忍之心，出之卽惻隱，而若羞惡、若辭讓、若是非，皆是心之所發也；不忍之心，斂之卽仁，而曰義、曰禮、曰智，皆是心之所存也。愛心感而惻隱生，乃仁之露其端也；羞惡之萌於有耻，則爲義之端矣。敬心感而辭讓著，乃禮之呈其端也；是非之形於有別，則爲智之端矣。有是情悉根是性，得之非自外也；有是性斯顯是情，主之常在中也。然則人之有是四端也，非卽其有四體乎？吾知所存乎
translation_en:
…"The feeling of modesty and deference is the sprout of ritual propriety; the feeling of approving and disapproving is the sprout of wisdom. That human beings have these four sprouts is just like their having four limbs."

Yan Shixuan 閻士選

Associate Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Zeng comments: [Precise, incisive, and crystal clear; reciting it brings sudden enlightenment.]
Examiner, Academician Reader-in-Waiting (shidu) Luo comments: [Experientially realized and genuinely earnest.]
Examiner, Right Companion to the Heir Apparent (you zhongyun) Gao comments: [Meticulous, orderly, and elegant.]

When the Great Worthy [Mencius] discusses the innate good mind, he traces how each of its feelings arises from human nature, thereby making clear that all human beings necessarily possess them. Now, human nature is the principle of the mind, while the feelings are the function of human nature; is this not why the innate good mind is necessarily present in everyone?

Mencius's meaning is that human beings receive the mind of Heaven and Earth, and the mind wondrously integrates the virtues of human nature and the feelings. Why is it that every human being possesses this mind? Indeed, when the mind that cannot bear to see the sufferings of others is expressed outward, it is none other than commiseration; and feelings such as shame and dislike, modesty and deference, and approving and disapproving are all issuances of this mind. When the mind that cannot bear to see the sufferings of others is gathered inward, it is none other than benevolence; and what are called righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom are all what is preserved within this mind.

When a loving mind is stirred and commiseration arises, that is benevolence revealing its sprout; when shame and dislike bud forth from having a sense of disgrace, that is the sprout of righteousness. When a reverent mind is stirred and modesty and deference become manifest, that is ritual propriety presenting its sprout; when approving and disapproving take form in making distinctions, that is the sprout of wisdom. Having these feelings is entirely rooted in having this nature—they are not acquired from outside; having this nature consequently manifests these feelings—their master constantly abides within. This being so, that human beings have these four sprouts—is it not just like their having four limbs? I know that as for what is preserved in…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
人者豈無仁義之心哉仁必有惻隱義必有羞
惡是惟無感感斯通矣豈無禮智之心哉禮必
有辭讓智必有是非是惟無觸觸斯應矣非獨
先王爲然也苟未至物欲陷溺者皆有之四端
充足於心不猶四體各足於身乎非獨乍見爲
然也苟未至旦晝牿亡者皆有之四端具而爲
人不猶四體備而成形乎夫使四端非人之所
有是必不出於性者也焉有情而離性乎哉雖
然良心人固同具而聖凡卒至相遠者何耶蓋
===
心體雖大而其端實微先王有之而天下運掌
者察而充也衆人有之而自賊與賊人者弗察
而充也他日破三品之說復致詳焉而乃歸于
不能盡其才噫有才而不盡伊誰之咎與
