Later ages did not fail to desire to invigorate the overarching principles of order so as to sustain the realm; yet some were blind to the exaltation of fundamental essentials and delighted in the habit of tedious harshness, or neglected the responsibility of relying on assistive ministers and trusted in the monopolization of their own eyes and ears. Their intentions were indeed far removed from those of the sages—what wonder, then, that…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
其治之不古若哉雖然君心亦未易言也虛靈
之中理欲相爲貞勝而矧四方之聲色玩好日
爲吾蠹者又雜然交於其前是故貴有以養之
而養之之功則莫要於主敬夫惟戒謹於燕閒
之暇緝熙於宥密之衷使此心純然天理一毫
物欲不得以累之而又親賢臣遠小人于以講
明乎義理之歸而閉塞其私邪之路故不勞而
庶績熙無爲而天下治也此又恭已之本也
表
===
擬輔臣恭撰
進
䌫肅殿箴表
陸大成
同考試官訓導郭　批〔詞藻豐贍體裁典重又多因文 □□□□〕
以抒忠愛
同考試官訓導張　批〔體莊而雅辭典而麗懇懇忠悃〕
溢於言表
同考試官教諭范　批〔以莊雅之詞抒忠悃之素旨哉〕
punctuated:
其治之不古若哉？雖然，君心亦未易言也。虛靈之中，理欲相爲貞勝，而矧四方之聲色玩好日爲吾蠹者，又雜然交於其前。是故貴有以養之，而養之之功則莫要於主敬。夫惟戒謹於燕閒之暇，緝熙於宥密之衷，使此心純然天理，一毫物欲不得以累之；而又親賢臣、遠小人，于以講明乎義理之歸，而閉塞其私邪之路。故不勞而庶績熙，無爲而天下治也。此又恭已之本也。

表

擬輔臣恭撰進《䌫肅殿箴》表
陸大成
同考試官訓導郭　批〔詞藻豐贍，體裁典重，又多因文□□□□〕以抒忠愛。
同考試官訓導張　批〔體莊而雅，辭典而麗，懇懇忠悃〕溢於言表。
同考試官教諭范　批〔以莊雅之詞，抒忠悃之素，旨哉！〕
translation_en:
…that their governance does not match that of antiquity? Even so, the ruler's mind is no easy matter to speak of. Within its empty and numinous awareness, principle and desire contend to prevail over one another; how much more so when the sights, sounds, and curiosities from all quarters, which daily act as pests upon us, also crowd together in confusion before it! Therefore, what is valued is having the means to nourish it, and in the effort of nourishing it, nothing is more essential than holding fast to reverence. Only by being cautious and apprehensive during moments of private leisure, and by continuing in bright radiance within the quiet depths of the inner heart, can one make this mind purely Heavenly Principle, so that not the slightest speck of material desire is able to encumber it; and furthermore, by drawing close to worthy ministers and keeping petty men at a distance, one thereby clarifies the ultimate course of moral principle and blocks up the paths of selfish perversity. Thus, without toil, all achievements shine forth, and through non-action, the empire is well governed. This, in turn, is the foundation of reverent self-restraint.

Memorial

Imitation of a Memorial by the Grand Secretaries Respectfully Composing and Presenting the Admonitions for the Yongsu [?] Palace (䌫肅殿箴)
Lu Dacheng 陸大成
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Guo 郭 comments: 〔The diction is rich and abundant, the form is classical and dignified, and moreover it frequently uses the text [4 illegible characters]〕 to express loyalty and affection.
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Zhang 張 comments: 〔The style is solemn and refined, the phrasing is classical and elegant, and earnest loyal sincerity〕 overflows beyond the words.
Associate Examiner and Instructor Fan 范 comments: 〔With solemn and refined words, he expresses his abiding loyal sincerity—how admirable in meaning!〕

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
考試官侍讀羅　批〔莊重典雅尤得大臣箴規之義錄之〕
考試官右中允高　批〔語質直而意忠款進規表之有則者〕
萬曆七年某月某日臣某等恭撰
雝肅殿箴
進呈者伏以
聰明作后
九重益儆於銘盤矇瞍奏公一得粗申于納牖
帝治撫泰交之運
聖心廑乾惕之圖職忝疑丞
===
美宜將順臣某等誠惶誠恐頓首頓首上言王
者宅中圖大功先宥密之嚴人臣憂治危
明忠殫謀猷之告故堯兢舜業洛汭戒於
危微而益賛皐謨矢颺言于喜起交儆之
風如在維新之命若開帝謂文王予懷明
德亦臨亦保而畏天之威不識不知以順
帝之則肆閨門肇基風化藹雝雝而在宮
迺鬼神常享克誠凜肅肅其在廟罔時恫
罔時怨禋祀允惠於宗公御于家御于邦
punctuated:
考試官侍讀羅　批〔莊重典雅，尤得大臣箴規之義。錄之。〕
考試官右中允高　批〔語質直而意忠款，進規表之有則者。〕

萬曆七年某月某日，臣某等恭撰《雝肅殿箴》進呈者。伏以聰明作后，九重益儆於銘盤；矇瞍奏公，一得粗申于納牖。帝治撫泰交之運，聖心廑乾惕之圖。職忝疑丞，美宜將順。臣某等誠惶誠恐，頓首頓首，上言：王者宅中圖大，功先宥密之嚴；人臣憂治危明，忠殫謀猷之告。故堯兢舜業，洛汭戒於危微；而益賛皐謨，矢颺言于喜起。交儆之風如在，維新之命若開。帝謂文王：「予懷明德。」亦臨亦保，而畏天之威；不識不知，以順帝之則。肆閨門肇基風化，藹雝雝而在宮；迺鬼神常享克誠，凜肅肅其在廟。罔時恫，罔時怨，禋祀允惠於宗公；御于家，御于邦，
translation_en:
Examiner and Academician Reader-in-waiting Luo comments: [Dignified, weighty, classic, and refined; it especially captures the spirit of a great minister's admonition. Record it.]
Examiner and Right Companion to the Heir Apparent Gao comments: [The language is plain and direct while the intent is loyal and sincere; it is a memorial of admonition that conforms to the proper standard.]

On a certain day of a certain month in the seventh year of the Wanli era [1579], Your Servants so-and-so and others respectfully compose the "Admonition for the Hall of Harmony and Reverence" (Yongsu dian zhen) for presentation to the throne.

Humbly we reflect that when one of intelligence and insight becomes sovereign, the Ninefold Palace grows ever more vigilant through the inscription on the bathing basin; and as the blind musicians perform their duties, our single humble insight is roughly set forth as if offering counsel through a window. Imperial governance now embraces an era of harmonious communion between heaven and earth, yet the sagely mind remains earnestly attentive to plans of unceasing vigilance. Unworthily occupying the offices of the Four Auxiliaries, it is fitting that we comply with and further Your Majesty's virtues.

With utmost trepidation and awe, Your Servants so-and-so and others bow our heads to the ground again and again and speak to Your Majesty: When a true king occupies the center and plans for greatness, his achievement begins with the strictness of serene profundity; when a minister worries in times of order and feels peril in times of enlightenment, his loyalty is exhausted in reporting his counsels and plans. Thus Yao was cautious and Shun was industrious, warning at the bend of the Luo River of the precariousness of the human mind and the subtlety of the moral mind; and Yi assisted the counsels of Gao Yao, setting forth his lofty words in the songs of rejoicing and rising to action. The custom of mutual admonition seems still present today, as if the Mandate made new were just opening before us. The Lord on High said to King Wen: "I cherish your bright virtue." Whether in the presence of others or in seclusion, he revered the majesty of Heaven; without conscious effort or artifice, he followed the pattern of the Lord. Therefore, within the inner quarters he laid the foundation of moral transformation, mild and harmonious in the palace; and the spirits ever accepted his utmost sincerity, awe-inspiring and reverent in the ancestral temple. None was caused distress and none harbored resentment, as his pure sacrifices truly accorded with the ancestral dukes; governing his family and governing his state, …

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
儀刑遍乎乎下國今聞浹而亹亹景祿序
其皇皇自純德旣遐而徽猷遂邈密房邃
寢忘嗜慾之滑和瓊室瑶臺甘逸豫以滅
德自非
聖以繼聖孰能防之又防茲蓋恭遇
皇帝陛下
天啓神明
日新德業
宮闈體正覯協氣之橫流
===
廟祀躬虔歌
孝思之維則九族旣睦尚
獨觀和順之原萬國咸賓猶
深切怠荒之戒迺聿新乎
堯室爰特表以周謨
出入斯欽
憲章益邇自是緝熙
聖域功不越乎戶庭因而
垂拱明堂化遂彌于海宇臣等學寡淵源心勤
punctuated: 儀刑遍乎乎下國。今聞浹而亹亹，景祿序其皇皇。自純德旣遐，而徽猷遂邈。密房邃寢，忘嗜慾之滑和；瓊室瑶臺，甘逸豫以滅德。自非聖以繼聖，孰能防之又防？茲蓋恭遇皇帝陛下：天啓神明，日新德業。宮闈體正，覯協氣之橫流；廟祀躬虔，歌孝思之維則。九族旣睦，尚獨觀和順之原；萬國咸賓，猶深切怠荒之戒。迺聿新乎堯室，爰特表以周謨。出入斯欽，憲章益邇。自是緝熙聖域，功不越乎戶庭；因而垂拱明堂，化遂彌于海宇。臣等學寡淵源，心勤
translation_en: …and his model conduct spread throughout the subordinate states. His fine reputation[?] pervaded everywhere, tireless and unceasing; great blessings followed in magnificent succession. Once such pure virtue receded into the distance, those admirable counsels likewise became remote. In secluded chambers and deep bedchambers, rulers forgot how indulgences and desires disturb inner harmony; on jade terraces and in瓊 palaces, they willingly gave themselves over to ease and pleasure, thereby destroying their virtue. Unless sage succeeds sage, who is able to guard against this again and again? Now we respectfully encounter Your Majesty the Emperor: Heaven has inspired your divine intelligence, and day by day you renew your virtuous achievements. With the inner palace rectified in principle, we witness harmonious ether flowing abroad in abundance; with the ancestral temple sacrifices performed in personal reverence, we sing of how your filial thoughts serve as the model. Though the nine grades of kinsmen are already in harmony, you still look in solitude into the source of concord and compliance; though the myriad states all submit as guests, you still take deeply to heart the warning against indolence and neglect. Thus you have newly refurbished the chambers of Yao, and specially set forth the counsels of Zhou. In going out and coming in you maintain reverence, and the constitutional models are brought ever closer. From this, as you continuously brighten the realm of sagehood, the effort does not go beyond doorway and courtyard; and thereby, as you let your robes hang down with hands folded in the Hall of Light, your transforming influence fills the entire world within the seas. Your servants, whose learning is shallow in its origins, yet whose hearts are diligent in…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
獻納惟
深宮幽獨之地眞
明命鑒觀之時雖聖哲圖存方顯陳於
講幄而隱微幾著宜遂養于
淵居謹隨事以納忠輒因經而演訓勿作好勿
作惡懋
建極於中和無荒色無荒禽愼防微于豫怠處
玄默若萬幾之臨在
燕閒同四國之正琴瑟未御而德靡悔允矣身
修家齊黍稷匪馨而福不回祇哉神鑒民
悅敬勝義勝敢云繼響於微言惟時惟幾
竊欲揚休于炯誡詞兼得失義舉艱危接
===
自
帝心容備芻蕘之擇屛之
御座庶方鞀鐸之陳昔大寶敷言徒蒙恩於奬
拔洎丹扆納誨未救患於荒遊繄
上下之一心實古今之希覯亶勉勉而
望道式弘未見之懷於穆穆以
punctuated: 獻納。惟深宮幽獨之地，眞明命鑒觀之時。雖聖哲圖存，方顯陳於講幄；而隱微幾著，宜遂養于淵居。謹隨事以納忠，輒因經而演訓：勿作好、勿作惡，懋建極於中和；無荒色、無荒禽，愼防微于豫怠。處玄默若萬幾之臨，在燕閒同四國之正。琴瑟未御而德靡悔，允矣身修家齊；黍稷匪馨而福不回，祇哉神鑒民悅。敬勝義勝，敢云繼響於微言；惟時惟幾，竊欲揚休于炯誡。詞兼得失，義舉艱危。接自帝心，容備芻蕘之擇；屛之御座，庶方鞀鐸之陳。昔《大寶》敷言，徒蒙恩於奬拔；洎《丹扆》納誨，未救患於荒遊。繄上下之一心，實古今之希覯。亶勉勉而望道，式弘未見之懷；於穆穆以
translation_en: … offering counsel. We reflect that the secluded privacy of the deep palace is truly the moment when the bright Mandate looks down in scrutiny. Although the pictorial records of sages and worthies are already displayed openly in the lecture tent, the subtle springs of action that become manifest in solitude ought accordingly to be nourished in Your quiet residence. We carefully offer our loyalty in accordance with each matter, and forthwith elaborate the lessons based on the Classics: "Make no partial fondness and make no partial hatred," exerting Yourself to establish the supreme standard in centrality and harmony; "be not wildly addicted to women and be not wildly addicted to hunting," cautiously guarding against the slightest beginnings of indolence and ease. Dwell in profound silence as though facing a myriad affairs of state; abide in private leisure just as when rectifying the four quarters of the realm. Before the zithers and lutes are even played, Your virtue leaves nothing to regret—truly the person is cultivated and the family regulated; it is not the millet that is fragrant, yet blessings do not turn away—reverently the spirits behold and the people rejoice. With reverence prevailing and righteousness prevailing, how dare we claim to echo the subtle words of old? Only by being timely and attentive to the minutest springs of action do we humbly wish to extol the splendor of these bright admonitions. The words encompass both successes and failures, and the meaning sets forth hardships and perils. Received directly by the Imperial mind, may they serve for selection among the words of grass-cutters and wood-gatherers; placed upon the screens by the Imperial throne, may they be comparable to the counsel presented to the beat of hand-drums and bells. In the past, when the "Inscriptions on the Great Treasure" (Dabao zhen) set forth its words, its author merely received favor through promotion; and when the "Six Admonitions for the Cinnabar Screen" (Danyi liuzhen) offered instruction, it failed to rescue the ruler from the disaster of dissolute excursions. Truly, this unity of heart between sovereign and subjects is a rare sight from antiquity to the present. Truly striving untiringly and gazing toward the Way, expanding the mindset of one who seems not yet to have seen it; in profound solemnity…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
熙文允洽有聲之聞咸而受益敬乃
日躋有以思謙順惟
天祐伏願
無然援羨
遹求寧成
冲和養威履平康之周道殷憂起
聖見敬止之文王
陟降不違
基命於無聲無臭
===
左右有赫
凝神乎不諫不聞惟
心和則氣和囿六合同春之化本
施敬而民敬昭四方拱
極之神臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹以所撰
雖肅殿箴隨
表上
punctuated: 熙文，允洽有聲之聞。咸而受益，敬乃日躋；有以思謙，順惟天祐。伏願無然援羨，遹求寧成。冲和養威，履平康之周道；殷憂起聖，見敬止之文王。陟降不違，基命於無聲無臭；左右有赫，凝神乎不諫不聞。惟心和則氣和，囿六合同春之化；本施敬而民敬，昭四方拱極之神。臣等無任瞻天仰聖，激切屏營之至，謹以所撰《雖肅殿箴》隨表上
translation_en:
…make radiant Your civil virtue, truly harmonizing with the renown that resounds abroad. By being receptive, one receives benefit, and through reverence, one ascends daily; by possessing the wherewithal to ponder humility, in compliance one enjoys the blessing of Heaven.

We humbly pray that Your Majesty will neither snatch nor covet, and will follow the path of seeking tranquility and completion. Nourish Your majesty in balanced harmony, treading the Zhou Way of peace and prosperity; let deep concern give rise to sagehood, manifesting King Wen who abided in reverence. Ascending and descending without deviation, establish the Mandate in what has neither sound nor scent; with resplendent presence on the left and right, concentrate Your spirit in what is neither remonstrated with nor heard [?]. Only when the mind is harmonious is the vital breath harmonious, encompassing the transformation that brings universal spring to the Six Directions; when the ruler's own practice is rooted in reverence, the people are reverent, illuminating the spiritual efficacy by which the four quarters turn toward the imperial pole.

Your servants are overcome to the utmost with earnestness and trepidation as we gaze up at Heaven and look up to Your Sacred Majesty, and we reverently submit the Admonition for the Yongsu Hall [written 雖肅殿箴] that we have composed, accompanying this memorial, to…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
進以
聞
第叅場
策五道
第一問
陸大成
同考試官教諭李　批
郊丘
合祀
===
二祖
竝配此我
皇上嘉納輔臣以定萬世不刊之盛典也是策博綜遠覽條答精詳援引斷議確有歸指且仁孝
之論深爲知本是士之具實用者宜錄
同考試官教諭潘　批我
皇祖
郊祀一制垂憲百王乃今議欲舉行我
聖上虛懷嘉納誠萬世之希覯也是作不獨闡明分合異同之義而末復括以仁孝之實忠悃溢
於言表尤足爲
punctuated:
進以聞。

第叅場
策五道
第一問
陸大成
同考試官教諭李　批：郊丘合祀、二祖竝配，此我皇上嘉納輔臣，以定萬世不刊之盛典也。是策博綜遠覽，條答精詳，援引斷議，確有歸指；且仁孝之論，深爲知本。是士之具實用者，宜錄。
同考試官教諭潘　批：我皇祖郊祀一制，垂憲百王，乃今議欲舉行，我聖上虛懷嘉納，誠萬世之希覯也。是作不獨闡明分合異同之義，而末復括以仁孝之實，忠悃溢於言表，尤足爲
translation_en:
…presented for Your Majesty's hearing.

Third Session
Five Policy Essays
First Question
Lu Dacheng 陸大成
Associate Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Li, comments: The combined sacrifice at the Suburban Altars and the joint pairing of the Two Founders—this is a grand and immutable institution for ten thousand generations, established by Our August Emperor through his gracious acceptance of the counsel of his grand secretaries. This policy essay is broadly synthesized and far-reaching in its reading; its point-by-point responses are precise and detailed; and its citations and judgments have a firm and clear direction. Moreover, its discussion of benevolence and filial piety shows a deep understanding of the fundamentals. This is a scholar equipped for practical service; it ought to be selected for recording.
Associate Examiner, Instructor Pan, comments: Our Imperial Founder's system of a unified suburban sacrifice sets a standard for a hundred kings. Now that deliberations have sought to put it into practice, Our Sacred Emperor has accepted the advice with an open mind—truly a rare sight in ten thousand generations. This composition not only elucidates the principles of separation and union, divergence and agreement, but at the end further encompasses the substance of benevolence and filial piety. Loyal sincerity overflows beyond the words, making it especially sufficient to serve as…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
聖脩之助
考試官侍讀羅　批
郊丘
合祀確有定見而綜覽考據至詳且明末復申之仁孝之說是足稗
廟謨矣敬錄之爲
當宁獻
考試官右中允高　批
郊丘
合祀
===
竝配我
祖
宗睿謨裁畫永垂不刊之典我
皇上嗣大曆服制倫兼盡方欲仰承
前烈而舉行之子能評古質今折衷允當首錄之以備采擇
明於天之道者禮其可以興乎通於聖之
撰者禮其可以言乎蓋傳稱帝王之事莫
大乎承天之序承天之序莫重於郊祀而
孝經云孝莫大於嚴父嚴父莫大於配天
punctuated:
聖脩之助。
考試官侍讀羅　批：郊丘合祀，確有定見，而綜覽考據，至詳且明；末復申之仁孝之說，是足稗廟謨矣。敬錄之，爲當宁獻。
考試官右中允高　批：郊丘合祀、竝配，我祖宗睿謨裁畫，永垂不刊之典。我皇上嗣大曆服，制、倫兼盡，方欲仰承前烈而舉行之。子能評古質今，折衷允當，首錄之以備采擇。
明於天之道者，禮其可以興乎！通於聖之撰者，禮其可以言乎！蓋傳稱：「帝王之事，莫大乎承天之序；承天之序，莫重於郊祀。」而《孝經》云：「孝莫大於嚴父，嚴父莫大於配天。」
translation_en:
… an aid to the Sage's self-cultivation.

Examiner and Academician Reader-in-waiting Luo 羅 comments: On the combined sacrifice at the suburban altars and sacred mounds, this essay possesses a firm and settled view, while its comprehensive survey and textual research are most detailed and clear. At the close, it further expounds the doctrine of benevolence and filial piety, which is sufficient to benefit the counsels of the ancestral temple [reading 稗 as 裨]. I respectfully select it to present to His Majesty on the throne.

Examiner and Right Companion to the Heir Apparent Gao 高 comments: The combined sacrifice and joint pairing of ancestors at the suburban altars and sacred mounds were decided and planned by the wise counsels of our Imperial Ancestors, handing down forever an immutable institution. Our August Emperor, having succeeded to the great mandate and realm, fulfills both ritual institutions and human relations to the utmost, and is just now seeking to respectfully carry on the meritorious achievements of his predecessors and put them into practice. You have been able to evaluate antiquity and examine the present, striking a fair and fitting balance; I record this in first place to prepare it for imperial selection.

For one who understands the Way of Heaven, can ritual then be raised up? For one who comprehends the creations of the Sages, can ritual then be spoken of? Indeed, the commentary states: "Among the affairs of emperors and kings, none is greater than upholding the order of Heaven; in upholding the order of Heaven, nothing is more important than the suburban sacrifice." And the Classic of Filial Piety (Xiaojing) says: "In filial piety nothing is greater than revering one's father; in revering one's father nothing is greater than pairing him with Heaven." …

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
斯二體者所以接天人之奧極仁孝之情
非聖神莫能與也故曰毋輕議禮而況
昭代之制裁成于
太祖紹尊于
列聖而飭新于
世宗尤未易措論其間者也往者
皇上御極肇舉
郊禋維時輔臣考據彝章列爲圖說以
獻曠然欲復
===
合祀
竝配之舊折衷至當莫之能易矣而執事猶欲
愚生博研經義參酌古今以佐
大議之末斯豈管闚所及哉請先述郊丘分
合所繇而後論配享之同異焉蓋虞書言
類上帝禋六宗望徧山川羣神而獨不及
地祇類者萃合之名也祀上帝則地祇必
在焉不稱地祇者所以尊上帝也此後世
言合祀者所繇昉與周禮大司樂冬日至
punctuated:
斯二體者，所以接天人之奧，極仁孝之情，非聖神莫能與也。故曰「毋輕議禮」，而況昭代之制，裁成于太祖，紹尊于列聖，而飭新于世宗，尤未易措論其間者也。往者，皇上御極，肇舉郊禋，維時輔臣考據彝章，列爲圖說以獻，曠然欲復合祀、竝配之舊，折衷至當，莫之能易矣。而執事猶欲愚生博研經義，參酌古今，以佐大議之末，斯豈管闚所及哉？請先述郊丘分合所繇，而後論配享之同異焉。

蓋《虞書》言「類上帝，禋六宗，望徧山川羣神」，而獨不及地祇。類者，萃合之名也，祀上帝則地祇必在焉，不稱地祇者，所以尊上帝也，此後世言合祀者所繇昉與？《周禮》大司樂冬日至……
translation_en:
… These two principles serve to connect the profound mysteries of Heaven and humanity and to bring the feelings of benevolence and filial piety to their utmost; none who lacks sage and spirit-like virtue can participate in them. Thus it is said, "Do not lightly deliberate on the rites." How much more so with the institutions of our illustrious dynasty, which were fashioned and completed by the Grand Progenitor (Taizu 太祖), inherited and revered by the successive sage emperors, and rectified and renewed by Shizong 世宗—making it all the more difficult to interpose discussions among them! In the past, when His Majesty ascended the throne and first performed the suburban sacrifice (jiaoyin 郊禋), the Grand Secretaries at that time examined the constant statutes and arranged them into illustrated explanations to present to the throne, broadly wishing to restore the old system of joint sacrifice and dual coadjutor worship. Their balanced judgment was most appropriate, and nothing could alter it. Yet Your Excellency still wishes this ignorant student to broadly investigate the meanings of the Classics and weigh the ancient and modern in order to assist at the margins of this great deliberation—how could this be within the reach of my narrow, tube-like view? Allow me first to recount the origins of the separation and combination of the suburban altars, and afterward to discuss the similarities and differences in coadjutor worship.

Now, the Book of Yu (Yushu 虞書) speaks of "performing the lei sacrifice to the Lord on High, the yin sacrifice to the Six Honored Ones, and the wang sacrifice in sequence to the mountains, rivers, and myriad spirits," yet makes no mention of the Earthly Deities (diqi 地祇) alone. "Lei" is a term denoting gathering and combining; when sacrificing to the Lord on High, the Earthly Deities were surely included therein, and the reason the Earthly Deities were not separately named was to honor the Lord on High. Is this not where the later advocacy of joint sacrifice originated? In the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli 周禮), under the Director of Music (Dasiyue 大司樂), at the winter solstice…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
地上圓丘之制曰禮天神夏日至澤中方
丘之制曰禮地祇此言分祀者所繇昉與
夫周頌昊天有成命小序以爲郊祀天地
周禮大宗伯以禋祀祀昊天上帝而不及
地祇則周家固亦合祀矣若乃蒼璧黃琮
四圭兩圭之類特其禮神之器數施於天
地者不同而未可據爲分祀之證也後世
所稱引者僅大司樂數語而胡宏吳澂已
謂其剌謬非知禮之言矣又可深泥之哉
===
漢氏而降大都王合祀者什六七而主分
祀者什二三漢高增秦畤爲五祀五帝自
武帝以來竝郊見泰畤于甘泉武帝又因
幸汾陰立后土祠脽上然甘泉脽竝在遠
非都邑之郊也祀泰畤以正月后土以三
月非二至之期也成帝建始中罷甘泉汾
陰定南北郊于長安劉向深以爲不可至
光武竟采元始故事合祀天地于南郊漢
志稱爲圓壇八陛中又爲重壇天地位其
punctuated: 地上圓丘之制，曰禮天神；夏日至澤中方丘之制，曰禮地祇。此言分祀者所繇昉與？夫《周頌·昊天有成命》小序以爲郊祀天地，《周禮》大宗伯以禋祀祀昊天上帝，而不及地祇，則周家固亦合祀矣。若乃蒼璧、黃琮、四圭、兩圭之類，特其禮神之器數施於天地者不同，而未可據爲分祀之證也。後世所稱引者，僅大司樂數語，而胡宏、吳澂已謂其剌謬，非知禮之言矣，又可深泥之哉？漢氏而降，大都王合祀者什六七，而主分祀者什二三。漢高增秦畤爲五，祀五帝。自武帝以來，竝郊見泰畤于甘泉；武帝又因幸汾陰，立后土祠脽上。然甘泉、脽竝在遠，非都邑之郊也；祀泰畤以正月，后土以三月，非二至之期也。成帝建始中，罷甘泉、汾陰，定南北郊于長安，劉向深以爲不可。至光武，竟采元始故事，合祀天地于南郊，《漢志》稱「爲圓壇八陛，中又爲重壇，天地位其
translation_en:
…of a round mound upon the ground, which it calls honoring the spirits of Heaven, and at the summer solstice the system of a square mound in the marsh, which it calls honoring the deities of Earth—is this not where those who advocate separate sacrifices trace their origin? Now, the "Lesser Preface" to "Haotian you chengming" (August Heaven Has a Determinate Mandate) in the Sacrificial Odes of Zhou (Zhou song) takes it to be the suburban sacrifice to Heaven and Earth; and in the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli), the Grand Master of Ceremonies (Da zongbo) sacrifices to August Heaven the Supreme Di with the pure burnt offering without mentioning the deities of Earth—thus the house of Zhou certainly also practiced joint sacrifice. As for the azure bi-disc, the yellow cong-tube, the four-tablet scepter, the two-tablet scepter, and the like, these merely reflect differences in the ritual vessels and numbers applied to Heaven and Earth in honoring the spirits, and cannot be relied upon as proof of separate sacrifices. What later generations have cited is nothing more than a few words under the Director of Music (Da siyue), yet Hu Hong 胡宏 and Wu Cheng 吳澂 already pronounced them perverse and erroneous, not the words of one who understands ritual—how then can one cling to them so obstinately?

From the Han dynasty onward, on the whole those who favored [reading 王 as 主] joint sacrifice have been six or seven out of ten, while those who favored separate sacrifices have been two or three out of ten. Emperor Gao of Han increased the Qin altars (zhi) to five to sacrifice to the Five Emperors. From Emperor Wu onward, they performed the suburban sacrifice at the Grand Altar (Taizhi) at Ganquan; Emperor Wu also, on the occasion of an imperial progress to Fenyin, established a shrine to Sovereign Earth (Houtu) upon the Sui mound. Yet both Ganquan and the Sui mound were far away, not in the suburbs of the capital city; and sacrificing at the Grand Altar in the first month and to Sovereign Earth in the third month did not match the dates of the two solstices. During the Jianshi era (32–29 BCE) of Emperor Cheng, the cults at Ganquan and Fenyin were abolished and the northern and southern suburban altars were established at Chang'an, which Liu Xiang 劉向 deeply disapproved of. By the time of Emperor Guangwu, he ultimately adopted the precedent of the Yuanshi era (1–5 CE), jointly sacrificing to Heaven and Earth at the southern suburb. The Treatises of the History of the Han (Hanzhi) state that "they made a round altar with eight flights of steps, and within it made an inner tiered altar; the seats of Heaven and Earth were placed…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
上皆南鄉西上是也唐開元禮皇地祇于
南郊合祭宋自建隆以來皆合祭元豐一
議元祐再議紹聖三議訖主于合蓋分而
不合者惟魏太和周建德隋開皇唐先天
宋元豐六年凡五見耳愚嘗究覽禮家聚
訟之談主合祀者曰天包乎地地不可與
天抗也曰天地如父母同牢而食不可以
異位也主分祀者曰順陰陽辨時位各依
象類以求之其指各有攸當愚以爲禮非
從天降非從地出由人心生者也易不云
乎乾稱乎父坤稱乎母王者君天下而爲
之子崇母以抗父而判列爲二非人道之
經也使父母隔室而處邈焉南北非人情
之順也揆之禮義合祀其正矣烏可局守
類求之說徦云黷亂厖雜并事天地明察
之道而砦之哉洪惟我
太祖高皇帝誕膺
寳命爲神靈主有天下之初卽建
punctuated: 上，皆南鄉西上是也。唐《開元禮》，皇地祇于南郊合祭。宋自建隆以來皆合祭，元豐一議，元祐再議，紹聖三議，訖主于合。蓋分而不合者，惟魏太和、周建德、隋開皇、唐先天、宋元豐六年，凡五見耳。愚嘗究覽禮家聚訟之談，主合祀者曰：「天包乎地，地不可與天抗也。」曰：「天地如父母，同牢而食，不可以異位也。」主分祀者曰：「順陰陽，辨時位，各依象類以求之。」其指各有攸當。愚以爲禮非從天降，非從地出，由人心生者也。《易》不云乎：「乾稱乎父，坤稱乎母。」王者君天下而爲之子，崇母以抗父，而判列爲二，非人道之經也；使父母隔室而處，邈焉南北，非人情之順也。揆之禮義，合祀其正矣。烏可局守類求之說，徦云黷亂厖雜，并事天地明察之道而砦之哉？洪惟我太祖高皇帝誕膺寳命，爲神靈主，有天下之初，卽建
translation_en:
…upon it, both facing south with the west as the seat of honor—this is it. In the Kaiyuan Ritual Code (Kaiyuan li) of the Tang, the August Earth Spirit was jointly sacrificed to at the southern suburb. In the Song, from the Jianlong era (960–963) onward, they were always jointly sacrificed to; it was deliberated once in the Yuanfeng era (1078–1085), deliberated a second time in the Yuanyou era (1086–1094), and deliberated a third time in the Shaosheng era (1094–1098), ultimately settling in favor of joint sacrifice. Indeed, separating and not joining them was seen only five times in all: in the Taihe era of the Northern Wei, the Jiande era of the Northern Zhou, the Kaihuang era of the Sui, the Xiantian era of the Tang, and the sixth year of the Yuanfeng era (1083) of the Song.

I have thoroughly examined the contentious debates of the ritualists. Those who advocate joint sacrifice say: "Heaven encompasses Earth; Earth cannot rival Heaven as an equal." And they say: "Heaven and Earth are like father and mother, sharing the same sacrificial animals and dining together; they must not be placed in separate seats." Those who advocate separate sacrifices say: "One should accord with yin and yang, distinguish seasons and positions, and seek each according to its symbolic category." Their arguments each have their own validity. Yet I consider that ritual does not descend from Heaven, nor does it emerge from Earth; it is born from the human heart. Does the Book of Changes (Yi) not say: "Qian is called father, and Kun is called mother"? The true king rules All under Heaven and is their son. To elevate the mother to rival the father, dividing and arraying them as two, is not the constant principle of the human way; to cause father and mother to dwell in separate chambers, far apart in the south and north, is not in harmony with human feelings. Measured against the principles of ritual, joint sacrifice is the proper way. How could one narrowly cling to the doctrine of seeking by category, rashly [?] calling it irreverent confusion and杂 [promiscuous/motley] disorder, and thereby disparage [?] even the way of serving Heaven and Earth with clear discernment?

Humbly reflecting on our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu Gao Huangdi), when he grandly received the Precious Mandate and became the lord of spirits and numina, at the very beginning of his possession of the empire, he immediately built…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
圜丘于鍾山之陽
方丘于鍾山之陰每歲分祀
天地行之數年雨暘未若洪應愆休乃斷自
宸衷定爲
合祀之制以十二年春肇行于
大祀殿其夕天宇澄霽星緯昭煥祥飈慶雲光
彩燁煜若有響荅於是
親製樂歌以著明貺焉夫天地竝祀有合食之
親無分抗之迹得其順矣首春上辛先庶
事而舉又三陽之月地天交泰得其時矣
===
六宗山川羣神各爲壇以從祀合乎有虞
肆類之典矣立兆國陽爲屋而祭蓋兼用
周家泰壇明堂之制而不盡拘司樂之文
矣於卓哉精當明備丕天之大律也
列聖祗循行之百六十餘年
上帝鑒歆萬靈嘉饗休徵具歛祉福叢臻有由
然哉迨我
世宗肅皇帝中興建極擅百王禮樂之宗于時
punctuated: 圜丘于鍾山之陽、方丘于鍾山之陰，每歲分祀天地。行之數年，雨暘未若，洪應愆休，乃斷自宸衷，定爲合祀之制，以十二年春肇行于大祀殿。其夕，天宇澄霽，星緯昭煥，祥飈慶雲，光彩燁煜，若有響荅。於是親製樂歌，以著明貺焉。夫天地竝祀，有合食之親，無分抗之迹，得其順矣；首春上辛，先庶事而舉，又三陽之月，地天交泰，得其時矣；六宗、山川、羣神，各爲壇以從祀，合乎有虞肆類之典矣；立兆國陽，爲屋而祭，蓋兼用周家泰壇、明堂之制，而不盡拘《司樂》之文矣。於，卓哉！精當明備，丕天之大律也。列聖祗循，行之百六十餘年，上帝鑒歆，萬靈嘉饗，休徵具歛，祉福叢臻，有由然哉！迨我世宗肅皇帝，中興建極，擅百王禮樂之宗。于時
translation_en: … the Round Mound (Huanqiu) to the south of Mount Zhong (Zhongshan) and the Square Mound (Fangqiu) to the north of Mount Zhong, sacrificing separately to Heaven and Earth each year. After this was practiced for several years, rain and sunshine were not yet seasonable, and the great responses fell short of auspiciousness. Thereupon, deciding from His Imperial Mind, He established the institution of joint sacrifice, initiating its performance in the spring of the twelfth year [of Hongwu, 1379] in the Hall of the Great Sacrifice (Dasi dian). That evening, the vault of heaven was clear and fair, the stars and planets shone brightly, and auspicious breezes and felicitous clouds gleamed with resplendent radiance, as if in resonant answer. At this, He personally composed musical songs to make manifest the luminous blessing. Now, when Heaven and Earth are sacrificed to side by side, there is the intimacy of partaking of food together and no trace of divided rivalry—thus attaining what is harmonious. Performing it on the first *xin* day of the first month of spring, ahead of all other affairs, which is moreover the month of three *yang* lines [forming the hexagram *Tai*, Peace] when Earth and Heaven mingle in harmony—this attains the proper season. Setting up individual altars for the Six Honored Ones, the mountains and rivers, and the host of spirits as auxiliary sacrifices accords with the canon of the *si* and *lei* sacrifices of the Lord of Yu [Shun]. Establishing the sacred precinct to the south of the capital and building a roofed structure in which to sacrifice combines the systems of the Grand Altar (Taitan) and the Hall of Light (Mingtang) of the House of Zhou, without being wholly bound by the literal text of the Director of Music (Siyue) [in the Rites of Zhou]. Oh, how magnificent! Precise, fitting, luminous, and complete—it is the great statute for matching vast Heaven. The successive Sacred Emperors reverently followed it, practicing it for more than one hundred and sixty years. The Lord on High looked down and savored the offerings, the myriad spirits joyfully accepted the feast, auspicious verifications were gathered in full, and blessings arrived in abundance—truly there was a reason for this! Coming down to our Emperor Shizong Su [the Jiajing Emperor], who achieved a dynastic revival and established the supreme standard, commanding the mastery of rites and music over a hundred kings—at that time…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
諸臣爭言新易制度以順
上指遂改建
南北郊分祀
天地圓丘方丘之制掃地露拜之儀冬夏二至
之期壹遵周禮典章文物燦然改觀焉然
周家以建子月爲歲首祀天至午月乃祀
地尚云適先後之宜我
朝用夏正自夏徂冬則地先天祭越次而食
矣且郊者祀天之名地不得而干也故兆
於南郊禮文載之北郊之名乃匡衡輩緣
飾緯書以對南郊非周禮所有也豈得盡
爲符合也哉蓋建議之臣泥司樂之隻辭
而不察虞周之備典信建始之曲學而不
===
考歷代之通行知
聖祖初制當遵而不知分而復合是
神謨淵識所裁爲定禮而不可改也知
存心録備載儀章爲可據而不知
大祀文之訓明白嚴正不可忽也蓋
punctuated: 諸臣爭言新易制度以順上指，遂改建南北郊，分祀天地。圓丘、方丘之制，掃地露拜之儀，冬、夏二至之期，壹遵《周禮》，典章文物燦然改觀焉。然周家以建子月爲歲首祀天，至午月乃祀地，尚云適先後之宜；我朝用夏正，自夏徂冬，則地先天祭，越次而食矣。且郊者，祀天之名，地不得而干也。故兆於南郊，禮文載之；北郊之名，乃匡衡輩緣飾緯書以對南郊，非《周禮》所有也，豈得盡爲符合也哉？蓋建議之臣，泥《司樂》之隻辭，而不察虞、周之備典；信建始之曲學，而不考歷代之通行；知聖祖初制當遵，而不知分而復合是神謨淵識所裁爲定禮而不可改也；知《存心録》備載儀章爲可據，而不知《大祀文》之訓明白嚴正不可忽也。蓋
translation_en: … the various officials vied to propose changing and renewing the institutional system in order to conform to the Emperor's wishes, and thereupon the Southern and Northern Suburbs were rebuilt to offer separate sacrifices to Heaven and Earth. The institutions of the Round Mound and Square Mound, the ceremony of sweeping the ground and worshiping in the open air, and the timing at the winter and summer solstices all strictly followed the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli), and the statutes, regulations, and ritual accoutrements took on a brilliantly new appearance. Yet the House of Zhou took the Zi month [the eleventh lunar month] as the beginning of the year and sacrificed to Heaven then, and only when it reached the Wu month [the fifth lunar month] did it sacrifice to Earth, which could still be said to fit the proper sequence of first and last. Our Dynasty uses the Xia calendar; moving from summer to winter means that Earth is sacrificed to before Heaven, partaking of the offerings out of proper order. Moreover, "suburban sacrifice" (jiao) is the name for sacrificing to Heaven, upon which Earth may not encroach. Therefore, setting up the altar precinct in the Southern Suburb is recorded in the ritual texts, whereas the name "Northern Suburb" was merely embellished from apocryphal texts (weishu) by Kuang Heng and his like to pair with the Southern Suburb; it is not something found in the Rites of Zhou. How could this be considered completely in accord with it? Indeed, the officials who proposed this measure clung stubbornly to a single phrase in the "Grand Director of Music" (Yueshi / Da siyue) section without examining the complete canons of Yu [Shun] and Zhou; they trusted the distorted scholarship of the Jianshi reign period [of the Han dynasty, 32–29 BCE] without investigating the established practice of successive dynasties; they knew that the Sacred Ancestor's [Emperor Taizu's] initial institution ought to be followed, yet did not know that separating and then re-combining the sacrifices was an established rite decided upon by His divine counsel and profound insight, which must not be altered; they knew that the Record of Preserving the Mind (Cunxin lu), which fully records the ritual statutes, could be relied upon, yet did not know that the instructions of the Text for the Great Sacrifice (Dasi wen) are clear, stern, and upright, and must not be neglected. For although…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
世宗雖建立
二郊而中世以後第行
祈穀
大饗于
內殿
圓方之祭竟不親舉豈非
聖心亦有所未安俟
後聖之更定者耶至于尊祖配天之禮古有以
始祖配者周之后稷是也有以受命之君
===
配者漢之高祖是也夫配天以功德而功
德孰大于開剏者則周之祀稷固明德光
靈之遠也而漢之祀高祖非以崛起在位
爲帝者首乎有天帝各配者周以稷配郊
又以文王配明堂漢以高祖配郊又以光
武配明堂是也有祖宗竝配者唐垂拱開
元以高祖太宗配昊天宋至道以太祖太
宗配圓丘是也夫廟壓于祖昭穆對向非
嫌也郊壓于天祖宗序列非嫌也然則天
punctuated: 世宗雖建立二郊，而中世以後，第行祈穀、大饗于內殿，圓、方之祭，竟不親舉，豈非聖心亦有所未安，俟後聖之更定者耶？至于尊祖配天之禮，古有以始祖配者，周之后稷是也；有以受命之君配者，漢之高祖是也。夫配天以功德，而功德孰大于開剏者？則周之祀稷，固明德光靈之遠也；而漢之祀高祖，非以崛起在位，爲帝者首乎？有天帝各配者，周以稷配郊，又以文王配明堂；漢以高祖配郊，又以光武配明堂是也。有祖宗竝配者，唐垂拱、開元以高祖、太宗配昊天，宋至道以太祖、太宗配圓丘是也。夫廟壓于祖，昭穆對向非嫌也；郊壓于天，祖宗序列非嫌也。然則天…
translation_en:
…Even though Emperor Shizong (世宗, the Jiajing Emperor) established the Two Suburban Sacrifices (二郊), from the middle years of his reign onward he merely performed the Sacrifice of Prayer for Grain (祈穀) and the Great Banquet Sacrifice (大饗) in the inner palace halls, while in the end he no longer personally conducted the sacrifices at the Round Altar and the Square Altar. Was this not because the sacred mind also felt some unease in the matter, leaving it for later sage rulers to revise and settle?

As for the rite of honoring ancestors by associating them as correlates in the sacrifice to Heaven (尊祖配天), in antiquity there was the practice of making the remote founding ancestor the correlate, such as Houji (后稷) in the Zhou dynasty; and there was the practice of making the ruler who received the Mandate the correlate, such as Emperor Gaozu (高祖) in the Han dynasty. Now, associating an ancestor with Heaven is based on merit and virtue—and what merit and virtue could be greater than founding a dynasty? Thus the Zhou sacrifice to Houji certainly recognized the far-reaching brilliance of his luminous virtue and divine spirit; and was not the Han sacrifice to Gaozu due to his having risen up to take the throne as the first among its emperors?

There was also the practice of assigning separate correlates to Heaven (天) and the Supreme Lord (帝): in the Zhou, Houji was the correlate at the suburban sacrifice (郊) while King Wen (文王) was the correlate at the Hall of Light (明堂); in the Han, Gaozu was the correlate at the suburban sacrifice while Emperor Guangwu (光武) was the correlate at the Hall of Light. And there was the practice of associating both founding ancestor (祖) and illustrious progenitor (宗) together as co-correlates: in the Tang dynasty, during the Chuigong (垂拱, 685–688) and Kaiyuan (開元, 713–741) eras, Emperors Gaozu (高祖) and Taizong (太宗) were jointly associated with August Heaven (昊天); in the Song dynasty, during the Zhidao (至道, 995–997) era, Emperors Taizu (太祖) and Taizong (太宗) were jointly associated with the Round Mound (圓丘). Now, in the ancestral temple, everyone is subordinate to the First Ancestor, so for the zhao (昭) and mu (穆) generations to face each other across the hall gives no cause for impropriety; at the suburban altar, everyone is subordinate to Heaven, so for the founding ancestor and later progenitors to be arrayed in sequence gives no cause for impropriety. If that is so, then assigning separate correlates to Heaven and the Supreme Lord…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
帝各配者固章別之道也而祖宗竝配亦
何可以連衽接席議其非禮乎哉
太祖之始建
郊以
仁祖配是周祀后稷溯本祥源意也而
成祖以
太祖配則如漢奉高祖崇功德之特起矣
仁宗時以
二祖配是唐宋所已行稱情而合禮者也
===
世宗乃獨奉
太祖配
南北郊其
祈穀之祭以
成祖同配尋亦不行蓋始循稍采郊祀宗祀之
遺而終竟以父子相竝爲嫌矣夫
成祖再造區夏
奠鼎燕京
駿德豐功實同肇刱而推崇夫至非褻瀆
punctuated: 帝各配者，固章別之道也；而祖宗竝配，亦何可以連衽接席議其非禮乎哉！太祖之始建郊，以仁祖配，是周祀后稷，溯本祥源意也；而成祖以太祖配，則如漢奉高祖，崇功德之特起矣；仁宗時以二祖配，是唐宋所已行，稱情而合禮者也。世宗乃獨奉太祖配南北郊，其祈穀之祭，以成祖同配，尋亦不行，蓋始循稍采郊祀、宗祀之遺，而終竟以父子相竝爲嫌矣。夫成祖再造區夏，奠鼎燕京，駿德豐功，實同肇刱；而推崇夫至，非褻瀆
translation_en: … Heaven and the Supreme Di with separate ancestral associates is indeed the way of making clear distinctions; yet as for associating both the Founding Ancestor and the Second Ancestor together, how could one criticize it as contrary to ritual propriety on the grounds that they sit side by side with robes touching! When Ta祖 (the Hongwu Emperor) first established the suburban sacrifice, he associated Renzu with Heaven; this followed the meaning of the Zhou dynasty sacrificing to Hou Ji, tracing back to the root and the auspicious source. When Chengzu (the Yongle Emperor) associated Taizu with Heaven, it was like the Han dynasty venerating Gaozu, honoring the extraordinary rise of his merit and virtue. In the time of Renzong (the Hongxi Emperor), the Two Ancestors (Taizu and Chengzu) were both associated with Heaven; this was what the Tang and Song dynasties had already practiced, matching human feelings and conforming to ritual propriety. Shizong (the Jiajing Emperor), however, venerated Taizu alone as the associate at the Northern and Southern Suburban Sacrifices. In the sacrifice of Prayer for Grain (Qigu), he associated Chengzu alongside, but before long this too was discontinued. In the beginning he followed and somewhat adopted the legacy of the suburban sacrifice and the ancestral hall sacrifice (Bright Hall), yet in the end he ultimately considered it improper for father and son to be placed side by side. Now, Chengzu recreated the Chinese realm and established the imperial tripods at Yanjing (Beijing); his great virtue and abundant merit were truly equal to the initial founding of the dynasty. Yet failing to carry his exaltation to the utmost [reading 未至 for 夫至?] is not the ritual of [honoring—not profaning?]…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
前烈之禮也
配享百餘年一朝而罷之非孔安是若之義也
且今
祈穀之祭釐正已久而
郊丘配位未復非闕典甚者哉善乎輔臣之
獻議曰歲一舉
合祀而奉
二祖並配遵
太祖更定之制率
===
列聖世守之規體
世宗未安之情協時宜順人心合禮典應經義
上固已虛懷嘉納久矣惟霈然下
明詔諭中外博㕘之輿論而昭告之
靈祇不過一潤色恢定間而可以迓
睠顧之休隆繼述之績闡帝王之緒垂宇宙之
摹甚大美也何疑而不爲乎抑愚猶有
獻焉蓋聞議禮者當覈其文秉禮者貴探其
本夫莫尊于天地而合祀之誠父天母地
punctuated: 前烈之禮也。配享百餘年，一朝而罷之，非孔安是若之義也。且今祈穀之祭，釐正已久，而郊丘配位未復，非闕典甚者哉？善乎輔臣之獻議曰：「歲一舉合祀，而奉二祖並配，遵太祖更定之制，率列聖世守之規，體世宗未安之情，協時宜，順人心，合禮典，應經義。」上固已虛懷嘉納久矣。惟霈然下明詔，諭中外，博㕘之輿論，而昭告之靈祇，不過一潤色恢定間，而可以迓睠顧之休，隆繼述之績，闡帝王之緒，垂宇宙之摹，甚大美也！何疑而不爲乎？抑愚猶有獻焉：蓋聞議禮者當覈其文，秉禮者貴探其本。夫莫尊于天地，而合祀之，誠父天母地…
translation_en:
…the ritual due to the illustrious achievements of our predecessors. Having received associative offerings for more than a hundred years, to abolish them in a single morning is not in keeping with the principle of resting in what is thoroughly tranquil and right. Moreover, today the Sacrifice of Prayer for Grain has long since been rectified, yet the associative tablet at the Suburban Altar has not been restored—is this not an extreme deficiency in our state rituals?

Admirable indeed was the proposal submitted by the Grand Secretaries, which stated: "To perform the joint sacrifice once a year and revere the Two Progenitors (Taizu and Chengzu) together as associates follows the system revised and established by Taizu, adheres to the regulations preserved through the generations by the successive Sacred Emperors, embodies the sentiments of Shizong when his mind was not yet at rest, accords with what is appropriate to the times, complies with human hearts, conforms to the ritual canons, and corresponds to the meaning of the Classics." His Majesty has indeed long accepted this with an open mind and high approval. If he would only generously send down a clear edict to inform the court and the provinces, consult widely with public opinion, and solemnly announce it to the numinous spirits of Heaven and Earth, it would take no more than a moment of refinement and broad settlement to welcome the blessings of Heaven's loving regard, exalt the achievement of carrying on and recounting ancestral ways, illuminate the lineage of emperors and kings, and hand down a model for the universe—this would be a magnificent perfection! What doubt could there be to keep from doing it?

Yet I, in my simplicity, still have something to offer. For I have heard that those who deliberate on ritual ought to examine its outward forms, while those who uphold ritual value probing its fundamental root. Now, nothing is more exalted than Heaven and Earth, and to sacrifice to them jointly is truly to treat Heaven as father and Earth as mother…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
而致親之極也莫親于祖宗而竝配之郊
誠天其祖宗而致尊之極也故曰事天如
事親至仁也事親如事天至孝也仁不在
乎合祀之文昊天曰明及爾出王昊天曰
旦及爾游衍精神思慮渾乎孚通之不隔
者親之之實也孝不在乎崇配之文食則
見于羹坐則見于墻陟降上下懍乎保明
之不怠者尊之之實也斯道也
上聖性已得之益加之
===
聖心焉而憲
天法
祖之本立矣執其本以賁飾其文所謂建中和
之極兼總條貫金聲而玉振之煌煌乎萬
世之基不繇今其永垂哉
第二問
石崑玉
同考試官訓導李　批〔曆法甚關治具古今未有協一之論是對究極天人理數之奧歷歷可稽宜有俾於璣衡者故錄〕
punctuated:
而致親之極也；莫親于祖宗，而竝配之郊，誠天其祖宗而致尊之極也。故曰：「事天如事親，至仁也；事親如事天，至孝也。」仁不在乎合祀之文，「昊天曰明，及爾出王；昊天曰旦，及爾游衍」，精神思慮，渾乎孚通之不隔者，親之之實也。孝不在乎崇配之文，食則見于羹，坐則見于墻，陟降上下，懍乎保明之不怠者，尊之之實也。斯道也，上聖性已得之，益加之聖心焉，而憲天法祖之本立矣。執其本以賁飾其文，所謂建中和之極，兼總條貫，金聲而玉振之，煌煌乎萬世之基，不繇今其永垂哉！

第二問
石崑玉
同考試官訓導李　批：〔曆法甚關治具，古今未有協一之論。是對究極天人理數之奧，歷歷可稽，宜有俾於璣衡者，故錄。〕
translation_en:
… and attaining the utmost degree of intimacy. Nothing is closer to one than the imperial ancestors, yet pairing them together at the suburban sacrifices truly treats one's ancestors as Heaven and attains the utmost degree of reverence. Therefore it is said: "Serving Heaven as one serves one's parents is the highest benevolence; serving one's parents as one serves Heaven is the highest filial piety." Benevolence does not reside in the outward form of joint sacrifice. "Great Heaven is intelligent, and is with you in all your goings; Great Heaven is clear-seeing, and is with you in your wanderings and indulgences"—when one's spirit and thoughts are seamlessly in communion without barrier, that is the reality of treating Heaven as parent. Filial piety does not reside in the outward form of exalted pairing at sacrifices. Seeing them in the broth when eating, seeing them on the wall when sitting, and ascending and descending above and below in reverent, unremitting care and mindfulness—that is the reality of honoring them. This Way, His Majesty in his sagely nature has already attained; if he further applies his sagely mind to it, the foundation for modeling himself on Heaven and emulating the Ancestors will be established. Holding fast to this foundation in order to adorn the outward ritual forms is what is meant by establishing the ultimate standard of equilibrium and harmony, comprehensively gathering the threads and principles, and sounding the bronze bells to begin the concert and striking the jade chimes to bring it to a close. How resplendent! Shall not the foundation for ten thousand generations be handed down forever from this day forth?

Second Question
Shi Kunyu 石崑玉
Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Li 李 comments: [Calendrical astronomy is closely bound up with the instruments of governance, yet from antiquity to the present there has never been a unified consensus. This response thoroughly investigates the profound principles and numerical regularities of Heaven and humanity, with every point verifiable; it should be of assistance to those who manage the armillary sphere, and is therefore selected for publication.]

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭程　批〔談古今曆法甚悉而外訛之由　延訪之論尤中肯綮蓋留心象數而有得者〕
同考試官教諭朱　批〔曆法差忒由星官失職所致此　作辨訛訂舛考據甚悉足究心天文之學者宜錄之俟治曆者觀焉〕
同考試官教諭向　批〔曆法深渺難言獨此策考據辨　析至極分秒尤足爲占天迎日者準故錄〕
考試官侍讀羅　批〔曆法甚玄關繫最大是策考據歷代得失　折衷以廣招募精考校修舉星官之職是知政所先者錄之不徒以文也〕
考試官右中允高　批〔今司天鮮究其術往往推策多失經紀見　是作能不悚然〕
===
曆法之難言也尚矣書曰在璿璣玉衡以
齊七政易曰澤火革君子以治曆明時夫
七政之運盈縮疎密逆順進退至雜揉靡
定也而奚以使之齊曆象之法考古校今
積算推步宜有術可操也而奚以取諸革
蓋起數於微渺測驗於星躔其運行者有
常而其員機者不滯至一也而至不一也
三才之妙管是矣夫惟沉幾熟慮經緯化
punctuated:
同考試官教諭程批：〔談古今曆法甚悉，而外訛之由、延訪之論，尤中肯綮，蓋留心象數而有得者。〕
同考試官教諭朱批：〔曆法差忒，由星官失職所致。此作辨訛訂舛，考據甚悉，足究心天文之學者。宜錄之，俟治曆者觀焉。〕
同考試官教諭向批：〔曆法深渺難言，獨此策考據辨析，至極分秒，尤足爲占天迎日者準，故錄。〕
考試官侍讀羅批：〔曆法甚玄，關繫最大。是策考據歷代得失，折衷以廣招募、精考校、修舉星官之職，是知政所先者。錄之，不徒以文也。〕
考試官右中允高批：〔今司天鮮究其術，往往推策多失經紀。見是作，能不悚然！〕
曆法之難言也尚矣。《書》曰：「在璿璣玉衡，以齊七政。」《易》曰：「澤火革，君子以治曆明時。」夫七政之運，盈縮疎密，逆順進退，至雜揉靡定也，而奚以使之齊？曆象之法，考古校今，積算推步，宜有術可操也，而奚以取諸革？蓋起數於微渺，測驗於星躔，其運行者有常，而其員機者不滯，至一也，而至不一也，三才之妙管是矣。夫惟沉幾熟慮，經緯化…
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Cheng: [He discusses ancient and modern calendrical methods in great detail, and his account of the causes of errors [?] and his argument for inviting knowledgeable specialists particularly hit the mark. Clearly this is someone who has paid close attention to astronomical phenomena and numerical calculation and gained real insight.]
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Zhu: [Discrepancies in the calendar arise from court astronomers failing in their duties. This essay distinguishes errors and corrects mistakes with very thorough textual evidence, sufficing for scholars who devote their minds to astronomy. It should be recorded to await inspection by those who regulate the calendar.]
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Xiang: [Calendrical science is profound, abstruse, and difficult to discuss, yet this policy essay alone examines the evidence and analyzes the issues down to the finest fractions and seconds, making it especially worthy to serve as a standard for those who observe the heavens and calculate the solar cycles; therefore it is recorded.]
Comment by Examiner and Academician Reader-in-Waiting Luo: [Calendrical science is exceedingly Subtle and of the greatest consequence. This policy essay examines the successes and failures of successive dynasties and strikes a balanced conclusion by proposing to broaden recruitment, refine evaluations, and restore the duties of the astronomical officials. This shows an understanding of what governance must prioritize. We record it not merely for its literary merit.]
Comment by Examiner and Right Companion to the Heir Apparent Gao: [Nowadays those in charge of the Directorate of Astronomy rarely master their art, and in their calculations they often lose track of the governing principles. Seeing this composition, how could they not be struck with awe!]
That calendrical science is difficult to speak of has been true since antiquity. The Book of Documents (Shu) says: "Examine the jade-adorned armillary sphere and the sighting tube to bring into harmony the Seven Regulators [sun, moon, and five planets]." The Book of Changes (Yi) says: "Lake and Fire form Revolution (Ge); the noble man thus regulates the calendar and clarifies the seasons." Now, the movements of the Seven Regulators—their waxing and waning, sparsity and density, retrograde and prograde motions, advances and retreats—are utterly mingled and unfixed; how then can they be brought into harmony? And in the methods of calendrical astronomy—examining antiquity and comparing the present, accumulating calculations and pacing the heavens—there ought to be fixed techniques to hold fast to; why then does one draw inspiration from Revolution [change]? It is because numbers originate in the infinitesimal and measurements are verified against the stellar paths; their courses have constancy, yet their revolving mechanism never stagnates—they are supremely unified, and yet supremely varied. The mystery of the Three Powers [Heaven, Earth, and Man] is encompassed right here. Only through deep foresight and mature deliberation, weaving together and transforming…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
裁雨戒之外無徵不窺四游之內靡神不
洽乃可以與於此然則司其事者詎不甚
重乎哉在昔顓頊氏有重黎唐虞有羲和
夏有昆吾商有巫咸周有萇弘各司其官
以資調燮故晦朔弦望適其節分至啓閉
協其期欽若敬授之化終將賴焉嗣是而
秦漢之間史官喪紀疇人失業故其詳不
可得聞一時言曆象者舉溺其職矣張蒼
本五勝而詘於論著公孫卿射姓輩議造
===
漢曆而不諳算法張盛景防等署弦望月
食而不通曆元持衡相仗推算依違太常
奉詔雜議迄無所據太史明知錯謬而不
能更握乾者憂之乃始不愛祿爵廣延宣
問挾技殫慮之士輻湊竝進而自獻於前
雜候鉤校則張壽王徐禹各呈其効先大
先小則編訢衛崇各闘其捷太初四分之
用則亶誦張衡各恣其辨得失更迭劇於
聚訟雖紛呶莫決而爲說寖詳歷代以還
punctuated: 裁，雨戒之外，無徵不窺；四游之內，靡神不洽，乃可以與於此。然則司其事者，詎不甚重乎哉！在昔顓頊氏有重黎，唐、虞有羲、和，夏有昆吾，商有巫咸，周有萇弘，各司其官，以資調燮。故晦朔弦望適其節，分至啓閉協其期，欽若敬授之化，終將賴焉。嗣是而秦、漢之間，史官喪紀，疇人失業，故其詳不可得聞。一時言曆象者，舉溺其職矣。張蒼本五勝而詘於論著；公孫卿、射姓輩議造漢曆而不諳算法；張盛、景防等署弦望月食而不通曆元。持衡相仗，推算依違。太常奉詔雜議，迄無所據；太史明知錯謬，而不能更。握乾者憂之，乃始不愛祿爵，廣延宣問。挾技殫慮之士，輻湊竝進而自獻於前。雜候鉤校，則張壽王、徐禹各呈其効；先大先小，則編訢、衛崇各闘其捷；太初、四分之用，則亶誦、張衡各恣其辨。得失更迭，劇於聚訟。雖紛呶莫決，而爲說寖詳。歷代以還，
translation_en:
…and tailoring [their methods to nature's transformations], so that beyond the two celestial divisions [? 雨戒, likely a variant/print for 兩戒] no subtle sign goes unexamined, and within the four seasonal displacements of the earth no mysterious principle fails to be encompassed—only then can one partake in this work. That being so, how could those in charge of this matter not carry the utmost weight! In antiquity, under Zhuanxu there were Chong and Li; under Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun] there were Xi and He; in the Xia dynasty there was Kunwu; in the Shang there was Wu Xian; and in the Zhou there was Chang Hong. Each presided over his office to aid in harmonizing [heaven and earth]. Thus the dark of the moon, the new moon, the quarter moons, and the full moon met their proper intervals, while the equinoxes, solstices, and the beginnings of the seasons accorded with their appointed times; the transforming governance of reverently following Heaven and respectfully bestowing the seasons ultimately depended on this.

Thereafter, between the Qin and Han dynasties, the court historians lost their records and the hereditary astronomers lost their craft, so the details could no longer be heard of. For a time, all who spoke of calendrical phenomena failed in their duties. Zhang Cang 張蒼 based himself on the conquest cycle of the Five Phases yet fell short in his theoretical writings; Gongsun Qing 公孫卿, She Xing 射姓, and their ilk deliberated on creating a Han calendar without understanding mathematical methods; Zhang Sheng 張盛, Jing Fang 景防, and others recorded the quarter moons, full moons, and lunar eclipses without comprehending the calendrical epoch. Holding the balance, they merely leaned on one another, and their calculations were tentative and equivocal. When the Chamberlain for Ceremonials (Taichang) received an imperial decree to hold joint deliberations, in the end they had no firm basis; the Grand Astrologer (Taishi) clearly knew of the errors and discrepancies, yet was unable to reform them.

Those who held the reins of sovereign power were troubled by this, and only then did they begin to spare neither emoluments nor noble ranks, issuing broad invitations and public inquiries. Men who possessed technical skills and exhausted their thoughts converged like spokes at a hub, advancing together to present themselves before the throne. In observing diverse phenomena and cross-checking calculations, Zhang Shouwang 張壽王 and Xu Yu 徐禹 each displayed his results; in debating whether to place a long or short month first, Bian Xin 編訢 and Wei Chong 衛崇 each competed in ingenuity; regarding the adoption of the Grand Inception (Taichu) or Quarter-Remainder (Sifen) system, Dan Song 亶誦 and Zhang Heng 張衡 each gave free rein to his arguments. Successes and failures alternated in turn, more fiercely than a clamor of litigants. Yet although the noisy disputes could not be settled, the theories gradually grew more detailed. Down through the successive dynasties…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
法制斯備或起於鍾律或起於蓍策或起
於晷景此推驗之法以漸而變矣劉洪悟
月行有遲疾劉倬悟日行有盈縮何承天
悟測景以定氣序姜岌悟以月行所衝之
宿爲日所在之度祖冲之始悟歲差張子
信悟月行有交道表裏五星有見伏向背
李淳風悟定朔之制幷氣朔閏餘皆同一
術此推驗之法以漸而精矣惟勝國之授
時曆出於許衡郭守敬所定參别同異酌
===
取中數積日積年之算悉屛不用以之攷
古則增歲餘而損歲差以之推來則增歲
差而損歲餘當時稱其法者謂能發順天
求合之徵證前人附會之失自古及今未
有能逮者也我
太祖高皇帝
太統曆稍采授時之舊設官則幷合華夏占候
則參綜古今儀式精詳神機妙運卽使大
撓執役隸首布算奚足以方焉以故用之
punctuated: 法制斯備：或起於鍾律，或起於蓍策，或起於晷景，此推驗之法以漸而變矣。劉洪悟月行有遲疾，劉倬悟日行有盈縮，何承天悟測景以定氣序，姜岌悟以月行所衝之宿爲日所在之度，祖冲之始悟歲差，張子信悟月行有交道表裏、五星有見伏向背，李淳風悟定朔之制，幷氣朔閏餘皆同一術，此推驗之法以漸而精矣。惟勝國之《授時曆》出於許衡、郭守敬所定，參别同異，酌取中數，積日積年之算悉屛不用；以之攷古則增歲餘而損歲差，以之推來則增歲差而損歲餘。當時稱其法者，謂能發順天求合之徵，證前人附會之失，自古及今，未有能逮者也。我太祖高皇帝《太統曆》稍采《授時》之舊，設官則幷合華夏，占候則參綜古今。儀式精詳，神機妙運，卽使大撓執役、隸首布算，奚足以方焉！以故用之
translation_en: …the institutional methods became complete: some originated from musical bells and pitch-pipes, some from yarrow-stalk divination, and some from gnomon shadow measurements; thus the methods of calculation and verification gradually changed. Liu Hong 劉洪 realized that the moon's motion has retardation and acceleration; Liu Zhuo 劉倬 realized that the sun's motion has expansion and contraction; He Chengtian 何承天 realized how to measure gnomon shadows to determine the sequence of solar terms; Jiang Ji 姜岌 realized how to take the lunar lodge directly opposite the moon's path as the degree where the sun is located; Zu Chongzhi 祖冲之 first realized the precession of the equinoxes; Zhang Zixin 張子信 realized that the moon's path has an inside and outside relative to the nodal intersections, and that the five planets have appearances, disappearances, and varying orientations; and Li Chunfeng 李淳風 realized the system of fixing the true new moon, uniting solar terms, new moons, and intercalary remainders all under a single method—thus the methods of calculation and verification gradually grew more precise. Only the Season-Granting Calendar (Shoushi li 授時曆) of the vanquished [Yuan] dynasty, established by Xu Heng 許衡 and Guo Shoujing 郭守敬, compared and distinguished similarities and differences, weighed and adopted median values, and completely discarded the calculations of accumulated days and accumulated years [from a grand epoch]. When using it to investigate antiquity, one increases the tropical year remainder and reduces the precession of the equinoxes; when using it to project the future, one increases the precession of the equinoxes and reduces the tropical year remainder. Those of the time who praised its method said that it was able to reveal the evidence of following heaven to seek conformity and prove the errors of forced interpretations by predecessors; from antiquity to the present, none had been able to equal it. The Great Concordance Calendar (Datong li 大統曆 [written 太統曆]) of our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu Gao Huangdi 太祖高皇帝), slightly adapted the old system of the Season-Granting Calendar; in establishing astronomical offices it combined Chinese and foreign [methods], and in observational divination it synthesized ancient and modern [practices]. Its models and formulas are refined and detailed, and its marvelous mechanism operates with wondrous subtlety—even if Da Nao 大撓 were to perform the labor and Li Shou 隸首 were to lay out the counting rods, how would they suffice to compare with it! For this reason, having used it…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
至今晝一靡爽視彼漢唐以後未數歲而
輒差者其精密固已相懸即正嘉間之交
食時刻分秒起復方位稍與推驗不協然
比之永平永元之際先後背馳日月乖異
者又奚啻徑庭哉繇斯以譚雖俟諸萬世
無敝可也乃頃者星官失職乖舛易常遠
邇傳聞以爲駭異夫數出於秒曶以成毫
釐毫釐積累遂成分寸初行生分積分成
度此於法至玄矣乃若躔度儀式粲然可
===
覩即卜祝能辯之而輒已違舛若茲曲算
旁占安所復望萬一閏餘失次交食靡驗
有能如楊岑之先識宗紺之獻言者乎宜
乎廑執事之問也愚生管窺蠡測何足與
知顧嘗竊聞之前人曰天道無端惟理可
以推其幾天道至妙因數可以窮其理理
緣數顯數從理出故班孟堅言治曆之所
當急者三謂專門之裔明理之儒精算之
士均之不可缺一也昔元封間下詔徵募
punctuated: 至今畫一靡爽。視彼漢、唐以後，未數歲而輒差者，其精密固已相懸。即正、嘉間之交食，時刻、分秒、起復、方位稍與推驗不協，然比之永平、永元之際，先後背馳，日月乖異者，又奚啻徑庭哉！繇斯以譚，雖俟諸萬世無敝可也。乃頃者星官失職，乖舛易常，遠邇傳聞，以爲駭異。夫數出於秒曶，以成毫釐，毫釐積累，遂成分寸，初行生分，積分成度，此於法至玄矣。乃若躔度儀式，粲然可覩，即卜祝能辯之，而輒已違舛若茲，曲算旁占，安所復望？萬一閏餘失次，交食靡驗，有能如楊岑之先識、宗紺之獻言者乎？宜乎廑執事之問也。愚生管窺蠡測，何足與知？顧嘗竊聞之前人曰：「天道無端，惟理可以推其幾；天道至妙，因數可以窮其理。」理緣數顯，數從理出。故班孟堅言治曆之所當急者三，謂專門之裔、明理之儒、精算之士，均之不可缺一也。昔元封間下詔徵募，
translation_en: …to the present day, it has remained uniform and without error. Compared to those systems since the Han and Tang dynasties that fell into discrepancy after scarcely a few years, its precision is already worlds apart. Even though during the Zhengde (1506–1521) and Jiajing (1522–1566) eras, the hours, quarters, minutes, and seconds, as well as the phases of onset and recovery and the directional bearings of solar and lunar eclipses, were slightly out of accord with predictive observations, yet compared to the Yongping (58–75) and Yongyuan (89–105) eras, when predictions and observations ran counter to one another and the sun and moon were out of step, how could the difference be merely a wide gulf! Speaking from this perspective, even if we expect it to endure for ten thousand generations without defect, that is altogether possible. Yet recently, the astronomical officials have been derelict in their duties, falling into errors that depart from the norm, so that as word spreads far and near, people regard it with astonishment. Now, numbers arise from tiny fractions (miao and hu) to form hairs and threads (hao and li); hairs and threads accumulate to form tenths of an inch and inches (fen and cun); the initial movement generates fractions, and accumulated fractions form degrees. In terms of method, this is most abstruse. Yet when it comes to the orbital degrees and the established formulas, which are brilliantly clear to see—matters that even diviners and invocators can distinguish—if they already fall into such errors as this, what hope is there left for intricate calculations and auxiliary prognostications? If by some chance the intercalary remainders lose their proper sequence and eclipses fail to match verification, will there be anyone capable of the foresight of Yang Cen or the submitted counsel of Zong Gan? It is fitting indeed that this should trouble the Examiner to ask! With my narrow, shortsighted understanding, how am I worthy of knowing about this? Yet I have ventured to hear from predecessors: "The Way of Heaven has no fixed beginning; only through principle (li) can one infer its subtle springs. The Way of Heaven is supremely marvelous; through numbers (shu) one can fathom its principle." Principle becomes manifest through numbers, and numbers issue from principle. Therefore Ban Mengjian (Ban Gu 班固) said that in regulating the calendar there are three urgent necessities: the descendants of hereditary specialists, Confucian scholars who understand principle, and gentlemen skilled in calculation—not one of the three can be dispensed with. In the past, during the Yuanfeng era (110–105 BCE), an edict was issued to recruit experts…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
而鄧平都閎諸人出焉延光之曆聚而議
者百餘人今占天之書雖
國法所禁而治曆之科徵募得無有未廣乎
馮光郭香之爭詔下三府與儒林明道者
詳議務得道真司馬遷雖號博雅而所言
歲次閏朔猶多與經傳不相符合今儒者
棄去曆象不講即有論篡疑涉齊諧明理
之儒將安所得而用之乎太史之官自古
隆之我
===
太祖高皇帝得諸儒龔斆等拜爲春夏官至置
爲四輔告于
太廟以重其事今任用之法得無太輕即有耆
碩之士將無擬步前郤者乎夫天下之事
務於紛更則矯枉而過正狃於積習則踵
敝而承訛矧治曆明時典莫重焉時以作
事事以厚生自古帝王所以釐百工而熙
庶績若五紀而備庶徵者咸不能違詎可
泛焉不爲之所哉方今
punctuated: 而鄧平、都閎諸人出焉；延光之曆，聚而議者百餘人。今占天之書，雖國法所禁，而治曆之科，徵募得無有未廣乎？馮光、郭香之爭，詔下三府，與儒林明道者詳議，務得道真。司馬遷雖號博雅，而所言歲次、閏朔，猶多與經傳不相符合。今儒者棄去曆象不講，即有論篡，疑涉《齊諧》，明理之儒，將安所得而用之乎？太史之官，自古隆之。我太祖高皇帝得諸儒龔斆等，拜爲春、夏官，至置爲四輔，告于太廟，以重其事。今任用之法，得無太輕？即有耆碩之士，將無擬步前郤者乎？夫天下之事，務於紛更，則矯枉而過正；狃於積習，則踵敝而承訛。矧治曆明時，典莫重焉。時以作事，事以厚生，自古帝王所以釐百工而熙庶績、若五紀而備庶徵者，咸不能違，詎可泛焉不爲之所哉？方今
translation_en: … and men such as Deng Ping 鄧平 and Du Hong 都閎 came forward; for the calendar of the Yanguang 延光 era (122–125 CE), more than a hundred people gathered to deliberate. Today, although books on celestial divination are prohibited by the laws of the state, in the specialized field of calendar reform, could it be that recruitment and summoning have not been sufficiently broad? During the dispute between Feng Guang 馮光 and Guo Xiang 郭香 [Chen Huang 陳晃], an imperial decree was sent down to the Three Ducal Offices to deliberate in detail with Confucian scholars who understood the Way, striving to attain the true principles. Although Sima Qian 司馬遷 was renowned for his broad learning and elegance, what he said about the Jupiter stations, intercalary months, and new moons still frequently failed to accord with the Classics and their commentaries. Nowadays, Confucian scholars cast aside calendrical phenomena and do not discuss them; even if someone compiles a treatise on the subject, they are suspected of dabbling in tales of the bizarre like the Qi Xie 齊諧. Where, then, are we to find and employ Confucian scholars who illuminate the underlying principles? The office of Grand Scribe (Taishi 太史) has been held in high esteem since antiquity. When Our Grand Progenitor, the Emperor Gao (Taizu Gaohuangdi 太祖高皇帝), obtained the Confucian scholars Gong Xiao 龔斆 and others, he appointed them as Officials of Spring and Summer, even establishing them as the Four Auxiliaries (Sifu 四輔) and announcing it at the Imperial Ancestral Temple to give weight to their responsibilities. Today, could it be that the methods of appointment and employment take them too lightly? Even if there are venerable and eminent scholars, will they not hesitate, stepping forward only to shrink back? Now, in the affairs of the world, if one is bent on disorderly alterations, one overcorrects in righting a wrong; if one is bound by accumulated habits, one follows in the footsteps of decay and perpetuates errors. How much more is this true for regulating the calendar and clarifying the seasons, than which no institution is more important! The seasons are used to initiate affairs, and affairs are used to enrich livelihoods. That whereby the emperors and kings of antiquity regulated the hundred artisans and brightened all achievements, conformed to the Five Regulators and prepared for the various verifications—none of them could depart from this. How could one treat it perfunctorily and fail to make proper provision for it? At present, …

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
聖明在上百度惟貞攝提順紀
曆數得序固無庸輕有所修改以滋惆擾之端
唯是二三疇人僅挾一技史所謂陰陽家
耳顧欽若敬授之鉅典悉揭而界之其事
則重其學則末此歐陽修氏所慨嘆也且
其訛舛相襲漫無校證昔人謂獨非莫知
獨是莫曉其旨正與此類彼又何所憚而
不戢且弛耶故先臣大學士丘濬請詔求
天下通星曆者以任考驗之責盡講究之
===
方禮部主事鄭善夫請擇海內儒術中有
究心天人之學使得盡觀秘書加以歲月
俾上按往古下訂來今而疇人金鍾慨司
候之弛業亦請歲會月試甄別去留大計
之期並嚴黜陟事有似緩而實急者此類
是也今誠倣此意行之自世業子弟至於
草澤布衣博加延訪論定後官如漢人署
職課候覈其中否以爲上下又如魏人命
高堂隆楊偉輩推校天文更相劾奏俟其
punctuated: 聖明在上，百度惟貞，攝提順紀，曆數得序，固無庸輕有所修改，以滋惆擾之端。唯是二三疇人，僅挾一技，史所謂陰陽家耳，顧欽若敬授之鉅典，悉揭而界之。其事則重，其學則末，此歐陽修氏所慨嘆也。且其訛舛相襲，漫無校證。昔人謂「獨非莫知，獨是莫曉」，其旨正與此類，彼又何所憚而不戢且弛耶？故先臣大學士丘濬請詔求天下通星曆者，以任考驗之責，盡講究之方；禮部主事鄭善夫請擇海內儒術中有究心天人之學，使得盡觀秘書，加以歲月，俾上按往古，下訂來今；而疇人金鍾慨司候之弛業，亦請歲會月試，甄別去留，大計之期，並嚴黜陟。事有似緩而實急者，此類是也。今誠倣此意行之，自世業子弟至於草澤布衣，博加延訪，論定後官。如漢人署職課候，覈其中否以爲上下；又如魏人命高堂隆、楊偉輩推校天文，更相劾奏。俟其
translation_en: … His Sacred Majesty reigns above, and all institutional measures are upright; the *sheti* (Jupiter cycle) follows its regular course, and the calendrical calculations are in proper order, so there is indeed no need to lightly make alterations that would only give rise to confusion and disturbance. Yet these few hereditary astronomers possess merely a single technical skill—what the histories call the "Yin-Yang school." Nevertheless, the grand canon of reverently following Heaven and respectfully bestowing the seasons is entirely handed over to them. The responsibility is weighty, yet their learning is superficial; this is what Ouyang Xiu 歐陽修 lamented. Moreover, they pass down errors and discrepancies from one to another without any verification or correction. As someone of old said, "When they alone are wrong, no one knows; when they alone are right, no one understands"—the meaning applies precisely to such cases. What then do they have to fear that would keep them from being presumptuous [?] and lax? Therefore, the former official and Grand Secretary Qiu Jun 丘濬 requested an imperial edict seeking out those throughout the realm versed in astrology and calendrical science to take on the responsibility of testing and verification and to exhaustively pursue methods of study; Secretary in the Ministry of Rites Zheng Shanfu 鄭善夫 requested that Confucian scholars within the seas who had devoted their minds to the study of Heaven and Man be selected and permitted to read all the secret imperial books, granting them years and months so that they might examine antiquity above and correct the present and future below; and the astronomer Jin Zhong 金鍾, lamenting that the observers had grown lax in their profession, likewise requested annual evaluations and monthly tests to screen and determine who should stay or leave, and at the time of the Great Reckoning (triennial evaluation) to strictly enforce demotions and promotions. Among affairs that appear unurgent yet are in fact pressing, this is just such a case. If today we truly emulate this intent and put it into practice—widely seeking out and inviting everyone from the sons and younger brothers of hereditary astronomical families down to commoners in the countryside, assessing their merits before appointing them to office; just as the men of Han assigned posts to test astronomical observations and verified their accuracy to determine higher or lower rank, or as the men of Wei commanded Gaotang Long 高堂隆, Yang Wei 楊偉, and others to calculate and check celestial phenomena and impeach one another in memorials—and wait until they …

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
積有勞勩即顯陟隨之則術業寖興人心
競奮庶幾有深明曆理如楊雄善立差法
如邵雍沉潛智巧如許衡郭守敬者以應
當宁之求而于敬天勤民之務未必無少補矣
若謂中和位育無關於器數此迂儒之闊
論非明問意也愚何敢贅陳焉
第三問
甯瑞鯉
同考試官訓導郭　批〔以聖賢之奧蘊廣漢魏之英葩〕
===
同考試官訓導張　批〔古聖賢兼善獨善是能立德立業者茲作善發其蘊且格調語詞皆在秦漢之上其立言者與敬錄〕
可誦可傳
同考試官教諭范　批〔獨善兼善之旨發揮明盡且叙事斷制種種臻妙殆非炎祚以後文字可以傳矣〕
考試官侍讀羅　批〔善無窮達此聖學也是策品隲精確發揮明盡必有養之士宜錄以式〕
考試官右中允高　批〔此一策道術人心所關子乃辨析幾微論議激切非具卓識者不能宜錄〕
punctuated:
積有勞勩，即顯陟隨之，則術業寖興，人心競奮。庶幾有深明曆理如楊雄，善立差法如邵雍，沉潛智巧如許衡、郭守敬者，以應當宁之求，而于敬天勤民之務，未必無少補矣。若謂中和位育無關於器數，此迂儒之闊論，非明問意也，愚何敢贅陳焉。

第三問
甯瑞鯉
同考試官訓導郭批〔以聖賢之奧蘊，廣漢魏之英葩，可誦可傳。〕
同考試官訓導張批〔古聖賢兼善獨善，是能立德立業者。茲作善發其蘊，且格調語詞皆在秦漢之上，其立言者與！敬錄。〕
同考試官教諭范批〔獨善兼善之旨，發揮明盡，且叙事斷制種種臻妙，殆非炎祚以後文字，可以傳矣。〕
考試官侍讀羅批〔善無窮達，此聖學也。是策品隲精確，發揮明盡，必有養之士，宜錄以式。〕
考試官右中允高批〔此一策道術人心所關，子乃辨析幾微，論議激切，非具卓識者不能，宜錄。〕
translation_en:
… once they have accumulated merit and toil, prominent promotion will follow immediately; then technical expertise will gradually flourish, and men's minds will strive with vigor. Perhaps there will emerge those who deeply understand the principles of the calendar like Yang Xiong 楊雄, who excel at establishing methods of variation (chafa) like Shao Yong 邵雍, or who possess profound and ingenious skill like Xu Heng 許衡 and Guo Shoujing 郭守敬, to answer the call of the reigning sovereign; and in the task of revering Heaven and laboring diligently for the people, this will not fail to be of some small assistance. As for claiming that equilibrium and harmony and the proper ordering of Heaven and Earth and nourishment of the myriad things have nothing to do with instruments and mathematical calculations, that is the pedantic talk of impractical scholars and not the intent of Your brilliant question; how could I dare to present superfluous words on it?

Third Question
Ning Ruili 甯瑞鯉
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Guo: [He takes the profound stores of the sages and worthies and expands them with the splendid literary flowers of the Han and Wei; it is worthy of being recited and transmitted.]
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Zhang: [The ancient sages and worthies, whether extending goodness to all or cultivating goodness in solitude, were able to establish virtue and establish achievement. This composition skillfully brings out those depths, and moreover its style and diction are above those of the Qin and Han—surely he is one who establishes enduring words! Respectfully recorded.]
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Fan: [The purport of cultivating goodness in solitude and extending goodness to all is expounded with complete clarity, and the narration of events and the judgments rendered reach perfection in every respect. It is hardly the writing of an era later than the Han dynasty, and is worthy of being transmitted.]
Comment by Examiner and Expositor-in-waiting Luo: [That goodness does not depend on poverty or eminence—this is the learning of the sages. This policy essay evaluates with precision and expounds with complete clarity. He must be a scholar of deep cultivation; it should be recorded as a model.]
Comment by Examiner and Right Companion to the Heir Apparent Gao: [This policy question concerns the Way, its methods, and the human mind. You analyze the subtle incipiencies and argue with passionate urgency; none without outstanding insight could do this. It should be recorded.]

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
天下之善無定名凡公於人者是已天下
之不善亦無定名凡私於已者是已故善
不至於忘已雖善猶私也學不至於公天
下之善非聖人之學也聖人之視天下猶
一身然目不能以兼聽而耳之所觸目不
轉睫而矚之足不能以兼握而手之所探
足不旋踵而赴之蓋其五臟六腑四肢百
骸相為聯絡流貫以成一身之用而有不
然者則且以為跋盭挺解而鍼砭隨之矣
===
聖人之於天下猶是耳聖人不以天下視
天下而以吾身視天下故不以一已之善
為善而以天下之善為善蓋常疑於孟氏
之言曰窮則獨善其身達則兼善天下夫
達而兼善固也即窮矣亦安得而獨善乎
哉人之生也無一日不與斯世斯人相酬
酢內而父子兄弟夫婦外而君臣朋友人
或我施此或彼應其誰能離之而孑然孤
立者乎不能以孤立而不可以獨善也亦
punctuated: 天下之善無定名，凡公於人者是已；天下之不善亦無定名，凡私於已者是已。故善不至於忘已，雖善猶私也；學不至於公天下之善，非聖人之學也。聖人之視天下，猶一身然。目不能以兼聽，而耳之所觸，目不轉睫而矚之；足不能以兼握，而手之所探，足不旋踵而赴之。蓋其五臟六腑、四肢百骸，相為聯絡流貫，以成一身之用；而有不然者，則且以為跋盭挺解，而鍼砭隨之矣。聖人之於天下，猶是耳。聖人不以天下視天下，而以吾身視天下；故不以一已之善為善，而以天下之善為善。蓋常疑於孟氏之言曰：「窮則獨善其身，達則兼善天下。」夫達而兼善，固也；即窮矣，亦安得而獨善乎哉？人之生也，無一日不與斯世斯人相酬酢。內而父子、兄弟、夫婦，外而君臣、朋友，人或我施，此或彼應，其誰能離之而孑然孤立者乎？不能以孤立，而不可以獨善也，亦
translation_en:
The good in the world has no fixed name: whatever is shared impartially with others is good. What is not good in the world likewise has no fixed name: whatever is kept selfishly for oneself is not good. Therefore, if goodness does not reach the point of forgetting oneself, even though it be good, it is still selfish; if learning does not reach the point of making the good of the whole world public and shared, it is not the learning of the sages.

The sage regards all under heaven just as a single body. The eyes cannot also hear, yet toward whatever strikes the ear, the eyes direct their gaze without the blink of an eyelash; the feet cannot also grasp, yet toward whatever the hand reaches for, the feet hasten without turning on the heel. This is because the five viscera and six bowels, the four limbs and hundred bones, are interconnected and flow through one another to fulfill the function of a single body; and if there is any part that fails to do so, it is regarded as crippled, contorted, stiff, or disjointed, and acupuncture and stone probes follow upon it. It is just the same with the sage in relation to all under heaven. The sage does not regard the world merely as the world, but regards the world as his own body; therefore he does not take the goodness of his own person alone to be good, but takes the goodness of the whole world to be good.

Indeed, I have often had doubts about the words of Mencius (Mengshi 孟氏): "In obscurity, a man makes his own person good in solitude; in prominence, he makes the whole world good together with himself." Now, when prominent, to make the whole world good together with oneself is certainly so; yet even when in obscurity, how could one possibly make oneself good in solitude? In human life, there is not a single day in which one does not interact and exchange with this world and these people. Within the family, between father and son, elder and younger brothers, husband and wife; outside it, between ruler and minister, and among friends—others may bestow upon me, or this side may respond to that. Who could sever himself from them and stand utterly alone in isolation? Since one cannot stand in isolation, that one cannot make oneself good in solitude is also …

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
明矣故必曰修身見於世然後知善吾身
乃所以善天下而天下之兼善始吾身之
善完也不然則爲忘世爲徇物而異端之
害紛紛矣胡善之足云哉古之與人爲善
者莫大乎舜當舜之徵庸在位朝四岳二
十有二牧而帝天下也史稱其重華協帝
四方風動善之所及何其遠也然考其
素陶河濵漁雷澤異地而同化耕讓畔行
讓道異人而同和夫非畎畝未發之跡乎
===
孟氏謂自耕稼以至爲帝無非取諸人者
安在其達而後兼也吾夫子轍環天下席
不暇煖至削跡接淅干七十二君而不一
遇其窮何如也然羣弟子洙泗之濵聞道
者蓋三千人幾遍域中矣而刪詩書作春
秋直紹百王而憲萬世故宰我賢孔子於
堯舜而孟氏猶願學焉謂夫子之窮而止
於獨善豈其然乎夫舜與孔子其至者也
伊尹五就湯五就桀而身任天下之重信
punctuated: 明矣。故必曰「修身見於世」，然後知善吾身乃所以善天下，而天下之兼善，始吾身之善完也。不然，則爲忘世，爲徇物，而異端之害紛紛矣，胡善之足云哉？古之與人爲善者，莫大乎舜。當舜之徵庸在位，朝四岳、二十有二牧而帝天下也，史稱其「重華協帝」，「四方風動」，善之所及，何其遠也！然考其素，陶河濵，漁雷澤，異地而同化；耕讓畔，行讓道，異人而同和，夫非畎畝未發之跡乎？孟氏謂自耕稼以至爲帝，無非取諸人者，安在其達而後兼也？吾夫子轍環天下，席不暇煖，至削跡、接淅，干七十二君而不一遇，其窮何如也！然羣弟子洙、泗之濵，聞道者蓋三千人，幾遍域中矣。而刪《詩》、《書》，作《春秋》，直紹百王而憲萬世。故宰我賢孔子於堯、舜，而孟氏猶願學焉。謂夫子之窮而止於獨善，豈其然乎？夫舜與孔子，其至者也。伊尹五就湯、五就桀，而身任天下之重，信
translation_en:
… is clear indeed. Therefore, one must say, "cultivate the self so that it is manifested in the world"; only then does one understand that perfecting oneself is the means by which to perfect the world, and that only when the world is jointly perfected is the perfection of one's own self complete. Otherwise, it would amount to turning one's back on the world or losing oneself in external things, and the harms of heterodox teachings would proliferate in confusion—how then could one even speak of goodness?

Among the ancients who joined with others in doing good, none was greater than Shun 舜. When Shun was summoned to service and occupied the throne, receiving at court the Four Peaks (Siyue 四岳) and the Twelve Pastors (Ershiyouer mu 二十有二牧) and ruling the world as Emperor, the histories praised him as having "double radiance in harmony with the Emperor" and causing "the four quarters to be moved as by the wind"—how far-reaching was the extent of his goodness! Yet if we examine his earlier life in obscurity: when he made pottery on the banks of the Yellow River and fished at Lei Marsh (Leize 雷澤), the places differed yet the transforming influence was the same; those who plowed yielded the boundary ridges, and those who traveled yielded the road—the people differed yet the harmony was the same. Were these not the traces of his life in the fields before he had risen to prominence? Mencius (Mengshi 孟氏) said that from the time he plowed and sowed until he became Emperor, there was nothing he did not take from others to do good—where, then, is the idea that one must first attain prominence before jointly perfecting others?

Our Master [Confucius] traveled around the world in his carriage, his sitting mat never having time to grow warm, to the point of having his footprints erased [in Wei] and departing [Qi] with washed rice still wet in hand; he sought audience with seventy-two rulers without once meeting with success—how extreme was his困 distress! Yet among the assembled disciples on the banks of the Zhu 洙 and Si 泗 rivers, those who heard the Way numbered some three thousand, reaching nearly throughout the realm. Moreover, he edited the *Odes* (*Shi* 詩) and the *Documents* (*Shu* 書) and composed the *Spring and Autumn Annals* (*Chunqiu* 春秋), directly continuing the legacy of the hundred kings and establishing a model for ten thousand generations. Therefore Zai Wo 宰我 deemed Confucius賢 superior to Yao 堯 and Shun, and Mencius wished to learn from him. To say that because of the Master's adversity he stopped at merely perfecting himself alone—could that possibly be so?

Now, Shun and Confucius represent the ultimate pinnacle. Yi Yin 伊尹 went five times to Tang 湯 and five times to Jie 桀, taking upon himself the heavy responsibility of the world; truly …

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
汲汲於兼善也然誦詩讀書以樂堯舜之
道其修爲於有莘者果何物哉彼得成湯
爲之後先故行而益遠矣而善非有加也
孟氏稱其聖之任諒矣顔子簞食瓢飲終
身陋巷而不改其樂謂之獨善誰曰不宜
乃問仁問爲邦内聖外王之學宛然天下
爲度也彼方進德於夫子之門故潛而未
見耳而善非有損也孟氏稱其賢與禹稷
並其知顔子哉夫伊尹顔子其次者也伯
===
夷矯節於首陽而風之激也至廉頑起懦
百世師清焉柳下惠蒙恥於三黜而風之
淳也至敦薄銷鄙百世師和焉夫曰師百
世則當時可推矣二子之不遇也如此而
善之及人也如彼謂窮之必獨善可乎直
其心固曰不善足以浼我吾拒之云耳不
善不足以浼我吾玩之云耳而猶不免於
形骸爾我之隔故孟氏謂其隘與不恭而
不由也夫夷下惠又其次者也逌後楊朱
punctuated: 汲汲於兼善也。然誦詩讀書，以樂堯舜之道，其修爲於有莘者，果何物哉？彼得成湯爲之後先，故行而益遠矣，而善非有加也。孟氏稱其「聖之任」，諒矣！顔子簞食瓢飲，終身陋巷而不改其樂，謂之獨善，誰曰不宜？乃問仁、問爲邦，内聖外王之學，宛然天下爲度也。彼方進德於夫子之門，故潛而未見耳，而善非有損也。孟氏稱其賢與禹、稷並，其知顔子哉！夫伊尹、顔子，其次者也。伯夷矯節於首陽，而風之激也，至廉頑起懦，百世師清焉；柳下惠蒙恥於三黜，而風之淳也，至敦薄銷鄙，百世師和焉。夫曰「師百世」，則當時可推矣。二子之不遇也如此，而善之及人也如彼，謂窮之必獨善，可乎？直其心固曰：「不善足以浼我，吾拒之」云耳；「不善不足以浼我，吾玩之」云耳。而猶不免於形骸爾我之隔，故孟氏謂其「隘」與「不恭」而不由也。夫夷、下惠，又其次者也。逌後楊朱
translation_en: … earnestly devoted to extending goodness to all the world. Yet when he chanted the Odes and read the Documents to delight in the Way of Yao and Shun, what indeed was it that he cultivated and practiced in the fields of Youshen? Because he gained Cheng Tang to assist him before and after, his Way was put into practice and reached ever farther; yet his goodness itself had nothing added to it. When Mencius (Mengshi 孟氏) praised him as "the responsible among the sages," how true that was! As for Master Yan (Yanzi 顔子, Yan Hui), with a single bamboo dish of rice and a gourd of drink, living out his life in a mean alley without altering his joy—if one called this perfecting oneself in solitude, who would say it is inappropriate? Yet he inquired about humanity and inquired about governing a state; in his learning of inward sageliness and outward kingliness, he clearly took the whole world as his measure. He was just then advancing in virtue at the gate of the Master, and so remained hidden and not yet manifest; yet his goodness itself suffered no diminution. When Mencius praised his worthiness as equal to that of Yu and Ji, how well he understood Master Yan! Now Yi Yin and Master Yan represent the next tier. Bo Yi (伯夷) upheld his uncompromising integrity on Mount Shouyang, and the stirring force of his moral example was such that it made the greedy pure and the cowardly resolute, becoming a teacher of purity for a hundred generations. Liuxia Hui (柳下惠) endured the disgrace of being dismissed three times, and the gentle warmth of his moral example was such that it made the mean generous and the narrow-minded broad, becoming a teacher of harmony for a hundred generations. Now, if they are called teachers for a hundred generations, their influence in their own time can well be inferred. That these two masters met with such ill fortune in their careers, and yet their goodness reached others to such a degree—can one really say that in obscurity one must only perfect oneself in solitude? It is simply that in their hearts the one stubbornly said, "What is not good is enough to defile me, so I reject it," and nothing more; while the other said, "What is not good is not enough to defile me, so I trifle with it," and nothing more. Thus they still could not avoid a separation between bodily self and other, between "you" and "I"; therefore Mencius called them "narrow" and "lacking in respect" and would not follow their path. Now Bo Yi and Liuxia Hui represent the tier after that. Thereafter, Yang Zhu (楊朱)…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
氏則倡爲爲我之說墨翟氏則倡爲兼愛
之說楊氏不取悉天下以奉一身不與損
一毛以利天下主於尊生捐死離世絕俗
以爲義故曰人人不損一毛人人不利天
下則天下平矣夫一毛不爲我天下不爲
人故孟氏斥之以爲無君無足怪也至墨
氏言崇儉則茅茨土階也言尚同則協恭
和衷也言上賢則尊賢使能也言明鬼則
尊尊親親也吾是堯舜彼亦是堯舜吾非
桀紂彼亦非桀紂韓愈氏且稱孔子必用
墨子故後世往往以孔墨竝稱而孟氏至
斥其無父之禍同於楊子而不少貸何也
且當孟氏時處士橫議異說紛拏玄虛家
則有若老莊氏法律家則有若申商氏縱
橫家則有若蘇張氏堅白異同家則有若
公孫龍氏誕漫汪洋捭闔變化至不可窮
詰而其說之足以禍天下及後世宜亦不
減於二氏而孟氏斥絕之猶不數數然至
punctuated: 氏則倡爲「爲我」之說，墨翟氏則倡爲「兼愛」之說。楊氏不取悉天下以奉一身，不與損一毛以利天下，主於尊生捐死、離世絕俗以爲義，故曰：「人人不損一毛，人人不利天下，則天下平矣。」夫一毛不爲我，天下不爲人，故孟氏斥之以爲「無君」，無足怪也。至墨氏言崇儉，則茅茨土階也；言尚同，則協恭和衷也；言上賢，則尊賢使能也；言明鬼，則尊尊親親也。吾是堯、舜，彼亦是堯、舜；吾非桀、紂，彼亦非桀、紂。韓愈氏且稱「孔子必用墨子」，故後世往往以孔、墨竝稱。而孟氏至斥其「無父」之禍同於楊子，而不少貸，何也？且當孟氏時，處士橫議，異說紛拏：玄虛家則有若老、莊氏，法律家則有若申、商氏，縱橫家則有若蘇、張氏，堅白異同家則有若公孫龍氏。誕漫汪洋，捭闔變化，至不可窮詰，而其說之足以禍天下及後世，宜亦不減於二氏。而孟氏斥絕之猶不數數然，至
translation_en: … [Yang Zhu 楊朱] advocated the doctrine of "each for himself," while Mo Di 墨翟 advocated the doctrine of "universal love." Yang's school would not take the whole world to serve a single person, nor would it give up a single hair to benefit the world. It centered on prizing life and spurning death, withdrawing from the world and severing ties with custom as its principle of righteousness; hence it said: "If no one gives up a single hair and no one benefits the world, the world will be at peace." Now, not giving a single hair is not even acting for oneself, and ignoring the world is not acting for others; therefore, it is no wonder that Mencius (Mengshi 孟氏) denounced him as "acknowledging no ruler." As for Mo's school: when it speaks of exalting frugality, it resembles the thatched roofs and earthen steps of the sage-kings; when it speaks of identifying with the superior, it resembles harmonious reverence and concord of heart; when it speaks of exalting the worthy, it resembles honoring the worthy and employing the capable; when it speaks of percipient ghosts, it resembles honoring the noble and loving one's kin. We affirm Yao 堯 and Shun 舜, and they too affirm Yao and Shun; we condemn Jie 桀 and Zhou 紂, and they too condemn Jie and Zhou. Han Yu 韓愈 even declared that "Confucius would certainly have made use of Mozi," and thus later generations often paired Confucius and Mozi together. Yet Mencius went so far as to denounce the calamity of Mozi's "acknowledging no father" as equal to that of Yangzi, without the slightest leniency—why was this? Moreover, in the time of Mencius, unemployed scholars indulged in unbridled disputation and heterodox doctrines clashed in profusion: among the exponents of abstruse vacuity there were those like Laozi 老子 and Zhuangzi 莊子; among the Legalists, those like Shen Buhai 申不害 and Shang Yang 商鞅; among the School of Vertical and Horizontal Alliances, those like Su Qin 蘇秦 and Zhang Yi 張儀; and among the sophists of "hard and white" and "similarity and difference," those like Gongsun Long 公孫龍. Their doctrines were extravagant and boundless, opening and closing in endless permutations beyond exhaustive refutation, and the capacity of their teachings to bring calamity upon the world and later generations was surely no less than that of those two schools [of Yang and Mo]. Yet Mencius did not repeatedly reject and denounce them, and when it came to…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
老莊公孫則略不道矣不此之少攻而唯
彼之深闢何也蓋吾夫子惡似是而非彼
公孫龍之誕妄即鄒衍已勝之矣老莊蔑
棄仁義掊擊聖王說若高虛而易聽亦激
於一時憤世之言而未必行事之實也至
申商之刑名蘇張之功利大抵皆枉尋直
尺希世取寵之事在鄉黨自好者猶羞稱
