之矣惟楊氏爲我似獨善而實非獨善墨
氏兼愛似兼善而實非兼善窮而鼓其喙
===
猶足以陷人心妨政事使達而行其敎其
不胥天下而無父無君不止矣故孟氏至
比其害於洪水夷狄猛獸而猶曰能言距
楊墨者聖人之徒也蓋至是而孟氏兼善
之志見矣繇斯以譚洪鍾之在簴小叩小
鳴大叩大鳴聲出於叩而不在叩也寶劒
之在匣陸斷犀兕水斷蛟龍利出於斷而
不在斷也聖人之於窮達猶鍾劒之於叩
斷耳而其本則在吾心矣聖人之心何心
punctuated: 老、莊、公孫，則略不道矣。不此之少攻，而唯彼之深闢，何也？蓋吾夫子惡似是而非。彼公孫龍之誕妄，即鄒衍已勝之矣。老、莊蔑棄仁義，掊擊聖王，說若高虛而易聽，亦激於一時憤世之言，而未必行事之實也。至申、商之刑名，蘇、張之功利，大抵皆枉尋直尺、希世取寵之事，在鄉黨自好者猶羞稱之矣。惟楊氏「爲我」，似「獨善」而實非獨善；墨氏「兼愛」，似「兼善」而實非兼善。窮而鼓其喙，猶足以陷人心、妨政事；使達而行其敎，其不胥天下而無父無君不止矣！故孟氏至比其害於洪水、夷狄、猛獸，而猶曰：「能言距楊、墨者，聖人之徒也。」蓋至是而孟氏兼善之志見矣。繇斯以譚，洪鍾之在簴，小叩小鳴，大叩大鳴，聲出於叩而不在叩也；寶劒之在匣，陸斷犀兕，水斷蛟龍，利出於斷而不在斷也。聖人之於窮達，猶鍾、劒之於叩、斷耳，而其本則在吾心矣。聖人之心，何心
translation_en: …Laozi, Zhuangzi, and Gongsun Long, he did not mention them at all. Why did he not attack these even slightly, yet refuted only those two so deeply? It is because our Master hated what seems right but is actually wrong. As for the absurdities of that Gongsun Long, even Zou Yan 鄒衍 had already bested him. Laozi and Zhuangzi cast aside benevolence and righteousness and attacked the sage kings; although their doctrines seemed lofty, empty, and easy on the ear, they too were words provoked by a momentary indignation at the world, and not necessarily actual deeds put into practice. As for the legalism of Shen Buhai and Shang Yang, and the utilitarianism of Su Qin and Zhang Yi, these were generally matters of bending eight feet to straighten one foot and pandering to the world to curry favor—things that even a self-respecting villager would be ashamed to speak of. Only Yang Zhu's "for oneself" resembles "cultivating oneself in solitude" yet in reality is not cultivating oneself in solitude; Mozi's "impartial love" resembles "bringing goodness to all" yet in reality is not bringing goodness to all. Even when in obscurity and merely wagging their tongues, they are enough to ensnare people's minds and harm governance; if they were to attain prominence and put their teachings into practice, they would not stop until they had led the entire world into acknowledging neither father nor ruler! Therefore Mencius went so far as to compare their harm to floods, barbarian tribes, and fierce beasts, and further said: "Whoever is able to speak out to resist Yang and Mo is a follower of the sages." Indeed, at this point Mencius's aspiration to bring goodness to all was made manifest. Speaking from this perspective, when a great bell hangs on its stand, struck lightly it rings softly, and struck hard it rings loudly; the sound emerges from the striking, yet does not reside in the striking. When a precious sword rests in its scabbard, on land it cleaves rhinoceroses and buffaloes, and in water it severs flood-dragons; its sharpness emerges from the severing, yet does not reside in the severing. The sage's relation to obscurity and prominence is just like the bell's and the sword's relation to striking and severing—while the root resides in our own mind. What sort of mind is the mind of the sage…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
也無窮達無人我無可無不可渾然萬物
一體者也果其爲一體萬物之心雖窮如
孔顔且不得以獨善名之而況進此者乎
少有私一己之心雖聖如夷惠且以隘與
不恭病之而況異此者乎蓋惟聖人以天
下爲一身故精神血脉流暢而無滯而不
爲遺世者之忍以吾身視天下故貴賤小
大較然其有辨而不爲尚同者之愚夫如
是則烏覩乎吾身之爲小而天下之爲大
===
耶又烏覩乎兼善之爲達而獨善之爲窮
耶借曰必達而後爲兼善則孔子不足大
顔淵不足仁夷惠不足師而墨氏之說滋
矣窮而卽爲獨善則虞舜不必聞於側陋
伊尹不必樂於莘野而楊氏之說横矣然
則學聖人者宜何如舜與夫子尚矣其次
則顔子伊尹乎顔子學在克已復禮而極
其效於天下歸仁之遠吾窮取之以善吾
身而莫非兼也伊尹志在堯舜君民而植
punctuated: 也？無窮達，無人我，無可無不可，渾然萬物一體者也。果其爲一體萬物之心，雖窮如孔、顔，且不得以獨善名之，而況進此者乎？少有私一己之心，雖聖如夷、惠，且以隘與不恭病之，而況異此者乎？蓋惟聖人以天下爲一身，故精神血脉流暢而無滯，而不爲遺世者之忍；以吾身視天下，故貴賤小大較然其有辨，而不爲尚同者之愚。夫如是，則烏覩乎吾身之爲小而天下之爲大耶？又烏覩乎兼善之爲達而獨善之爲窮耶？借曰必達而後爲兼善，則孔子不足大、顔淵不足仁、夷惠不足師，而墨氏之說滋矣；窮而卽爲獨善，則虞舜不必聞於側陋、伊尹不必樂於莘野，而楊氏之說横矣。然則學聖人者宜何如？舜與夫子尚矣，其次則顔子、伊尹乎！顔子學在克已復禮，而極其效於天下歸仁之遠，吾窮取之以善吾身，而莫非兼也；伊尹志在堯、舜君民，而植
translation_en: … is it? It knows neither adversity nor success, neither others nor self, neither fixed approval nor fixed disapproval; it is an undivided whole forming one body with the myriad things. If indeed one possesses a mind that forms one body with the myriad things, then even in such adversity as that of Confucius and Yan Yuan, one still cannot describe it as merely cultivating oneself in solitude—how much less when one advances beyond that! Conversely, if there is the slightest selfishness in one's mind, even sages like Bo Yi and Liuxia Hui are faulted for narrowness or lack of respect—how much more those who diverge from them! For only the sage regards the entire world as a single body; therefore, his vital spirit and lifeblood flow freely without obstruction, and he does not fall into the callousness of those who forsake the world. At the same time, he views the world through the measure of his own person; therefore, noble and base, great and small are clearly distinguished, and he does not fall into the folly of those who exalt undifferentiated uniformity. This being so, how could one possibly view one's own person as small and the world as great? And how could one view sharing goodness with all as belonging only to success, and cultivating oneself alone as belonging only to adversity? Suppose one were to say that one must first achieve success before sharing goodness with all: then Confucius would not suffice to be considered great, Yan Yuan would not suffice to be considered humane, Bo Yi and Liuxia Hui would not suffice to be taken as teachers, and the doctrines of Mozi would proliferate! And suppose being in adversity meant nothing more than cultivating oneself in solitude: then Shun of Yu would not have needed to become renowned from humble obscurity, Yi Yin would not have needed to delight in the fields of Youxin, and the doctrines of Yang Zhu would run rampant! How, then, should one who studies to become a sage proceed? Shun and the Master are supreme; next after them are surely Master Yan and Yi Yin! Master Yan's learning lay in overcoming the self and returning to ritual propriety, yet its ultimate efficacy extended as far as the whole world turning toward humaneness; in adversity, I draw upon him to cultivate my own person, and yet none of it fails to be for all as well. Yi Yin's ambition lay in making his ruler and people like Yao and Shun, yet he planted…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
其節於一介取予之嚴吾達取之以善乎
天下而莫非獨也要使吾萬物一體之心
盎然充乎中而溢乎外如元氣之周於一
身而耳聽目視手持足行無入而不自得
然後無忝於聖人之學而聖人之心在我
矣彼異端者吾烏乎攻之
第四問
史懋文
同考試官推官舒　批〔論治者先吏將今每以乏才爲請蓋選任之未盡也子援古証今切中時弊而未復歸重守令之選尤〕
===
知時務之要者録之
考試官侍讀羅　批〔吏循將良盛世事也而本諸課馭得其本矣兼以雄偉之文權古今之變足見博通文武者録之〕
考試官右中允高　批〔選置吏將乃安攘要務子以采實立說篇末尤歸本得民益通達治體者〕
聖王所以安内攘外分猷共理者非吏與
將哉然未得其人則擇之不可不精也既
得其人則任之不可不至也蓋以天下之
punctuated:
其節於一介取予之嚴。吾達取之以善乎天下，而莫非獨也。要使吾萬物一體之心，盎然充乎中而溢乎外，如元氣之周於一身，而耳聽、目視、手持、足行，無入而不自得，然後無忝於聖人之學，而聖人之心在我矣。彼異端者，吾烏乎攻之？

第四問
史懋文
同考試官推官舒　批〔論治者先吏、將，今每以乏才爲請，蓋選任之未盡也。子援古証今，切中時弊，而未復歸重守令之選，尤〕知時務之要者，録之。
考試官侍讀羅　批〔吏循將良，盛世事也，而本諸課馭，得其本矣。兼以雄偉之文，權古今之變，足見博通文武者，録之。〕
考試官右中允高　批〔選置吏、將，乃安攘要務。子以采實立說，篇末尤歸本得民，益通達治體者。〕

聖王所以安内攘外、分猷共理者，非吏與將哉？然未得其人，則擇之不可不精也；既得其人，則任之不可不至也。蓋以天下之
translation_en:
… his integrity in the strictness of not taking or giving even a single trifle. In success, we draw upon his example to bring good to the world, yet none of it is anything other than perfecting oneself in solitude. In essence, we must cause our mind, which forms one body with all things, to abundantly fill the interior and overflow to the exterior—just as primordial vital energy (yuanqi) circulates throughout the entire body, so that in the ears' hearing, the eyes' seeing, the hands' grasping, and the feet's walking, there is no situation one enters where one is not at ease with oneself. Only then will we bring no shame to the learning of the sages, and the mind of the sages will reside within us. As for those heterodox teachings, why would we even need to attack them?

Fourth Question
Shi Maowen 史懋文

Associate Examiner, Prefectural Judge Shu 舒, comments: 〔Those who discuss governance put civil officials and military commanders first. Today people constantly lament a lack of talent, which is really because selection and appointment have not been carried out to the fullest. You cite antiquity to verify the present, hitting squarely upon the弊 (abuses) of the times, and at the end [reading 未 as 末] you return to emphasizing the selection of prefects and magistrates. This especially〕 shows someone who understands the essentials of current affairs; we record it for publication.

Examiner, Expositor-in-Waiting Luo 羅, comments: 〔Upright civil officials and capable generals are the hallmark of a flourishing age, and by grounding them in evaluation and control, you have grasped the root of the matter. Combined with magnificent prose that weighs the changes from antiquity to the present, this is sufficient to show someone broadly conversant in both civil and military affairs; we record it for publication.〕

Examiner, Right Companion to the Heir Apparent Gao 高, comments: 〔Selecting and appointing civil officials and military commanders is the essential task for pacifying the interior and repelling external threats. You establish your argument on gathering substantive realities, and at the end of the essay you especially return to the fundamental issue of winning the people—truly someone who thoroughly understands the principles of governance.〕

Are not the means by which the sage kings pacified the interior and repelled external threats, sharing plans and jointly governing, none other than civil officials and military commanders? Yet before one has obtained the right men, their selection cannot be anything less than meticulous; and once one has obtained the right men, their entrustment with responsibility cannot be anything less than complete. For given the vastness of the world …

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
大非盡乏之才也譬之枇幹栝栢隨地而生
必大匠操繩引以求之而後可收以充梁
柱夫擇人者亦猶是矣人才之出非盡無
適於用也譬之御騕褭之馬者非驅策之
有方必不得使之服銜勒而至千里夫任
人者亦猶是矣擇之精則所得者皆良任
之至則所用者畢効由是以之安內以之
攘外而帝王順治威嚴之績不可坐而致
哉蓋聞之昔人云守令者民之本言吏重
===
也乃史遷之傳循吏必取經術潤飾吏事
者何耶蓋吏不尚夫能而尚夫循彼埶識
趫敏懼或流於詐丰稜踔厲懼或入於暴
修姱廉隅懼或失於矯詷擿伏匿懼或傷
於譎藉令一能吏足辦之矣惟用經術者
乃有以鏡作牧之理而弘學道之用然後
悶悶於政事泯泯於聲聞其質惇也寧爲
保障不爲繭絲寧爲鸞鳳不爲鷹鸇其惠
流也循行阡陌與民興利敎之以孝弟禮
punctuated: 大，非盡乏之才也。譬之枇幹栝栢，隨地而生，必大匠操繩引以求之，而後可收以充梁柱，夫擇人者亦猶是矣。人才之出，非盡無適於用也。譬之御騕褭之馬者，非驅策之有方，必不得使之服銜勒而至千里，夫任人者亦猶是矣。擇之精，則所得者皆良；任之至，則所用者畢効。由是以之安內，以之攘外，而帝王順治威嚴之績，不可坐而致哉？蓋聞之昔人云：「守令者，民之本。」言吏重也。乃史遷之傳循吏，必取經術潤飾吏事者，何耶？蓋吏不尚夫能，而尚夫循。彼埶識趫敏，懼或流於詐；丰稜踔厲，懼或入於暴；修姱廉隅，懼或失於矯；詷擿伏匿，懼或傷於譎。藉令一能吏，足辦之矣。惟用經術者，乃有以鏡作牧之理，而弘學道之用。然後悶悶於政事，泯泯於聲聞，其質惇也；寧爲保障，不爲繭絲，寧爲鸞鳳，不爲鷹鸇，其惠流也；循行阡陌，與民興利，敎之以孝弟禮…
translation_en:
…the vastness [of the realm], it is not that it utterly lacks talent. Take for example timber of loquat, juniper, and cypress: they grow everywhere, yet only when a master carpenter holds the ink-line to seek them out can they be gathered to serve as beams and pillars. Selecting men is just like this. When men of talent emerge, it is not that they are altogether unsuited for use. Take for example driving a Yaoniao steed: unless one has the proper method of urging and whipping it on, one certainly cannot make it submit to bit and bridle and cover a thousand li. Employing men is just like this. If selection is discerning, then all whom one obtains will be virtuous; if trust in employing them is complete, then all whom one uses will give their utmost service. Thereby using them to pacify the interior and using them to repel external threats, can the imperial achievements of compliant governance and awesome majesty not be attained while seated at ease?

Indeed, I have heard that the ancients said: "Prefects and magistrates are the foundation of the people." This means that civil officials are of great importance. Yet why is it that Sima Qian 司馬遷, in his biographies of Upright Officials (Xunli), invariably chose those who used classical learning to adorn their administrative affairs? It is because in officials one prizes not mere capability, but uprightness and adherence to the law. Those whose grasp of affairs is nimble and quick, one fears may lapse into deceit; those whose bearing is sharp and fierce, one fears may veer into cruelty; those who cultivate an ostentatious and angular integrity, one fears may err through affectation; those who pry into and expose hidden matters, one fears may do harm through trickery. Even a merely capable official would suffice to manage such things. Only those who employ classical learning have the means to mirror the principles of shepherding the people and broaden the application of studying the Way. Only then are they unostentatious in governance and indifferent to reputation—their substance is sincere; they would rather act as a protective bulwark than unwind silk from cocoons [by exacting heavy taxes], and would rather be phoenixes than hawks and falcons—their benevolence flows forth; they tour the field paths, promote what is beneficial for the people, and instruct them in filiality, brotherly respect, ritual…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
義之性其澤究也夫此則非循吏不能也
史遷其知言哉又云將者國之輔言將重
也乃晉人之謀元帥必取說禮樂而敦詩
書者何耶蓋將不以才勝而以賢勝彼鷄
張虎視不足逞其雄鷹搏猿射不足程其
技六化四廂不足藏其智三書八符不足
沉其幾藉令一才將足勝之矣惟習詩禮
者乃有以審公私之分而軌德義之途然
後受命忘家援枹鼓忘身以節殉也泰山
===
崩而不變麋鹿興而不瞬以氣定也戰如
守守如戰有功如幸以志攝也夫此則非
賢將不能也晉人殆聞道哉愚嘗俯仰今
昔吏之稱良者惟漢世爲盛夷考其人通
春秋而守成都者非文翁乎修學宫以造
士蜀地比齊魯之風舉明經而守渤海者
非龔遂乎散盜賊以歸農齊民易刀劍之
俗卓茂以習禮聞爲密令而視民如子詔
有名冠天下之褒魯恭以習詩著宰中牟
punctuated:
義之性，其澤究也。夫此則非循吏不能也，史遷其知言哉！又云：「將者，國之輔。」言將重也。乃晉人之謀元帥，必取說禮樂而敦詩書者，何耶？蓋將不以才勝，而以賢勝。彼鷄張虎視，不足逞其雄；鷹搏猿射，不足程其技；六化四廂，不足藏其智；三書八符，不足沉其幾。藉令一才將足勝之矣，惟習詩禮者，乃有以審公私之分，而軌德義之途。然後受命忘家，援枹鼓忘身，以節殉也；泰山崩而不變，麋鹿興而不瞬，以氣定也；戰如守，守如戰，有功如幸，以志攝也。夫此則非賢將不能也，晉人殆聞道哉！
愚嘗俯仰今昔，吏之稱良者，惟漢世爲盛。夷考其人：通《春秋》而守成都者，非文翁乎？修學宫以造士，蜀地比齊、魯之風；舉明經而守渤海者，非龔遂乎？散盜賊以歸農，齊民易刀劍之俗；卓茂以習《禮》聞，爲密令而視民如子，詔有「名冠天下」之褒；魯恭以習《詩》著，宰中牟
translation_en:
…and righteousness; thus his beneficence is exhaustive. Indeed, none but an upright and law-abiding official could achieve this! Truly Sima Qian 司馬遷 knew whereof he spoke! It is also said: "A general is the bulwark of the state," which speaks to the weighty importance of generals. Why, then, when the men of Jin deliberated on choosing a commander-in-chief, did they insist upon selecting one who delighted in ritual and music and was steeped in the Odes (Shi) and Documents (Shu)? It is because a general triumphs not through mere talent, but through worthiness. Strutting like a cock and glaring like a tiger are not enough to display his valor; striking like a falcon and shooting like an ape are not enough to measure his skill; the six transformations and four flank-formations are not enough to store his wisdom; the Three Books and Eight Talismans are not enough to deepen his subtlety. Even if a merely talented general were equal to those feats, only one well-versed in the Odes and Rites is able to discern the distinction between public duty and private interest and follow the path of virtue and righteousness. Only then, upon receiving his commission, does he forget his family, and upon taking up the drumstick, forget his own person—devoting himself through integrity; though Mount Tai crumble before him his countenance does not change, and though a stag start up before him his eyes do not blink—steadying himself through inner vital force; he attacks as cautiously as he defends, defends as resolutely as he attacks, and regards achievement as mere good fortune—governing himself through firmness of will. Indeed, none but a worthy general could achieve this! The men of Jin had surely heard the Way!
I have reflected on past and present: among officials praised as virtuous and capable, those of the Han dynasty were the most flourishing. Let us examine these men: was it not Wen Weng 文翁 who mastered the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) and served as Grand Administrator of Chengdu? He repaired the school宮 to cultivate scholars, until the customs of the Shu region rivaled those of Qi and Lu. Was it not Gong Sui 龔遂 who was recommended as a Classicist (mingjing) and served as Grand Administrator of Bohai? He dispersed bandits and returned them to farming, so that the common people traded away their custom of wearing swords and knives. Zhuo Mao 卓茂 was renowned for his study of the Rites (Li); as Magistrate of Mi, he regarded the people as his own children, and an imperial edict praised his reputation as "foremost in the empire." Lu Gong 魯恭 was distinguished for his study of the Odes (Shi); as Magistrate of Zhongmou…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
而用德爲理掾有三異還白之狀所謂經
術潤飾者兹非極選與不然何以純任教
化如此也若乃鉅當用投書趙廣漢之在潁
川非不流威名也然專厲鋒氣卒以此賈
敗矣虎穴揍獄尹賞之在長安非不入高
等也然卒務殘賊卒以此坐免矣吾姑取
其能可耳而經術則何知馬將之稱良者
亦惟漢世爲盛夷考其人陳湯好書博達
甞副西域都護因矯制徵兵遂斬郅支之
===
首馮奉世涉春秋大義甞送大宛諸客因
持節傳諭竟誅莎車之王號大樹將軍者
則通左氏之馮異也時赤眉煽亂乃奮翼
破之於澠池稱北道主人者則尚經學之
耿弇也時劇虜猖狂乃振旅降之於淄水
所謂敦說禮樂詩書者兹非流亞與不然
何以義急國事如此也若乃韓信登於亡
卒而名成垓下功烈非不偉也獨以勇略
震主而於謀身亦既踈矣衛青起於人奴
punctuated: 而用德爲理，掾有「三異」還白之狀。所謂「經術潤飾」者，兹非極選與？不然，何以純任教化如此也？若乃鉅當用投書，趙廣漢之在潁川，非不流威名也，然專厲鋒氣，卒以此賈敗矣；虎穴揍獄，尹賞之在長安，非不入高等也，然卒務殘賊，卒以此坐免矣。吾姑取其能可耳，而經術則何知馬？將之稱良者，亦惟漢世爲盛。夷考其人：陳湯好書博達，甞副西域都護，因矯制徵兵，遂斬郅支之首；馮奉世涉《春秋》大義，甞送大宛諸客，因持節傳諭，竟誅莎車之王。號「大樹將軍」者，則通《左氏》之馮異也，時赤眉煽亂，乃奮翼破之於澠池；稱「北道主人」者，則尚經學之耿弇也，時劇虜猖狂，乃振旅降之於淄水。所謂「敦說禮樂詩書」者，兹非流亞與？不然，何以義急國事如此也？若乃韓信登於亡卒，而名成垓下，功烈非不偉也，獨以勇略震主，而於謀身亦既踈矣；衛青起於人奴，
translation_en:
… and used virtue as his principle of administration, so that the subaltern official returned to report on his "Three Marvels." As for what is called "adorning administration with classical learning," were these men not the ultimate choices? Otherwise, how could they have relied purely on moral transformation like this? As for using a receptacle [for竹筩, transcribed 鉅當] to receive anonymous letters, when Zhao Guanghan 趙廣漢 was in Yingchuan 潁川, it was not that he failed to spread an awe-inspiring reputation; yet he devoted himself exclusively to sharpening his fierce spirit, and ultimately brought about his own ruin by this means. And in making a "tiger's den" to assemble prisoners [揍獄, for 瘞獄, burying/confining prisoners], when Yin Shang 尹賞 was in Chang'an 長安, it was not that he failed to enter the highest rating; yet he ultimately devoted himself to cruelty and ruthlessness, and in the end was dismissed for this offense. We may provisionally accept their competence, yet what did they know of classical learning [reading 馬 as 焉]?

Among generals praised as good, it was likewise in the Han era that they were most numerous. Let us examine these men: Chen Tang 陳湯 loved books and had broad understanding; he once served as Assistant Protector-General of the Western Regions (Xiyu duhu 西域都護), and by forging an imperial decree to levy troops, he succeeded in cutting off the head of Zhizhi 郅支. Feng Fengshi 馮奉世 was versed in the great principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu 春秋); while escorting the various guests from Dayuan 大宛, he used his imperial insignia of authority to transmit instructions to the states, and ultimately executed the King of Shache 莎車 (Yarkand). The one styled the "Big Tree General" (Dashu jiangjun 大樹將軍) was Feng Yi 馮異, who had mastered the Zuo Commentary (Zuoshi 左氏); when the Red Eyebrows (Chimei 赤眉) stirred up rebellion, he spread his wings at Mianchi 澠池 and crushed them. The one whom the emperor called his "Host of the Northern Road" (Beidao zhuren 北道主人) was Geng Yan 耿弇, who esteemed classical scholarship; when formidable enemies ran rampant, he marshaled his troops and forced their surrender at the Zi River (Zishui 淄水). As for what is called "earnestly delighting in the Rites, Music, Odes, and Documents," were these men not of that very caliber? Otherwise, how could they have hastened to the rescue of state affairs out of righteousness like this? As for Han Xin 韓信, who rose from a runaway soldier and achieved fame at Gaixia 垓下, his meritorious deeds were not unmagnificent; only because his bravery and strategy made his ruler tremble, he was altogether careless in planning for his own preservation. And Wei Qing 衛青, who rose from a household slave …

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
而威振狼胥勳伐非不茂也獨以和柔嬀
上而於天下固無稱矣吾第取其才可耳
而詩書則何觀焉夫論績效之遲速則德
禮之化或謝於武健之操第恐法令滋章
者終不若絃頌入人之尤深矣論扞禦之
勇怯則文墨之士或殿於介胄之夫第恐
一劒爲任者終不若樽俎折衝之尤易矣
然則議置吏將者雖不必拘之以方問之
以類而誠得經明之士於民社封疆不尚
===
有利哉我
國家以六合元元之命係于守令於是除之
於科目拔之於鄉貢循資以注銓量材以
授職諸不在執經之列若必弁與其選焉
蓋庶幾哉烝烝之治矣顧今臧否渾殽習
緣隋窳其能者不自激發而徒興乎紛結
之嘆不能者益以怠廢而自甘于闒茸之
歸吏而能揚其職者或尠其人也又以三
軍存亡之道係於將帥於是進之以武舉
punctuated:
而威振狼胥，勳伐非不茂也，獨以和柔嬀上，而於天下固無稱矣。吾第取其才可耳，而詩書則何觀焉？夫論績效之遲速，則德禮之化或謝於武健之操；第恐法令滋章者，終不若絃頌入人之尤深矣。論扞禦之勇怯，則文墨之士或殿於介胄之夫；第恐一劒爲任者，終不若樽俎折衝之尤易矣。然則議置吏將者，雖不必拘之以方、問之以類，而誠得經明之士，於民社封疆，不尚有利哉！

我國家以六合元元之命係于守令，於是除之於科目，拔之於鄉貢，循資以注銓，量材以授職，諸不在執經之列，若必弁與其選焉，蓋庶幾哉烝烝之治矣。顧今臧否渾殽，習緣隋窳，其能者不自激發，而徒興乎紛結之嘆；不能者益以怠廢，而自甘于闒茸之歸。吏而能揚其職者，或尠其人也。又以三軍存亡之道係於將帥，於是進之以武舉，
translation_en:
…and his awe shook the Langxu Mountains. His meritorious achievements were certainly not unflourishing, yet solely because he curried favor [?] with the ruler through compliant gentleness, he had nothing for which to be praised by the world. In their cases, we may simply take their talent; as for the Odes (Shi) and Documents (Shu), what is there to observe in them?

Now, if we discuss the speed of achieving results, transformation through virtue and ritual might yield to harsh and vigorous administration; yet one fears that multiplying laws and ordinances will ultimately never sink as deeply into people's hearts as the music of strings and the chanting of odes. If we discuss bravery and cowardice in defense, scholars of letters and ink might lag behind men in armor and helmets; yet one fears that taking a single sword as one's responsibility will ultimately never be as easy as repelling enemy thrusts across wine goblets and meat stands at a diplomatic banquet. This being so, when deliberating on the appointment of civil officials and military commanders, although one need not restrict them by fixed methods or interrogate them by narrow categories, if we truly obtain men who clearly understand the Classics, would that not still be advantageous for the people, the altars of soil and grain, and the frontiers?

Our Dynasty considers that the lives of the common people throughout the universe depend upon Prefects and Magistrates. Therefore, it appoints them through the examination system and selects them through local tribute, following qualifications to register their selection and measuring talent to confer office. As for all those not in the ranks of holding the Classics, it seems none are ever permitted to participate [?] in the selection—thus coming close indeed to a flourishing and progressive governance! Yet nowadays, good and bad are muddled together, and customs follow along in indolence and decay. Those who are capable do not rouse themselves, merely sighing over tangled complexities; those who are incapable grow ever more negligent and remiss, willingly accepting the lot of the base and mediocre. Among civil officials, those able to exalt their duties are perhaps few indeed. Furthermore, considering that the way of survival or ruin for the Three Armies depends upon generals and commanders, the court advances them through the Military Examinations…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
試之以騎射購方略之伎而攬智勇之英
卽不皆治經之儒亦豈無博習古今者焉
蓋庶幾哉桓桓之武矣顧今柄置乖剌競
攫梁肥以弓馬得者不過挽强引重矜尚
蹶張之能以策試中者亦循塵飯塗羹無
當韜鈐之用將而克稱其舉者亦鮮乎聞
也夫賢人志士欲有所樹立以著不朽於
後世者甚於人君之求才茲求之者非不
勤而應之者亦非不至乃一當緩急則無
===
異試割於鉛刀求濟於土�castle者此何故也
患在名實之相冒而已有名而實不副則
飾名之術益工有實而名不彰則敦實之
志不固故今吏與將之所務皆名也騖遠
以自旌托之乎卓異株守以累日托之乎
循理藻繢以博譽托之乎恢張詘附以弭
謗托之乎謹畏甚至溼薪操下愁疾閭閻
漁獵取盈殫空杼柚而亦得以善狀聞焉
幸有矯俗者欲修破觚斲琱之意則其形
punctuated: 試之以騎射，購方略之伎，而攬智勇之英，卽不皆治經之儒，亦豈無博習古今者焉？蓋庶幾哉桓桓之武矣。顧今柄置乖剌，競攫梁肥，以弓馬得者，不過挽强引重，矜尚蹶張之能；以策試中者，亦循塵飯塗羹，無當韜鈐之用。將而克稱其舉者，亦鮮乎聞也。夫賢人志士欲有所樹立，以著不朽於後世者，甚於人君之求才。茲求之者非不勤，而應之者亦非不至，乃一當緩急，則無異試割於鉛刀、求濟於土castle者，此何故也？患在名實之相冒而已。有名而實不副，則飾名之術益工；有實而名不彰，則敦實之志不固。故今吏與將之所務，皆名也。騖遠以自旌，托之乎卓異；株守以累日，托之乎循理；藻繢以博譽，托之乎恢張；詘附以弭謗，托之乎謹畏。甚至溼薪操下，愁疾閭閻，漁獵取盈，殫空杼柚，而亦得以善狀聞焉。幸有矯俗者，欲修破觚斲琱之意，則其形
translation_en:
…testing them in horsemanship and archery, seeking skills in strategic planning, and gathering heroes of wisdom and courage. Even if they are not all scholars who study the Classics, how could there not be among them those broadly versed in antiquity and the present? Thus one might almost hope for martial valor in all its might! Yet nowadays the placement of authority is perverse, and men compete to seize fine and lucrative posts. Those who succeed through bow and horse do no more than draw stiff bows and lift heavy weights, boasting of their ability to cock crossbows with their feet; those who pass through the policy questions merely follow after meals of dust and soups of mud, of no practical use in military strategy. Commanders who are truly worthy of their selection are likewise rarely heard of.

Now, the desire of worthy men and aspiring scholars to establish achievements so as to make an imperishable name for posterity is even stronger than the ruler's desire to seek talent. Here, those who seek are not diligent enough? No, they are not undiligent, and those who respond are not failing to come forward. Yet once an emergency arises, it is no different from trying to cut with a lead knife or seeking to cross a river in a clay boat [?]. Why is this? The trouble lies simply in name and reality being confused for one another. When there is a name without the corresponding reality, the art of embellishing one's reputation becomes ever more ingenious; when there is reality but the name is not made manifest, the resolve to cultivate substance becomes unsteady.

Therefore, what civil officials and military commanders pursue nowadays is all mere reputation. Those who chase after distant goals to distinguish themselves claim the guise of "outstanding excellence"; those who cling to ruts to accumulate days in office claim the guise of "abiding by principle"; those who use华丽 ornamentation to win praise claim the guise of "broad and expansive administration"; and those who bend and curry favor to forestall criticism claim the guise of "cautious reverence." It even reaches the point where they bind their subordinates like wet firewood, bringing grief and distress to the common folk, or fish and hunt for full quotas until the looms are utterly emptied—and yet they still manage to be reported with favorable evaluations! If by chance there is someone who wishes to correct vulgar customs and cultivate the spirit of breaking square corners into round and replacing carved ornament with plainness, then his outward appearance…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
無足以飾目聲無足以飾耳且曹起而議
其無能將不久而去之矣此吏之所以日
靡於名也擐腕而先登見謂猛以敢閉壘
而自固見謂安以重馳突而飈舉見謂疾
以速虛聲而遮邀見謂威以備甚至牧馬
屯牛鞠爲椎剽啇夫樵婦鼙作俘囚而亦
得以中律稱焉幸有伉節者欲厲死綏任
咎之志則其肘爲之所掣足爲之所維且
從中而疑其專制將觀釁而危之矣此將
===
之所以日靡於名也然則欲挽今日之弊
奚繇哉亦惟知人善任而責以實焉可也
夫卽墨以積毀受封而王成以僞增賜爵
則課吏難也必也嚴綜核之法愼會計之
典行業勤修下璽書以示勸功庸竟緒增
爵秩以致褒治有異等之蹟雖超遷而不
爲驟民有服習之美寧久任而不爲淹如
是則吏修實效卽甘棠之詠不足多矣寧
文翁諸人可道哉夫趙括撓敗於知書而
punctuated: 無足以飾目，聲無足以飾耳，且曹起而議其無能，將不久而去之矣。此吏之所以日靡於名也。擐腕而先登，見謂猛以敢；閉壘而自固，見謂安以重；馳突而飈舉，見謂疾以速；虛聲而遮邀，見謂威以備。甚至牧馬屯牛，鞠爲椎剽；啇夫樵婦，鼙作俘囚，而亦得以中律稱焉。幸有伉節者，欲厲死綏任咎之志，則其肘爲之所掣，足爲之所維，且從中而疑其專制，將觀釁而危之矣。此將之所以日靡於名也。然則欲挽今日之弊，奚繇哉？亦惟知人善任，而責以實焉可也。夫卽墨以積毀受封，而王成以僞增賜爵，則課吏難也。必也嚴綜核之法，愼會計之典；行業勤修，下璽書以示勸；功庸竟緒，增爵秩以致褒。治有異等之蹟，雖超遷而不爲驟；民有服習之美，寧久任而不爲淹。如是則吏修實效，卽《甘棠》之詠不足多矣，寧文翁諸人可道哉！夫趙括撓敗於知書，而
translation_en:
…form is insufficient to adorn the eye and his reputation is insufficient to adorn the ear; moreover, people will rise up in droves to criticize his incompetence, and before long he will be dismissed. This is why officials are daily swept away by the pursuit of reputation.

Rolling up one's sleeves to be the first to scale the walls is regarded as fierce and daring; shutting the ramparts to secure oneself is regarded as steady and prudent; charging forward like a whirlwind is regarded as swift and rapid; making empty bluster to intercept the enemy is regarded as awe-inspiring and well-prepared. It even goes so far that pastured horses and garrison cattle are utterly plundered, and merchants and wood-gathering women are paraded to the beat of war drums as prisoners of war—and yet such men still manage to be praised as acting in accordance with military discipline. Should there fortunately be someone of upright integrity who wishes to rouse the resolve to die in battle or take the blame for defeat, his elbows will be held back and his feet tethered; moreover, those at court will suspect him of acting arbitrarily, and will watch for a pretext to imperil him. This is why generals are daily swept away by the pursuit of reputation.

If so, then by what means can the abuses of today be reversed? It is simply a matter of knowing men, employing them well, and holding them accountable for realities. Now, the defender of Jimo 卽墨 received an enfeoffment despite accumulated slanders, whereas Wang Cheng 王成 was granted a noble rank through falsified population increases—thus evaluating civil officials is difficult. One must enforce strict laws of comprehensive verification and exercise care in the statutes of fiscal accounting. When conduct and achievements are diligently cultivated, send down an imperial letter under the personal seal to show encouragement; when meritorious service is brought to full completion, increase noble rank and emolument to confer praise. If governance shows achievements of an exceptional grade, even a rapid promotion beyond the normal sequence is not too sudden; if the people enjoy the beauty of being accustomed to and compliant with his rule, it is better to keep him long in office without considering it stagnation. In this way, officials will cultivate real results; even the ode "Sweet Pear" (Gantang) would not be enough to outshine them—how could the likes of Wen Weng 文翁 even be worth mentioning!

Now, Zhao Kuo 趙括 suffered a crushing defeat despite knowing the military books, whereas…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
孟明立功於屢衂則馭將難也必也先察
其行能申校其聲實便宜可假則假之而
命不從中制肝膽可託則託之而讒不得
外搖勝敵者賞卹有薄罪而亦貰沒軍者
誅或有微功而亦錄如是則將崇實功卹
江漢之歌不足致矣寧陳湯諸人可語哉
蓋世之競名猶水之赴壑固不可禦也而
下之從上猶景之隨表必不能違也上精
吏治則天下多廩廩德讓之流上徵將能
===
則天下富赳赳腹心之士聖王所以轉移
變動鼓舞一世之才賢者固如此愚又聞
之傳曰視民如嬰兒故可與赴深谿愛民
如赤子故可與俱死是故民爲上出死力
擊虜不可禁則魏尚雲中之化也橄屬縣
講兵肄射輸租以給軍則寇恂河内之治
也斯可見制敵尤本得民而守令之選固
急於將帥也在執計者辨之而已
第五問
punctuated:
孟明立功於屢衂，則馭將難也。必也先察其行能，申校其聲實；便宜可假則假之，而命不從中制；肝膽可託則託之，而讒不得外搖；勝敵者賞，卹有薄罪而亦貰；沒軍者誅，或有微功而亦錄。如是則將崇實功，卹《江漢》之歌不足致矣，寧陳湯諸人可語哉？蓋世之競名，猶水之赴壑，固不可禦也；而下之從上，猶景之隨表，必不能違也。上精吏治，則天下多廩廩德讓之流；上徵將能，則天下富赳赳腹心之士。聖王所以轉移變動、鼓舞一世之才賢者，固如此。愚又聞之《傳》曰：「視民如嬰兒，故可與赴深谿；愛民如赤子，故可與俱死。」是故民爲上出死力，擊虜不可禁，則魏尚雲中之化也；橄屬縣講兵肄射，輸租以給軍，則寇恂河内之治也。斯可見制敵尤本得民，而守令之選固急於將帥也。在執計者辨之而已。

第五問
translation_en:
… Mengming 孟明 achieved merit after repeated defeats, then managing generals is difficult. One must first examine their conduct and abilities, and repeatedly compare their reputation against reality. Where discretionary authority can be granted, grant it, without commands being controlled from the court; where utmost loyalty can be entrusted, entrust it, without slander being able to shake it from the outside. Reward those who vanquish the enemy, and even if they have minor offenses, pardon them; execute those who lose their armies, though if they have slight merits, record those as well. In this way, generals will esteem substantive achievements, and even the ode "Jiang Han" 江漢 will not be difficult to bring about—how could the likes of Chen Tang 陳湯 even be worth mentioning? Indeed, the world's competition for fame is like water rushing into a gully, which certainly cannot be stopped; yet subordinates following superiors is like a shadow following a gnomon, which surely cannot deviate. When the ruler refines civil governance, the realm abounds with men of reverent virtue and yielding; when the ruler verifies the ability of generals, the realm is rich in martial men of trusted loyalty. Such is truly the way by which sage kings transform, move, and inspire the talented and worthy of an entire generation. I have also heard it said in tradition: "Regard the people as infants, and thus they can be led into deep ravines; love the people as newborn babes, and thus they will go with you unto death." Therefore, when the people put forth their mortal strength for their superiors and could not be held back from striking the caitiffs, such was the transformative rule of Wei Shang 魏尚 in Yunzhong 雲中; when circular orders [橄, for 檄?] were sent to subordinate counties to drill troops and practice archery, and tax grain was transported to supply the army, such was the governance of Kou Xun 寇恂 in Henei 河內. From this it can be seen that subduing the enemy is above all rooted in winning the people, and the selection of prefects and magistrates is indeed more urgent than that of generals and commanders. It simply rests with those who hold the reins of policy to discern this.

The Fifth Question

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
閻士選
同考試官教諭曾　批〔從來治河無奇策此作獨能歷歷數往迹之利害備舉善後之遠謨非通方之士越拘攣之見者不能經〕
〔濟才也〕
考試官侍讀羅　批〔河難治也亦難言也是策洞晰源委較計失得要歸之預防善後其知言哉而勁筆雄詞混混百折不迴之勢有〕
〔學有識士也錄之允宜〕
考試官右中允高　批〔策治河獨主塞是齊變之論而善後諸議俱鑿鑿可行取之〕
===
執事以河防策諸士夫河大患也治河大
事也議事以制患大計也敢不一抒愚臆
以復盖聞河之害中國所從來久矣自昔
君臣相與嵩目嘔心未聞有稱善治者河
也以治之之者誠難也河源自星宿逾崑
崙已折而趨積石乃會雍浮汴以達于淮
夫以萬里奔騰之勢無重岡巨磵以闌之
故常衝決而不可禁此一難也河有出有
過有逕有合有分有逕有注有入何多變
punctuated:
閻士選
同考試官教諭曾　批〔從來治河無奇策，此作獨能歷歷數往迹之利害，備舉善後之遠謨。非通方之士，越拘攣之見者不能。經濟才也。〕
考試官侍讀羅　批〔河難治也，亦難言也。是策洞晰源委，較計失得，要歸之預防善後，其知言哉！而勁筆雄詞，混混百折不迴之勢，有學有識士也，錄之允宜。〕
考試官右中允高　批〔策治河獨主塞，是齊變之論，而善後諸議俱鑿鑿可行，取之。〕
執事以河防策諸士。夫河，大患也；治河，大事也；議事以制患，大計也。敢不一抒愚臆以復？盖聞河之害中國，所從來久矣。自昔君臣相與嵩目嘔心，未聞有稱善治者，河也。以治之之者誠難也。河源自星宿，逾崑崙，已折而趨積石，乃會雍、浮汴，以達于淮。夫以萬里奔騰之勢，無重岡巨磵以闌之，故常衝決而不可禁，此一難也。河有出、有過、有逕、有合、有分、有逕、有注、有入，何多變…
translation_en:
Yan Shixuan 閻士選
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Zeng 曾: 〔There has never been a miraculous strategy for controlling the Yellow River, yet this essay alone is able to recount clearly the advantages and disadvantages of past undertakings and set forth in full long-term plans for aftermath management. None could do this save a scholar of comprehensive understanding who transcends narrow, hidebound views. He is a talent fit for statecraft.〕
Comment by Examiner Academician Reader-in-waiting Luo 羅: 〔The Yellow River is difficult to control, and difficult to speak of as well. This policy essay thoroughly understands its origins and course, weighs the gains and losses, and ultimately comes down to preventive measures and aftermath management—truly one who knows how to speak of the matter! Moreover, with vigorous brushwork and powerful diction, it flows on with a momentum that bends a hundred times without turning back. He is a scholar of both learning and insight; it is altogether fitting to record this for printing.〕
Comment by Examiner Right Companion of the Heir Apparent Gao 高: 〔In proposing policy for controlling the River, he uniquely advocates diking and blocking; this is a discourse suited to managing change, and his various proposals for aftermath management are all concrete and practicable. Accepted.〕
Your Excellency has posed a policy question to us scholars concerning defenses against the Yellow River. Now, the River is a great affliction; controlling the River is a great affair; and deliberating on the affair so as to check the affliction is a great plan of state. How could I dare not set forth my humble thoughts in reply? Indeed, I have heard that the harm done to China by the River is of long standing. Since antiquity, rulers and ministers have gazed out in anxious concern and poured out their hearts together, yet where none has been heard to be praised as skilled in control, it is with the River. This is because controlling it is truly difficult. The River has its source at Xingxiu 星宿, crosses Kunlun 崑崙, then bends to hasten toward Jishi 積石, whereupon it gathers the waters of Yong 雍, floats past Bian 汴, and reaches the Huai 淮. Now, with the momentum of rushing and surging across ten thousand li, and without layered ridges or great ravines to hold it back, it constantly batters and breaches its banks and cannot be checked—this is the first difficulty. The River has points where it emerges, passes through, skirts by, converges, divides, skirts by [again], pours into, and enters—how manifold are its changes…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
也乃其行則至悍猛而不安爲順豈緩急
能釃其流而殺其怒此二難也河之性善
下斯得其平而不爭今亘齊梁之野曠衍
如砥而以洪濤洄洑于其間卒有方數千
里之水欲其建瓴於地中也得乎此三難
也河雜灉沙游泥非有迅流常滌之則勢
必益墊而其身亙鬱起而高於岸夫隄出
于岸流自湍之況霖潦百川復爲之灌集
與此四難也夫誠難其治也而遂委之于
===
不治則非也治之已難也而使不得其所
治之道則尤難也蓋上世惟陶唐時鴻水
沸出民人升降移徙崎嶇而不安禹起而
治之乃行山表木灑沈澹菑故道河自積
石下砥柱歷盟津雒汭至于大伾乃廝爲
二渠過洚水至大陸又播爲九河夫由大
伾以上地形高而水峻急易瀉合乎其所
不得不合也由大伾以下地形卑而土輕
脆善潰分乎其所不得不分也故曰禹之
punctuated: 也！乃其行則至悍猛而不安爲順，豈緩急能釃其流而殺其怒？此二難也。河之性善下，斯得其平而不爭。今亘齊、梁之野，曠衍如砥，而以洪濤洄洑于其間，卒有方數千里之水，欲其建瓴於地中也，得乎？此三難也。河雜灉沙游泥，非有迅流常滌之，則勢必益墊，而其身亙鬱起而高於岸。夫隄出于岸，流自湍之，況霖潦百川復爲之灌集與？此四難也。夫誠難其治也，而遂委之于不治則非也；治之已難也，而使不得其所治之道，則尤難也。蓋上世惟陶唐時鴻水沸出，民人升降移徙，崎嶇而不安。禹起而治之，乃行山表木，灑沈澹菑，故道河自積石下砥柱，歷盟津、雒汭，至于大伾，乃廝爲二渠；過洚水至大陸，又播爲九河。夫由大伾以上，地形高而水峻急易瀉，合乎其所不得不合也；由大伾以下，地形卑而土輕脆善潰，分乎其所不得不分也。故曰：「禹之
translation_en: …! Moreover, in its course it is extremely fierce and violent and does not rest in docility; how could one adjust to its urgency or slackness so as to divide its current and abate its fury? This is the second difficulty. The nature of the Yellow River delights in flowing downward; thus it attains its equilibrium and does not contend. Now, stretching across the plains of Qi and Liang, the land is vast, flat, and level as a whetstone, yet when tremendous waves eddy and swirl amidst it, and suddenly there are waters gathered from several thousand square li, could one possibly make them pour down like water from a rooftop pitcher within the earth? This is the third difficulty. The River is mixed with turbid sand and shifting silt; unless there is a swift current constantly scouring it, the tendency is that it will inevitably silt up even more, and its bed will rise up continuously until it is higher than the banks. Now, when dikes rise above the banks, the current naturally rushes against them—how much more so when torrential rains and a hundred streams again pour in and gather into it? This is the fourth difficulty. Now, it is truly difficult to control, yet to consequently abandon it to non-control is wrong; controlling it is already difficult, yet if one fails to grasp the proper way of controlling it, it is even more difficult. In remote antiquity, during the time of Yao of Taotang, the great flood boiled forth, and the people climbed up and down, migrating amidst ruggedness and insecurity. Yu arose to control it; he traveled the mountains and marked the trees, dispersing the sunken waters and abating the disaster. Thus he channeled the River from Jishi down past Dizhu, passing Mengjin and the confluence of the Luo, until it reached Dapi, where he split it into two canals; passing the Jiang waters to Dalu, he again spread it out into the Nine Rivers. Now, above Dapi, the terrain is high and the water is steep, swift, and easily discharged, so he united it where it could not but be united; below Dapi, the terrain is low and the soil is light, fragile, and prone to collapsing, so he divided it where it could not but be divided. Therefore it is said: "Yu's…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
治水水之道也此禹所以通其法也嗣後
殫石畫之思者發盈庭之論逞奇譎之慮
者競作舍之謀故有欲以人力勝者則曰
塞之便愚以爲是鄣之也有惟諉于天事
勝者則曰不塞便愚以爲是循潹蔓也何
也水氣之導也過爲防壅終必盈溢焉能
築垣而久居水乎然蟻孔之變禍且不測
而欲徐觀其所自定又惡可得也眉山氏
曰不塞汜濫不止塞之則水未必聽是塞
===
與不塞皆非所以永持至安之長策也夫
使其決也而幸不至戎毒可且勿塞脫或
溢皐汨陸將有闔殫爲河之患固莫若隨
決隨塞即不能保其勿壞尚足支數十載
寬近憂歐陽氏曰治水本無奇策相地勢
謹隄防而已是塞也者猶爲猝可倚救敗
術也胡不引漢事觀之乎蓋自周定王時
河徙砏礫禹之故道無可求者故迄於西
京而其爲害益綿綿而不絕孝文時嘗決
punctuated: 治水，水之道也。此禹所以通其法也。嗣後殫石畫之思者，發盈庭之論；逞奇譎之慮者，競作舍之謀。故有欲以人力勝者，則曰「塞之便」，愚以爲是鄣之也；有惟諉于天事勝者，則曰「不塞便」，愚以爲是循潹蔓也。何也？水，氣之導也。過爲防壅，終必盈溢，焉能築垣而久居水乎？然蟻孔之變，禍且不測，而欲徐觀其所自定，又惡可得也？眉山氏曰：「不塞，汜濫不止；塞之，則水未必聽。」是塞與不塞，皆非所以永持至安之長策也。夫使其決也，而幸不至戎毒，可且勿塞；脫或溢皐汨陸，將有闔殫爲河之患，固莫若隨決隨塞，即不能保其勿壞，尚足支數十載，寬近憂。歐陽氏曰：「治水本無奇策，相地勢、謹隄防而已。」是塞也者，猶爲猝可倚救敗術也。胡不引漢事觀之乎？蓋自周定王時，河徙砏礫，禹之故道無可求者，故迄於西京，而其爲害益綿綿而不絕。孝文時，嘗決
translation_en: … regulation of the waters followed the natural way of water itself. This was how Yu mastered his method. Thereafter, those who exhausted their thoughts on rock-solid plans filled the court with their debates, while those who indulged in strange andingenious schemes vied in plans like building a house by the roadside [with too many advisers]. Thus, those who wished to prevail through human effort said, "It is advantageous to block the breaches," which I humbly consider to be merely damming them up; whereas those who wished only to leave the victory to Heaven's course said, "It is advantageous not to block them," which I humbly consider to be merely letting the trickling waters spread unchecked. Why is this? Water is guided by vital force (qi). If one excessively dikes and obstructs it, in the end it will surely brim over and flood; how can one build walls and expect water to dwell within them for long? Yet a breach starting from an ant-hole can lead to unpredictable disaster; if one wishes to watch unhurriedly and wait for the water to settle by itself, how can that be achieved either? Master Meishan (Su Shi 蘇軾) said: "If you do not block it, the flooding will not stop; if you do block it, the water will not necessarily obey." Thus neither blocking nor not blocking is a long-term strategy for permanently maintaining supreme peace. Now, suppose a breach occurs and fortunately does not cause great harm; then one may leave it unblocked for the time being. But if by chance it overflows the marshes and submerges the dry land, threatening the disaster of turning entire regions completely into river, then truly nothing is better than blocking breaches as soon as they occur. Even if one cannot guarantee that the dikes will never break again, it is still enough to hold out for several decades and relieve immediate worries. Master Ouyang (Ouyang Xiu 歐陽修) said: "In regulating water there is fundamentally no marvellous strategy; it is simply a matter of examining the terrain and carefully maintaining the dikes." Thus blocking breaches remains a remedial technique that can be relied upon in an emergency. Why not cite the events of the Han dynasty and examine them? Ever since the time of King Ding of Zhou, when the Yellow River shifted its course at Boli [Su礫], the old channels of Yu could no longer be traced; thus down to the Western Han, the damage it caused continued unbroken. In the time of Emperor Xiaowen (Emperor Wen of Han), the river once breached its banks at…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
酸棗矣乃大興東郡卒塞之故金隄之潰
旋復而白馬之波不揚終帝之世瀕河民
不識濡足之患孝武時再決瓠子矣乃自
臨河湛璧馬扈從將軍已下皆負薪使二
卿將卒寘決口已而築宮宣防後其盛由
是而觀用塞之效可覩已夫孝文海內富
庶非不足修禹之業而計卒出于塞且僅
再傳而復決武以雄才大略猶然長歌悲
感旣徼靈于河祇窮數年之力而始塞蓋
===
即一塞且不易如此甚矣河之難治也我
朝歲漕淮取濟黃流宋之疏汴元之引汶皆
所倚爲用焉利盡東南半天下之賦由此
以進若人之咽喉然繫至重矣然惟南行
則利漕或東決則害漕今之言治者正利
害相持之際也乃欲盡去其害而獨資其
利則難之難矣蓋嘗槩水患而測之河非
汴不得合于淮故漕之憂常在汴猶之內
關之疾也假令汴可無憂矣則虞其轉而
punctuated: 酸棗矣，乃大興東郡卒塞之，故金隄之潰旋復，而白馬之波不揚，終帝之世，瀕河民不識濡足之患。孝武時，再決瓠子矣，乃自臨河，湛璧馬，扈從將軍已下皆負薪，使二卿將卒寘決口，已而築宮宣防，後其盛。由是而觀，用塞之效可覩已。夫孝文海內富庶，非不足修禹之業，而計卒出于塞，且僅再傳而復決；武以雄才大略，猶然長歌悲感，旣徼靈于河祇，窮數年之力而始塞。蓋即一塞且不易如此，甚矣河之難治也！我朝歲漕淮，取濟黃流，宋之疏汴、元之引汶，皆所倚爲用焉。利盡東南，半天下之賦由此以進，若人之咽喉然，繫至重矣。然惟南行則利漕，或東決則害漕，今之言治者，正利害相持之際也。乃欲盡去其害而獨資其利，則難之難矣。蓋嘗槩水患而測之：河非汴不得合于淮，故漕之憂常在汴，猶之內關之疾也。假令汴可無憂矣，則虞其轉而
translation_en:
… at Suanzao. Thereupon soldiers of Dong Commandery were mobilized on a grand scale to plug it. Consequently, the breach in the Golden Dike was soon repaired, the waves at Baima did not surge, and to the end of the Emperor's reign the people along the Yellow River knew no disaster of even wetting their feet. In the time of Emperor Xiaowu [Emperor Wu of Han], it breached again at Huzi. He then personally visited the River, sank jade bi-disks and a horse, had everyone in his retinue from generals on down carry firewood on their backs, and ordered two Nine Ministers to lead soldiers in filling the breach; afterward he built the Xuanfang Palace, restoring its former flourishing state. Viewed in this light, the efficacy of employing plugging can readily be seen. Now, under Emperor Xiaowen [Emperor Wen of Han] the empire within the seas was wealthy and populous—not lacking the resources to restore the enterprise of Yu—yet his plan ultimately came down to plugging, and after a mere two reigns it breached again. Emperor Wu, for all his heroic talent and grand strategy, still chanted a long song in悲 sorrowful emotion; having prayed for divine aid from the Spirit of the River, he exhausted the strength of several years before it was finally plugged. Indeed, if even simply plugging it is as difficult as this, how extreme is the difficulty of controlling the Yellow River!

Our Dynasty annually transports grain by canal across the Huai River, drawing aid from the Yellow River's flow; the Song dynasty's dredging of the Bian River and the Yuan dynasty's diverting of the Wen River are both relied upon for our use. Drawing all the wealth of the southeast, half the empire's tax grain advances by this route; like a person's throat, its importance is paramount. Yet only when the River flows south does it benefit the grain transport, whereas if it breaches to the east it harms the grain transport. Those who discuss river control today are at the very juncture where benefit and harm hang in the balance. To wish to completely eliminate its harm while solely availing ourselves of its benefit is the most difficult of difficulties. For I have tried to survey and gauge the water disasters as a whole: without the Bian channel, the Yellow River cannot join the Huai, and therefore anxiety over the grain transport always lies with the Bian, just like an illness of the internal passages. Even supposing the Bian could be free of worry, one fears that the River might veer and …

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
危我之汶泗汶泗定又虞其盤而危我之
清濟清濟定又虞其楲而危我之豐沛即
幸底定俱勿割又虞其畔而不南重爲運
道之戹然則奈何其治之易哉往事不具
論比者河失其行決于崔鎮潘池其縣邑
魚鼈其人民行河使以留告
上喟然南顧特爲置督府假以事權令一切理
水形便於是改邑起蕭縣之溺布楗堙崔
鎮之洪絙葦埽高隁之壩隤石襯淸口之
===
隄一日之內四役竝興諸使膢胝無胈庶
工膚革不毛而
朝廷重憫被灾之地首
詔賜民租又爲出司農錢鉅萬以哺諸隄繇使
鱗集竝河而爲之作吏有謀撓其計者即
褫厥官或媮墮僨事輒收逮之不貰乃今
天心叶順川靈效職水得所壑而緒業漸用即
功夫新顚木之邑非從民當衝之上策乎
闐滅決口非疏塞竝舉之故智乎捲諸埽
punctuated: 危我之汶、泗；汶、泗定，又虞其盤而危我之清濟；清濟定，又虞其楲而危我之豐、沛。即幸底定，俱勿割，又虞其畔而不南，重爲運道之戹。然則奈何其治之易哉？往事不具論。比者，河失其行，決于崔鎮，潘池其縣邑，魚鼈其人民。行河使以留告，上喟然南顧，特爲置督府，假以事權，令一切理水形便。於是改邑起蕭縣之溺，布楗堙崔鎮之洪，絙葦埽高隁之壩，隤石襯淸口之隄。一日之內，四役竝興，諸使膢胝無胈，庶工膚革不毛。而朝廷重憫被灾之地，首詔賜民租，又爲出司農錢鉅萬，以哺諸隄繇，使鱗集竝河而爲之作。吏有謀撓其計者，即褫厥官；或媮墮僨事，輒收逮之，不貰。乃今天心叶順，川靈效職，水得所壑，而緒業漸用即功。夫新顚木之邑，非從民當衝之上策乎？闐滅決口，非疏塞竝舉之故智乎？捲諸埽、
translation_en: …imperil our Wen and Si rivers; when the Wen and Si are stabilized, we then fear it may swirl around and imperil our clear Ji River; when the clear Ji is stabilized, we then fear it may be pent up [?] and imperil our Feng and Pei counties. Even if they are fortunately brought to stability and none suffer ruin, we still fear that it may rebel against its banks and fail to flow south, becoming a grave obstruction to the Grand Canal transport route. This being so, how could controlling it be easy? Past events need not be discussed in full. Recently, the Yellow River lost its course and breached at Cuizhen, turning county towns into swirling pools and reducing the people to fish and turtles. When the River-Inspecting Commissioner reported the stagnation, the Emperor sighed and looked southward with concern; he specially established a Supreme Commander's Office for it, delegated full authority to him, and ordered that all water-control measures be handled as circumstances warranted. Thereupon, the county seat was relocated to rescue Xiaoxian from drowning, bamboo-and-stone stakes were laid to plug the flood at Cuizhen, reed fascines were roped together at the dam of Gaoyan, and stones were dumped to line the dike at Qingkou. Within a single day, four great public works were launched simultaneously; the various commissioners developed callused hands and feet with no fine hair left on their shins, and the multitude of laborers had their skin worn bare of hair. Meanwhile, the Royal Court deeply pitied the disaster-stricken regions: first, an imperial edict granted the people a remission of land taxes, and then tens of millions in cash were disbursed from the Ministry of Revenue to feed the corvée laborers on the dikes, causing them to gather like fish scales along the river to work on it. Whenever officials plotted to obstruct these plans, they were immediately stripped of their offices; if any were remiss, lazy, and ruined the undertaking, they were promptly arrested and not pardoned. Now Heaven's heart is in harmony, the river spirits perform their duties, the waters have found their proper channels, and the enterprise is gradually achieving success. Now, building anew a county seat like a fallen tree sending forth new shoots [alluding to the relocation of capitals in the Book of Documents]—is this not the supreme strategy of moving the people out of the path of the torrent? Filling in and obliterating the breaches—is this not the ancient wisdom of dredging and diking simultaneously? Rolling up the various fascines and…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
治遥隄又非圖上請行之遺謀乎蓋昔人
焦心銷志殫數百年錯出之奇顧卒崇空
語者而盡施行于
今日此曠世之業也乃議者猶謂河有故道
宜及時恢圖興復茲過計也河流既久走
沙漸淤水沉滯難行自不得不棄而他徙
茲欲奪新河之所必趨強斡而回注于已
滅難明之故道非所以察形也往者孫渡
之役不有覆轍耶或又謂當別開一河以
===
備運道藉阻茲又過計也遠圖不可倖致
將胥糒備作必倚辦縣官勞費且什伯卒
未有能濟而乃設不必然之慮以徼難竟
之功非所以軌事也近日膠泇之役不苦
跋盭耶揆今之計亦曰慎預防之術覘善
後之宜而已是故長隄遠護非不可約欄
水勢然東強西傷之語未必妄也則畚鍤
之工可弗常飭與隳崇塡闕非不可抑遏
浚流然止啼塞口之喻未必誣也則棡落
punctuated: 治遥隄，又非圖上請行之遺謀乎？蓋昔人焦心銷志，殫數百年錯出之奇，顧卒崇空語者，而盡施行于今日，此曠世之業也。乃議者猶謂河有故道，宜及時恢圖興復，茲過計也。河流既久，走沙漸淤，水沉滯難行，自不得不棄而他徙。茲欲奪新河之所必趨，強斡而回注于已滅難明之故道，非所以察形也。往者孫渡之役，不有覆轍耶？或又謂當別開一河，以備運道藉阻，茲又過計也。遠圖不可倖致，將胥糒備作，必倚辦縣官，勞費且什伯，卒未有能濟；而乃設不必然之慮，以徼難竟之功，非所以軌事也。近日膠泇之役，不苦跋盭耶？揆今之計，亦曰慎預防之術，覘善後之宜而已。是故長隄遠護，非不可約欄水勢，然「東強西傷」之語未必妄也，則畚鍤之工可弗常飭與？隳崇塡闕，非不可抑遏浚流，然「止啼塞口」之喻未必誣也，則棡落…
translation_en: …and constructing distant dikes—are these not the bequeathed stratagems that were mapped out and submitted for implementation? Indeed, the extraordinary measures that men of the past racked their brains and exhausted their spirits over across several hundred years, yet which ultimately remained mere empty talk, have all been put into effect today; this is an achievement unmatched for generations. Yet some discussants still claim that the Yellow River has its old course and that we should take advantage of the moment to plan on a grand scale for its restoration. This is an over-calculation. Once the river has flowed for a long time, shifting sands gradually silt it up; the water becomes sluggish and difficult to move, so it naturally has no choice but to abandon that channel and shift elsewhere. Now, to wish to wrest away the inevitable tendency of the new river, forcibly turning it to pour back into an obliterated and indistinct old course, is no way to examine the topography. Did not the past project at Sundu provide an example of an overturned cart? Others claim that we ought to excavate a separate canal to prepare against the grain transport route being blocked. This too is an over-calculation. Far-reaching schemes cannot be achieved by luck. Gathering provisions and preparing the works must rely on the state treasury for funding; the labor and expense would be ten or a hundred times greater, and in the end nothing would succeed. Yet to set up anxieties over what need not happen in order to seek a success that is difficult to complete is no way to keep affairs on track. Have not the recent projects at the Jiao and Jia rivers suffered from intractable difficulties? Assessing the plan for today, it is simply a matter of being cautious in the techniques of precaution and observing what is appropriate for sustaining the aftermath. Therefore, protecting from afar with long dikes is not incapable of restraining the force of the water, yet the saying "strengthening the east injures the west" is not necessarily false—so how could the work of baskets and spades not be constantly kept in readiness? Leveling high mounds to fill breaches is not incapable of checking and holding back a deep current, yet the metaphor of "stuffing the mouth to stop a child's crying" is not necessarily baseless—so how could the stakes and fascines [?]…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
之具可弗時集與歲當夏秋信水既漲而
忽有非時之客水乗之則其潰也必暴故
平準之候人宜議選也地居河壖寸壤方
鬶而即數百丈之息壤因之則其陷也必
廣故巡視之番卒宜議補也上流不暢斯
騰涌而爲災水之由泗入者不可漸以濬
之乎下流不疾斯蕩漫而爲害水之由徐
入者不可漸以疏之乎而又于青兗冀豫
可田之處各正溝洫以引水之溉而披其
===
勢則治田亦以治河也衞博徐邳經漕之
所多開月河以伺水之横而折其猛則漕
通亦河之通也夫飭畚鍤而集栅落則戍
業保矣選候人而補番卒則警備嚴矣上
流濬而下流疏則原委導矣溝洫正而月
河開則水利廣矣所謂預防而善後者或
以斯乎昔管子論備害之道首請置水官
故其要尤在以擇官爲本謂宜妙簡經明
禹貢之士俾領河隄而又博求習水者分
punctuated: 之具，可弗時集與？歲當夏秋，信水既漲，而忽有非時之客水乗之，則其潰也必暴，故平準之候人，宜議選也。地居河壖，寸壤方鬶，而即數百丈之息壤因之，則其陷也必廣，故巡視之番卒，宜議補也。上流不暢，斯騰涌而爲災，水之由泗入者，不可漸以濬之乎？下流不疾，斯蕩漫而爲害，水之由徐入者，不可漸以疏之乎？而又于青、兗、冀、豫可田之處，各正溝洫，以引水之溉而披其勢，則治田亦以治河也；衞、博、徐、邳經漕之所，多開月河，以伺水之横而折其猛，則漕通亦河之通也。夫飭畚鍤而集栅落，則戍業保矣；選候人而補番卒，則警備嚴矣；上流濬而下流疏，則原委導矣；溝洫正而月河開，則水利廣矣。所謂預防而善後者，或以斯乎？昔管子論備害之道，首請置水官，故其要尤在以擇官爲本。謂宜妙簡經明《禹貢》之士，俾領河隄，而又博求習水者分
translation_en: …the materials for stakes and fascines not be gathered in season? In the summer and autumn months of each year, when the regular seasonal floods have already risen and unseasonable tributary waters suddenly surge in upon them, the resulting breaches are bound to be violent; therefore, we ought to deliberate on selecting gauge-watchers to monitor the water levels. Along the riverbanks, as soon as an inch of soil gives way [?], hundreds of zhang of banked earth follow after it, so the collapse is bound to be widespread; therefore, we ought to deliberate on filling the ranks of patrolling guards on rotational duty. When the upper reaches do not flow freely, the waters surge upward and cause disasters—can those waters entering by way of Si 泗 not be gradually dredged? When the lower reaches do not move swiftly, the waters spread wildly and cause harm—can those waters entering by way of Xu 徐 not be gradually channeled? Furthermore, in the arable areas of Qing 青, Yan 兗, Ji 冀, and Yu 豫 provinces, if we rectify the ditches and conduits in each place so as to draw the water for irrigation and divide its force, then managing the farmlands is also a means of managing the Yellow River. And at the points through which the Grand Canal passes in Wei 衞, Bo 博, Xu 徐, and Pi 邳, if we excavate numerous crescent-shaped bypass canals (yuehe 月河) to watch for when the water runs wild and break its ferocity, then keeping the canal open is also keeping the River open. Indeed, if baskets and spades are kept ready and stakes and fascines are gathered, the work of defense will be secured; if gauge-watchers are selected and patrolling guards are replenished, the precautions and alerts will be strict; if the upper reaches are dredged and the lower reaches channeled, the source and course will be guided; if ditches and conduits are rectified and bypass canals opened, the benefits of water control will be extended. Does what I called taking precautions beforehand and managing the aftermath not lie in this? In antiquity, when Master Guan (Guanzi 管子) discussed the way to guard against calamities, he first requested the establishment of water officials; thus the crux of the matter lies above all in taking the selection of officials as the foundation. I would say that we should carefully select scholars well-versed in the Classic's "Tribute of Yu" (Yu gong 禹貢) and have them take charge of the river dikes, while also broadly seeking out men experienced with waterways to separately…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
置其屬使之共行覩圖方略得便宜經理
則職任專而事功自立嘗聞江河在天地
間猶脈絡在人身中然則河之爲患非即
脈絡之病乎而擇官之說則良醫之求也
由前數說則鍼砭湯熨之法也誠采而行
之河之患庶其有瘳乎語云智則謀不肖
則頓愚之爲此言者不過剿曲士迂談而
私畫以爲時事之可行者無便於此若夫
洞利害之故究名數之分以謀萬載之大
計則非愚生所可及也
punctuated: 置其屬，使之共行覩圖方略，得便宜經理，則職任專而事功自立。嘗聞江河在天地間，猶脈絡在人身中；然則河之爲患，非即脈絡之病乎？而擇官之說，則良醫之求也；由前數說，則鍼砭湯熨之法也。誠采而行之，河之患庶其有瘳乎！語云：「智則謀，不肖則頓。」愚之爲此言者，不過剿曲士迂談，而私畫以爲時事之可行者無便於此。若夫洞利害之故，究名數之分，以謀萬載之大計，則非愚生所可及也。
translation_en: …appointed to be their subordinates. If we cause them to travel together to inspect the terrain and formulate strategic plans, and grant them the discretion to manage affairs as circumstances require, then their official responsibilities will be focused and practical achievements will naturally be established. I have heard that the Yangzi and the Yellow River between heaven and earth are like the vessels and channels within the human body. If so, then when the Yellow River causes disasters, is it not just like an illness in the body's vessels and channels? The proposal to select the right officials is thus a matter of seeking out a skilled physician, while the several proposals discussed previously are the methods of acupuncture, stone probes, decoctions, and hot compresses. If these are genuinely adopted and put into practice, then the affliction of the Yellow River may perhaps be cured! As the saying goes: "The wise devise plans, while the unworthy are stymied." In making these remarks, this foolish one has done no more than borrow the pedantic talk of parochial scholars, privately reckoning that among what is feasible for current affairs, nothing is more advantageous than this. As for penetrating the causes of benefit and harm and thoroughly investigating the distinctions of names and numbers so as to devise a grand plan for ten thousand generations—that is beyond what this foolish student can reach.

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
應天府鄉試錄後序
臣萬化
常稽古虞周之盛道
德隆治洽敎休明維時九德
宅俊之士敬應而出者皆足
以翊贊帝業黼黻王猷詩書
蓋不勝載焉此微獨聖作物
覩稱千載曠遇已也良繇古
===
人學爲實學用爲實用故出
入不悖如此我
國家設科取士專尚經術夫亦
欲士務實學以爲世用庶幾
帝臣王佐出其間耳二百年
來士繇斯軌以佐太平者史
不絕書斌斌盛矣曁我
punctuated:
應天府鄉試錄後序
臣萬化常稽古虞、周之盛，道德隆，治洽敎休明。維時九德宅俊之士，敬應而出者，皆足以翊贊帝業，黼黻王猷，《詩》、《書》蓋不勝載焉。此微獨聖作物覩，稱千載曠遇已也，良繇古人學爲實學，用爲實用，故出入不悖如此。我國家設科取士，專尚經術，夫亦欲士務實學以爲世用，庶幾帝臣王佐出其間耳。二百年來，士繇斯軌以佐太平者，史不絕書，斌斌盛矣。曁我
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination

Your servant [Liao] Wanhua (萬化) has often examined the flourishing eras of ancient Yu [Shun] and the Zhou dynasty, when moral virtue was lofty, governance was harmonious, and instruction was glorious and bright. At those times, scholars of the Nine Virtues and men of eminent talent who reverently responded to the call and came forth to serve were all capable of assisting the imperial enterprise and lending splendor to the kingly counsels; indeed, the Book of Odes (Shi) and the Book of Documents (Shu) contain more accounts of them than can be fully recorded. This was not merely because a sage had arisen and all creatures looked upon him, making it a rare encounter of a thousand years; it was truly because the ancients pursued learning as practical learning and applied it to practical use, so that their conduct in retirement and in office never contradicted each other like this.

Our dynasty established the civil service examinations to select scholars, exclusively prizing mastery of the Classics. Surely its intention is also to have scholars devote themselves to practical learning so as to be of service to the world, in the hope that imperial ministers and kingly assistants might emerge from among them. For the past two hundred years, scholars who have followed this path to assist in the Great Peace have been continuously recorded by historians in refined and flourishing abundance. Now that our…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
皇上以冲聖御極懋學右文廣厲
官師益崇雅道誠
虞周載覩而士敬應之時也迺
南都才藪爲
聖世鎬京涵濡景曜最先郡國而
諸挾策遊成均者又四方所
稱英俊之儔誠以彼才具而
===
遇若此有不絶然雅化遵道
德之途循仁義之軌者耶臣
萬化猥以凡庸被
命偕中允臣啓愚典試事獲與觀
文才之盛而竊附於以人事
君之義臣幸厚矣然臣嘗論之士
之致用者學也而所爲學者
punctuated: 皇上以冲聖御極，懋學右文，廣厲官師，益崇雅道，誠虞、周載覩，而士敬應之時也。迺南都才藪，爲聖世鎬京，涵濡景曜，最先郡國；而諸挾策遊成均者，又四方所稱英俊之儔。誠以彼才具而遇若此，有不絶然雅化，遵道德之途，循仁義之軌者耶？臣萬化猥以凡庸，被命偕中允臣啓愚典試事，獲與觀文才之盛，而竊附於以人事君之義，臣幸厚矣！然臣嘗論之：士之致用者，學也；而所爲學者，
translation_en: …His Majesty the Emperor ascended the throne in his youthful sagehood, diligently pursuing learning, esteeming civil culture, broadly encouraging officials and instructors, and ever more exalting theorthodox Way. Truly this is a time when the eras of Yu [Shun] and Zhou are witnessed once again, and when scholars reverently respond to it. Now the Southern Capital is agreat reservoir of talent, serving as the Haojing of our sacred age, steeped in glorious radiance ahead of all the commanderies and principalities; moreover, those who carry their books to study at the Directorate of Education (Chengjun) are peers of the finest and most outstanding men acclaimed throughout the four quarters. Truly, gifted with such talents and meeting with such an occasion, how could there be any who do not surpassingly transform themselves in refinement, follow the path of morality and virtue, and keep to the tracks of benevolence and righteousness? Your servant [Dai] Wanhua, unworthy and mediocre as I am, received the imperial command to join Left Advisor to the Heir Apparent (Zhongyun) your servant [Gao] Qiyu in taking charge of the examination affairs. Having had the privilege of witnessing the flourishing of literary talent and humbly associating myself with the principle of serving the ruler by recommending worthy men, my good fortune is profound indeed! Yet your servant has previously argued: that by which a scholar achieves practical service is learning, and the purpose of engaging in learning…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
以適用也學不在詞章之末
技用不在揮霍之虛聲處則
析義窮理以愼厥修出則肩
鉅謀大以楨王國夫然故士
重上亦重士而於世道有攸
賴已今士所屈首受業者非
六經孔孟乎易言時書言事
===
詩言志禮樂言和敬春秋言
名分孔孟言仁義士童而習
居而求此物此志也至其抒
而爲文章建而爲功業亦此
物此志也豈其空取聖賢之
訓誦讀之入耳而出口以希
世取寵不其然矣夫學而不
punctuated: 以適用也。學不在詞章之末技，用不在揮霍之虛聲。處則析義窮理以愼厥修，出則肩鉅謀大以楨王國。夫然，故士重，上亦重士，而於世道有攸賴已。今士所屈首受業者，非六經、孔、孟乎？《易》言時，《書》言事，《詩》言志，《禮》、《樂》言和敬，《春秋》言名分，孔、孟言仁義。士童而習，居而求，此物此志也；至其抒而爲文章，建而爲功業，亦此物此志也。豈其空取聖賢之訓誦讀之，入耳而出口，以希世取寵？不其然矣。夫學而不
translation_en: … is so that it may be suited to practical application. Learning does not lie in the trivial skill of literary composition, and practical application does not lie in the empty reputation of flamboyant display. In retirement, one analyzes righteousness and exhausts principle in order to be careful in one's self-cultivation; in public service, one shoulders heavy responsibilities and plans great enterprises in order to serve as a pillar of the royal state. Because this is so, scholars carry weight, the ruler likewise attaches weight to scholars, and the way of the world has something upon which to rely. Now, that in which scholars bow their heads to receive instruction—is it not the Six Classics, Confucius, and Mencius? The Classic of Changes (Yi) speaks of timeliness; the Classic of Documents (Shu) speaks of affairs; the Classic of Odes (Shi) speaks of intent; the Record of Rites (Li) and the Classic of Music (Yue) speak of harmony and reverence; the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) speaks of titles and duties; and Confucius and Mencius speak of benevolence and righteousness. What a scholar practices in youth and seeks in private life is this very matter and this very intent; and when he expresses it as literary writing and establishes it as meritorious achievement, it is likewise this very matter and this very intent. Could it be that one merely takes the teachings of the sages and worthies in vain and recites them—letting them enter the ear and exit the mouth—so as to flatter the age and curry favor? Surely it is not so! Now, to study and yet not …

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
適於用是飾韔也用用而遂舍
所學是委弁也飾韔者不可
與行遠委弁者不可與守貞
斯二者非所望於
聖世之士亦非士所以自待也故
臣茲校多士無徒櫛字比句
顓顓於繁縟崛奇之求也第
===
其詞平正通達氣渾厚爾雅
遠之不詭於先民之程近之
能詳乎當世之務而器識之
宏遠心術之端亮曉然若可
望而知者輒亟收之蓋曰因
文徵學因學徵用即未敢謂
拔十得十亦庶幾氣求神遇
punctuated: 適於用，是飾韔也；用用而遂舍所學，是委弁也。飾韔者不可與行遠，委弁者不可與守貞。斯二者，非所望於聖世之士，亦非士所以自待也。故臣茲校多士，無徒櫛字比句，顓顓於繁縟崛奇之求也。第其詞平正通達，氣渾厚爾雅，遠之不詭於先民之程，近之能詳乎當世之務，而器識之宏遠、心術之端亮，曉然若可望而知者，輒亟收之。蓋曰因文徵學，因學徵用，即未敢謂拔十得十，亦庶幾氣求神遇，
translation_en: … suited to practical use is like adorning an empty bow-case; and to be employed in office and thereupon abandon what one has learned is like casting aside a ceremonial cap once worn. With one who merely adorns a bow-case, one cannot travel far; with one who casts aside his cap, one cannot preserve integrity. Neither of these two is what is hoped for in the scholars of a sacred age, nor is it how scholars ought to regard themselves. Therefore, in examining the many scholars on this occasion, your servant has not merely combed through characters and matched phrases, single-mindedly seeking ornate elaboration or startling eccentricity. Rather, whenever their diction was balanced, lucid, and penetrating, and their vital spirit substantial, generous, and refined; whenever looking back to the past they did not deviate from the standards of the ancients, and looking to the present they could speak in detail on the affairs of the contemporary world; and whenever the breadth and farsightedness of their capacity and insight, along with the uprightness and clarity of their intentions, were so manifest that they could be recognized at a glance—I immediately selected them. This was on the principle of verifying learning through writing, and verifying practical capability through learning. Even if I dare not claim to have selected ten and obtained ten worthy men, perhaps through congeniality of spirit and resonance of mind, …

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
可籍手報萬分一耳然此豈
臣
之明能遽必哉異日諸士
果學易者誠知變化學書者
誠審因革學詩者誠敦溫厚
學禮樂者誠會中和學春秋
者誠嚴法戒佩服孔孟體仁
集義肫肫然棄華修實與九
===
德宅俊之士相後先焉乃可
謂體用一原之學不負
虞周之時矣脫一有不售是靜言
庸違而無所容於
聖世者也詎惟多士喪厥重卽臣
且蒙不任之罰可弗戒耶夫
期千里者慎跬步累層臺者
punctuated: 可籍手報萬分一耳。然此豈臣之明能遽必哉？異日，諸士果學《易》者誠知變化，學《書》者誠審因革，學《詩》者誠敦溫厚，學《禮》《樂》者誠會中和，學《春秋》者誠嚴法戒，佩服孔孟，體仁集義，肫肫然棄華修實，與九德宅俊之士相後先焉，乃可謂體用一原之學，不負虞、周之時矣。脫一有不售，是靜言庸違，而無所容於聖世者也。詎惟多士喪厥重，卽臣且蒙不任之罰，可弗戒耶？夫期千里者慎跬步，累層臺者
translation_en: … may serve in hand to repay one ten-thousandth of a part. Yet how could Your Servant's discernment be able hastily to guarantee this? In future days, if these scholars who study the Book of Changes (Yi) truly understand transformation and change; those who study the Book of Documents (Shu) truly discern continuity and reform; those who study the Book of Odes (Shi) truly cultivate warmth and generosity; those who study the Rites (Li) and Music (Yue) truly comprehend centrality and harmony; and those who study the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) truly uphold the rigor of models and warnings—reverently following Confucius and Mencius, embodying benevolence and accumulating righteousness, earnestly casting aside floridness to cultivate substance, and matching step for step with men of the nine virtues and the three eminence positions (zhaijun)—only then may it be called learning in which substance and function share a single origin, worthy of an age like those of Yu (Shun) and Zhou. Should even a single one fail to live up to his promise, this would be "speaking smoothly when quiet, yet acting perversely when employed," for which there is no tolerance in a sacred age. Would it merely be that the many scholars lose their standing? Even Your Servant would incur the punishment for incompetence. How could we not be on guard? Now, he who aims at a thousand li is careful with each half-step; he who builds up a multi-storied terrace …

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
先正基多士往矣行且隨牒
詣
闕下駸駸乎嚮用期矣詩曰京邑
翼翼四方之極又曰彼都人
士萬民之望其立極四方也
唯爾多士固始今日其歘萬
民之望也唯爾多士亦始今
日臣重言之矣尚相與重圖
之其往可哉
翰林院侍讀羅萬化謹序
punctuated:
先正基。多士往矣，行且隨牒詣闕下，駸駸乎嚮用期矣。《詩》曰：「京邑翼翼，四方之極。」又曰：「彼都人士，萬民之望。」其立極四方也，唯爾多士，固始今日；其歘萬民之望也，唯爾多士，亦始今日。臣重言之矣，尚相與重圖之，其往可哉！
翰林院侍讀羅萬化謹序。
translation_en:
… first rectifies the foundation. Go forth, you scholars! Soon you will travel with your official credentials to the Imperial Court, moving swiftly toward the moment of your employment in office. The Book of Odes (Shijing) says: "The capital is well-ordered and grand, the model for the four quarters." And again it says: "Those gentlemen of the capital are looked up to by the myriad people." Whether you establish a standard for the four quarters, for you scholars, surely begins today; or whether you suddenly forfeit [?] the hopes of the myriad people, for you scholars, likewise begins today. Your servant has spoken of this with deep solemnity; may you together plan for it with equal solemnity. Go forth, then!
Respectfully prefaced by Luo Wanhua 羅萬化, Expositor-in-waiting in the Hanlin Academy.

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
應天府鄉試錄序
皇上嗣登寶位之七年是爲萬曆
己卯天下復當大比士屆期
應天府府尹臣　府丞臣
自脩職在提調以例
請
上命中允臣啓愚侍讀臣萬化往
===
典試事先是禮官數條議科
指大抵以正文體端士習爲
務而其要在愼簡校錄者旣
荷
綸俞令四方行之矣玆復申飭所
司奉揚祗事視昔加嚴臣乃
惕然思曰士習之漸於風靡
punctuated:
應天府鄉試錄序
皇上嗣登寶位之七年，是爲萬曆己卯，天下復當大比士。屆期，應天府府尹臣　、府丞臣自脩職在提調，以例請。上命中允臣啓愚、侍讀臣萬化往典試事。先是，禮官數條議科指，大抵以正文體、端士習爲務，而其要在愼簡校錄者。旣荷綸俞，令四方行之矣；玆復申飭所司，奉揚祗事，視昔加嚴。臣乃惕然思曰：「士習之漸於風靡，
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Yingtian Prefectural Provincial Examination

In the seventh year after His Majesty succeeded to the precious throne, which was the jimao year of the Wanli reign (1579), the empire was once again due for the triennial examination of scholars. When the time arrived, His Majesty's servant [blank], Prefect of Yingtian Prefecture, and His Majesty's servant [Zhu] Zixiu 自脩, Vice Prefect, whose duties were to serve as Proctors, submitted a request in accordance with precedent. The Emperor commanded His Majesty's servant [Gao] Qiyu 啓愚, Companion in the Secretariat of the Heir Apparent, and His Majesty's servant [Luo] Wanhua 萬化, Academician Reader-in-Waiting, to go and take charge of the examination affairs. Prior to this, ritual officials had submitted several itemized deliberations regarding the guidelines for the examinations, generally taking the rectification of literary style and the straightening of scholars' habits as the priority, while the crux of the matter lay in carefully selecting those who would grade and record the papers. Having already received the imperial endorsement, orders were given for the four quarters of the empire to put them into effect; now the relevant authorities were again admonished to uphold and promote them and attend reverently to the affair with even greater strictness than in the past. Your servant thereupon reflected with trepidation, saying: "As for scholars' habits gradually succumbing to prevailing fashions, …

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
文體之競於俗尚猶江河之
流愈趨愈變也乃所以正之
端之者皆將於舉者求多焉
斯不已重乎脫有不能稱
明詔謂
任使何矧臣學術淺薄才至不
肖而濫竽玆役寔惴惴乎有
===
餘懼矣已復念以人事
君人臣之大義儻藉是勉竭其愚
或得一二士足以樹尺寸於
他日則臣銜報
高厚之私庶可萬一少圖塞又得
不踴躍奮厲思所自効乎比
至其地維時府臣飭具旣備
punctuated:
文體之競於俗尚，猶江河之流愈趨愈變也。乃所以正之、端之者，皆將於舉者求多焉，斯不已重乎！脫有不能稱明詔，謂任使何？矧臣學術淺薄，才至不肖，而濫竽玆役，寔惴惴乎有餘懼矣。已復念以人事君，人臣之大義。儻藉是勉竭其愚，或得一二士足以樹尺寸於他日，則臣銜報高厚之私，庶可萬一少圖塞，又得不踴躍奮厲，思所自効乎！」

比至其地，維時府臣飭具旣備，
translation_en:
…and the competition of literary styles after popular fashion, are like the flow of rivers and streams, changing ever more the further they rush along. Yet the means to rectify and straighten them are all to be demanded heavily of those who select the candidates—is this responsibility not weighty indeed! Should I fail to live up to the illustrious decree, what could be said of the commission entrusted to me? How much more so given that your servant's learning is shallow and meager, and my talent utterly unworthy; occupying a place undeservedly in this assignment, I am truly filled with trembling and lingering dread. Yet upon further reflection, serving the Sovereign by recommending worthy men is the highest duty of a minister. If by means of this opportunity I strive to exhaust my humble abilities, and perhaps obtain one or two scholars capable of achieving some modest merit in days to come, then my private desire to repay Your Majesty's heaven-high and earth-thick grace might in some tiny measure be fulfilled—how, then, could I not leap with enthusiasm and rouse myself to think of how to render my utmost service!"

When we arrived at the place, at that time the prefectural officials had already made all the necessary preparations,…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
而御史臣應訓臣一鯤暨臣
楊際熙臣張友舜相與申約
東畿防閑內外唯謹乃進諸
曹六館及先後提學御史臣
郭莊臣李學詩臣李時成所
選士凡四千六百有奇三試
之而與同考官推官臣邦儒
===
敎諭臣士弘臣善臣稑臣曰
仁臣萃臣來鳳臣三省訓導
臣茂魁臣世美臣然胥誓胥
戒窮日夜肆力校閱拔儁者
百三十五人並錄其文以
獻遵
制也臣因諗諸衆曰自昔人才之
punctuated: 而御史臣應訓、臣一鯤，暨臣楊際熙、臣張友舜，相與申約東畿，防閑內外唯謹。乃進諸曹、六館，及先後提學御史臣郭莊、臣李學詩、臣李時成所選士凡四千六百有奇，三試之。而與同考官推官臣邦儒、教諭臣士弘、臣善、臣稑、臣曰仁、臣萃、臣來鳳、臣三省，訓導臣茂魁、臣世美、臣然，胥誓胥戒，窮日夜肆力校閱，拔儁者百三十五人，並錄其文以獻，遵制也。臣因諗諸衆曰：自昔人才之
translation_en: …while the Censors, Your servants [Lou] Yingxun 應訓 and [Zhou] Yikun 一鯤, together with Your servants Yang Jixi 楊際熙 and Zhang Youshun 張友舜, jointly reiterated the regulations in the eastern metropolitan area [?], maintaining strict precautions inside and outside the examination compound. Thereupon, we admitted the scholars selected from the various ministries and offices, the six halls of the Directorate of Education, and by the successive Education-intendant Censors, Your servants Guo Zhuang 郭莊, Li Xueshi 李學詩, and Li Shicheng 李時成—numbering more than four thousand six hundred in all—and tested them in three sessions. Together with the Associate Examiners—the Prefectural Judge, Your servant Bangru 邦儒; the Confucian Instructors, Your servants Shihong 士弘, Shan 善, Lu 稑, Yueren 曰仁, Cui 萃, Laifeng 來鳳, and Sanxing 三省; and the Assistant Instructors, Your servants Maokui 茂魁, Shimei 世美, and Ran 然—we swore oaths and admonished one another, exerting all our strength day and night to collate and grade the papers. We selected one hundred and thirty-five outstanding candidates and recorded their essays to present to the throne, in compliance with the imperial system. Your servant thereupon announced to all assembled: Since antiquity, the…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
生毓由地之所鍾迨其出而
昌國也則獨盛于休明熙洽
之日我
聖祖甫入金陵即建禮賢館徵青
田劉基輩與論經史治道既
定鼎廿餘載
覩奎壁間黑祲消滅乃
===
慶文運之當興蓋在
肇造初而
國家億萬載儒術之隆文明之
熾固可預卜矣
列聖代作振新文教益紹明而光
大之肆我
皇上亶
punctuated: 生毓，由地之所鍾；迨其出而昌國也，則獨盛于休明熙洽之日。我聖祖甫入金陵，即建禮賢館，徵青田劉基輩，與論經史治道；既定鼎廿餘載，覩奎壁間黑祲消滅，乃慶文運之當興。蓋在肇造初，而國家億萬載儒術之隆、文明之熾，固可預卜矣。列聖代作，振新文教，益紹明而光大之。肆我皇上亶
translation_en: …birth and nurturing stem from the concentration of terrestrial vitality, yet when they step forth to bring prosperity to the state, they flourish uniquely in eras of auspicious brilliance and harmonious peace. As soon as Our Sacred Ancestor [Emperor Taizu] entered Jinling [Nanjing], he immediately established the Pavilion for Honoring the Worthy (Lixian guan) and summoned Liu Ji (劉基) of Qingtian and his peers to discuss the Classics, the Histories, and the Way of governance. More than twenty years after establishing the dynastic Tripods, upon observing the dark ominous vapors between the Kui and Bi constellations vanish, he rejoiced that the fortune of literary culture was destined to rise. Indeed, at the very beginning of the founding of the dynasty, the flourishing of Confucian learning and the splendor of civilization for our State through myriad ages could already be foretold. Successive Sacred Emperors arose one after another, revitalizing literary and moral education, further continuing, illuminating, and magnifying this legacy. And now Our Emperor, truly endowed with…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
濬哲之資履
君師之位
聖德天縱
帝學日新七載于玆
道化殷流內寧外謐而尤夙夜
孜孜籲俊登彥用丕隆治理
士伏巖穴者卽遐陬萬里外
罔不思見其才美以幸際
===
聖明矧都人士身躡禮賢之地仰
奎壁之輝而
鎬京辟廱之化又得躬被其盛
意必有卓然名世者感奮興
起于其間而無從覯之也玆
得縱觀諸士所爲文言卽人
punctuated: 濬哲之資，履君師之位，聖德天縱，帝學日新，七載于玆，道化殷流，內寧外謐。而尤夙夜孜孜，籲俊登彥，用丕隆治理。士伏巖穴者，卽遐陬萬里外，罔不思見其才美，以幸際聖明。矧都人士身躡禮賢之地，仰奎壁之輝，而鎬京辟廱之化，又得躬被其盛，意必有卓然名世者，感奮興起于其間，而無從覯之也。玆得縱觀諸士所爲文，言卽人
translation_en: … possessed of profound wisdom, occupies the position of both ruler and teacher. With sacred virtue bestowed by Heaven and imperial learning renewed day by day, for seven years now the moral transformation of the Way has flowed abundantly, bringing peace within and tranquility abroad. Moreover, from dawn to dusk His Majesty is untiringly diligent in calling forth men ofoutstanding talent and advancing the worthy, thereby greatly exalting the order of governance. Even scholars hidden away in mountain caves in remote corners ten thousand li away all long to display their fine talents, counting themselves fortunate to encounter an era of sacred enlightenment. How much more so the scholars of the southern capital, who personally tread the ground where the worthy were honored, look up to the radiance of the Kui and Bi constellations, and directly receive the flourishing transformative influence of the Imperial Academy of Haojing! I had thought there must be preeminent figures of world-renowned caliber who were inspired to rise up among them, though I had no way to meet them in person. Now I have been able to survey at length the essays composed by these scholars; though their words…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
人殊類皆抒性靈之眞闡皇
王之緒而辨晳理道敷鬯化
猷弗以奇袤險僻相衒質文
不幾近於正乎而緣是以覘
諸士之習若握贄以徵禮采
言以貢俗臣亦可據而知其
弗頗也顧臣於此則猶悚意
===
大懼焉何也蓋臣之盱衡擊
節於諸士者文也諸士異日
之標著於行業者則質而不
徒以其文也文非不可行遠
而每忌其太盛文太盛則質
易漓而世道人心攸繫之矣
昔者帝王質文相變以濟天
punctuated: 人殊，類皆抒性靈之眞，闡皇王之緒，而辨晳理道，敷鬯化猷，弗以奇袤險僻相衒，質文不幾近於正乎？而緣是以覘諸士之習，若握贄以徵禮，采言以貢俗，臣亦可據而知其弗頗也。顧臣於此則猶悚意大懼焉，何也？蓋臣之盱衡擊節於諸士者，文也；諸士異日之標著於行業者，則質而不徒以其文也。文非不可行遠，而每忌其太盛；文太盛則質易漓，而世道人心攸繫之矣。昔者帝王質文相變以濟天
translation_en:
… varies from person to person, yet nearly all of them express the truth of their innate sensibility, elucidate the heritage of the sovereigns and kings, analyze and clarify moral principles and the Way, and set forth in full the plans for transformative governance, without showing off to one another through strange, deviant, perilous, or obscure expressions. In substance and literary pattern, do they not come close to orthodoxy? And if on this basis one observes the habits of the scholars—just as one holds gifts of introduction to verify ritual propriety or collects sayings to present popular customs to the court—your servant can likewise rely on this to know that they are not偏 [biased/skewed].

Yet in this regard your servant still feels anxious in thought and greatly fearful. Why is that? Because what makes your servant raise his brows and beat time in admiration for these scholars is their literary writing; whereas that by which these scholars in future days will distinguish themselves in conduct and achievement is substance, and not merely their literary writing. It is not that literary writing cannot travel far, yet one always dreads its becoming overly flourishing; when literary pattern is overly flourishing, substance easily grows thin, and the Way of the world and the minds of men are bound up with this. In ancient times, emperors and kings alternated between substance and pattern in order to bring aid to the…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
下質敝則佐之以文文敝則
復之以質蓋爲世道人心計
者然也乃其潛移默運之機
則自求賢加之意焉耳我
朝設科之始唯以文質相稱爲
諭故其時最稱得人自是以後人
文漸以宣朗而敦厚純朴之
===
風不能不隨時而少變今
天子纂圖立極日嘉惠四方士嘗
廣厲學官看在
功令一切崇雅黜浮期得眞才
需實效毅然欲挽斯世之文
而盡歸于質
聖意所嚮指蓋可仰窺矣玆諸士
punctuated: 下：質敝則佐之以文，文敝則復之以質，蓋爲世道人心計者然也。乃其潛移默運之機，則自求賢加之意焉耳。我朝設科之始，唯以文質相稱爲諭，故其時最稱得人。自是以後，人文漸以宣朗，而敦厚純朴之風不能不隨時而少變。今天子纂圖立極，日嘉惠四方士，嘗廣厲學官，看在功令，一切崇雅黜浮，期得眞才，需實效，毅然欲挽斯世之文而盡歸于質，聖意所嚮指，蓋可仰窺矣。玆諸士
translation_en: … the realm: when substance deteriorated, they supplemented it with literary refinement; when literary refinement deteriorated, they restored it with substance. This was because they were taking thought for the way of the world and the minds of men. Yet the mechanism for bringing about this subtle and imperceptible transformation lies simply in paying special heed to the search for worthies. When our dynasty first established the examination system, its edicts emphasized only that literary refinement and substance should be in balance; hence, that era was most renowned for obtaining capable men. From that time onward, cultural refinement gradually grew more brilliant and expressive, while the customs of magnanimity and pure simplicity could not help but change somewhat with the times. Now the Son of Heaven, having succeeded to the imperial enterprise and ascended the throne, daily bestows his favor upon the scholars of the four quarters. He has broadly encouraged the educational officials, as seen in the examination regulations [?], in all respects exalting elegance and dismissing superficiality, hoping to obtain true talent and looking for practical results, resolutely wishing to turn back the literary refinement of this age and return it wholly to substance. The direction to which His Sacred Intention points can indeed be reverently glimpsed. Now, can these scholars…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
應里選而來業已考言見收
于舉者行且續食赴
公車用備
主上驅使果能振衣彈冠力脩其
行業以見于世而不至庸違
先資之言斯為質與文稱庶
幾哉不負
===
今日之所求固臣之願也其或
情奪於聲利而志眩於紛華
將在璞者琱出蒙者汨而攀
悅雖工第以弁髦視之耳於
上意則奚當焉此臣之懼所以謁
謁無已也臣又聞之龍噓致
雲雷震起蟄是故正鵠表中
punctuated: 應里選而來，業已考言見收于舉者，行且續食赴公車，用備主上驅使。果能振衣彈冠，力脩其行業以見于世，而不至庸違先資之言，斯為質與文稱，庶幾哉不負今日之所求，固臣之願也。其或情奪於聲利，而志眩於紛華，將在璞者琱，出蒙者汨，而攀悅雖工，第以弁髦視之耳，於上意則奚當焉？此臣之懼所以謁謁無已也。臣又聞之：龍噓致雲，雷震起蟄。是故正鵠表中，
translation_en:
…who have come in response to the local selection and have already had their words tested and been accepted among the recommended graduates, will soon be provided with provisions along the road to proceed to the public carriages at the capital, so as to be ready for the Sovereign's employment. If they can indeed shake out their robes and dust off their caps, strenuously cultivating their conduct and achievements to manifest themselves in the world, without lazily violating the words they offered as their initial pledge of service, then substance and literary refinement will be a match. Perhaps then they will not fail what is sought today—which is truly Your servant's wish.

Yet if their passions are carried away by fame and profit, and their ambitions dazzled by ostentatious splendor, then what was uncut jade will be over-carved and what emerged from youthful innocence will be muddied. Even if their ornate rhetoric is skillful, they will treat their examination essays merely as cast-off juvenile caps once they have climbed to success—how then could that correspond to His Majesty's intentions? This is why Your servant's anxiety continues unabated.

Your servant has also heard that when the dragon breathes, it summons the clouds; when thunder crashes, it rouses hibernating creatures. Therefore, when the target's bull's-eye is set up in the center…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
兩耦決拾枹鼓當壘三軍奮
臂誠捷於所從也昔董仲舒
啓武帝以損周之文用夏之
忠夫忠則進乎質而渾然者
也董生當射策初尚未識帝
之意爲何如而惓惓以此說
進則其用世之畧固可知已
===
爾諸士抱經術負賢良視董
生當不少遜也矧
上以質求蓋旣示之以
意而猶不以質應之耶矧諸士被
化首善振奮而起旣有徵於其
文顧不能副之以質耶臣固
信諸士之必不如是而臣之
