punctuated: 兩耦決拾；枹鼓當壘，三軍奮臂，誠捷於所從也。昔董仲舒啓武帝以損周之文、用夏之忠。夫忠則進乎質而渾然者也。董生當射策初，尚未識帝之意爲何如，而惓惓以此說進，則其用世之畧固可知已。爾諸士抱經術、負賢良，視董生當不少遜也。矧上以質求，蓋旣示之以意，而猶不以質應之耶？矧諸士被化首善，振奮而起，旣有徵於其文，顧不能副之以質耶？臣固信諸士之必不如是，而臣之
translation_en: …the two pairs of archers put on their thumb-rings and arm-guards; when the drumstick and drum face the ramparts, the three armies raise their arms in ardor—truly, how swiftly they follow what leads them! In the past, Dong Zhongshu 董仲舒 advised Emperor Wu 武帝 to diminish the cultural refinement of the Zhou and employ the loyal devotion of the Xia. Now, loyal devotion advances toward substantiality and is unadorned and whole. When Master Dong first answered the policy questions, he did not yet know what the Emperor's intentions were, yet he earnestly presented this argument; from this, his strategy for serving the world can certainly be known. You scholars embrace classical learning and possess worthiness and goodness; compared to Master Dong, you surely do not fall short in the least. How much more so when His Majesty seeks substantiality and has already shown His intention—would you still not respond to Him with substantiality? And how much more so when you scholars, having been transformed by the moral influence of the premier place of goodness [the capital region], have roused yourselves to rise up and have already given proof of it in your literary compositions—could you yet fail to match it with substantiality? I certainly trust that you scholars will surely not be like this, and that my…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
懼亦自量其終可釋也詩不
云乎王國克生維周之楨又
云行歸于周萬民所望夫士
幸生王國而且能周其行以
爲民望俾後之按是錄而稱
願然曰其良士某良士則司
校錄者之與諸士不均有無
窮之聞哉
右春坊右中允兼翰林院編
修高啓愚謹序
punctuated:
懼，亦自量其終可釋也。《詩》不云乎：「王國克生，維周之楨。」又云：「行歸于周，萬民所望。」夫士幸生王國，而且能周其行以爲民望，俾後之按是錄而稱願然曰：「其良士，某良士。」則司校錄者之與諸士，不均有無窮之聞哉！
右春坊右中允兼翰林院編修高啓愚謹序。
translation_en:
…anxiety, I also reckon, may in the end be dispelled. Does the Book of Odes (Shijing) not say: "The royal kingdom is able to bring them forth; they are the pillars of Zhou"? And does it not also say: "His conduct is completely loyal, and on him the myriad people place their hopes"? Now, when scholars have the good fortune to be born in the royal domain and are moreover able to perfect their conduct so as to become the hope of the people—causing those in later times who examine this record to speak with admiration, saying, "Truly a worthy scholar! Such-and-such is a worthy scholar!" [reading 其 as 某, "Such-and-such is a worthy scholar, so-and-so is a worthy scholar"]—will not those in charge of grading and recording, along with the scholars themselves, alike enjoy boundless renown?

Respectfully prefaced by Gao Qiyu 高啓愚, Right Companion in the Right Secretariat of the Heir Apparent and concurrently Junior Compiler in the Hanlin Academy.

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
舜亦以命禹
凡事豫則立不豫則廢言前定則不跲事
前定則不困行前定則不疚道前定則
不窮在下位不獲乎上民不可得而治
矣獲乎上有道不信乎朋友不獲乎上
矣信乎朋友有道不順乎親不信乎朋
友矣順乎親有道反諸身不誠不順乎
親矣誠身有道不明乎善不誠乎身矣
===
惻隱之心仁之端也羞惡之心義之端也
辭讓之心禮之端也是非之心智之端
也人之有是四端也猶其有四體也
易
象曰火在天上大有君子以遏惡揚善順
天休命
柔在內而剛得中
初六藉用白茅无咎子曰苟錯諸地而可
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
「舜亦以命禹。」
「凡事豫則立，不豫則廢。言前定則不跲，事前定則不困，行前定則不疚，道前定則不窮。在下位不獲乎上，民不可得而治矣；獲乎上有道，不信乎朋友，不獲乎上矣；信乎朋友有道，不順乎親，不信乎朋友矣；順乎親有道，反諸身不誠，不順乎親矣；誠身有道，不明乎善，不誠乎身矣。」
「惻隱之心，仁之端也；羞惡之心，義之端也；辭讓之心，禮之端也；是非之心，智之端也。人之有是四端也，猶其有四體也。」

易
「《象》曰：火在天上，大有；君子以遏惡揚善，順天休命。」
「柔在內而剛得中。」
「初六，藉用白茅，无咎。子曰：苟錯諸地而可…
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books:
"Shun also used these words to charge Yu." [Analects 20.1]
"In all things, success depends on previous preparation, and without such preparation there is sure to be failure. If what is to be spoken be previously determined, there will be no stumbling. If affairs be previously determined, there will be no difficulty with them. If one's actions have been previously determined, there will be no sorrow in connection with them. If principles of conduct have been previously determined, the practice of them will be inexhaustible. When those in inferior positions do not obtain the confidence of the sovereign, they cannot succeed in governing the people. There is a way to obtain the confidence of the sovereign: if one is not trusted by his friends, he will not obtain the confidence of his sovereign. There is a way to be trusted by one's friends: if one is not obedient to his parents, he will not be trusted by his friends. There is a way to be obedient to one's parents: if one, on turning his thoughts in upon himself, finds a want of sincerity, he will not be obedient to his parents. There is a way to the attainment of sincerity in oneself: if a man does not understand what is good, he will not attain sincerity in himself." [Doctrine of the Mean 20]
"The feeling of commiseration is the principle of benevolence. The feeling of shame and dislike is the principle of righteousness. The feeling of modesty and complaisance is the principle of propriety. The feeling of approving and disapproving is the principle of knowledge. Men have these four principles just as they have their four limbs." [Mencius 2A.6]

Book of Changes (Yi):
"The Image (Xiang) says: Fire above heaven—Great Possession (Dayou). Thus the superior man represses evil and promotes good, in obedience to the benevolent mandate of Heaven." [Hexagram 14, Dayou]
"The yielding is within, and the firm attains the central position." [Hexagram 37, Jiaren, Commentary on the Decision]
"Six at the beginning: For a mat, one uses white rushes; there is no blame. The Master said: If one simply places things on the ground, that would do…" [Hexagram 28, Daguo, and Great Commentary (Xici) I.8]

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
矣藉之用茅何咎之有慎之至也夫茅
之爲物薄而用可重也慎斯術也以往
其无所失矣
立人之道曰仁與義
書
禹曰都帝慎乃在位帝曰俞
惟王不邇聲色不殖貨利德懋懋官功懋
懋賞用人惟巳改過不吝克寛克仁彰
信兆民
===
曰皇極之敷言是彞是訓于帝其訓凡厥
庶民極之敷言是訓是行以近天子之
光曰天子作民父母以爲天下王
文王卑服卽康功田功徽柔懿恭懷保小
民惠鮮鰥寡自朝至于日中昃不遑暇
食用咸和萬民文王不敢盤于遊田以
庶邦惟正之供
詩
騏騮是中騧驪是驂
punctuated:
矣，藉之用茅，何咎之有？慎之至也。夫茅之爲物薄，而用可重也。慎斯術也以往，其无所失矣。
立人之道，曰仁與義。
書：
禹曰：「都！帝，慎乃在位。」帝曰：「俞。」
惟王不邇聲色，不殖貨利；德懋懋官，功懋懋賞；用人惟巳，改過不吝；克寛克仁，彰信兆民。
曰：皇極之敷言，是彞是訓，于帝其訓。凡厥庶民，極之敷言，是訓是行，以近天子之光，曰：「天子作民父母，以爲天下王。」
文王卑服，卽康功田功。徽柔懿恭，懷保小民，惠鮮鰥寡。自朝至于日中昃，不遑暇食，用咸和萬民。文王不敢盤于遊田，以庶邦惟正之供。
詩：
騏騮是中，騧驪是驂。
translation_en:
… [Simply placing them on the ground would suffice;] if one spreads white cogon grass beneath them, what fault can there be? This is the utmost of caution. Now, as an object, cogon grass is slight, yet its use can be of great weight. If one goes forward cautiously practicing this art, one will suffer no loss.”

They established the Way of Man, calling it benevolence and righteousness.

Book of Documents (Shu):

Yu said, “Alas! O Emperor, be cautious in the throne you occupy.” The Emperor said, “Yes.”

The king did not draw near to sensual music and women, nor did he amass goods and profit. Where virtue was great, he greatly rewarded it with office; where merit was great, he greatly rewarded it with prizes. He employed others as if their abilities were his own, and he was not reluctant to reform his faults. Capable of寬 (magnanimity) and benevolence, he manifested trustworthiness to the millions of the people.

It is said: This setting forth of words of the August Ultimate is the constant norm, is the instruction—indeed, it is the instruction of the Supreme Ruler. All the common people, taking these set-forth words of the Ultimate as their instruction and putting them into practice, thereby draw near to the glory of the Son of Heaven, saying, “The Son of Heaven acts as father and mother to the people, and thereby becomes sovereign of all under Heaven.”

King Wen wore humble attire and applied himself to the work of pacification and the work of agriculture. Admirable in his gentleness and piękny (exemplary) in his reverence, he cherished and protected the common people, and showed kindness to the destitute, widowers, and widows. From morning until midday and the sun’s decline, he had no leisure to eat, thereby bringing harmony to all the myriad people. King Wen did not dare to indulge in the pleasures of excursion and hunting, receiving from the various states only their regular tribute.

Book of Odes (Shi):

The dappled bays and red-maned bays are the inside pair; the yellow-mouthed blacks and pure blacks are the outside trace-horses.

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
彼交匪紓天子所予樂只君子天子命之
樂只君子福祿申之
瑟彼玉瓚黃流在中豈弟君子福祿攸降
鳶飛戾天魚躍于淵豈弟君子遐不作
人
嗟嗟臣工敬爾在公王釐爾成來咨來茹
春秋
三月鄭伯使宛來歸祊〔隱公八年〕
夏六月公會齊侯宋公陳侯鄭伯同盟于
===
幽〔莊公二十有七年〕六月公會宋公陳
侯衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯晉趙盾癸酉同
盟于新城〔文公十有四年〕
冬十月公會晉侯宋公衛侯鄭伯曹伯莒
子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子同圍齊
〔襄公十有八年〕公至自伐齊〔襄公十有〕
九年
宋公陳侯衛侯曹伯會晉師于棐林伐鄭
〔宣公元年〕公會晉師于瓦〔定公八年〕
punctuated:
彼交匪紓，天子所予。樂只君子，天子命之；樂只君子，福祿申之。
瑟彼玉瓚，黃流在中。豈弟君子，福祿攸降。鳶飛戾天，魚躍于淵。豈弟君子，遐不作人？
嗟嗟臣工，敬爾在公。王釐爾成，來咨來茹。
《春秋》：
三月，鄭伯使宛來歸祊〔隱公八年〕。
夏六月，公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、鄭伯同盟于幽〔莊公二十有七年〕。六月，公會宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯、晉趙盾，癸酉，同盟于新城〔文公十有四年〕。
冬十月，公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、鄭伯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子同圍齊〔襄公十有八年〕。公至自伐齊〔襄公十有〕九年。
宋公、陳侯、衛侯、曹伯會晉師于棐林，伐鄭〔宣公元年〕。公會晉師于瓦〔定公八年〕。
translation_en:
In their intercourse with one another there is no remissness; on them the Son of Heaven bestows his gifts. Happy be the noble lords! The Son of Heaven gives them his commands. Happy be the noble lords! Happiness and emoluments are renewed to them.
Brightly carved is that libation ladle of jade, with the yellow herbal wine within it. Easy and self-possessed is our prince, on whom happiness and dignity descend. The hawk flies up to heaven; the fishes leap in the deep. Easy and self-possessed is our prince—how does he not rouse men to virtue?
Ah! you ministers and officers, be reverent in your public duties. The king has given you perfect rules; come and consult, come and deliberate.
Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu):
In the third month, the Earl of Zheng sent Wan to come and surrender Beng [8th year of Duke Yin].
In summer, in the sixth month, the Duke met the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, and the Earl of Zheng, and together they made a covenant at You [27th year of Duke Zhuang]. In the sixth month, the Duke met the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the Earl of Cao, and Zhao Dun of Jin; on the guiyou day, together they made a covenant at Xincheng [14th year of Duke Wen].
In winter, in the tenth month, the Duke met the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, and the Viscount of Little Zhu, and together they besieged Qi [18th year of Duke Xiang]. The Duke arrived back from attacking Qi [19th year of Duke Xiang].
The Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, and the Earl of Cao met the army of Jin at Feilin and attacked Zheng [1st year of Duke Xuan]. The Duke met the army of Jin at Wa [8th year of Duke Ding].

詐爲制書
第叁場
策五道
===
問祀典莫大乎
郊自昔帝王皆隆之乃禮家之指則犂然殊云
主合祀者本虞書肆類之文主分祀者
宗周禮司樂之制孰爲得歟漢氏而降
分合之議紛如不一所遵用者孰多歟
尊祖祀天之禮有奉始祖者有奉受命
之君者有天帝各配者有祖宗竝配者
將何所折衷乎洪惟我
太祖高皇帝初定天下即建
punctuated:
雝肅殿箴表

判語五條：
官員襲廕；
舶商匿貨；
御賜衣物；
行宮營門；
詐爲制書。

第叁場

策五道

問：祀典莫大乎郊，自昔帝王皆隆之，乃禮家之指，則犂然殊云。主合祀者，本《虞書》肆類之文；主分祀者，宗《周禮》司樂之制。孰爲得歟？漢氏而降，分合之議，紛如不一，所遵用者孰多歟？尊祖祀天之禮，有奉始祖者，有奉受命之君者，有天帝各配者，有祖宗竝配者，將何所折衷乎？洪惟我太祖高皇帝初定天下，即建

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
南北郊分祀
天地後乃改而合祀
列聖祗循百六十餘年至
世宗肅皇帝又改而分祀當時議禮之臣固壹
以周禮爲準果盡符合否
國家自
仁廟而後皆奉
太祖及
文皇帝配
===
天而嘉靖間始獨以
太祖配有其舉之一朝而更又何所見歟我
皇上寅御大寶肇舉
郊禋輔臣恭
進圖說典章沿革考據明悉至欲復
合祀
竝配之舊眞善體
世宗之心以光
太祖之定制
punctuated: 南北郊，分祀天地，後乃改而合祀。列聖祗循百六十餘年，至世宗肅皇帝又改而分祀。當時議禮之臣，固壹以《周禮》爲準，果盡符合否？國家自仁廟而後，皆奉太祖及文皇帝配天，而嘉靖間始獨以太祖配。有其舉之，一朝而更，又何所見歟？我皇上寅御大寶，肇舉郊禋，輔臣恭進《圖說》，典章沿革，考據明悉。至欲復合祀、竝配之舊，眞善體世宗之心，以光太祖之定制…
translation_en: … the Southern and Northern Suburbs to offer separate sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, and later changed this to a joint sacrifice. Successive emperors reverently followed this practice for more than a hundred and sixty years, until Emperor Shizong Su (the Jiajing Emperor) again changed it back to separate sacrifices. The ministers who deliberated on ritual at that time took the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) as their sole standard—did this truly conform to it in every respect? Since the reign of Emperor Renzong (the Hongxi Emperor), the dynasty had consistently honored both Taizu (the Hongwu Emperor) and Emperor Wen (the Yongle Emperor) as coadjutors in the sacrifice to Heaven, yet during the Jiajing era Taizu alone came to be honored as coadjutor. Once such a rite had been instituted, on what grounds was it altered in a single morning? When His Majesty reverently ascended the great throne and first performed the suburban sacrifice, the Grand Secretaries respectfully presented the Illustrated Explanations (Tushuo), in which the historical evolution of the institutions and statutes was examined clearly and thoroughly. As for their desire to restore the former practice of joint sacrifice and dual coadjutors, they truly understood well the mind of Shizong and thereby brought glory to the established system of Taizu…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
觀者夫獨是莫曉獨非莫知此古人所
以論律曆也今之司其事者將無狃於
是說與萬一訛舛有甚於斯者可漫爾
不爲之計與夫法久則凱凱則必飭諸
士試陳所以振飭之術詳著于篇俟執
事者採焉
問學莫大乎與人同善夫與人同善斯兼
善矣舜自耕稼以至帝天下皆用此道
也而孟氏乃曰窮則獨善達則兼善窮
===
與達果二施歟伯夷柳下惠所遭遇不
可謂達矣乃其風能使百世與起焉要
非止於獨善者孟氏顧猶少之而願學
孔子其所以異者安在孔子生春秋寧
削跡絕糧而不忍於忘世洙泗之濱羣
弟子蓋三千焉其汲汲於兼善如此豈
顧不安於窮歟伊尹身任天下之重謂
之兼善宜也迺顏子終身陋巷耳孟氏
至稱其賢與禹稷竝其所以同者又安
punctuated:
觀者。夫「獨是莫曉，獨非莫知」，此古人所以論律曆也。今之司其事者，將無狃於是說與？萬一訛舛有甚於斯者，可漫爾不爲之計與？夫法久則凱，凱則必飭。諸士試陳所以振飭之術，詳著于篇，俟執事者採焉。

問：學莫大乎與人同善。夫與人同善，斯兼善矣。舜自耕稼以至帝天下，皆用此道也。而孟氏乃曰：「窮則獨善，達則兼善。」窮與達果二施歟？伯夷、柳下惠所遭遇，不可謂達矣，乃其風能使百世與起焉，要非止於獨善者；孟氏顧猶少之，而願學孔子，其所以異者安在？孔子生春秋，寧削跡、絕糧，而不忍於忘世，洙泗之濱，羣弟子蓋三千焉；其汲汲於兼善如此，豈顧不安於窮歟？伊尹身任天下之重，謂之兼善，宜也；迺顏子終身陋巷耳，孟氏至稱其賢與禹、稷竝，其所以同者又安
translation_en:
…observers. Now, "when one alone is right, no one understands; when one alone is wrong, no one knows"—this was how the ancients discussed pitch-pipes and the calendar. Are those in charge of the matter today not perhaps accustomed to this argument? If by some chance errors and discrepancies become even worse than these, can we carelessly fail to make plans for them? When a system has lasted a long time, it deteriorates [凱, OCR for 敝?], and when it deteriorates, it must be rectified. Let you gentlemen try to set forth the arts for reviving and rectifying it, writing them out in detail in your essays, to await selection by the authorities in charge.

Question: In learning, nothing is greater than sharing goodness with others. Now, to share goodness with others is to cultivate goodness for all together (jianshan 兼善). From the time Shun 舜 plowed and sowed until he ruled all under Heaven as Emperor, he always used this Way. Yet Mencius (Mengshi 孟氏) said: "In obscurity, cultivate goodness in oneself alone (dushan 獨善); in prominence, cultivate goodness for all together." Are obscurity and prominence truly two different applications? What Boyi 伯夷 and Liuxia Hui 柳下惠 encountered in their lives cannot be called prominence, yet their moral influence could inspire a hundred generations to rise up [與, OCR for 興?]—in sum, they did not stop at cultivating goodness in themselves alone. Yet Mencius still thought them insufficient, and wished instead to learn from Confucius (Kongzi 孔子); wherein lies the difference? Confucius was born in the Spring and Autumn period; he would rather have his footprints erased in Wei and run out of food in Chen than bear to forget the world, and on the banks of the Zhu 洙 and Si 泗 rivers, his assembled disciples numbered some three thousand. Being so tirelessly eager to cultivate goodness for all together, was he after all not content in obscurity? Yi Yin 伊尹 personally took upon himself the heavy burden of all under Heaven; to call this cultivating goodness for all together is fitting. Yet Master Yan (Yanzi 顏子) spent his whole life in a mean alley, and still Mencius praised his worthiness and placed him alongside Yu 禹 and Ji 稷; wherein lies their similarity…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
在楊氏爲我以忘世爲高而孟氏斥之
猶易辨也墨翟之名至與孔子並稱彼
其說主於兼相愛交相利則與兼善又
何以異且當其時異端之說紛紛矣孟
氏顧不此之攻而惟楊墨之深闢抑又
何歟夫學術之辨不明則趨嚮不正似
是之防有不得不嚴者爾諸士皆以兼
善來也幸相與殫其說主司將以是徵
所養焉
===
問今用人之要以治郡邑在吏以靖疆圉
在將昔人傳循吏者惟曰經術潤飾乃
謀置帥者必先禮樂詩書無亦以士之
明經爲國家用而用莫急於茲二者歟
而或謂人之材情運量固有不能盡同
焉則又安所爲倚也試即漢世數人相
與評之立學成都者齊魯比風平盜渤
海者刀劒易俗子視密人者下詔褒名
德理中牟者按掾推異斯皆明經吏也
punctuated:
在？楊氏爲我，以忘世爲高，而孟氏斥之，猶易辨也；墨翟之名，至與孔子並稱，彼其說主於兼相愛、交相利，則與兼善又何以異？且當其時，異端之說紛紛矣，孟氏顧不此之攻，而惟楊、墨之深闢，抑又何歟？夫學術之辨不明，則趨嚮不正，似是之防有不得不嚴者。爾諸士皆以兼善來也，幸相與殫其說，主司將以是徵所養焉。
問：今用人之要，以治郡邑在吏，以靖疆圉在將。昔人傳循吏者，惟曰經術潤飾；乃謀置帥者，必先禮、樂、詩、書。無亦以士之明經爲國家用，而用莫急於茲二者歟？而或謂人之材情運量，固有不能盡同焉，則又安所爲倚也？試即漢世數人相與評之：立學成都者，齊、魯比風；平盜渤海者，刀劒易俗；子視密人者，下詔褒名；德理中牟者，按掾推異。斯皆明經吏也，
translation_en:
… does that lie? Yang Zhu (楊氏) advocated acting for oneself, treating the forgetting of the world as lofty, and when Mencius rejected him, that was still easy to discern. Yet the name of Mo Di (墨翟) was even paired with that of Confucius; since his doctrine centered on universal mutual love and reciprocal benefit, how then did it differ from "bringing goodness to the whole world" (jianshan 兼善)? Moreover, in that era, heterodox doctrines were springing up in profusion; why did Mencius not attack those others, instead deeply refuting only Yang and Mo? Indeed, if the distinction in scholarly learning is not made clear, one's orientation will not be upright, and the defense against what is speciously right cannot but be strict. All of you scholars have come here with the aim of bringing goodness to the whole world; please set forth your views in full, for the Examiners will use this to gauge what you have cultivated.

Question: Today, the essentials of employing men lie in civil officials for governing commanderies and districts, and in generals for pacifying the frontiers. When people of the past wrote biographies of upright officials, they said only that they adorned their governance with classical statecraft; and when deliberating on appointing a commander, one always prioritized the Rites, Music, Odes, and Documents. Is this not because scholars who understand the Classics are of service to the state, and no service is more urgent than these two? Yet some say that men's talents, dispositions, and capacities cannot all be entirely the same—then on what can one rely? Let us evaluate together several men of the Han dynasty: he who established schools in Chengdu [Wen Weng 文翁] made its customs comparable to Qi and Lu; he who pacified bandits in Bohai [Gong Sui 龔遂] transformed habits so swords and knives were traded for farm tools; he who regarded the people of Mi County as his children [Zhuo Mao 卓茂] had an imperial decree issued in praise of his name; and he who governed Zhongmou through virtue [Lu Gong 魯恭] was commended as extraordinary by the investigating clerk. These were all officials who understood the Classics, …

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
而以斵竄虎穴爲能者何亦與之竝其
稱歟矯制徵兵者郅支授首持節傳諭
者莎車就戮大樹著號者立破赤眉北
道可主者卒降劇虜斯皆明經將也他
若抜於亡卒人奴者亦赫然成功何歟
我
朝設文武科羅天下俊傑而又參之以貢舉
之途騎射之技宜其得人斌斌盛矣而
緩急之際猶未盡適於用者其故何也
===
夫天下未嘗無才計
國家每進之士不啻什伯漢世乃事業聲稱
則少遜焉豈責實者容有未至歟今欲
吏咸加理將不失職以其成清寧悠遠
之治則何道而可
問水之大而爲中國患者莫如河則治河
之役宜急今日之務也乃往往屈羣策
卒未聞以一奇見者何哉昔者禹抑洪
水用乂諸夏詩書所稱於今爲烈焉其
punctuated:
而以斵竄虎穴爲能者，何亦與之竝其稱歟？矯制徵兵者，郅支授首；持節傳諭者，莎車就戮；大樹著號者，立破赤眉；北道可主者，卒降劇虜：斯皆明經將也。他若抜於亡卒、人奴者，亦赫然成功，何歟？我朝設文武科，羅天下俊傑，而又參之以貢舉之途、騎射之技，宜其得人斌斌盛矣，而緩急之際猶未盡適於用者，其故何也？夫天下未嘗無才，計國家每進之士，不啻什伯漢世，乃事業聲稱則少遜焉，豈責實者容有未至歟？今欲吏咸加理，將不失職，以其成清寧悠遠之治，則何道而可？

問：水之大而爲中國患者，莫如河，則治河之役，宜急今日之務也。乃往往屈羣策，卒未聞以一奇見者，何哉？昔者禹抑洪水，用乂諸夏，《詩》《書》所稱，於今爲烈焉。其
translation_en:
…Yet how is it that one whose skill lay in hacking down and routing the bandits in their “tiger’s den” [Yin Shang 尹賞] also shared equal renown with them? One who forged an imperial decree to mobilize troops took the head of Zhizhi [Chen Tang 陳湯]; one who held the imperial credentials to proclaim an edict brought the king of Yarkand (Suoju 莎車) to execution [Feng Fengshi 馮奉世]; one known by the sobriquet “Big Tree” immediately crushed the Red Eyebrows [Feng Yi 馮異]; and one who could serve as host on the northern road ultimately forced ferocious marauders to surrender [Kou Xun 寇恂]—all of these were generals well-versed in the Classics. Yet why is it that others, such as those raised up from among runaway soldiers [Ying Bu 英布 / Han Xin 韓信] or bondservants [Wei Qing 衛青], also achieved illustrious success? Our Dynasty has established civil and military examination categories to net the outstanding talents of the empire, and has further supplemented them with the avenues of tribute recommendation and the skills of horsemanship and archery. It ought to be that the men obtained are flourishing in refined abundance; yet in times of crisis they are still not entirely suited for practical use—what is the reason for this? Now, the empire has never lacked talent. Counting the scholars advanced by the State on each occasion, they are not merely ten or a hundred times those of the Han era; yet their accomplishments and reputations are somewhat inferior. Could it be that our exigir of practical results perhaps falls short? If today we wish for civil officials all to promote good governance and for generals not to fail in their duties, so as thereby to achieve an era of pure peace and enduring order, by what way may this be accomplished?

Question: Among great waters that pose a menace to China, none compares to the Yellow River; thus the labor of regulating the River ought to be an urgent task among today’s affairs. Yet why is it that it so often exhausts the collective plans of all, and in the end we have not heard of anyone distinguishing himself with a single extraordinary strategy? In antiquity, Yu 禹 curbed the floodwaters and thereby brought order to the Chinese states; what is praised in the Book of Odes (Shi 詩) and the Book of Documents (Shu 書) remains illustrious to this day. Can his…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
故法可參綜而行之歟嗣後議者紛紛
總之不離塞與不塞兩說將技止此矣
抑或有一道而見偶未之及歟河自砱
礫旣徙惟西京受害特甚當文武盛時
則力主於塞其效蓋有可覩者豈塞猶
愈於不塞歟夫法與時宜利因勢導揆
今時勢謀於塞不塞間而用之果孰爲
便歟比歲河決不治致厪
上慮特爲置督府使董其事唯是
===
聖德格
天百靈效職業已漸底于績矣然思患貴防於
初作事當善其後乃議者或謂黃河之
故道宜復或謂宜別開一河以備非常
是歟否歟茲欲於斯二者外別求所謂
萬全長策焉
國計民生永賴之也則將安出歟往代嘗博
徵能浚治者莫有應書執事者羞之爾
諸士抱業而來寧無有槪於中耶其各
punctuated: 故法可參綜而行之歟？嗣後議者紛紛，總之不離塞與不塞兩說。將技止此矣，抑或有一道而見偶未之及歟？河自砱礫旣徙，惟西京受害特甚，當文、武盛時，則力主於塞，其效蓋有可覩者。豈塞猶愈於不塞歟？夫法與時宜，利因勢導，揆今時勢，謀於塞、不塞間而用之，果孰爲便歟？比歲河決不治，致厪上慮，特爲置督府，使董其事。唯是聖德格天，百靈效職，業已漸底于績矣。然思患貴防於初，作事當善其後，乃議者或謂黃河之故道宜復，或謂宜別開一河以備非常，是歟？否歟？茲欲於斯二者外，別求所謂萬全長策焉，國計民生永賴之也，則將安出歟？往代嘗博徵能浚治者，莫有應書，執事者羞之。爾諸士抱業而來，寧無有槪於中耶？其各
translation_en: …old methods be consulted, synthesized, and put into practice? Thereafter, commentators have offered a multitude of opinions, which, in sum, do not depart from the two theories of blocking or not blocking the river. Does the art of river control stop at this, or is there another way that people's views have happened not to reach? After the Yellow River shifted course from Lili [Suge], the Western Han era suffered particularly severe harm; during the flourishing reigns of Emperors Wen and Wu, they strongly advocated blocking the breaches, and the results were indeed visible. Could it be that blocking is still better than not blocking? Now, methods should suit the times, and benefits should be guided according to the circumstances. Judging by present times and circumstances, if we deliberate between blocking and not blocking and apply one of them, which would truly be more advantageous? In recent years, the breaches of the Yellow River have gone uncontrolled, causing concern to His Majesty, who specially established a Supreme Commander's Office to direct the matter. Only because His Sacred Virtue reaches Heaven and the hundred spirits perform their duties has the work already gradually come to fruition. Yet in contemplating disasters, one values guarding against them at the outset, and in undertaking affairs, one must properly manage their aftermath. Now, some commentators say that the old course of the Yellow River should be restored, while others say that another channel should be opened separately to prepare against extraordinary emergencies—are they right or wrong? If we now wish to seek, beyond these two options, a so-called thoroughly sound and long-term strategy upon which the state finances and the people's livelihood may permanently rely, from where shall it come? In former dynasties, when the court broadly summoned those capable of dredging and controlling the river, no one answered the call, to the shame of those in charge of affairs. You gentlemen have come here cherishing your learning—could you have no deeply felt views within yourselves? Let each of you…
