title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
之戒舜之首聞於堯者然也玆命禹以之而造
虞者因爲啓夏之謨上奉神明之依天意固有
攸歸矣乃命以祈天之本不過即放勳之咨者
一吖嚀焉道雖始於堯而其傳固在舜也下撫
有衆之戴人心固有攸屬矣乃命以安人之要
不過即文祖之受者一重申焉道雖託之禹而
其責實在舜也是非不能易也帝王大經大法
本於是堯可語舜舜不可語禹乎亦非不敢加
也天下萬事萬物原於是舜可紹堯禹不可紹
舜乎由是禹起而光大之千聖相傳之法不亦
===
衍於無窮哉吁此三聖相授而守一道也與嘗
論中者天命也執其中者天心也命同則心同
而舜益以微危精一云者何哉堯舜心與天一
而克勤克儉不矜不伐非人道幾希間乎乃精
一交致蓋執焉者事也故曰禹見而知之至是
而禹亦堯舜矣亦天矣誰謂入聖域而未優
□□□凡事豫則立不豫則廢言前定則不跲事
□□□前定則不困行前定則不疚道前定則
punctuated:
之戒，舜之首聞於堯者然也。玆命禹以之，而造虞者因爲啓夏之謨。上奉神明之依，天意固有攸歸矣，乃命以祈天之本，不過即放勳之咨者一吖嚀焉，道雖始於堯，而其傳固在舜也；下撫有衆之戴，人心固有攸屬矣，乃命以安人之要，不過即文祖之受者一重申焉，道雖託之禹，而其責實在舜也。是非不能易也，帝王大經大法本於是，堯可語舜，舜不可語禹乎？亦非不敢加也，天下萬事萬物原於是，舜可紹堯，禹不可紹舜乎？由是禹起而光大之，千聖相傳之法，不亦衍於無窮哉！吁！此三聖相授而守一道也與！嘗論中者，天命也；執其中者，天心也。命同則心同，而舜益以「微危精一」云者，何哉？堯、舜心與天一，而「克勤克儉，不矜不伐」，非人道幾希間乎？乃精一交致，蓋執焉者事也。故曰「禹見而知之」。至是而禹亦堯、舜矣，亦天矣，誰謂入聖域而未優□□□？

凡事豫則立，不豫則廢。言前定則不跲，事□□□前定則不困，行前定則不疚，道前定則
translation_en:
… admonition; such was what Shun 舜 first heard from Yao 堯. Now in charging Yu 禹 with this, that which established the house of Yu 虞 thereby became the plan that inaugurated the house of Xia 夏. Above, he upheld the reliance of the divine spirits, for the will of Heaven indeed had a place to which it turned; thus, in charging him with the fundamental principle for praying to Heaven, he did nothing more than reiterate with earnest injunctions [吖嚀, sc. 叮嚀] what Fangxun 放勳 [Yao] had proclaimed in his charge—although the Way began with Yao, its transmission indeed rested with Shun. Below, he comforted the allegiance of the multitude, for the hearts of the people indeed had a place to which they belonged; thus, in charging him with the essential principle for bringing peace to the people, he did nothing more than repeat anew what had been received in the Temple of the Cultured Ancestor (Wenzu 文祖)—although the Way was entrusted to Yu, the responsibility for it truly lay with Shun.

This is not because he was unable to alter it: the great standards and great laws of emperors and kings are rooted in this; if Yao could speak of it to Shun, could Shun not speak of it to Yu? Nor is it because he did not dare to add to it: the myriad affairs and myriad things of the world originate in this; if Shun could continue Yao, could Yu not continue Shun? From this, Yu arose and gloriously magnified it; would not the method transmitted through a thousand sages thus be extended无穷 without end! Ah! Is this not how the Three Sages handed it down to one another and guarded a single Way?

One may consider that the Mean (zhong 中) is the Mandate of Heaven, and holding fast to the Mean is the mind of Heaven. Where the Mandate is the same, the mind is the same; why then did Shun add the words about being "subtle and perilous, refined and single-minded"? The minds of Yao and Shun were one with Heaven, yet Yu's being "able to be diligent and able to be frugal, not boastful and not bragging"—was this not within the slight margin between the human mind and the mind of the Way? Thus, applying both refinement and single-mindedness together was a matter of how one holds fast to it. Therefore it is said, "Yu saw it and knew it." At this point, Yu too was Yao and Shun, and was Heaven as well; who would say that he had entered the realm of the sages and yet was not amply [?]…

"In all things, if there is preparation, they will succeed; if there is no preparation, they will fail. If words are determined beforehand, there will be no stumbling; if affairs [?] are determined beforehand, there will be no distress; if actions are determined beforehand, there will be no regret; if the Way is determined beforehand, there will be…"

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
不窮在下位不獲乎上民不可得而治
矣獲乎上有道不信乎朋友不獲乎上
矣信乎朋友有道不順乎親不信乎朋
友矣順乎親有道反諸身不誠不順乎
親矣誠身有道不明乎善不誠乎身矣
甯瑞鯉
同考試官教諭李　批〔簡練直確非〕〔邃養者不能到〕
同考試官教諭潘　批〔體裁純正而〕〔詞復典雅可式〕
考試官侍讀羅　批〔明順〕
考試官右中允高　批〔豫定意善發〕
===
中庸究言事之當豫而益推明其意焉夫豫之
於事也尚矣由言事行道及在下位推之而事
之當豫不益明乎中庸若曰天下無常事吾心
有常誠亦存乎豫而已何則自達道達德以至
九經之屬凡事也凡誠之所行也唯勿二勿三
素豫吾內則事以有本而立有不爲爲斯成矣
使一時一事襲取於外則事以無本而廢有不
動動斯僨矣何以明其然也出身加民之謂言
punctuated:
不窮。在下位不獲乎上，民不可得而治矣；獲乎上有道，不信乎朋友，不獲乎上矣；信乎朋友有道，不順乎親，不信乎朋友矣；順乎親有道，反諸身不誠，不順乎親矣；誠身有道，不明乎善，不誠乎身矣。

甯瑞鯉

同考試官教諭李　批：〔簡練直確，非〕〔邃養者不能到。〕
同考試官教諭潘　批：〔體裁純正，而〕〔詞復典雅可式。〕
考試官侍讀羅　批：〔明順。〕
考試官右中允高　批：〔豫定意善發。〕

《中庸》究言事之當豫，而益推明其意焉。夫豫之於事也，尚矣。由言、事、行、道及在下位推之，而事之當豫，不益明乎？《中庸》若曰：天下無常事，吾心有常誠，亦存乎豫而已。何則？自達道、達德以至九經之屬，凡事也，凡誠之所行也。唯勿二勿三，素豫吾內，則事以有本而立，有不爲，爲斯成矣；使一時一事襲取於外，則事以無本而廢，有不動，動斯僨矣。何以明其然也？出身加民之謂言，
translation_en:
… will not be exhausted.

"When one is in a subordinate position and does not win the confidence of his superior, the common people cannot be governed. There is a Way to win the confidence of one's superior: if one is not trusted by one's friends, one will not win the confidence of one's superior. There is a Way to be trusted by one's friends: if one is not obedient to one's parents, one will not be trusted by one's friends. There is a Way to be obedient to one's parents: if upon examining oneself one is not sincere, one will not be obedient to one's parents. There is a Way to make oneself sincere: if one does not understand what is good, one will not make oneself sincere."

Ning Ruili 甯瑞鯉

Associate Examiner, Instructor Li, comments: Concise, polished, direct, and precise; none without profound cultivation could attain this.
Associate Examiner, Instructor Pan, comments: The form and style are pure and correct, and the diction is moreover refined and elegant, worthy of serving as a model.
Examiner, Hanlin Reader-in-waiting Luo, comments: Clear and smooth.
Examiner, Right Companion to the Heir Apparent Gao, comments: The meaning of prior determination is well developed.

The Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) thoroughly discusses how affairs ought to be prepared for in advance, and further extends and clarifies this meaning. Indeed, advance preparation in affairs is of the highest importance! Extending the principle from words, affairs, conduct, and the Way down to being in a subordinate position, does it not become all the clearer that affairs ought to be prepared for in advance? It is as if the Doctrine of the Mean were saying: In the world there are no fixed affairs, yet in our minds there is a constant sincerity, which simply resides in advance preparation and nothing more. Why is this? From the universal ways (dadao) and universal virtues (dade) all the way to the nine standard rules (jiujing) and the like, all are affairs, and all are that by which sincerity is put into practice. Only when, without duplicity or wavering, we have long prepared within ourselves, will affairs be established through having a root; there may be things we do not undertake, but once undertaken, they are accomplished. If at a given moment or in a given affair we merely seize upon things externally, then affairs will fail for lack of a root; there may be times we do not act, but once we act, they are ruined. How can we make it clear that this is so? That which issues from one's person and reaches the people is called words, …

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
而措諸天下者事事也必前定焉則言無不順而
事以時舉也不然跲且困隨之矣發邇見遠之
謂行而率諸吾性者道也必前定焉則行無不
慊而道以時出也不然疚且窮隨之矣斯非獨
居上然也至在下位未甞不欲治其民者然能
治民未甞不先獲乎上者以獲上道在信友非
信而譽命弗逮矣以信友道在順親非順而志
行弗孚矣順親之道誠身其本也不誠未有能
順者也誠身之道明善其要也不明未有能誠
===
者也蓋自治民而推極於身則無不豫必誠身
而達順於治斯無不立下位且然況凡事耶信
乎誠而不豫猶爲無誠而道德九經悉妄也已
豫之義大矣哉而君人者可以思矣抑此聖學
也文之緝熈武之敬義胥此焉在故當其時道
德純明而周官之法度燦然大備無廢而不立
者矣不然雖周禮具文耳而豫可弗講耶豫之
何如曰明善誠身無上下一也
惻隱之心仁之端也羞惡之心義之端也
punctuated:
而措諸天下者，事事也；必前定焉，則言無不順而事以時舉也，不然，跲且困隨之矣。發邇見遠之謂行，而率諸吾性者，道也；必前定焉，則行無不慊而道以時出也，不然，疚且窮隨之矣。斯非獨居上然也，至在下位，未甞不欲治其民者，然能治民，未甞不先獲乎上者。以獲上，道在信友，非信而譽命弗逮矣；以信友，道在順親，非順而志行弗孚矣。順親之道，誠身其本也，不誠未有能順者也；誠身之道，明善其要也，不明未有能誠者也。蓋自治民而推極於身，則無不豫；必誠身而達順於治，斯無不立。下位且然，況凡事耶？信乎誠而不豫，猶爲無誠，而道德、九經悉妄也已。豫之義大矣哉！而君人者可以思矣。抑此聖學也，文之緝熈、武之敬義，胥此焉在。故當其時，道德純明，而《周官》之法度燦然大備，無廢而不立者矣。不然，雖《周禮》具文耳，而豫可弗講耶？豫之何如？曰：明善誠身，無上下一也。

「惻隱之心，仁之端也；羞惡之心，義之端也；
translation_en:
…and what is put into practice throughout the empire is business [or affairs; reading 事事 as a dittographic printing of 事]. When these are determined beforehand, words will never fail to be smooth and affairs will be carried out at the proper time; otherwise, stumbling and distress will follow right behind. What issues forth nearby and is seen afar is called conduct, and what follows from our nature is the Way. When these are determined beforehand, conduct will never fail to bring satisfaction and the Way will come forth at the proper time; otherwise, remorse and exhaustion will follow right behind. This is not only true for those who occupy high positions. Even among those in subordinate positions, there is no one who does not wish to govern the people well; yet to be able to govern the people, there is no one who does not first win the confidence of the sovereign. To win the confidence of the sovereign, the way lies in being trusted by one's friends—without trust, reputation and appointment will not reach one. To be trusted by one's friends, the way lies in being obedient to one's parents—without obedience, one's intentions and conduct will not inspire confidence. In the way of obeying one's parents, making one's own person sincere is the root; without sincerity, no one has ever been able to be obedient. In the way of making one's own person sincere, understanding the good is the essential point; without understanding, no one has ever been able to be sincere. Thus, when one traces back from governing the people all the way to one's own person, there is nothing that does not require preparation beforehand; only when one makes one's person sincere and extends obedience all the way to governance will there be nothing that is not established. If this is true even for those in subordinate positions, how much more so for all affairs in general! Truly, sincerity without prior preparation is no different from having no sincerity at all, and the universal Way, the universal virtues, and the nine standard rules would all be reduced to falsehood. Great indeed is the meaning of preparation beforehand! He who rules over men may well ponder this. Moreover, this is the learning of the sages: King Wen's continuous bright敬 [reverence] and King Wu's reverence and righteousness both resided right here. Therefore, in their age, the Way and virtue were pure and illustrious, and the laws and institutions of the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan) were brilliantly and completely provided, with nothing neglected or left unestablished. Otherwise, even the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) would be mere empty text—so how could one fail to study preparation beforehand? And how does one prepare beforehand? One says: Understanding the good and making one's person sincere are one and the same for both superior and inferior alike.

"The feeling of commiseration is the beginning of benevolence; the feeling of shame and dislike is the beginning of righteousness; …"

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
人者豈無仁義之心哉仁必有惻隱義必有羞
惡是惟無感感斯通矣豈無禮智之心哉禮必
有辭讓智必有是非是惟無觸觸斯應矣非獨
先王爲然也苟未至物欲陷溺者皆有之四端
充足於心不猶四體各足於身乎非獨乍見爲
然也苟未至旦晝牿亡者皆有之四端具而爲
人不猶四體備而成形乎夫使四端非人之所
有是必不出於性者也焉有情而離性乎哉雖
然良心人固同具而聖凡卒至相遠者何耶蓋
心體雖大而其端實微先王有之而天下運掌
者察而充也衆人有之而自賊與賊人者弗察
而充也他日破三品之說復致詳焉而乃歸于
不能盡其才噫有才而不盡伊誰之咎與
===
易
象曰火在天上大有君子以遏惡揚善順
天休命
陸大成
同考試官訓導郭　批〔古雅精純說作有自更爲□〕
punctuated:
人者，豈無仁義之心哉？仁必有惻隱，義必有羞惡，是惟無感，感斯通矣。豈無禮智之心哉？禮必有辭讓，智必有是非，是惟無觸，觸斯應矣。非獨先王爲然也，苟未至物欲陷溺者，皆有之。四端充足於心，不猶四體各足於身乎？非獨乍見爲然也，苟未至旦晝牿亡者，皆有之。四端具而爲人，不猶四體備而成形乎？夫使四端非人之所有，是必不出於性者也，焉有情而離性乎哉？雖然，良心人固同具，而聖凡卒至相遠者，何耶？蓋心體雖大，而其端實微。先王有之，而天下運掌者，察而充也；衆人有之，而自賊與賊人者，弗察而充也。他日破三品之說，復致詳焉，而乃歸于不能盡其才。噫！有才而不盡，伊誰之咎與？

易
象曰：「火在天上，大有；君子以遏惡揚善，順天休命。」
陸大成
同考試官訓導郭　批〔古雅精純，說作有自，更爲□〕
translation_en:
… As for human beings, how could they lack minds of benevolence and righteousness? Benevolence necessarily involves a feeling of commiseration, and righteousness necessarily involves a feeling of shame and dislike; only when nothing stirs them do they remain dormant, for once stirred, they flow forth. How could they lack minds of propriety and wisdom? Propriety necessarily involves a feeling of modesty and deference, and wisdom necessarily involves a sense of right and wrong; only when nothing touches them do they remain still, for once touched, they respond. It was not only the Former Kings who were thus; anyone who has not yet been drowned by material desires possesses them. The Four Beginnings being fully present in the mind—is this not just like the four limbs each being complete on the body? It is not only at a sudden sight that this is so; anyone who has not yet had their innate goodness fettered and destroyed by the actions of the day possesses them. Having the Four Beginnings complete in order to be a human being—is this not just like having the four limbs complete in order to form a physical body? Now, suppose the Four Beginnings were not intrinsic to human beings; then they would necessarily not issue from human nature. How could there be feelings that are severed from nature? Even so, the innate good mind is certainly shared by all people alike; why is it, then, that sages and ordinary people ultimately end up so far apart? It is because although the substance of the mind is great, its beginnings are in fact subtle. That the Former Kings possessed them and could turn the world in the palms of their hands was because they discerned and extended them; that the multitude possess them and yet harm themselves and harm others is because they fail to discern and extend them. On another day, when refuting the theory of the three grades of human nature, Mencius again elaborated on this in detail, and attributed the difference to an inability to fully develop one's natural capacities. Alas! To possess such capacities and yet fail to develop them fully—whose fault is that?

Book of Changes (Yi)
The Commentary on the Images (Xiang) says: "Fire above heaven: Great Possession (Dayou). The noble man, in accordance with this, represses evil and promotes good, and so obeys the beneficent mandate of Heaven."
Lu Dacheng 陸大成
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Guo 郭: 〔Classic in elegance, refined and pure; his explanation and composition have a solid foundation, and furthermore [?]…〕

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
耀焉蓋帝心所簡吾順而顯庸之耳而寧有一
毫作好以奸其命耶威福之柄擅之我而不僭
不濫聰明之實憲乎天而克類克君此君子所
以命自我出而求孚于休也使賞罰滋章而賢
否倒置逆天甚矣而能必纍棄之不萌哉呼治
有者可觀象於斯矣抑有本焉吾心之天洞若
觀火善惡消長之際而天命之逆順决矣此危
微精一之訓所以尤諄諄於帝舜也不然當紹
堯之治天下之有大矣而四凶之誅十六族之
舉何遽而能以服天下耶故曰有天德然後可
語王道信夫
===
立人之道曰仁與義
曹良貴
同考試官訓導郭　批〔說理精詳措辭溫雅〕
同考試官訓導張　批〔以心學發性命之奧明盡可式〕
同考試官教諭范　批〔渾融精潔非深養者不能作〕
考試官侍讀羅　批〔典實不浮〕
考試官右中允高　批〔潔淨雅稱易義〕
punctuated:
耀焉。蓋帝心所簡，吾順而顯庸之耳，而寧有一毫作好以奸其命耶？威福之柄擅之我，而不僭不濫；聰明之實憲乎天，而克類克君。此君子所以命自我出，而求孚于休也。使賞罰滋章而賢否倒置，逆天甚矣，而能必纍棄之不萌哉？呼！治有者可觀象於斯矣。抑有本焉。吾心之天洞若觀火，善惡消長之際，而天命之逆順决矣。此危微精一之訓，所以尤諄諄於帝舜也。不然，當紹堯之治，天下之有大矣，而四凶之誅、十六族之舉，何遽而能以服天下耶？故曰：「有天德，然後可語王道。」信夫！

立人之道，曰仁與義。
曹良貴
同考試官訓導郭批：〔說理精詳，措辭溫雅。〕
同考試官訓導張批：〔以心學發性命之奧，明盡可式。〕
同考試官教諭范批：〔渾融精潔，非深養者不能作。〕
考試官侍讀羅批：〔典實不浮。〕
考試官右中允高批：〔潔淨，雅稱易義。〕
translation_en:
…shine forth brightly. For those whom the Supreme Ruler's mind has selected, we simply follow along and openly employ them; how could there be the slightest personal偏 predilection ("making of fondness") to violate His mandate? The handle of awe and blessing is wielded by us, yet without usurpation or excess; the reality of clear hearing and vision is modeled upon Heaven, being truly able to discriminate and truly able to rule. This is how the noble man issues commands from himself while seeking to accord with Heaven's blessings. Suppose rewards and punishments were multiplied and made ostentatious while the worthy and unworthy were inverted—this would be an extreme defiance of Heaven; how then could one guarantee that cumulative ruin and abandonment [?] would not sprout? Alas! Those who govern Great Possession (Dayou) may observe the hexagram's image here. Yet there is a root to it. When the Heaven within our own mind is as clear as gazing at fire, at the juncture where good and evil wax and wane, defiance of or compliance with the Mandate of Heaven is decided. This is why the admonition regarding the "precarious and subtle, refined and single-minded" was especially earnest and repeated by Emperor Shun. Otherwise, when he succeeded to Yao's governance, the "Great Possession" of the world was vast indeed—how could the execution of the Four Fiends and the promotion of the Sixteen Clans have so readily brought the world to submission? Therefore it is said: "Only when one possesses Heavenly virtue can one speak of the Kingly Way." Truly it is so!

"What establishes the Way of Man is called benevolence and righteousness."
By Cao Lianggui 曹良貴.
Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Guo 郭 comments: [The exposition of principle is precise and detailed; the phrasing is gentle and elegant.]
Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Zhang 張 comments: [Using the learning of the mind-and-heart to reveal the profundities of human nature and destiny; clear and thorough, worthy of serving as a model.]
Associate Examiner Instructor Fan 范 comments: [Harmonious, refined, and pure; none without deep cultivation could have composed this.]
Examiner Reader-in-waiting Luo 羅 comments: [Substantial and grounded in the classics, without superficiality.]
Examiner Right Companion to the Heir Apparent Gao 高 comments: [Pure and clean, admirably befitting the meaning of the Book of Changes.]

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
說卦論人道之所由立而知易理之原焉夫人
之有道也仁義而已矣人道之所由立不在是
哉此性命之理具於人而聖人作易之原也蓋
曰三才不同其理一也故陰陽備而天道立於
上矣剛柔備而地道立於下矣至於人也者天
生之地成之而肖形其內者不囿於器之小崇
效天卑法地而成位其中者必具乎道之全果
何以立耶曰仁與義而已蓋天之陽地之剛在
人則爲仁也天之陰地之柔在人則爲義也寬
===
裕溫柔仁足以容也而有義以裁其過心之德
與心之制合而謂人之靈於物者靈以此也發
強剛毅義足以執也而有仁以濟其偏物之宜
與物之愛恊而謂人之貴於己者貴以此也繼
之者善而善非仁義不備以舒以慘之命自維
皇之降衷則然矣成之者性而性非仁義不全
克寬克嚴之德自生民之受衷則然矣蓋猶天
之有陰陽也地之有剛柔也而人之所以並立
爲三者由此道具耳借曰有仁而無義有義而
punctuated: 《說卦》論人道之所由立，而知易理之原焉。夫人之有道也，仁義而已矣。人道之所由立，不在是哉？此性命之理具於人，而聖人作《易》之原也。蓋曰：三才不同，其理一也。故陰陽備而天道立於上矣，剛柔備而地道立於下矣。至於人也者，天生之，地成之，而肖形其內者，不囿於器之小；崇效天，卑法地，而成位其中者，必具乎道之全。果何以立耶？曰仁與義而已。蓋天之陽、地之剛，在人則爲仁也；天之陰、地之柔，在人則爲義也。寬裕溫柔，仁足以容也，而有義以裁其過，心之德與心之制合，而謂人之靈於物者，靈以此也。發強剛毅，義足以執也，而有仁以濟其偏，物之宜與物之愛恊，而謂人之貴於己者，貴以此也。繼之者善，而善非仁義不備，以舒以慘之命，自維皇之降衷則然矣。成之者性，而性非仁義不全，克寬克嚴之德，自生民之受衷則然矣。蓋猶天之有陰陽也，地之有剛柔也，而人之所以並立爲三者，由此道具耳。借曰有仁而無義，有義而
translation_en: The Discussion of the Trigrams (Shuogua) discourses on that whereby the Way of Man is established, and through this one knows the origin of the principles of the Changes. Now, that man possesses the Way lies in benevolence and righteousness, and nothing more. Does not that whereby the Way of Man is established lie precisely in this? This is the principle of human nature and destiny endowed within man, and the origin of the sages' creation of the Changes. It is as if to say: the Three Powers differ, yet their principle is one. Therefore, when yin and yang are complete, the Way of Heaven is established above; when the firm and the yielding are complete, the Way of Earth is established below. As for man: Heaven generates him and Earth brings him to completion, so that he who resembles their forms within them is not confined to the smallness of a mere vessel; he who emulates Heaven in its loftiness, models himself on Earth in its lowliness, and establishes his position between them must be endowed with the totality of the Way. By what, indeed, is it established? It is called benevolence and righteousness, and nothing more. For the yang of Heaven and the firmness of Earth, in man, become benevolence; the yin of Heaven and the yieldingness of Earth, in man, become righteousness. Magnanimous, generous, gentle, and soft—benevolence is sufficient to be forbearing; yet there is righteousness to restrain its excesses. The virtue of the mind and the regulation of the mind unite, and when it is said that man is more spiritual than the myriad things, he is spiritual by virtue of this. Vigorous, strong, firm, and resolute—righteousness is sufficient to hold fast; yet there is benevolence to temper its partialities. What is fitting for things and the love for things harmonize, and when it is said that man has what is noble within himself, he is noble by virtue of this. That which succeeds it is goodness, and goodness is not complete without benevolence and righteousness; the decree of expansion and severity has been thus ever since the August Heaven sent down the moral sense. That which brings it to completion is human nature, and human nature is not whole without benevolence and righteousness; the virtue capable of both leniency and strictness has been thus ever since the people received the moral sense. For it is just like Heaven's having yin and yang, and Earth's having the firm and the yielding; and the reason why man stands alongside them as the Three Powers is simply because this Way is fully present in him. Suppose one were to say that there is benevolence without righteousness, or righteousness…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
無仁人道或幾乎毀矣而何以立哉性命之理
具於人蓋如此抑是仁義也對而言之則爲二
合而言之一道而已蓋道爲虛位仁與義爲定
名虛者一之神定者兩之化一不可知兩不可
執此天地之至妙也而況人乎聖人兼兩以作
易而三才之道管是矣謂易爲性命之書非哉
書
禹曰都帝愼乃在位帝曰俞
甯瑞鯉
===
同考試官教諭李　批〔思精詞雅發明愼位之旨警切〕
同考試官教諭潘　批〔理精詞古深得君臣交儆之義〕
考試官侍讀羅　批〔發明懇切可式〕
考試官右中允高　批〔聖世君臣氣象宛然〕
聖君得大臣謹位之謨而然之一保治之心也
夫愼位所以保治也臣謨之而君契焉此其都
俞之盛哉且治忽有相乘之幾而君位非得肆
之地禹之孜孜固保治意也而未已也乃嘆美
而告帝曰帝位天下之至尊也亦知爲天下之
punctuated:
無仁，人道或幾乎毀矣，而何以立哉？性命之理具於人，蓋如此。抑是仁義也，對而言之則爲二，合而言之一道而已。蓋道爲虛位，仁與義爲定名；虛者一之神，定者兩之化。一不可知，兩不可執，此天地之至妙也，而況人乎！聖人兼兩以作《易》，而三才之道管是矣。謂《易》爲性命之書，非哉！

《書》
「禹曰：『都！帝，愼乃在位。』帝曰：『俞！』」
甯瑞鯉
同考試官教諭李　批〔思精詞雅，發明愼位之旨，警切。〕
同考試官教諭潘　批〔理精詞古，深得君臣交儆之義。〕
考試官侍讀羅　批〔發明懇切，可式。〕
考試官右中允高　批〔聖世君臣氣象，宛然。〕

聖君得大臣謹位之謨而然之，一保治之心也。夫愼位所以保治也，臣謨之而君契焉，此其都俞之盛哉！且治忽有相乘之幾，而君位非得肆之地。禹之孜孜，固保治意也，而未已也。乃嘆美而告帝曰：帝位，天下之至尊也，亦知爲天下之
translation_en:
… without humaneness, the Way of Man would be almost destroyed; how then could it be established? The principle of human nature and Heaven's decree as endowed in man is indeed like this. Moreover, as for humaneness and righteousness, spoken of in contrast they are two, but spoken of together they are simply one Way. For the Way is an open concept, whereas humaneness and righteousness are fixed names; what is open is the unfathomable spirit of the One, and what is fixed is the transformation of the Two. The One cannot be fathomed, and the Two cannot be rigidly clung to—this is the ultimate mystery of Heaven and Earth, how much more so for man! The sages encompassed this duality to compose the Book of Changes (Yi), and the Way of the Three Powers is governed herein. To call the Book of Changes a book of human nature and destiny—is that not right?

Book of Documents (Shu)
"Yu said, 'Oh! Emperor, be cautious on your throne.' The Emperor said, 'Yes!'"
Ning Ruili 甯瑞鯉
Associate Examiner Instructor Li 李 comments: [The thought is refined and the diction elegant; its elucidation of the purport of being cautious on the throne is admonitory and incisive.]
Associate Examiner Instructor Pan 潘 comments: [The reasoning is precise and the phrasing ancient; it deeply grasps the meaning of mutual admonition between ruler and minister.]
Examiner Reader-in-waiting Luo 羅 comments: [The elucidation is earnest and incisive, worthy of serving as a model.]
Examiner Right Companion to the Heir Apparent Gao 高 comments: [The spirit of ruler and minister in a sage age is vividly present.]

When a sage ruler receives a grand minister's counsel on being cautious on the throne and affirms it, they are united in one mind to preserve good governance. Now, being cautious on the throne is the means to preserve good governance. The minister counsels it and the ruler accords with it—how flourishing is this harmony of "Oh!" and "Yes!"! Moreover, order and neglect have subtle triggers by which they overtake one another, and the ruler's position is no place for self-indulgence. Yu's untiring diligence was assuredly born of his intention to preserve good governance, yet he did not stop there. Thus he exclaimed in admiration and admonished the Emperor, saying: The imperial throne is the most exalted position in the world; do you also know that it is the world's…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
至艱乎故必享粒食之成罔游于逸也常若懷
襄未平而不能自安于其上撫作乂之盛罔淫
于樂也常若昏墊未復而不敢晏處乎其尊一
念不慎且有深憂守以克艱可也一日不慎且
有隱患持以儆戒可也否則君心狃于治安而
世變生于所忽能保其終哉然慎乃有位本帝
舜之心也遂答曰俞焉意以履帝位者以圖終
爲至理而論君道者以敬慎爲大原民雖粒食
矣豈其使一人肆于民上而位可逸哉汝之言
===
誠持盈之要道也可不兢業以居之耶邦雖作
乂矣豈其以一人奄有萬邦而位可樂哉汝之
言誠保泰之良規也可或怠荒以失之耶吁禹
惟愛君無已故君位已安而不忘乎矢謨帝惟
求治無窮故履位不疚而尤勤于納諫此都俞
之風不可及歟然敬脩可願舜嘗受之堯矣豈
待禹言而慎邪蓋臣恐君自足而危言儆之君
恐臣不言而虛懷契之聖世君臣之心固如此
風降而堂陛疎則有陳治安疏十漸而不終納
punctuated: 至艱乎？故必享粒食之成，罔游于逸也，常若懷襄未平，而不能自安于其上；撫作乂之盛，罔淫于樂也，常若昏墊未復，而不敢晏處乎其尊。一念不慎，且有深憂，守以克艱可也；一日不慎，且有隱患，持以儆戒可也。否則君心狃于治安，而世變生于所忽，能保其終哉？然慎乃有位，本帝舜之心也，遂答曰「俞」焉。意以履帝位者，以圖終爲至理；而論君道者，以敬慎爲大原。民雖粒食矣，豈其使一人肆于民上而位可逸哉？汝之言，誠持盈之要道也，可不兢業以居之耶？邦雖作乂矣，豈其以一人奄有萬邦而位可樂哉？汝之言，誠保泰之良規也，可或怠荒以失之耶？吁！禹惟愛君無已，故君位已安而不忘乎矢謨；帝惟求治無窮，故履位不疚而尤勤于納諫。此都俞之風不可及歟！然「敬脩可願」，舜嘗受之堯矣，豈待禹言而慎邪？蓋臣恐君自足而危言儆之，君恐臣不言而虛懷契之，聖世君臣之心固如此。風降而堂陛疎，則有陳《治安》、疏《十漸》而不終納
translation_en:
…most difficult in All-under-Heaven? Therefore, even as you enjoy the achievement of the people having grain to eat, you must not wander into idleness, always acting as though the enveloping and rising floodwaters were not yet pacified and you could not rest easy above them; even as you preside over the flourishing state of order and governance, you must not indulge excessively in pleasure, always acting as though the people's benightedness and drowning were not yet relieved and you dared not dwell in comfort in your exalted station. If a single thought is not cautious, there will be deep sorrow—you must guard your position by overcoming its difficulties; if a single day is not cautious, there will be hidden perils—you must maintain it with vigilance and admonition. Otherwise, if the ruler's mind grows accustomed to peace and order, while worldly upheavals arise from what is neglected, how can he preserve things to the very end?'

Yet being cautious in his position was originally in the heart of Emperor Shun himself, and so he replied, 'Yes, it is so!' His meaning was that for one who occupies the imperial throne, planning for the end is the ultimate principle; and for one who discusses the Way of the ruler, reverent caution is the great foundation: 'Although the people now have grain to eat, how could it be that one man is placed recklessly above the people so that his position may be one of idleness? Your words are truly the essential Way for holding on to fullness; how could I not occupy it with fear and trembling? Although the states are now brought to order, how could it be that one man possesses the myriad states so that his position may be one of pleasure? Your words are truly a fine rule for preserving peace and prosperity; how could I ever lose it through negligence and waste?'

Alas! Because Yu loved his sovereign without cease, even when the ruler's position was already secure he did not forget to set forth his counsels; and because the Emperor sought good governance without end, even though he occupied his position without fault he was all the more diligent in accepting remonstrance. Is not this spirit of mutual praise and agreement beyond reach? Yet 'reverently cultivating what is desirable' was something Shun had already received from Yao; why did he need to wait for Yu's words to be cautious? It is simply that the minister feared the ruler might become self-satisfied and thus admonished him with alarming words, while the ruler feared the minister might not speak and thus agreed with him with an open mind. Such indeed were the hearts of sovereign and minister in a sage age. When customs declined and the distance between the throne hall and the steps below grew wide, there were those who presented memorials on Peace and Order [Zhi'an ce] or submitted memorials on the Ten Gradual Failings [Shijian shu], and yet to the end were not accepted…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
者故人君先于虛巳斯責難者不爲空言矣夫
曰皇極之敷言是彝是訓于帝其訓凡厥
庶民極之敷言是訓是行以近天子之
光曰天子作民父母以爲天下王
錢大復
同考試官教諭李　批〔天人意旦見卓識而文更爽健〕
同考試官教諭潘　批〔簡潔圓融足爲崇雅之式〕
考試官侍讀羅　批〔醇雅不浮〕
考試官右中允高　批〔沖粹可誦〕
===
君子著敷言之訓通乎天人者也蓋極本天人
合一之理也由同天之妙以觀感人之深而敷
言豈可已哉箕子告武王意謂人君繼天以立
極必代天以立言所以通吾心于民心者其道
繇之也吾觀皇極之敷言根乎天常而易簡得
天下之理其民秉之彝乎示乎物則而一言盡
天下之道其淑世之訓乎理曰常理則理出乎
天一帝命之有赫也訓曰大訓則言純乎天一
帝則之孔昭也敷言之妙如此皇極之君所以
punctuated:
者，故人君先于虛巳，斯責難者不爲空言矣夫。

「曰：皇極之敷言，是彝是訓，于帝其訓。凡厥庶民，極之敷言，是訓是行，以近天子之光，曰：天子作民父母，以爲天下王。」
錢大復
同考試官教諭李　批〔天人意旦見卓識，而文更爽健。〕
同考試官教諭潘　批〔簡潔圓融，足爲崇雅之式。〕
考試官侍讀羅　批〔醇雅不浮。〕
考試官右中允高　批〔沖粹可誦。〕

君子著敷言之訓，通乎天人者也。蓋極本天人合一之理也。由同天之妙以觀感人之深，而敷言豈可已哉？箕子告武王，意謂人君繼天以立極，必代天以立言，所以通吾心于民心者，其道繇之也。吾觀皇極之敷言，根乎天常，而易簡得天下之理，其民秉之彝乎；示乎物則，而一言盡天下之道，其淑世之訓乎。理曰常理，則理出乎天，一帝命之有赫也；訓曰大訓，則言純乎天，一帝則之孔昭也。敷言之妙如此，皇極之君所以
translation_en:
… Therefore, if a ruler puts humbling himself first, then those who demand the difficult of him will not be speaking empty words!

“It is said: This amplification in words of the Royal Perfection is the unchanging norm, is the instruction; indeed, it is the Lord’s instruction. All the common people implement and practice this amplification in words of Perfection, so as to draw near to the glory of the Son of Heaven, saying: ‘The Son of Heaven is parent to the people, and thus sovereign over all under Heaven.’” [Book of Documents, “Great Plan” (Hongfan)]
Qian Dafu 錢大復
Associate Examiner, Instructor Li 李, comments: “The meaning of Heaven and man clearly reveals outstanding insight, and the writing is even more brisk and vigorous.”
Associate Examiner, Instructor Pan 潘, comments: “Concise and well-rounded, sufficient to serve as a model for prizing elegance.”
Examiner, Reader-in-waiting Luo 羅, comments: “Pure and elegant, without superficiality.”
Examiner, Right Companion to the Heir Apparent Gao 高, comments: “Serene and pure, worthy of recitation.”

When the noble man sets forth the instruction of his amplified words, it connects Heaven and humanity. For Ultimate Perfection is rooted in the principle of the unity of Heaven and humanity. Observing the depth with which it moves people through the subtlety of its accord with Heaven, how could one cease from amplifying it in words? When the Viscount of Ji (Jizi 箕子) addressed King Wu 武王, his meaning was that a ruler who succeeds Heaven in establishing Ultimate Perfection must speak on behalf of Heaven in establishing words; the way by which he connects his own mind with the minds of the people proceeds from this. When I observe the amplified words of Royal Perfection, they are rooted in the constant norms of Heaven, and through ease and simplicity attain the principles of all under Heaven—are they not the unchanging norms held fast by the people? They manifest the rules of things, and in a single word exhaust the Way of all under Heaven—are they not the instruction that betters the world? Calling its principle the constant principle means that the principle issues from Heaven, wholly as resplendent as the mandate of the Supreme Lord; calling its instruction the great instruction means that the words are purely of Heaven, wholly as brilliantly manifest as the pattern of the Supreme Lord. Such is the subtlety of the amplified words; that by which the sovereign of Royal Perfection …

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
宣著其光輝而長育乎天下者恃有此耳而所
感何如哉凡厥庶民誦諸口者非彝訓弗道也
措諸躬者非彝訓弗履也則本至德以敷言在
天子固光昭于無外由訓行以入德在庶民亦
相近而不違蓋至是而情分之所屬者益切矣
乃頌之曰天子作民父母焉感帝訓之勤而知
生我成我者有同親也又頌之曰天子為天下
王焉仰帝訓之嚴而知治我教我者有常尊也
會歸合而造就純錫保深而淫朋化斯皇極之
===
民也哉吁上以昭達天之妙而下以孚民心之
天信乎敷言之不容已矣大抵以人感人難以
天感人易禹謨之勸以九歌箕疇之敷以彝訓
一天之相為感也故言易入而其化神然君心
之天乃萬化所從出者心則不純而強民以訓
無乃已疎乎日監在茲順帝之則言純心事天
也建極者尚求端焉
詩
瑟彼玉瓚黃流在中豈弟君子福祿攸降
punctuated:
宣著其光輝而長育乎天下者，恃有此耳。而所感何如哉？凡厥庶民，誦諸口者，非彝訓弗道也；措諸躬者，非彝訓弗履也。則本至德以敷言，在天子固光昭于無外；由訓行以入德，在庶民亦相近而不違。蓋至是而情分之所屬者益切矣。乃頌之曰：「天子作民父母」焉，感帝訓之勤，而知生我成我者有同親也；又頌之曰：「天子為天下王」焉，仰帝訓之嚴，而知治我教我者有常尊也。會歸合而造就純，錫保深而淫朋化，斯皇極之民也哉！吁！上以昭達天之妙，而下以孚民心之天，信乎敷言之不容已矣。大抵以人感人難，以天感人易。禹謨之勸以九歌，箕疇之敷以彝訓，一天之相為感也，故言易入而其化神。然君心之天，乃萬化所從出者，心則不純，而強民以訓，無乃已疎乎？「日監在茲」，「順帝之則」，言純心事天也，建極者尚求端焉。
詩
「瑟彼玉瓚，黃流在中。豈弟君子，福祿攸降。」
translation_en:
… manifest his radiant splendor and nurture the world relies solely upon this. And what is the response it inspires? Among all the common people, whatever they recite with their mouths, if it is not the constant instruction, they do not speak it; whatever they practice in their conduct, if it is not the constant instruction, they do not tread it. Thus, basing himself on supreme virtue to set forth his words, the Son of Heaven shines forth boundlessly; and proceeding from the practice of these instructions to enter into virtue, the common people likewise draw near and do not deviate. Indeed, at this point, the bond of affection and duty becomes ever deeper. Thereupon they praise him, saying, "The Son of Heaven is parent to the people"—moved by the diligence of the sovereign's instruction, they recognize that he who gives them life and brings them to completion is just like their own parents. Again they praise him, saying, "The Son of Heaven is king over all under Heaven"—looking up to the majesty of the sovereign's instruction, they recognize that he who governs and teaches them holds an enduringly exalted station. When their convergence and allegiance are united, their cultivation becomes pure; when the bestowal and protection are deep, licentious factions are transformed—such indeed are the people of the August Ultimate!

Ah! Above, to manifest the wonder of reaching Heaven, and below, to inspire trust in the Heaven within the people's minds—truly, the setting forth of words cannot be dispensed with! On the whole, to move people through what is merely human is difficult, whereas to move people through Heaven is easy. The exhortation with the Nine Songs in the "Counsels of Yu" (Yu mo) and the spreading of the constant instructions in the "Plan of Jizi" (Ji chou) are one and the same in moving others through Heaven; therefore, the words easily enter their minds and the transformation is wondrous. Yet the Heaven within the ruler's mind is the source from which all transformations issue. If his mind is not pure, and yet he forces instructions upon the people, is that not wide of the mark? "Daily inspecting us here" and "following the pattern of the Supreme Lord" speak of serving Heaven with a pure mind; may he who establishes the Ultimate seek the fundamental source therein!

Book of Odes (Shi)

"Brightly carved is that jade libation ladle, with yellow-gold spiced millet wine within it. Easy and self-possessed is our lord, on whom happiness and blessings descend. …"

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
鳶飛戾天魚躍于淵豈弟君子遐不作
人
石崑玉
同考試官訓導李　批〔發詩旨明儆雅〕〔蔚宜冠多士〕
同考試官教諭程　批〔聖德必應之理〕〔精透融徹〕
同考試官教諭朱　批〔格莊詞雅洞〕〔見詩作〕
同考試官教諭向　批〔天人協應正見〕〔文王之德旨哉〕
考試官侍讀羅　批〔理明詞〕〔顯〕
考試官右中允高　批〔詞氣〕〔暢達〕
===
詩人兩興聖德之純而天人之協應也蓋德本
流通於上下者也自非豈弟之聖德烏能得天
化人之如是哉詩人咏歌之意若謂人君一身
天心視爲向背人心視爲從違而其本在德者
也吾於文王稽其盛矣彼瑟然王瓚則黃流在
其中注寶器以珍味固物理之相須也况君子
豈弟中涵正天之所篤厚者有不足以獲福乎
但見太和默感而維皇眷祐多福壽考之駢臻
也至順潛孚而上帝寵綏明命方國之畢受也
punctuated:
鳶飛戾天，魚躍于淵。豈弟君子，遐不作人。」

石崑玉

同考試官訓導李　批：〔發詩旨明儆雅〕〔蔚，宜冠多士。〕
同考試官教諭程　批：〔聖德必應之理，〕〔精透融徹。〕
同考試官教諭朱　批：〔格莊詞雅，洞〕〔見詩作。〕
同考試官教諭向　批：〔天人協應，正見〕〔文王之德，旨哉！〕
考試官侍讀羅　批：〔理明詞〕〔顯。〕
考試官右中允高　批：〔詞氣〕〔暢達。〕

詩人兩興聖德之純，而天人之協應也。蓋德本流通於上下者也，自非豈弟之聖德，烏能得天化人之如是哉？詩人咏歌之意，若謂人君一身，天心視爲向背，人心視爲從違，而其本在德者也。吾於文王稽其盛矣。彼瑟然王瓚，則黃流在其中，注寶器以珍味，固物理之相須也；况君子豈弟中涵，正天之所篤厚者，有不足以獲福乎？但見太和默感，而維皇眷祐，多福壽考之駢臻也；至順潛孚，而上帝寵綏，明命方國之畢受也。
translation_en:
… "The hawk flies up to heaven; the fishes leap in the deep. Easy and self-possessed was our prince—did he not exert an influence upon men?"

Shi Kunyu 石崑玉

Comment by Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Li: [Expounds the meaning of the Ode with clarity, incisiveness, elegance, and richness; fitting to top the multitude of scholars.]
Comment by Associate Examiner, Instructor Cheng: [The principle that sagely virtue necessarily evokes a response is articulated with refined penetration and thorough comprehension.]
Comment by Associate Examiner, Instructor Zhu: [Dignified in form and elegant in diction, showing deep insight into the composition of the Ode.]
Comment by Associate Examiner, Instructor Xiang: [The harmonious response of Heaven and humanity truly manifests the virtue of King Wen—how profound!]
Comment by Examiner, Reader-in-waiting Luo: [Clear in principle and lucid in diction.]
Comment by Examiner, Right Companion Gao: [Diction and vitality are fluent and expressive.]

The poet uses two evocative images to illustrate the purity of sagely virtue and how Heaven and humanity respond to it in harmony. Indeed, virtue inherently circulates between above and below; were it not for an easy and self-possessed sagely virtue, how could one win the favor of Heaven and transform humanity like this? The intent of the poet's song is as if to say that upon the person of the ruler alone, the mind of Heaven looks to decide its favor or disfavor, and the minds of men look to decide their allegiance or defiance—and the root of this lies in virtue. In King Wen I have examined its flourishing perfection. Look at that bright jade libation-cup [reading 王 as 玉]: the yellow-tinctured herb-flavored spirits are within it; pouring a precious delicacy into a treasured vessel is inherently the mutual complementarity of things in nature. How much more so when the princely man harbors easy self-possession within—precisely that which Heaven richly favors—could this be insufficient to obtain blessings? One sees only that supreme harmony silently moves Heaven, and the August One looks down with protective grace, so that abundant blessings and longevity arrive side by side; utmost顺 (compliance) subtly inspires trust, and the Lord on High bestows favor and peace, so that the bright mandate and the states of the four quarters are all received in full. …

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
蓋雖非預爲徼福之地然以易簡之天德迓申
錫之天庥自將不期而至矣而君子何容心哉
鳶飛魚躍則戾天而在淵莘化機以自適固物
性之相忘也况君子豈弟內藴正人之所則倣
者有不足以作人乎但見中和以建極而化導
旁敷盡在野在朝而丕變也平易以近民而薫
陶覃被合有德有造而兼成也蓋雖未嘗强斯
民之從然以吾心之先得感人心之同然自將
不戒而孚矣而君子何庸力哉夫一德格於上
===
下而丕應協於天人如此文王之德其可謂至
德也已矣雖然文王敢以是自足哉推其心方
且翼翼翼昭事而已視民如傷而已使後人能世
其軌則蒼姬之曆可衍於無窮奈之何顛覆厥
德而卒貽昊天降戾無自立辟之刺也嗚呼自
古基命之主未有不本於格天導民者而守成
業者恒失之讀此詩可以知所監矣
嗟嗟臣工敬爾在公王釐爾成來咨來茹
顧龍禎
punctuated:
蓋雖非預爲徼福之地，然以易簡之天德，迓申錫之天庥，自將不期而至矣，而君子何容心哉？鳶飛魚躍，則戾天而在淵，莘化機以自適，固物性之相忘也。况君子豈弟內藴，正人之所則倣者，有不足以作人乎？但見中和以建極，而化導旁敷，盡在野在朝而丕變也；平易以近民，而薫陶覃被，合有德有造而兼成也。蓋雖未嘗强斯民之從，然以吾心之先得，感人心之同然，自將不戒而孚矣，而君子何庸力哉？夫一德格於上下，而丕應協於天人如此，文王之德，其可謂至德也已矣。雖然，文王敢以是自足哉？推其心，方且翼翼翼昭事而已，視民如傷而已。使後人能世其軌，則蒼姬之曆可衍於無窮；奈之何顛覆厥德，而卒貽「昊天降戾」、「無自立辟」之刺也！嗚呼！自古基命之主，未有不本於格天導民者，而守成業者恒失之，讀此詩可以知所監矣。

嗟嗟臣工，敬爾在公。王釐爾成，來咨來茹。
顧龍禎
translation_en:
For although he did not make prior preparations to court blessings, yet by meeting the repeatedly bestowed favors of Heaven with his easy and simple heavenly virtue, those blessings would naturally arrive without being expected—so what deliberate calculation could the noble man harbor in his mind? The hawk flies and the fishes leap, reaching up to heaven and plunging into the deep; gathering [?] the springs of transformation for their own contentment, it is naturally the way of creatures' natures to be oblivious of one another. How much more so when the noble man stores easy and cheerful virtue within, which is precisely what men take as their model and pattern—could this be insufficient to rouse and cultivate men? One sees only that through equilibrium and harmony he establishes the supreme standard, and his transforming guidance spreads far and wide, bringing about a great change among all, whether in the rustic wilds or at court; through plainness and ease he draws near to the people, and his nurturing influence extends broadly, bringing both those of established virtue and those of promising achievement to completion together. For although he never forced the people to follow him, yet by stirring the common disposition of human hearts with what his own heart had first attained, they would naturally be won over in trust without having to be admonished—so what exertion of force did the noble man need to employ? Now, when a single pure virtue reaches above and below, and the grand response harmonizes Heaven and man in such a manner, the virtue of King Wen may truly be called supreme virtue indeed! Even so, would King Wen dare to be self-satisfied with this? If we fathom his heart, he was all the while simply serving brightly with reverent care, and simply regarding the people as if they were wounded. Had his descendants been able to follow his tracks from generation to generation, the calendar of the house of Zhou could have been extended without end; how was it that they overthrew their virtue, and in the end left behind the satirical reproaches of "Vast Heaven sends down calamity" and "Do not set up laws of your own"? Alas! From antiquity, rulers who laid the foundations of the Mandate have never failed to base themselves on reaching Heaven and guiding the people, whereas those who guard an established patrimony constantly lose it. Reading this ode, one may know what to take as a mirror.

"Ah, you ministers and officers, be reverent in your public duties. The king has given you perfect rules; come to consult and deliberate."
Gu Longzhen 顧龍禎

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導李　批〔詞宛意盡得周家重農之旨〕
同考試官教諭程　批〔詞語諄切發重農之意殆盡〕
同考試官教諭朱　批〔發周王訓戒之意諄切可録〕
同考試官教諭向　批〔格調典雅文詞懇切佳士也〕
考試官侍讀羅　批〔渾融明爽〕
考試官右中允高　批〔須義莊而和〕
王者戒農官以盡職亦惟王章之求而已夫人
臣必敬乃在位也而况成法有當遵者可不圖
以講求之乎昔成王以重農爲心而知農官乃
===
其專責也故進而戒之曰國家設官分職而稼
穡之政爾實司之所以重民天亦以厚國本也
嗟爾臣工尚其敬之哉無怠無荒者陳力之常
而爾以勞民勸相爲任祗愼尤所宜先也有嚴
有翼者奉公之度而爾以率作興事爲務儆惕
尤所宜切也以其身爲國家濟康阜則王事不
容以緩圖匪敬而瘝曠之咎至矣以其職爲百
姓導安養則民命不可以漫視匪敬而玩愒之
愆萌矣且今廟堂之經畫在一王有成憲焉凡
punctuated:
同考試官訓導李批：〔詞宛意盡，得周家重農之旨。〕
同考試官教諭程批：〔詞語諄切，發重農之意殆盡。〕
同考試官教諭朱批：〔發周王訓戒之意，諄切可録。〕
同考試官教諭向批：〔格調典雅，文詞懇切，佳士也。〕
考試官侍讀羅批：〔渾融明爽。〕
考試官右中允高批：〔須義莊而和。〕

王者戒農官以盡職，亦惟王章之求而已。夫人臣必敬乃在位也，而况成法有當遵者，可不圖以講求之乎？昔成王以重農爲心，而知農官乃其專責也，故進而戒之曰：「國家設官分職，而稼穡之政爾實司之，所以重民天，亦以厚國本也。嗟爾臣工，尚其敬之哉！無怠無荒者，陳力之常；而爾以勞民勸相爲任，祗愼尤所宜先也。有嚴有翼者，奉公之度；而爾以率作興事爲務，儆惕尤所宜切也。以其身爲國家濟康阜，則王事不容以緩圖，匪敬而瘝曠之咎至矣。以其職爲百姓導安養，則民命不可以漫視，匪敬而玩愒之愆萌矣。且今廟堂之經畫，在一王有成憲焉，凡
translation_en:
Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Li李, comments: [The wording is graceful and the meaning thoroughly expressed, capturing the purport of the Zhou house's emphasis on agriculture.]
Associate Examiner, Instructor Cheng程, comments: [The diction is earnest and urgent, bringing out the meaning of emphasizing agriculture almost exhaustively.]
Associate Examiner, Instructor Zhu朱, comments: [It brings out the meaning of the Zhou king's admonition; earnest and worthy of recording.]
Associate Examiner, Instructor Xiang向, comments: [The style is classical and elegant, the language sincere and earnest—a fine scholar.]
Examiner, Expositor-in-waiting Luo羅, comments: [Harmonious, well-integrated, clear, and brisk.]
Examiner, Right Companion to the Heir Apparent Gao高, comments: [The exposition of meaning [?] is dignified yet harmonious.]

When a true king admonishes his agricultural officials to fulfill their duties, he asks only that they seek out the royal statutes. Now, a minister must be reverent in holding his office; how much more so, when there are established laws that ought to be followed, can he fail to take measures to study and inquire into them? In antiquity, King Cheng took emphasis on agriculture to heart, and knowing that the agricultural officials held this as their specialized responsibility, he summoned them forward and admonished them, saying: "The state establishes offices and apportions duties, and you are indeed in charge of the administration of sowing and reaping; this is the means to honor that which the people regard as Heaven, and also to strengthen the foundation of the state. Ah, you ministers and officers, may you be reverent in your public duties! To be neither negligent nor idle is the constant norm of exerting one's strength in service, yet since your responsibility is to encourage and assist the toiling people, reverent caution is especially what you should put first. To be solemn and翼 (watchful/respectful) is the proper measure of serving the public interest, yet since your task is to lead the people in labor and initiate farming works, vigilance is especially what you should take to heart. Because you use your own persons to bring about peace and abundance for the state, the king's business admits of no tardy planning; without reverence, the blame for neglecting your office will arrive. Because you use your offices to guide the common people toward security and nourishment, the lives of the people cannot be regarded casually; without reverence, the fault of trifling away time will sprout. Moreover, in the present plans of the court, there are the established constitutions of our reigning king. In all that…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
其諄諄爲獻畝言者爾當來咨之而延訪以博
其見也訓典之宣布在羣工有明賜焉凡其孳
孳爲粒食計者爾當來茹之而參度以究其故
也稟已行之紀法而曲盡夫持循之方務使無
負宵旰之慮斯已耳率不易之章程而殫效夫
考據之力務使無失小民之依斯已耳此求爾
法者正所以敬爾公也而爾可不惕然以省哉
抑人主深居九重而王食萬方非若開創之君
躬親稼穡之艱難也乃今在廷之訓戒顧凜凜
===
于閭閻之憂何其勤民之切哉然必上以眞實
操法令而後下以敬畏奉法守否則日懸象魏
而申飭之猶空文也願治者其審諸
春秋
夏六月公會齊侯宋公陳侯鄭伯同盟于
幽〔莊公二十有七年〕六月公會宋公陳
侯衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯晉趙盾癸酉同
盟于新城〔文公十有四年〕史懋文
punctuated:
其諄諄爲獻畝言者，爾當來咨之，而延訪以博其見也；訓典之宣布，在羣工有明賜焉，凡其孳孳爲粒食計者，爾當來茹之，而參度以究其故也。稟已行之紀法，而曲盡夫持循之方，務使無負宵旰之慮，斯已耳；率不易之章程，而殫效夫考據之力，務使無失小民之依，斯已耳。此求爾法者，正所以敬爾公也，而爾可不惕然以省哉？抑人主深居九重，而王食萬方，非若開創之君，躬親稼穡之艱難也。乃今在廷之訓戒，顧凜凜于閭閻之憂，何其勤民之切哉！然必上以眞實操法令，而後下以敬畏奉法守，否則日懸象魏而申飭之，猶空文也。願治者其審諸！
《春秋》
夏六月，公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、鄭伯同盟于幽。〔莊公二十有七年〕六月，公會宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯、晉趙盾，癸酉，同盟于新城。〔文公十有四年〕
史懋文
translation_en:
…earnestly spoken on behalf of the fields and furrows [reading 獻畝 for 畎畝], you should come and consult on them, inquiring widely to broaden your view; in the promulgation of instructive canons, the various officials have been given clear bestowals, and in all that has been diligently planned for the people's grain food, you should come and deliberate on them, examining and measuring to get to the bottom of their causes. Receive the established laws and regulations that are already in force, and exhaust every means of upholding and following them, striving only not to fail the sovereign's anxious thoughts from before dawn until after dark; follow the immutable statutes and rules, and devote your utmost strength to examining and verifying, striving only not to lose that upon which the common people depend. This demand that you seek out the laws is precisely the means by which you show reverence for your public duty—how then could you not examine yourselves with vigilance and awe?

Moreover, the ruler of men dwells deep within the ninefold palace and enjoys the royal delicacies of all regions; he is not like a founding monarch who personally experienced the hardships of sowing and reaping. Yet today the instructions and admonitions at court are nonetheless filled with awe-inspiring concern for the sorrows of the village lanes—how earnest is this diligence on behalf of the people! Even so, it is only when the superior wields laws and ordinances with genuine reality that subordinates will uphold and guard the laws with reverent awe; otherwise, even if one suspends them daily from the palace gates and repeatedly enjoins them, they are still mere empty words. May those who desire good governance examine this carefully!

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)

"In summer, in the sixth month, the Duke met the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, and the Earl of Zheng, and together they made a covenant at You." [Twenty-seventh year of Duke Zhuang] "In the sixth month, the Duke met the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the Earl of Cao, and Zhao Dun of Jin; on the guiyou day, together they made a covenant at Xincheng." [Fourteenth year of Duke Wen]

By Shi Maowen 史懋文.

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
同考試官推官舒 批〔義正辭嚴最得聖人尊王之旨〕
考試官侍讀羅 批〔嚴整可式〕
考試官右中允高 批〔發書同意殆盡〕
二伯協尊攘之信經皆志其同欲也此見春秋
不可無伯亦不可無從伯之諸侯于幽新城之
盟君子爲世道幸矣蓋昔黍離之賦天下傷之
自伯圖肇興王綱攸賴聖人於會盟離合之間
每致意焉是故我莊之世創伯者齊也維時侯
度無統東向之轅未堅伯業其難以濟矣乃今
===
之盟于幽也安攘之勢既成觀望之情漸一雖
反覆如鄭亦受盟壇坫而帖然聽命之不遑焉
即一鄭而衆志可知已北杏倡會以來玆非其
獨盛者哉噫夾輔之風邈矣修世勳以奬王室
徼齊桓將誰與歸也則多助之人心豈其所可
少者經故特書曰同幸諸侯之從齊耳我文之
世嗣伯者晉也維時晉君方少北圖之釁日啟
中國且胥爲夷矣乃今之盟新城也推戴之念
惟均攘郤之謀允協雖從楚如三國亦衆奉齊
punctuated:
同考試官推官舒批：〔義正辭嚴，最得聖人尊王之旨。〕
考試官侍讀羅批：〔嚴整可式。〕
考試官右中允高批：〔發書同意殆盡。〕

二伯協尊攘之信，經皆志其同欲也。此見春秋不可無伯，亦不可無從伯之諸侯；于幽、新城之盟，君子爲世道幸矣。蓋昔《黍離》之賦，天下傷之。自伯圖肇興，王綱攸賴，聖人於會盟離合之間，每致意焉。是故我莊之世，創伯者齊也。維時侯度無統，東向之轅未堅，伯業其難以濟矣。乃今之盟于幽也，安攘之勢既成，觀望之情漸一；雖反覆如鄭，亦受盟壇坫，而帖然聽命之不遑焉。即一鄭，而衆志可知已。北杏倡會以來，玆非其獨盛者哉！噫！夾輔之風邈矣，修世勳以奬王室，徼齊桓將誰與歸也？則多助之人心，豈其所可少者？經故特書曰「同」，幸諸侯之從齊耳。我文之世，嗣伯者晉也。維時晉君方少，北圖之釁日啟，中國且胥爲夷矣。乃今之盟新城也，推戴之念惟均，攘郤之謀允協；雖從楚如三國，亦衆奉齊…
translation_en:
Associate Examiner and Prefectural Judge Shu comments: [Righteous in meaning and stern in diction, this best captures the Sage's intent in revering the king.]
Examiner and Academician Reader-in-Waiting Luo comments: [Rigorous, well-ordered, and worthy of serving as a model.]
Examiner and Right Companion to the Heir Apparent Gao comments: [It brings out the meaning of the Classic's writing of "together" almost exhaustively.]

When the two hegemons brought into harmony the good faith needed to revere the king and repel the barbarians, the Classic recorded in both instances their shared desire. This shows that the Spring and Autumn period could not do without hegemons, nor could it do without feudal lords who followed the hegemons; in the covenants at You and Xincheng, the gentleman rejoiced for the sake of the moral order of the world. For in the past, when the ode "Millet Lush" (Shuli) was composed, all under Heaven grieved over it. Once the hegemonic enterprise first arose, the royal綱 [bonds of royal authority] had something to rely upon, and the Sage always paid special attention to the comings together and partings in assemblies and covenants.

Therefore, in the era of our Duke Zhuang, the one who founded the hegemony was Qi. At that time, the conduct of the feudal lords lacked governing order, and the shafts of their carriages turned eastward were not yet resolute; the hegemonic enterprise was thus difficult to bring to success. Yet now, in the covenant at You, the momentum for pacifying the interior and repelling the exterior had already been established, and the sentiments of those who had been waiting and watching gradually became unified. Even a state as capricious as Zheng received the covenant at the altar steps and had scarcely time enough to submit docilely to commands. From Zheng alone, the will of the multitude can be known! Since Qi first initiated the assembly at Beixing, was this not uniquely flourishing? Alas! The custom of flanking and assisting the royal house had grown remote; in cultivating hereditary merit to aid and encourage the royal house, if not for Duke Huan of Qi, to whom could anyone turn? How, then, could the popular support that brings abundant help be dispensed with? The Classic therefore specially writes "together" (tong), rejoicing that the feudal lords followed Qi.

In the era of our Duke Wen, the one who succeeded to the hegemony was Jin. At that time, the ruler of Jin was still young, conflicts arising from southern ambitions toward the north were opening up day by day, and the Central States were on the verge of all becoming barbarian. Yet now, in the covenant at Xincheng, the desire to uphold and support the hegemon was uniform, and the plans for repelling and driving back the enemy were truly in harmony. Even states that had followed Chu, such as the three states [Chen, Zheng, and蔡/Song?], all joined the multitude in presenting the sacrificial…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
犧而幡然改圖之恐後焉即三國而衆志可知
已于扈耍盟以來茲不爲猶愈乎哉噫糾逖之
功遐矣振先烈以翼宗周于晉靈尚有厚望也
則偕好之友邦亦足倚爲重者經故特書曰同
幸諸侯之從晉耳夫聖人於齊晉奚私哉蓋爲
周室慮至惓惓也然自此而伐楚封衛一介不
遣桓亦幾於改物矣楚之爭鄭憑華竟與晉靈
之伯相爲終始同盟之諸侯將安用之嗟乎伯
業盛則天下以空名事王伯業衰則天下以空
===
名事伯亦其勢然也故春秋不得已而予齊桓
冬十月公會晉侯宋公衛侯鄭伯曹伯莒
子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子同圍齊
襄公十有八年公至自伐齊襄公十有
九年
湯以栢
同考試官推官舒　批〔發春秋抑強之意明盡可錄〕
考試官侍讀羅　批〔詞旨嚴正〕
考試官右中允高　批〔事核詞直〕
punctuated:
犧，而幡然改圖之恐後焉。即三國而衆志可知已。于扈耍盟以來，茲不爲猶愈乎哉？噫！糾逖之功遐矣，振先烈以翼宗周，于晉靈尚有厚望也。則偕好之友邦，亦足倚爲重者。經故特書曰「同」，幸諸侯之從晉耳。夫聖人於齊、晉奚私哉？蓋爲周室慮，至惓惓也。然自此而伐楚、封衛，一介不遣，桓亦幾於改物矣；楚之爭鄭憑華，竟與晉靈之伯相爲終始，同盟之諸侯將安用之？嗟乎！伯業盛則天下以空名事王，伯業衰則天下以空名事伯，亦其勢然也。故《春秋》不得已而予齊桓。

冬十月，公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、鄭伯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子同圍齊。〔襄公十有八年〕公至自伐齊。〔襄公十有九年〕

湯以栢

同考試官推官舒　批〔發《春秋》抑強之意，明盡，可錄。〕
考試官侍讀羅　批〔詞旨嚴正。〕
考試官右中允高　批〔事核詞直。〕
translation_en:
… sacrificial victims, and suddenly changed their plans, fearing only to be left behind. From these three states alone, the will of the multitude can already be known. Since the perfunctory covenant at Hu, is this not far better? Alas! The merit of uniting distant lands to punish the wayward had grown remote; yet in reviving the illustrious deeds of his predecessors to shelter the ancestral house of Zhou, great hopes were still placed in Duke Ling of Jin. Thus, the friendly states joining in amity were also sufficient to be relied upon as a weighty support. The Classic therefore specially records the word "together" (tong 同), rejoicing that the feudal lords followed Jin. Now, what private partiality did the Sage have toward Qi or Jin? Truly, in taking thought for the house of Zhou, his concern was most earnest. Yet from this point on, in attacking Chu and enfeoffing Wei, not a single emissary was dispatched to ask the King's leave, so that Duke Huan of Qi too came close to altering the royal prerogatives; and Chu's contention over Zheng and encroachment upon the central states ultimately lasted throughout the hegemony of Duke Ling of Jin—of what use, then, were the feudal lords of the shared covenant? Alas! When the hegemonic enterprise flourished, the realm served the King as an empty name; when the hegemonic enterprise declined, the realm served the hegemon as an empty name. Such was simply the inevitable trend of circumstances. Therefore, it was only out of necessity that the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) granted approval to Duke Huan of Qi.

"In winter, in the tenth month, the Duke met with the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, and the Viscount of Lesser Zhu, and together they besieged Qi." [Eighteenth year of Duke Xiang.] "The Duke arrived from invading Qi." [Nineteenth year of Duke Xiang.]

Tang Yibai 湯以栢

Associate Examiner, Prefectural Judge Shu 舒 comments: [It brings out the Spring and Autumn Annals' intent of curbing the overbearing thoroughly and clearly; worthy of selection.]
Examiner, Reader-in-waiting Luo 羅 comments: [The diction and purport are stern and upright.]
Examiner, Right Companion to the Heir Apparent Gao 高 comments: [The facts are verified and the language is forthright.]

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
春秋曲全諸侯討罪之兵而受兵者之惡著矣
夫國必自伐而後人伐之春秋之罪齊也亦抑
强暴之意與自魯齊有會圍齊之兵所爲合也
逮乎泝上還師而我公告至焉夫合黨凌人非
春秋所禁乎而奚以罪齊蓋聞之曰君子無始
禍無怙亂禍福之至靡弗自已求之者列國之
圍齊豈無故而加之兵哉良由齊也棄盟好而
日尋干戈肆凌虐而數伐隣國其稔惡非一朝
夕矣以故佳兵好還出爾有反爾之報重怒難
===
任不戢有自焚之災圻父之歌鴻鴈之賦仇齊
者一魯耳乃同仇之義㬥翕然不戒以自孚涉
河而誓沉玉而禱首事者一晉耳乃共事之人
心羣然不謀而自協平陰入而二臣獲齊之禍
深矣而其受之也非不幸雍門次而四郭焚諸
侯之憤洩矣而其加之也非爲暴何者今而後
得反之也向使齊無可加之釁則世胙大師股
肱之烈未泯纂乃祖考天王之命方新晉魯諸
國相率而親睦之恐後奚至剪爲仇讐若此哉
punctuated: 《春秋》曲全諸侯討罪之兵，而受兵者之惡著矣。夫國必自伐，而後人伐之。《春秋》之罪齊也，亦抑强暴之意與！自魯齊有會，圍齊之兵所爲合也；逮乎泝上還師，而我公告至焉。夫合黨凌人，非《春秋》所禁乎？而奚以罪齊？蓋聞之曰：「君子無始禍，無怙亂。」禍福之至，靡弗自已求之者。列國之圍齊，豈無故而加之兵哉？良由齊也，棄盟好而日尋干戈，肆凌虐而數伐隣國，其稔惡非一朝夕矣。以故佳兵好還，出爾有反爾之報；重怒難任，不戢有自焚之災。《圻父》之歌、《鴻鴈》之賦，仇齊者一魯耳，乃同仇之義㬥，翕然不戒以自孚；涉河而誓、沉玉而禱，首事者一晉耳，乃共事之人心，羣然不謀而自協。平陰入而二臣獲，齊之禍深矣，而其受之也非不幸；雍門次而四郭焚，諸侯之憤洩矣，而其加之也非爲暴。何者？今而後得反之也。向使齊無可加之釁，則世胙大師，股肱之烈未泯；纂乃祖考，天王之命方新。晉、魯諸國，相率而親睦之恐後，奚至剪爲仇讐若此哉？
translation_en:
The Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) goes out of its way to justify the punitive expedition of the feudal lords against a guilty party, and thereby the wickedness of the one subjected to arms is made manifest. Now, a state must first strike itself before others strike it. When the Spring and Autumn Annals condemns Qi, is this not also with the intention of curbing the strong and violent?

Ever since the meeting at Luji [reading 魯齊 for 魯濟], the troops for besieging Qi were thereby brought together; when the armies returned from the River Si [reading 泝 for 泗], our Duke reported his arrival back at the ancestral temple. Now, is not forming factions to bully others something forbidden by the Spring and Autumn Annals? Why then does it condemn Qi?

Indeed, I have heard it said: "The superior man does not initiate calamity, nor does he rely on disorder." In the arrival of misfortune or blessing, there is none that is not brought upon oneself. When the various states besieged Qi, how could they have inflicted arms upon it without cause? Truly it was because Qi cast aside covenant friendships and daily resorted to shields and spears, indulged in bullying and cruelty, and repeatedly attacked neighboring states—its accumulated evil was not the work of a single morning or evening. Therefore, fine weapons are fond of rebounding, and what goes out from you returns to you in retribution; heavy wrath is hard to bear, and failure to lay away arms brings the disaster of burning oneself.

With the singing of "Qifu" and the recitation of "Hongyan," the one bearing enmity toward Qi was Lu alone, yet once the righteous indignation of shared enmity was made plain [reading 㬥 as 暴], all came together in mutual trust without prior warning; in crossing the Yellow River to swear an oath and sinking jade in prayer, the one initiating the campaign was Jin alone, yet the hearts of those sharing in the enterprise all harmonized of themselves without prior consultation. When Pingyin was entered and two ministers were captured, Qi's calamity was deep indeed, yet its suffering this was no mere misfortune; when the armies encamped at Yongmen and the four outer walls were burned, the indignation of the feudal lords was vented, yet their inflicting this was not an act of tyranny. Why is this? Because only from this moment were they finally able to pay Qi back.

If previously Qi had given no provocation inviting attack, then as hereditary recipient of the Grand Preceptor's fief, the meritorious legacy of being the royal limbs would not have faded; and in succeeding to its ancestors, the charge from the Heavenly King would still have been fresh. The states of Jin, Lu, and the others would have led one another to cultivate亲睦 (amity) with Qi, fearing only to fall behind—how could they have come to cut ties and become mortal enemies like this?

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
經故書同圍齊以見其公書公至自伐齊以大
其事圍齊者無罪則見伐者之惡豈容掩哉雖
然晉亦未爲得也自于溫之宴歌詩弗類荀偃
一怒而高厚逃歸晉之欲甘心于齊舊矣故特
假鳩魯之名以逞其私而主之者則又荀偃也
天討之義馭下之權兩者胥失焉晉伯之日趨
於不競也宜哉
禮記
是故清明象天廣大象地終始象四時周
===
還象風雨五色成文而不亂八風從律
而不姦百度得數而有常小大相成終
始相生倡和清濁迭相爲經
闞士選
同考試官教諭曾　批〔冲雅明瑩　學搢得體錄之〕
考試官侍讀羅　批〔說理融洽〕
考試官右中允高　批〔縟節中有條貫〕
論大樂之作極其法之善焉蓋先王作樂之有
方也準造化而兼常變其法之善何如哉樂記
punctuated:
經故書「同圍齊」，以見其公；書「公至自伐齊」，以大其事。圍齊者無罪，則見伐者之惡，豈容掩哉？雖然，晉亦未爲得也。自于溫之宴，歌詩弗類，荀偃一怒而高厚逃歸，晉之欲甘心于齊，舊矣。故特假鳩魯之名以逞其私，而主之者則又荀偃也。天討之義、馭下之權，兩者胥失焉，晉伯之日趨於不競也，宜哉！

禮記
是故清明象天，廣大象地，終始象四時，周還象風雨。五色成文而不亂，八風從律而不姦，百度得數而有常。小大相成，終始相生。倡和清濁，迭相爲經。

闞士選
同考試官教諭曾　批〔冲雅明瑩，學搢得體，錄之。〕
考試官侍讀羅　批〔說理融洽。〕
考試官右中允高　批〔縟節中有條貫。〕

論大樂之作，極其法之善焉。蓋先王作樂之有方也，準造化而兼常變，其法之善何如哉！《樂記》
translation_en:
The Classic therefore records that they "jointly besieged Qi" in order to show their public-spiritedness, and records that "the Duke arrived from attacking Qi" in order to magnify the event. Since those who besieged Qi were blameless, how could the wickedness of the one who was attacked be concealed? Even so, Jin cannot be said to have been in the right either. Ever since the banquet at Wen, when the poem sung was inappropriate, Xun Yan flew into a rage and Gao Hou fled home, Jin had long wished to wreak its vengeance upon Qi. Thus it merely borrowed the pretext of giving relief to Lu in order to indulge its own private ends, and the one who directed the affair was moreover Xun Yan. Both the righteousness of Heaven's punitive expedition and the authority of controlling subordinates were lost together; that Jin's hegemony daily declined into weakness was fitting indeed!

Record of Rites (Liji)
"Therefore, in its brightness and purity it resembles heaven; in its vastness and greatness it resembles earth; in its endings and beginnings it resembles the four seasons; in its revolutions and turnings it resembles wind and rain. Like the five colors, it forms a pattern without confusion; like the eight winds, it follows the pitch-pipes without disorder; its hundred measures obtain their proper numbers and maintain constancy. Small and great complete one another; ending and beginning give birth to one another. Leading and responding, clear and turbid tones alternate with one another as warp and woof."

Kan Shixuan
Associate Examiner, Instructor Zeng, commented: "Serene, elegant, clear, and lustrous; scholarly and fitting in style [?]. Selected for inclusion."
Examiner, Expositor-in-waiting Luo, commented: "The explanation of principles is harmonious and thorough."
Examiner, Right Companion to the Heir Apparent Gao, commented: "Amidst elaborate details there is coherent order."

In discussing the creation of great music, the text carries the perfection of its method to the utmost. Indeed, the former kings had a definite method in creating music: taking the creative transformations of nature as their standard and encompassing both constancy and change, how supreme was the perfection of their method! The Record of Music (Yueji)…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
若謂先王之樂會本文之全昭功用之大樂之
所觀者深矣抑知其作之盡善乎是故天以清
明之氣上浮而樂有聲皆氣之爲也其皦然清
明者崇則效乎天地以廣大之質下凝而樂有
體皆質之具也其熙然廣大者卑則法乎地終
始運而樂之條理生矣則與四時之推遷者合
其序周還交而樂之變化見矣則與風雨之散
潤者符其節樂法造化如此其妙豈一端所能
盡哉語乎其常五聲配五行之色節奏合以成
===
文而何亂八音配八卦之風氣候協以從律而
何姦度出於律數起於度由一度之衍至百度
之繁參兩之而倚數也又何失其常乎語乎其
變以律小大而宮羽之稱交錯以相成以比終
始而鍾呂之序循環以相生倡和生於變清濁
從乎體以清濁之聲主倡和之應纍纍乎如貫
珠也又非迭相爲經乎吁樂法造化則達之常
變而自宜樂兼常變則參之造化而愈合由是
而效之獲也夫豈強致哉抑此特制作之迹耳
punctuated: 若謂：先王之樂，會本文之全，昭功用之大，樂之所觀者深矣；抑知其作之盡善乎？是故天以清明之氣上浮，而樂有聲，皆氣之爲也，其皦然清明者，崇則效乎天；地以廣大之質下凝，而樂有體，皆質之具也，其熙然廣大者，卑則法乎地。終始運而樂之條理生矣，則與四時之推遷者合其序；周還交而樂之變化見矣，則與風雨之散潤者符其節。樂法造化如此，其妙豈一端所能盡哉？語乎其常：五聲配五行之色，節奏合以成文，而何亂？八音配八卦之風，氣候協以從律，而何姦？度出於律，數起於度，由一度之衍，至百度之繁，參兩之而倚數也，又何失其常乎？語乎其變：以律小大，而宮羽之稱交錯以相成；以比終始，而鍾呂之序循環以相生。倡和生於變，清濁從乎體，以清濁之聲，主倡和之應，纍纍乎如貫珠也，又非迭相爲經乎？吁！樂法造化，則達之常變而自宜；樂兼常變，則參之造化而愈合。由是而效之獲也，夫豈強致哉？抑此特制作之迹耳，
translation_en:
… as if to say: The music of the former kings brings together the completeness of substance and refinement and manifests the greatness of its efficacy and function—what can be observed in music is profound indeed; yet does one know the perfection of its creation? Therefore, Heaven with its clear and bright vital energy floats upward, and music has sounds that are all the product of vital energy; in being radiantly clear and bright, in its loftiness it emulates Heaven. Earth with its vast and great material substance condenses downward, and music has forms that are all the embodiment of material substance; in being serenely vast and great, in its lowliness it models itself on Earth. As end and beginning revolve, the orderly coherence of music is born, matching in sequence the succession of the four seasons; as circling movements interact, the transformations of music are revealed, tallying in rhythm with the dispersal and moistening of wind and rain. Since music models itself on the creative forces of nature in this way, how could its subtlety be exhausted in a single aspect?

Speaking of its constancy: the five tones correspond to the colors of the Five Phases, their rhythms and cadences combining to form a pattern—how could there be disorder? The eight timbres correspond to the winds of the Eight Trigrams, their seasonal breaths harmonizing to follow the pitch-pipes—how could there be licentiousness? Measures arise from the pitch-pipes, and numbers originate from measures; extending from a single measure to the multiplicity of a hundred measures, combining them in threes and twos to establish the numbers—how could they ever lose their constancy?

Speaking of its variation: in governing the small and the great, the designations of the gong and yu tones interweave to complete one another; in aligning end and beginning, the sequence of the yang and yin pitch-pipes circulates to generate one another. Leading and responding arise from variation, while clear and turbid tones follow from the instrument's form; using clear and turbid sounds to govern the resonance of leading and responding, strung together like threaded pearls—do they not take turns serving as the guiding thread?

Ah! Because music models itself on the creative forces of nature, when extended to constancy and variation it is naturally fitting; because music encompasses both constancy and variation, when aligned with the creative forces of nature it is all the more in harmony. The results thus attained—how could they be brought about by force? Yet these are merely the outward traces of its creation; …

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
要之樂以章德德盛而樂斯備也君子反情比
類預立乎樂之本而後器數從之則始焉法造
化終且贊乎造化而體常盡變之間無非裁成
輔相之用矣否則將如樂何而矧於功化之妙
乎是故不聞性與天道而欲議樂者末也
孔子曰安上治民莫善於禮此之謂也
吳　棐
同考試官教諭曾　批〔發明安治之義古雅無一長語〕
考試官侍讀羅　批〔典雅明皂〕
===
考試官右中允高　批〔文亦典雅〕
觀聖人之言則知禮之爲用大矣夫禮者物之
致也由聖言觀之則其用之大不益明乎且夫
敬讓行而達之無往不順禮誠軌世之善物也
而非無徵也昔孔子嘗曰安上治民莫善於禮
蓋言上之道揆雖非一然有禮則安而藏身之
固庸禮之外無他事也下之法守雖非一然得
禮則治而民分之定達禮之餘無多術也孔子
之言如此其斯敬讓盡道而無入不得之謂乎
punctuated:
要之，樂以章德，德盛而樂斯備也。君子反情比類，預立乎樂之本，而後器數從之。則始焉法造化，終且贊乎造化，而體常盡變之間，無非裁成輔相之用矣。否則將如樂何？而矧於功化之妙乎？是故不聞性與天道，而欲議樂者，末也。
「孔子曰：『安上治民，莫善於禮。』此之謂也。」
吳棐
同考試官教諭曾批〔發明安治之義，古雅無一長語。〕
考試官侍讀羅批〔典雅明皂。〕
考試官右中允高批〔文亦典雅。〕
觀聖人之言，則知禮之爲用大矣。夫禮者，物之致也。由聖言觀之，則其用之大，不益明乎？且夫敬讓行而達之，無往不順，禮誠軌世之善物也，而非無徵也。昔孔子嘗曰：「安上治民，莫善於禮。」蓋言上之道揆雖非一，然有禮則安，而藏身之固，庸禮之外無他事也；下之法守雖非一，然得禮則治，而民分之定，達禮之餘無多術也。孔子之言如此，其斯敬讓盡道而無入不得之謂乎！
translation_en:
In sum, music serves to manifest virtue; when virtue is abundant, music is thereby complete. The gentleman reflects upon his feelings and compares categories, establishing in advance the foundation of music, after which the instruments and numbers follow. Thus, in the beginning one models oneself upon the creative forces of nature, and in the end one even assists those creative forces; between embodying constancy and exhausting change, there is nothing that is not the function of regulating and assisting nature. Otherwise, what can one do with music—much less the subtleties of its transformative achievements? Therefore, to wish to discuss music without having heard of human nature and the Way of Heaven is merely to concern oneself with trivialities.

"Confucius said: 'For securing the ruler above and governing the people below, nothing is better than ritual.' This is what is meant."
Wu Fei 吳棐
Associate Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Zeng 曾 comments: [It elucidates the meaning of securing and governing in an archaic and elegant style, without a single superfluous word.]
Examiner, Expositor-in-waiting (shidu) Luo 羅 comments: [Classic, elegant, and clearly distinguished [?].]
Examiner, Right Companion to the Heir Apparent (you zhongyun) Gao 高 comments: [The writing is likewise classic and elegant.]

When we observe the words of the Sage, we know that the function of ritual is great indeed. Now, ritual is the culmination of things. Viewed in light of the Sage's words, is not the greatness of its function all the more evident? Moreover, when reverence and deference are practiced and extended, there is nowhere they do not proceed smoothly; ritual is truly an excellent instrument for regulating the world, and this is not without proof. Formerly, Confucius once said: "For securing the ruler above and governing the people below, nothing is better than ritual." This means that although the principles by which superiors measure their conduct are not singular, with ritual they are secure, and for the firmness of safeguarding oneself, there is no other business beyond the practice of ritual; and although the laws and observances kept by inferiors are not singular, when they attain ritual they are well-governed, and for the settling of the people's lot, there are no further techniques beyond the extension of ritual. Such were the words of Confucius—is this not what is meant by reverence and deference exhausting the Way, so that nowhere can one enter without succeeding? …

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
夫自孔子言之若謂禮之切於上下云爾然禮
者嘉之會也由上下推之是故無物而不在禮
矣謂禮之繫於治安云爾然禮者衆之紀也由
治安推之是故禮周流無不徧矣宗廟朝廷上
下寓焉敬讓以行此而在廟極敬在朝極辨所
以通乎幽明之交者何安且治也然則孔子之
極言禮也非此之謂與室家鄉里上下寓焉敬
讓以行此而內和於室外理於鄉所以稱乎親
疏之情者何安且治也然則我之聞禮於孔子
===
也非此之謂與夫上以禮安則爲上而不知謹
禮者非也民以禮治則爲民而不知守禮者亦
非也然則隆由之功其可或已哉大抵治安之
善信莫如禮乃其道之所繇者何噫言之矣不
曰修已以敬而安人乎不曰以禮讓爲國乎惟
敬則篤恭之治神讓則太和之化洽此體信達
順之功唐虞三代之極致也獨有方士乎哉然
語聖學之要則尤在主敬秉禮者尚懋諸
第貳場
punctuated:
夫自孔子言之，若謂禮之切於上下云爾。然禮者，嘉之會也。由上下推之，是故無物而不在禮矣。謂禮之繫於治安云爾，然禮者，衆之紀也。由治安推之，是故禮周流無不徧矣。宗廟朝廷，上下寓焉。敬讓以行此，而在廟極敬，在朝極辨，所以通乎幽明之交者，何安且治也！然則孔子之極言禮也，非此之謂與？室家鄉里，上下寓焉。敬讓以行此，而內和於室，外理於鄉，所以稱乎親疏之情者，何安且治也！然則我之聞禮於孔子也，非此之謂與？夫上以禮安，則爲上而不知謹禮者非也；民以禮治，則爲民而不知守禮者亦非也。然則隆由之功，其可或已哉！大抵治安之善，信莫如禮。乃其道之所繇者何？噫，言之矣。不曰「修已以敬而安人」乎？不曰「以禮讓爲國」乎？惟敬則篤恭之治神，讓則太和之化洽。此體信達順之功，唐虞三代之極致也，獨有方士乎哉！然語聖學之要，則尤在主敬。秉禮者尚懋諸！

第貳場
translation_en:
Now, judging from Confucius's words, it is as if he were merely saying that ritual is closely pertinent to superiors and inferiors. Yet ritual is the convergence of excellence. Extending it from superiors and inferiors, therefore, there is nothing that does not reside in ritual. It is as if he were merely saying that ritual is tied to order and security. Yet ritual is the regulating thread of the multitude. Extending it from order and security, therefore, ritual circulates everywhere without fail. In the ancestral temple and the royal court, the distinction between superior and inferior is embodied. When reverence and deference are practiced to carry this out, utmost reverence is shown in the temple and utmost discernment of rank in the court; how secure and well-ordered is that by which communion between the unseen and the manifest is achieved! If so, when Confucius spoke in the highest terms of ritual, was it not this that he meant? In the family household and the local village, the distinction between superior and inferior is embodied. When reverence and deference are practiced to carry this out, there is harmony within the household and order outside in the village; how secure and well-ordered is that by which the feelings of intimacy and distance are properly matched! If so, what I have heard of ritual from Confucius—was it not this that was meant? Now, since superiors are made secure through ritual, to be a superior and not know to be careful of ritual is wrong; since the people are governed through ritual, to be among the people and not know to abide by ritual is also wrong. That being the case, how could the effort of exalting and following ritual ever cease! On the whole, for excellence in bringing about order and security, truly nothing compares to ritual. Yet what is the path from which it proceeds? Ah, it has already been stated! Did he not say, "Cultivate oneself with reverence so as to bring security to others"? Did he not say, "Govern a state with ritual deference"? Only through reverence does the governance of steadfast respect become wondrous; through deference, the transformation of supreme harmony becomes pervasive. This achievement of embodying trustworthiness and reaching compliance is the ultimate perfection of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties—how could it belong solely to the Master of Youfang [Ziyou] [?]? Yet if we speak of the essentials of sage learning, it lies above all in making reverence the master. Let those who uphold ritual strive therein!

Second Session

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
論
人主恭己於上
同考試官訓導李　批〔詞古意盡末重主敬親賢尤切要之論宜錄之以式多士〕　石崑玉
同考試官教諭程　批〔議論古雅才識宏遠發明恭己之由在信任宰執臺諫剴切明盡而末復歸之主敬親賢足占忠愛矣〕
同考試官教諭朱　批〔議論雄渾結構嚴密發揮綱紀風俗最得肯綮蓋有裨于治理者錄之非徒以其文也〕
===
同考試官教諭向　批〔高古之識雄偉之才正大之情具見此篇末尾歸之主敬親賢尤爲知本之論〕
考試官侍讀羅　批〔氣格渾融議論詳確允矣經世之文也宜錄以式〕
考試官右中允高　批〔亹亹數百言極論君心爲本得朱子告君之意〕
人君以其心運天下而不以其身狥天下夫心
者治之所從出也人君之御天下固將盡囿於
範圍之內而以四海之廣兆民之衆人情習尚
punctuated:
論

「人主恭己於上」

同考試官訓導李批：〔詞古意盡，末重主敬親賢，尤切要之論，宜錄之以式多士。〕　石崑玉
同考試官教諭程批：〔議論古雅，才識宏遠。發明恭己之由，在信任宰執臺諫，剴切明盡，而末復歸之主敬親賢，足占忠愛矣。〕
同考試官教諭朱批：〔議論雄渾，結構嚴密，發揮綱紀風俗，最得肯綮。蓋有裨于治理者，錄之非徒以其文也。〕
同考試官教諭向批：〔高古之識，雄偉之才，正大之情，具見此篇。末尾歸之主敬親賢，尤爲知本之論。〕
考試官侍讀羅批：〔氣格渾融，議論詳確，允矣經世之文也，宜錄以式。〕
考試官右中允高批：〔亹亹數百言，極論君心爲本，得朱子告君之意。〕

人君以其心運天下，而不以其身狥天下。夫心者，治之所從出也。人君之御天下，固將盡囿於範圍之內；而以四海之廣、兆民之衆，人情習尚，
translation_en:
Discourse

"The Ruler Maintains Reverent Self-Possession Above"

Comment by Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Li: [The diction is antique and the meaning fully realized; at the end, the emphasis on abiding in reverence and drawing close to the worthy is an especially pertinent and essential argument. It should be published to serve as a model for the many scholars.] — Shi Kunyu 石崑玉
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Cheng: [The argumentation is classic and refined, the talent and insight broad and far-reaching. In elucidating how reverent self-possession is achieved, it locates it in trusting the grand councillors and the Censorate and Remonstrance Bureau, which is incisive, clear, and thorough; and at the end it returns to abiding in reverence and drawing close to the worthy, which suffices to reveal loyalty and devotion.]
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Zhu: [The argumentation is vigorous and grand, the structure tight and precise, and its elaboration on state discipline and popular customs hits the very crux of the matter. Because it is beneficial to the principles of governance, we publish it not merely for its literary style.]
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Xiang: [Lofty and antique insight, grand and imposing talent, and upright and magnanimous sentiment are all evident in this piece. Its conclusion returning to abiding in reverence and drawing close to the worthy is especially an argument that understands the fundamental root.]
Comment by Examiner Academician Reader-in-waiting Luo: [Its spirit and form are harmonious and integrated, its argumentation detailed and exact. Truly it is a piece of writing for ordering the world; it should be published as a model.]
Comment by Examiner Right Companion to the Heir Apparent Gao: [In several hundred tireless words, it thoroughly argues that the ruler's mind is the root, capturing the intent of Master Zhu's (Zhu Xi 朱熹) counsels to his sovereign.]
