title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
若是其異齊苟徒以巍然者寄於上而無所以
治之之具則天下將狃于情之所嚮習之所便
浸淫至于極敝而人君又不能以一人之身殫
精畢力日役役焉爲天下用於是握其機之大
且要者與天下賢士共圖之而吾惟以一心超
然獨運於天下是故君享其逸臣任其勞而無
爲之治成此哲后之上務皇王之大業也昔朱
子論善治在振綱紀然必資宰執之秉持臺諫
之補察而推本於人主以大公至正之心恭已
===
於上而臨之蓋識體之說也請申其意蓋天爲
民而作之君將以治之安之也顧以天下之大
而民生於其間智者思以儇巧處其利而愚者
亦有所謀勇者思以雄桀重其權而怯者亦有
所逐以至衆寡小大莫不鬩然於好惡之異情
相與競騖而弗已則民生有欲而各求所以遂
之也夫以民各有必欲遂之私而勢又不可以
自致則不能無求於上求而無度量分界於是
將紛紛籍籍訖無底定而吾既以身任天下之
punctuated:
若是其異齊，苟徒以巍然者寄於上，而無所以治之之具，則天下將狃于情之所嚮、習之所便，浸淫至于極敝；而人君又不能以一人之身，殫精畢力，日役役焉爲天下用。於是握其機之大且要者，與天下賢士共圖之，而吾惟以一心超然獨運於天下。是故君享其逸，臣任其勞，而無爲之治成。此哲后之上務，皇王之大業也。昔朱子論善治在振綱紀，然必資宰執之秉持、臺諫之補察，而推本於人主以大公至正之心，恭已於上而臨之，蓋識體之說也。請申其意。

蓋天爲民而作之君，將以治之、安之也。顧以天下之大，而民生於其間，智者思以儇巧處其利，而愚者亦有所謀；勇者思以雄桀重其權，而怯者亦有所逐。以至衆寡小大，莫不鬩然於好惡之異情，相與競騖而弗已，則民生有欲，而各求所以遂之也。夫以民各有必欲遂之私，而勢又不可以自致，則不能無求於上；求而無度量分界，於是將紛紛籍籍，訖無底定。而吾既以身任天下之
translation_en:
…are so disparate and uneven, if he merely occupies an exalted position above without the means to govern them, then the realm will grow habituated to following its inclinations and adhering to its conveniences, gradually sinking into extreme decay. Yet the ruler cannot, in his single person, exhaust his spirit and strength, toiling day after day in the service of the realm. Therefore, he grasps the great and essential levers of authority and deliberates upon them together with the worthy gentlemen of the world, while he himself, with a single mind, transcends all and independently directs the realm. Thus the ruler enjoys ease, the ministers bear the toil, and governance through non-action is achieved. This is the supreme task of the wise sovereign and the great enterprise of august kings. In the past, Master Zhu [Zhu Xi 朱熹] argued that good governance lies in invigorating the fundamental laws and discipline, yet it must rely on the firm upholding by the Grand Councilors and Executive Officials and the remonstrance and surveillance by the Censors and Remonstrators, while tracing its root to the ruler presiding over them in reverent self-restraint from above with a mind of great impartiality and utmost rectitude—this is indeed a doctrine that understands the essentials of governance. Allow me to elaborate upon its meaning.

Heaven created the ruler for the sake of the people, intending that he should govern them and bring them peace. Yet given the vastness of the realm and the people born within it, the clever seek to secure advantage through agility and cunning, while even the foolish have their schemes; the brave seek to augment their power through valor and dominance, while even the timid have their pursuits. Extending to the many and the few, the great and the small, none fail to contend amidst differing sentiments of like and dislike, racing against one another without cease; this is because the people are born with desires, and each seeks the means to fulfill them. Now, since the people each have private desires that they are determined to fulfill, and yet by circumstance cannot achieve them on their own, they cannot help making demands upon their superiors. If they make demands without measure or boundary, everything will fall into tumultuous confusion, never reaching stability. And since I have already taken upon myself the…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
至正之心也蓋嘗觀天下之人至弗齊矣其迪
哲俊乂累行砥名足陟于上者有之寧無奇袤
險側澳忍浮沉可抑之使下乎其鎮撫救寧鴻
熙勳伐足懋其賞者有之寧無昏墨殘賊淫湎
毀常可威之以刑乎夫人主之心豈不樂天下
之皆賢而鮮不肖皆無罪而有功而勢之所在
固難必責其盡如吾意而勢不能盡如吾意又
甚非吾蕩平正直之道於是立爲綱紀以明示
天下如此而陟如此而黜如此而賞如此而刑
===
持于上者有一定之軌而承于下者有一定之
式使天下皆屈體扶伏以待榮辱生殺於我斯
人主之命常尊而天下之勢統於一致之周禮
八柄曰爵馭貴祿馭富予馭幸置馭行生馭福
奪馭貧廢馭罪誅馭過是綱紀之所布也而又
有作威作福之權焉有衆共衆棄之典焉蓋威
福之權固人主之所獨攬而必以之與衆則人
主亦不敢以自專也而況爲吾之宰執臺諫乎
坐廟堂而與相可否者宰執也立殿陛而與爭
punctuated: 至正之心也。蓋嘗觀天下之人，至弗齊矣。其迪哲俊乂，累行砥名，足陟于上者有之；寧無奇袤險側，澳忍浮沉，可抑之使下乎？其鎮撫救寧，鴻熙勳伐，足懋其賞者有之；寧無昏墨殘賊，淫湎毀常，可威之以刑乎？夫人主之心，豈不樂天下之皆賢而鮮不肖，皆無罪而有功？而勢之所在，固難必責其盡如吾意；而勢不能盡如吾意，又甚非吾蕩平正直之道。於是立爲綱紀，以明示天下：如此而陟，如此而黜，如此而賞，如此而刑。持于上者有一定之軌，而承于下者有一定之式，使天下皆屈體扶伏，以待榮辱生殺於我，斯人主之命常尊，而天下之勢統於一。致之《周禮》八柄，曰：爵馭貴，祿馭富，予馭幸，置馭行，生馭福，奪馭貧，廢馭罪，誅馭過。是綱紀之所布也，而又有作威作福之權焉，有衆共衆棄之典焉。蓋威福之權，固人主之所獨攬，而必以之與衆，則人主亦不敢以自專也，而況爲吾之宰執、臺諫乎？坐廟堂而與相可否者，宰執也；立殿陛而與爭
translation_en: … a mind of utmost rectitude. For if we observe the people of the world, they are most unequal indeed. There are those who walk in wisdom and are of outstanding talent, who accumulate virtuous deeds and polish their reputations, sufficient to be promoted to high positions; yet how could there not also be those who are perverse, treacherous, and crooked, who are secretive, callous, and drift along with the times, who ought to be suppressed and demoted? There are those who pacify, soothe, rescue, and bring tranquility, whose grand achievements and meritorious deeds are sufficient to warrant generous rewards; yet how could there not also be those who are benighted, corrupt, cruel, and rapacious, who indulge in excess and destroy moral norms, who ought to be awed with punishments? Now, in the heart of a ruler of men, how could he not delight in having all in the world be worthy and few unworthy, all free of offense and possessing merit? Yet given the nature of circumstances, it is inherently difficult to demand with certainty that everyone conform entirely to one's wishes; and where circumstances cannot conform entirely to one's wishes, to force them is moreover utterly contrary to our broad, impartial, and upright Way. Therefore, he establishes fundamental laws and institutions to clearly manifest them to the world: for such-and-such one is promoted, for such-and-such one is demoted, for such-and-such one is rewarded, and for such-and-such one is punished. What is upheld above follows a fixed track, and what is received below adheres to a fixed standard, causing all in the world to bow their bodies and prostrate themselves, awaiting honor or disgrace, life or death from me; thus the commands of the ruler of men are ever revered, and the power of the world is unified into one. Examining the Eight Handles in the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli), it says: rank controls status, emolument controls wealth, bestowal controls favor, appointment controls conduct, preservation of life controls fortune, deprivation controls poverty, dismissal controls guilt, and censure controls error. This is how fundamental laws and institutions are promulgated, and therein lies the authority to inspire awe and bestow blessings, as well as the canonical principle of sharing positions with the multitude and casting out those rejected by the multitude. For although the authority to inspire awe and bestow blessings is indeed grasped solely by the ruler of men, since it must be shared with the multitude, even the ruler of men dares not monopolize it for himself—how much less so with regard to our Grand Councillors and Censors and Remonstrators! Those who sit in the court and deliberate with him on what is acceptable and unacceptable are the Grand Councillors; those who stand at the palace steps and argue with him over …

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
是非者臺諫也宰執者政本之重而臺諫則闕
遺之司也故人主爲天下進一賢遐一不肖也
宰執曰可臺諫亦曰可然後黜陟行焉黜陟以
宰執以臺諫也吾心無作好作惡也間有異同
吾從而察之而後黜陟之亦此心也爲天下旌
一功罰一罪也宰執曰可臺諫亦曰可然後刑
賞加焉刑賞以宰執以臺諫也吾心無溢喜溢
怒也間有異同吾從而察之而後刑賞之亦此
心也是知綱紀者天下之綱紀宰執可行之臺
諫可言之而君心者尤綱紀之綱紀用宰執臺
===
諫而不有也唯明主獨觀化原既挈天下之綱
紀付之賢宰執又令二三臺諫得言之百司庶
府罔不循令而從事按法而業官而吾心直以
其公平正大者宰之譬之鑑焉烱然無私而天
下之妍媸弗能遁也譬之衡焉戛然不搖而天
下之輕重弗可欺也乃所以握是鑑與衡者匪
惟天下不得而知即人主不得而自知也此豈
以無心忘天下哉恭已於無爲而心運於有爲
punctuated: 是非者，臺諫也。宰執者，政本之重；而臺諫，則闕遺之司也。故人主爲天下進一賢、遐一不肖也，宰執曰可，臺諫亦曰可，然後黜陟行焉。黜陟以宰執、以臺諫也，吾心無作好作惡也；間有異同，吾從而察之，而後黜陟之，亦此心也。爲天下旌一功、罰一罪也，宰執曰可，臺諫亦曰可，然後刑賞加焉。刑賞以宰執、以臺諫也，吾心無溢喜溢怒也；間有異同，吾從而察之，而後刑賞之，亦此心也。是知綱紀者，天下之綱紀，宰執可行之，臺諫可言之；而君心者，尤綱紀之綱紀，用宰執、臺諫而不有也。唯明主獨觀化原，既挈天下之綱紀付之賢宰執，又令二三臺諫得言之，百司庶府罔不循令而從事、按法而業官，而吾心直以其公平正大者宰之。譬之鑑焉，烱然無私，而天下之妍媸弗能遁也；譬之衡焉，戛然不搖，而天下之輕重弗可欺也。乃所以握是鑑與衡者，匪惟天下不得而知，即人主不得而自知也。此豈以無心忘天下哉？恭已於無爲，而心運於有爲…
translation_en: …over right and wrong are the Censors and Remonstrators. The Grand Councilors carry the weight of the fundamental administration, while the Censors and Remonstrators are the officials charged with pointing out omissions and oversights. Therefore, when a ruler promotes a worthy man or dismisses an unworthy one for the sake of the empire, if the Grand Councilors say it is right and the Censors and Remonstrators also say it is right, only then are demotions and promotions carried out. Demotions and promotions are carried out through the Grand Councilors and the Censors and Remonstrators; in my own mind there is no indulgence in personal likes or dislikes. Should there occasionally be disagreement between them, I then examine into the matter and afterward demote or promote, which also stems from this same mind. When he honors a merit or punishes a crime for the sake of the empire, if the Grand Councilors say it is right and the Censors and Remonstrators also say it is right, only then are punishments and rewards applied. Punishments and rewards are applied through the Grand Councilors and the Censors and Remonstrators; in my own mind there is no overflowing joy or overflowing anger. Should there occasionally be disagreement between them, I then examine into the matter and afterward punish or reward, which also stems from this same mind. From this we know that the guiding principles and laws are the guiding principles and laws of the entire empire—the Grand Councilors may carry them out, and the Censors and Remonstrators may speak on them—whereas the sovereign's mind is especially the guiding principle of all guiding principles, employing the Grand Councilors and the Censors and Remonstrators without claiming possession of their functions for itself. Only an enlightened ruler uniquely perceives the source of transformation: having taken up the guiding principles and laws of the empire and entrusted them to worthy Grand Councilors, and furthermore having allowed a few Censors and Remonstrators to speak on them, all the hundred offices and numerous bureaus without exception follow orders in conducting affairs and abide by the law in fulfilling their official duties, while my mind simply governs them with what is fair, impartial, upright, and great. Compare it to a mirror: shining brightly without partiality, neither beauty nor ugliness in the empire can escape it. Compare it to a balance scale: standing firm without wavering, neither lightness nor heaviness in the empire can deceive it. Yet that by which one holds this mirror and balance is something that not only the empire cannot know, but even the ruler himself cannot consciously know. How could this mean forgetting the empire through having an empty mind? One maintains reverent self-composure in non-action, while the mind operates within active governance…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
也夫人主一心而天下則億萬心也天下雖億
萬心而賢之欲陟否之欲黜功之欲賞罪之欲
刑則億萬者皆同是心也人主不自役其智力
於天下而惟以天下之所同欲者經緯於虛明
空湛之中以求當乎天下之人之心是以端冕
凝旒於南面目不煩視耳不煩聽手不煩揮而
能使天下之人無不憬而悟趯而趨爭相勸勉
奮厲思所以去惡而從善冀得吾之陟與賞而
不至爲黜罰之所加是故綱維立而衆赴之如
===
流水風行而天下承之疾若偃草則以運之心
者神也噫此人主之所以恭已也自昔帝王稱
盛治者莫如堯舜觀其九德之采四凶之誅元
凱之舉渾沌三族之去蓋惟聽舜禹皐陶爲之
而獨以其兢業之懷允恭溫恭之度日臨于上
而未嘗自用其勞故曰垂衣裳而天下治者此
也後世非不欲振綱紀以維持天下然或闇於
體要之崇而悅乎煩苛之習忽於倚毗之任而
信乎耳目之專乃其意固與聖人遠矣又奚怪
punctuated: 也。夫人主一心，而天下則億萬心也。天下雖億萬心，而賢之欲陟、否之欲黜、功之欲賞、罪之欲刑，則億萬者皆同是心也。人主不自役其智力於天下，而惟以天下之所同欲者，經緯於虛明空湛之中，以求當乎天下之人之心。是以端冕凝旒於南面，目不煩視，耳不煩聽，手不煩揮，而能使天下之人無不憬而悟、趯而趨，爭相勸勉奮厲，思所以去惡而從善，冀得吾之陟與賞，而不至爲黜罰之所加。是故綱維立而衆赴之如流水，風行而天下承之疾若偃草，則以運之心者神也。噫！此人主之所以恭已也。自昔帝王稱盛治者，莫如堯、舜。觀其九德之采，四凶之誅，元凱之舉，渾沌三族之去，蓋惟聽舜、禹、皐陶爲之，而獨以其兢業之懷、允恭溫恭之度，日臨于上，而未嘗自用其勞。故曰「垂衣裳而天下治」者，此也。後世非不欲振綱紀以維持天下，然或闇於體要之崇，而悅乎煩苛之習；忽於倚毗之任，而信乎耳目之專。乃其意固與聖人遠矣，又奚怪
translation_en: …[making himself reverent in non-action while his mind operates in] action. Now, the ruler has a single mind, whereas the empire has hundreds of millions of minds. Although the empire has hundreds of millions of minds, in desiring that the worthy be promoted and the unworthy demoted, that merit be rewarded and crime punished, those hundreds of millions all share this same mind. The ruler does not tax his own intelligence and strength over the empire, but solely takes what the empire jointly desires and orders it within the empty brightness and clear stillness of his mind, seeking to correspond to the minds of the people of the empire. Therefore, with ceremonial cap set straight and pendant strings still as he faces south, his eyes do not trouble to look, his ears do not trouble to listen, and his hands do not trouble to wave, yet he is able to cause everyone in the empire without exception to awaken in realization and leap forward in haste, vying to encourage and rouse one another, pondering how to cast off evil and follow the good, hoping to obtain our promotion and reward and avoid being subjected to demotion and punishment. For this reason, when the overarching principles are established, the multitude flocks to them like flowing water; when his transformative influence moves like the wind, the empire submits to it as swiftly as grass bending before it. This is because that which operates within his mind is神 (wondrously spiritual). Ah! This is how the ruler makes himself reverent. Among emperors and kings since antiquity praised for flourishing governance, none equal Yao 堯 and Shun 舜. Observing the selection of those possessing the Nine Virtues, the punishment of the Four Culprits, the elevation of the "Eight Worthies" (Ba Yuan 八元) and "Eight Talents" (Ba Kai 八凱), and the banishment of Hundun 渾沌 and the other three clans, they simply left it to Shun, Yu 禹, and Gao Yao 皐陶 to carry out, while they alone, with a spirit of cautious diligence and a demeanor of sincere and gentle reverence, presided daily from above without ever expending their own toil. Thus, when it is said, "They let their robes hang down and the empire was governed," this is what is meant. Later ages did not fail to desire to rouse the overarching principles and discipline in order to sustain the empire; yet some were blind to the exaltation of essential principles while delighting in the habit of vexatious pettiness, or neglected the responsibility of relying on trusted ministers while putting faith in the monopoly of their own eyes and ears. Their intentions were indeed far removed from those of the sages—how then is it any wonder…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
其治之不古若哉雖然君心亦未易言也虛靈
之中理欲相爲貞勝而夠四方之聲色玩好日
爲吾蠹者又雜然交於其前是故貴有以養之
而養之之功則莫要於主敬夫惟戒謹於燕閒
之暇緝熙於宥密之衷使此心純然天理一毫
物欲不得以累之而又親賢臣遠小人于以講
明乎義理之歸而閑塞其私邪之路故不勞而
庶績熙無爲而天下治也此又恭己之本也
表
擬輔臣恭撰
===
雝肅殿箴表
進
陸大成
同考試官訓導郭　批〔訓□豐贍體裁典重〕〔又多因文〕
以抒忠愛
同考試官訓導張　批〔體莊而雅辭典而麗懇懇〕〔忠悃〕
溢於言表
同考試官教諭范　批〔以莊雅之詞抒忠悃之意〕〔昔哉〕
punctuated:
其治之不古若哉？雖然，君心亦未易言也。虛靈之中，理欲相爲貞勝，而夠四方之聲色玩好日爲吾蠹者，又雜然交於其前。是故貴有以養之，而養之之功，則莫要於主敬。夫惟戒謹於燕閒之暇，緝熙於宥密之衷，使此心純然天理，一毫物欲不得以累之；而又親賢臣，遠小人，于以講明乎義理之歸，而閑塞其私邪之路，故不勞而庶績熙，無爲而天下治也。此又恭己之本也。

表
擬輔臣恭撰《雝肅殿箴》，進表。
陸大成
同考試官訓導郭　批：〔訓□豐贍，體裁典重，〕〔又多因文〕以抒忠愛。
同考試官訓導張　批：〔體莊而雅，辭典而麗，懇懇〕〔忠悃，〕溢於言表。
同考試官教諭范　批：〔以莊雅之詞，抒忠悃之意，〕〔昔哉。〕
translation_en:
… that their governance does not match that of antiquity? Even so, the ruler's mind is no easy matter to speak of. Within its empty and numinous awareness, principle and desire contend to prevail over one another; meanwhile, the sights, sounds, and curiosities drawn [?] from all four quarters that daily eat away at us like pests mingle tumultuously before him. Therefore, it is vital to have the means to nourish it, and in the effort of nourishing it, nothing is more essential than holding fast to reverence. Only by maintaining caution and apprehension in moments of leisure and repose, and by continuing in bright purity within the quiet depths of the inner mind, can one render this mind purely Heavenly principle, unencumbered by the slightest shred of material desire. Furthermore, by drawing close to worthy ministers and keeping petty men at a distance, one elucidates where moral principle leads and blocks off the paths of selfish perversity. Thus, without toil, all achievements flourish; through non-action, all under Heaven is well governed. This, in turn, is the foundation of reverent self-possession.

Memorial
A memorial written in imitation of Grand Secretaries respectfully composing the "Admonition for the Hall of Harmonious Reverence" (Yongsu dian zhen) and presenting it to the throne.
Lu Dacheng 陸大成
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Guo 郭 comments: "Its admonitory words [?] are rich and ample, its form classical and weighty, and it frequently uses the text to express loyal affection."
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Zhang 張 comments: "Its style is dignified and refined, its diction classical and elegant; earnest and sincere loyalty overflows beyond the words."
Associate Examiner and Instructor Fan 范 comments: "With dignified and refined words, it expresses sentiments of sincere loyalty. Admirable indeed [?]!"

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
考試官侍讀羅　批〔莊重典雅允得大臣箴規之義錄之〕
考試官右中允高　批〔詞贊直而意忠款進規表之有則者〕
萬曆七年某月某日臣某等恭撰
雝肅殿箴
進呈者伏以
聰明作后
九重益儆於銘盤矇瞍奏公一得粗申于納牖
帝治撫泰交之運
聖心廑乾惕之圖職忝疑丞
===
美宜將順臣某等誠惶誠恐頓首頓首上言王
者宅中圖大功先宥密之嚴人臣憂治危
明忠殫謀猷之告故堯兢舜業洊衣戒於
危微而益贊皐謨矢颺言于喜起交儆之
風如在維新之命若開帝謂文王予懷明
德亦臨亦保而畏天之威不識不知以順
帝之則肆闈門肇基風化藹雝雝而在宮
迺鬼神常享克誠凜肅肅其在廟罔時恫
罔時怨禋祀允惠於宗公御于家御于邦
punctuated:
考試官侍讀羅　批：〔莊重典雅，允得大臣箴規之義，錄之。〕
考試官右中允高　批：〔詞贊直而意忠款，進規表之有則者。〕

萬曆七年某月某日，臣某等恭撰《雝肅殿箴》進呈者。伏以聰明作后，九重益儆於銘盤；矇瞍奏公，一得粗申于納牖。帝治撫泰交之運，聖心廑乾惕之圖。職忝疑丞，美宜將順。臣某等誠惶誠恐，頓首頓首，上言：王者宅中圖大，功先宥密之嚴；人臣憂治危明，忠殫謀猷之告。故堯兢舜業，洊衣戒於危微；而益贊皐謨，矢颺言于喜起。交儆之風如在，維新之命若開。帝謂文王，予懷明德。亦臨亦保，而畏天之威；不識不知，以順帝之則。肆闈門肇基風化，藹雝雝而在宮；迺鬼神常享克誠，凜肅肅其在廟。罔時恫，罔時怨，禋祀允惠於宗公；御于家，御于邦，
translation_en:
Examiner Academician Reader-in-Waiting Luo comments: "Dignified and classically elegant, it truly captures the spirit of a great minister's admonition; record it for publication."
Examiner Right Companion to the Heir Apparent Gao comments: "Its words are forthright in praise [?] and its intent loyally sincere; it is a memorial of remonstrance that serves as a model."

On a certain day of a certain month in the seventh year of the Wanli era (1579), Your servants so-and-so and others respectfully compose the "Admonition for the Hall of Harmony and Reverence" (Yongsu dian zhen) and present it to the throne.

We humbly reflect that as the intelligent andclairvoyant one becomes sovereign, the Ninefold Palace grows ever more vigilant through inscriptions on washbasins; and as blind musicians perform their public duty, a single humble insight is roughly set forth as if offering light through a window. Imperial governance embraces an era of harmonious communion between heaven and earth, while the Sacred Mind remains earnestly devoted to plans of unceasing vigilance. Unworthily holding office among the aides and counselors, it is fitting that we comply with and further Your Majesty's virtues.

With utmost trepidation and awe, Your servants so-and-so and others bow our heads to the ground again and again and speak to Your Majesty: When a true king dwells at the center and plans for greatness, his achievement begins with strictness in deep and quiet seclusion; when subjects worry in times of order and feel peril in times of enlightenment, their loyalty is exhausted in reporting counsels and plans. Thus Yao was cautious and Shun industrious, repeatedly robing themselves [?] in warnings over the precariousness of the human mind and the subtlety of the Moral Way; and Yi assisted while Gao Yao offered counsels, setting forth their lofty words in songs of rejoicing and rising action. The custom of mutual admonition seems still present; the mandate of renewal appears as if newly opened. The Lord on High said to King Wen, "I cherish your bright virtue." Whether approached by the spirits or preserved in peace, he stood in awe of the majesty of Heaven; without self-conscious knowledge or calculation, he followed the pattern of the Lord. Therefore, within the inner quarters he laid the foundation of transforming customs, genial and harmonious in the palace; and the spirits and gods constantly accepted his sincere offerings, solemn and reverent in the ancestral temple. With none grieving at the time and none resentful, the pure sacrifices truly accorded with the royal ancestors; governing the family and governing the state, …

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
儀刑過乎下國今聞洪而興亹亹乎宗禰序
其皇皇自純德既遐而徽猷遂邈密房邃
寢忘嗜慾之滑和瓊室瑤臺甘逸豫以滅
德自非
聖以繼聖孰能防之又防茲蓋恭遇
皇帝陛下
天啓神明
日新德業
宮闈體正覩協氣之橫流
===
廟祀躬虞歌
孝思之維則九族既睦尚
獨觀和順之原萬國咸賓猶
深切怠荒之戒迺聿新乎
堯室爰特表以周謨
出入斯欽
憲章益邇自是緝熙
聖域功不越乎戶庭因而
垂拱明堂化遂彌于海宇臣等學寡淵源心勤
punctuated: 儀刑過乎下國。今聞洪而興亹亹乎，宗禰序其皇皇。自純德既遐，而徽猷遂邈，密房邃寢，忘嗜慾之滑和；瓊室瑤臺，甘逸豫以滅德。自非聖以繼聖，孰能防之又防？茲蓋恭遇皇帝陛下：天啓神明，日新德業。宮闈體正，覩協氣之橫流；廟祀躬虞，歌孝思之維則。九族既睦，尚獨觀和順之原；萬國咸賓，猶深切怠荒之戒。迺聿新乎堯室，爰特表以周謨。出入斯欽，憲章益邇。自是緝熙聖域，功不越乎戶庭；因而垂拱明堂，化遂彌于海宇。臣等學寡淵源，心勤
translation_en: …and his model conduct reached across the subordinate states. As his renown [令聞, transcribed 今聞] grew vast and inspired tireless diligence, the ancestral and paternal shrines were arrayed in solemn majesty. Once pure virtue receded into the distant past, however, admirable counsels likewise grew remote: in secluded chambers and deep bedchambers, rulers forgot how sensual desires disturb inner harmony; in jade halls and jasper terraces, they indulged in ease and pleasure to the ruin of their virtue. Unless one sage succeeds another, who is able to guard against this again and again? Now we reverently encounter Your Majesty the Emperor: Heaven has inspired your divine intelligence, and day by day you renew your virtuous achievements. With the inner palace rectified in its proper form, one witnesses harmonious vital energy flowing far and wide; personally attending to the ancestral sacrifices with anxious reverence [? 躬虞], one sings of how your filial thoughts serve as a model. Though the nine grades of kinsmen are already in harmony, you still contemplate in solitude the source of concord and compliance; though the myriad states all come as guests in submission, you still take deeply to heart the warning against indolence and neglect. Thus, having newly renovated the halls of Yao, you have specially displayed the counsels of Zhou. Going out and coming in with reverent awe, you keep the exemplary statutes ever closer at hand. Henceforth, in bringing to radiant perfection the realm of sagehood, the effort does not go beyond doorway and courtyard; and thereby, as you let your robes hang down with hands folded in the Hall of Light, your transforming influence fills the world within the seas. Your servants, shallow in the deep springs of learning yet earnest in heart to…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
獻納惟
深宮幽獨之地眞
明命鑒觀之時雖聖哲圖存方顯陳於
講幄而隱微幾著宜豫養于
淵居謹隨事以納忠輒因經而演訓勿作好勿
作惡懋
建極於中和無荒色無荒禽愼防微于豫怠處
玄默若萬幾之臨在
燕閒同四國之正琴瑟未御而德靡悔允矣身
修家齊黍稷匪馨而福不回祇哉神鑒民
悅敬勝義勝敢云繼響於微言惟時惟幾
竊欲揚休于炯誡詞兼得失義舉艱危接
===
自
帝心容備芻蕘之擇扆之
御座庶方鞀鐸之陳昔大寶敷言徒蒙恩於獎
抜洎丹扆納誨未救患於荒遊繄
上下之一心實古今之希覯亶勉勉而
望道式私未見之懷於穆穆以
punctuated: 獻納。惟深宮幽獨之地，眞明命鑒觀之時。雖聖哲圖存，方顯陳於講幄；而隱微幾著，宜豫養于淵居。謹隨事以納忠，輒因經而演訓：勿作好、勿作惡，懋建極於中和；無荒色、無荒禽，愼防微于豫怠。處玄默若萬幾之臨，在燕閒同四國之正。琴瑟未御而德靡悔，允矣身修家齊；黍稷匪馨而福不回，祇哉神鑒民悅。「敬勝」、「義勝」，敢云繼響於微言；「惟時」、「惟幾」，竊欲揚休于炯誡。詞兼得失，義舉艱危。接自帝心，容備芻蕘之擇；扆之御座，庶方鞀鐸之陳。昔《大寶》敷言，徒蒙恩於獎抜；洎《丹扆》納誨，未救患於荒遊。繄上下之一心，實古今之希覯。亶勉勉而望道，式私未見之懷；於穆穆以
translation_en: … in offering advice and counsel. Only in the secluded solitude of the deep palace is it truly the moment when the Bright Mandate watches and inspects. Aunque the portraits and records of sages and wise men are presently displayed openly in the lecture tent, the subtle signs that first become manifest in the hidden and minute ought to be nurtured beforehand in Your Majesty's deep dwelling. We respectfully offer our loyalty according to each matter, and forthwith elaborate the teachings on the basis of the Classics: "Have no偏 [partial] likings, have no partial dislikes," and strive to establish the Supreme Ultimate in equilibrium and harmony; "Do not be wildly addicted to sensual pleasure, do not be wildly addicted to the chase," and cautiously guard against the minutest beginnings of indulgence and indolence. Abide in quiet silence as though attending to the myriad affairs of state; remain in leisure and ease as though rectifying the four quarters of the realm. Before the zithers and lutes are even played, virtue leaves nothing to regret—truly, the person is cultivated and the family regulated! Though millet and grain are not in themselves fragrant, blessings do not turn away—reverently indeed do the spirits inspect and the people rejoice! With "reverence prevailing" and "righteousness prevailing," how dare we claim to echo those subtle words? With "being timely" and "attending to theincipient," we humbly wish to extol the splendor of these shining admonitions. The words encompass both successes and failures, and the meanings set forth difficulties and perils. Received directly into the Emperor's heart, may they be permitted to serve among the selections from humble grass-cutters and wood-gatherers; set as a screen behind the Imperial Throne, may they match the presentations made to the hand-drum and wooden-clapper bell. In the past, when words were set forth in the "Inscription on the Great Treasure" (Dabao zhen), the author merely received favor through promotion and selection; and when admonitions were offered in the "Six Admonitions of the Cinnabar Screen" (Danyi liuzhen), they failed to rescue the ruler from the calamity of dissolute excursions. Truly, such unity of heart between ruler and subjects is a rare sight from antiquity to the present. Truly, striving tirelessly and gazing toward the Way, we cherish in private the feeling of not yet having seen it; oh, with august solemnity…

Third Session.

Five Policy Essays.

First Question: Lu Dacheng 陸大成.

Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Li: The combined sacrifice at the suburban altars and the joint pairing of the Two Progenitors is a grand institution established immutable for ten thousand generations through our Emperor's approving acceptance of the chief ministers' advice. This policy essay synthesizes broadly and surveys far, answering point by point with precision and detail; its citations and judgments have a firm direction. Moreover, its discussion of benevolence and filial piety deeply grasps the fundamental root. He is a scholar of practical utility and ought to be recorded.

Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Pan: Our Imperial Ancestor's institution of the suburban sacrifices sets a model for a hundred kings. Now, when deliberations proposed to carry it out, our Sacred Emperor devoutly cherished and approvingly accepted the advice—truly a rare sight in ten thousand generations. This composition not only elucidates the principles of separation and combination, difference and sameness, but at the end further summarizes the substance of benevolence and filial piety. title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
聖情之助
考試官侍讀羅　批
郊丘
合祀確有定見而綜覽考據至詳且明末復申以仁孝之說是足裨
廟謨矣敬錄之爲
當宁獻
考試官右中允高　批
郊丘
合祀
===
竝配我
祖
宗曆謨裁畫永垂不刊之典我
皇上嗣大曆服制倫兼盡方欲仰承
前烈而舉行之子能詳古質今折衷允當首錄之以備采擇
明於天之道者禮其可以興乎通於聖之
撰者禮其可以言乎蓋傳稱帝王之事莫
大乎承天之序承天之序莫重於郊祀而
孝經云孝莫大於嚴父嚴父莫大於配天
punctuated:
聖情之助。
考試官侍讀羅　批：郊丘合祀，確有定見，而綜覽考據，至詳且明；末復申以仁孝之說，是足裨廟謨矣，敬錄之爲當宁獻。
考試官右中允高　批：郊丘合祀、竝配，我祖宗曆謨裁畫，永垂不刊之典。我皇上嗣大曆服，制倫兼盡，方欲仰承前烈而舉行之。子能詳古質今，折衷允當，首錄之以備采擇。
明於天之道者，禮其可以興乎！通於聖之撰者，禮其可以言乎！蓋傳稱：「帝王之事，莫大乎承天之序；承天之序，莫重於郊祀。」而《孝經》云：「孝莫大於嚴父，嚴父莫大於配天。」…
translation_en:
…an aid to the sacred sentiments of the Emperor.

Examiner Luo, Expositor-in-waiting (侍讀), comments: On the combined sacrifice at the suburban altars, the candidate holds a firm and definite view, and his comprehensive survey and evidential research are extremely detailed and clear. At the end, he further expounds the doctrine of benevolence and filial piety. This is sufficient to assist the deliberations of the ancestral temple; I respectfully record it to present to the throne.

Examiner Gao, Right Companion of the Heir Apparent (右中允), comments: The combined sacrifice and joint pairing at the suburban altars was planned and decided by the wise counsels of our Imperial Ancestors, handing down forever an immutable canon. Our Augustus the Emperor, having succeeded to the great dynastic mandate and fully perfected both ritual institutions and human relationships, now wishes to reverently carry forward the illustrious achievements of his predecessors and put them into practice. The candidate is able to detail antiquity and examine the present, striking a fair and proper balance; I record this in first place to prepare it for imperial selection.

For one who understands the Way of Heaven, rites may indeed be raised up! For one who comprehends the works of the sages, rites may indeed be spoken of! For tradition states: "Among the affairs of emperors and kings, none is greater than upholding the order of Heaven; in upholding the order of Heaven, none is weightier than the suburban sacrifice." And the Classic of Filial Piety (Xiaojing 孝經) says: "In filial piety nothing is greater than revering one's father; in revering one's father nothing is greater than pairing him with Heaven." …

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
地上圓丘之制曰禮天神夏日至澤中方
丘之制曰禮地祇此言分祀者所繇昉與
夫周頌昊天有成命小序以爲郊祀天地
周禮大宗伯以禋祀祀昊天上帝而不及
地祇則周家固亦合祀矣若乃蒼璧黃琮
四圭兩圭之類特其禮神之器數施於天
地者不同而未可據爲分祀之證也後世
所稱引者僅大司樂數語而胡宏吳澂已
謂其剌繆非知禮之言矣又可深泥之哉
===
漢氏而降大都主合祀者什六七而主分
祀者什二三漢高增秦畤爲五祀五帝自
武帝以來竝郊見泰畤于甘泉武帝又因
幸汾陰立后土祠脽上然甘泉脽竝在遠
非都邑之郊也祀泰畤以正月后土以三
月非二至之期也成帝建始中罷甘泉汾
陰定南北郊于長安劉向深以爲不可至
光武寛采元始故事合祀天地于南郊漢
志稱爲圓壇八陛中又爲重壇天地位其
punctuated:
地上圓丘之制，曰「禮天神」；夏日至澤中方丘之制，曰「禮地祇」。此言分祀者所繇昉與？夫《周頌·昊天有成命》，《小序》以爲郊祀天地；《周禮·大宗伯》「以禋祀祀昊天上帝」，而不及地祇，則周家固亦合祀矣。若乃蒼璧、黃琮、四圭、兩圭之類，特其禮神之器數施於天地者不同，而未可據爲分祀之證也。後世所稱引者，僅《大司樂》數語，而胡宏、吳澂已謂其剌繆，非知禮之言矣，又可深泥之哉？
漢氏而降，大都主合祀者什六七，而主分祀者什二三。漢高增秦畤爲五，祀五帝。自武帝以來，竝郊見泰畤于甘泉；武帝又因幸汾陰，立后土祠脽上。然甘泉、脽竝在遠，非都邑之郊也；祀泰畤以正月，后土以三月，非二至之期也。成帝建始中，罷甘泉、汾陰，定南北郊于長安，劉向深以爲不可。至光武，寛采元始故事，合祀天地于南郊，《漢志》稱「爲圓壇八陛，中又爲重壇，天地位其
translation_en:
… the system of the Round Mound on high ground, which says "to worship the spirits of Heaven"; and at the summer solstice, the system of the Square Mound in the marsh, which says "to worship the deities of Earth." Is this not where the advocacy of separate sacrifices originated? Now, regarding "Haotian you chengming" (August Heaven Has a Determinate Mandate) in the Sacrificial Odes of Zhou (Zhou song), the Lesser Preface (Xiaoxu) takes it to be the suburban sacrifice to Heaven and Earth; and in the "Grand Master of Ceremonies" (Da zongbo) section of the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli), it speaks of "worshipping August Heaven the Supreme Di with the pure burnt offering" without mentioning the deities of Earth—thus the House of Zhou indeed also practiced joint sacrifice. As for the azure bi-jade, yellow cong-jade, four-pronged gui-tablet, two-pronged gui-tablet, and the like, these were merely differences in the ceremonial implements and quantities applied to Heaven and Earth in worshipping the spirits, and cannot be relied upon as proof of separate sacrifices. What later generations cited was merely a few words from the "Grand Director of Music" (Da siyue), yet Hu Hong 胡宏 and Wu Cheng 吳澂 already called them perverse and erroneous, not the words of someone who understands ritual—how then can one cling stubbornly to them?
From the Han dynasty onward, on the whole those who advocated joint sacrifice accounted for six or seven out of ten, while those who advocated separate sacrifices accounted for two or three out of ten. Emperor Gao of Han increased the Qin altars (zhi) to five to sacrifice to the Five Emperors. From Emperor Wu onward, they regularly performed the suburban audience at the Grand Altar (Taizhi) at Ganquan; Emperor Wu also, on the occasion of an imperial progress to Fenyin, established the Shrine of Sovereign Earth (Houtu) atop the Sui mound. Yet Ganquan and the Sui mound were both far away, not in the suburbs of the capital city; and sacrificing at the Grand Altar in the first month and to Sovereign Earth in the third month did not follow the timing of the two solstices. During the Jianshi era (32–29 BCE) of Emperor Cheng, Ganquan and Fenyin were abolished and the northern and southern suburban altars were established at Chang'an, which Liu Xiang 劉向 deeply considered improper. By the time of Emperor Guangwu, he broadly [?] adopted the precedents of the Yuanshi era (1–5 CE) and jointly sacrificed to Heaven and Earth at the southern suburb; the Treatise of the History of the Han (Hanzhi) states that "they made a round altar with eight flights of steps, and in the center made a second-tier altar, where the seats of Heaven and Earth were placed…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
上皆南鄉西上是也唐開元禮皇地祇于
南郊合祭宋自建隆以來皆合祭元豐一
議元祐再議紹聖三議訖于合蓋分而
不合者惟魏太和周建德隋開皇唐先天
宋元豐六年凡五見耳愚嘗究覽禮家聚
訟之談主合祀者曰天包乎地地不可與
天抗也曰天地如父母同牢而食不可以
異位也主分祀者曰順陰陽辨時位各依
象類以求之其指各有攸當愚以爲禮非
===
從天降非從地出由人心生者也易不云
乎乾稱乎父坤稱乎母王者君天下而爲
之子崇母以抗父而判剟爲二非人道之
經也使父母隔室而處邈焉南北非人情
之順也揆之禮義合祀其正矣烏可局守
類求之說很云黷亂厖雜昧事天地明察
之道而訾之哉洪惟我
太祖高皇帝誕膺
寶命爲神靈主有天下之初即建
punctuated: 上，皆南鄉，西上，是也。唐《開元禮》皇地祇于南郊合祭。宋自建隆以來皆合祭，元豐一議，元祐再議，紹聖三議，訖于合。蓋分而不合者，惟魏太和、周建德、隋開皇、唐先天、宋元豐六年，凡五見耳。愚嘗究覽禮家聚訟之談：主合祀者曰，天包乎地，地不可與天抗也；曰，天地如父母，同牢而食，不可以異位也。主分祀者曰，順陰陽，辨時位，各依象類以求之。其指各有攸當。愚以爲禮非從天降，非從地出，由人心生者也。《易》不云乎：「乾稱乎父，坤稱乎母。」王者君天下而爲之子，崇母以抗父，而判剟爲二，非人道之經也；使父母隔室而處，邈焉南北，非人情之順也。揆之禮義，合祀其正矣。烏可局守類求之說，很云黷亂厖雜、昧事天地明察之道而訾之哉？洪惟我太祖高皇帝，誕膺寶命，爲神靈主。有天下之初，即建
translation_en:
… top, both facing south, with the west as the seat of honor"—this is what is meant. In the Tang dynasty, the Rituals of the Kaiyuan Era (Kaiyuan li) prescribed the joint sacrifice to the Sovereign Earth Deity at the southern suburb. In the Song dynasty, from the Jianlong era (960–963) onward, they were always sacrificed to jointly; the matter was debated once in the Yuanfeng era (1078–1085), a second time in the Yuanyou era (1086–1094), and a third time in the Shaosheng era (1094–1098), ultimately ending in joint sacrifice. Indeed, the separation without joint sacrifice occurred only five times in all: during the Taihe era of the Northern Wei, the Jiande era of the Northern Zhou, the Kaihuang era of the Sui, the Xiantian era of the Tang, and the sixth year of the Yuanfeng era (1083) of the Song.

I have thoroughly examined the contentious debates among ritual specialists. Those who advocate joint sacrifice say: "Heaven encompasses Earth, so Earth cannot stand as an equal rival to Heaven"; and they say: "Heaven and Earth are like father and mother, who share the same sacrificial animals and dine together, and thus must not be placed in separate seats." Those who advocate separate sacrifices say: "One should accord with yin and yang, distinguish the seasons and positions, and seek each according to its emblematic category." Each of their arguments has its own validity. Yet I consider that ritual does not descend from Heaven, nor does it issue from Earth; it is born from the human heart. Does not the Book of Changes (Yi) say: "Qian is called the father, and Kun is called the mother"? The true king rules All under Heaven as their son. To elevate the mother to rival the father, cleaving and dividing them into two, is not the constant norm of the human way; to cause one's father and mother to dwell in separate chambers, far apart in the north and south, is not in accord with human feeling. Measured against the principles of ritual, joint sacrifice is the orthodox way. How could one narrowly cling to the theory of seeking by category, obstinately calling [joint sacrifice] promiscuous, disorderly, and雜 [mixed/confused], or criticize it for being blind to the way of serving Heaven and Earth with clear discernment [Cf. Book of Rites, Jiyi]?

Humbly reflecting upon our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu Gao Huangdi), he grandly received the precious Mandate and became the lord of spirits and numina. At the very beginning of his possession of All under Heaven, he immediately constructed…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
圜丘于鍾山之陽
方丘于鍾山之陰每歲分祀
天地行之數年雨暘未若洪應衍忒休乃斷自
宸衷定爲
合祀之制以十二年春肇行于
大祀殿其夕天宇澄霽星緯昭煥祥飈慶雲光
彩燁煜若有鑾荅於是
親製樂歌以著明貺焉夫天地並祀有合食之
親無分抗之迹得其順矣首春上辛先庶
===
事而舉又三陽之月地天交泰得其時矣
六宗山川羣神各爲壇以從祀合乎有虞
肆類之典矣立兆國陽爲屋而祭蓋兼用
周家泰壇明堂之制而不盡拘司樂之文
矣於卓哉精當明備丕天之大律也
列聖祗循行之百六十餘年
上帝鑒歆萬靈嘉饗休徵具歛祉福叢臻有由
然哉迨我
世宗肅皇帝中興建極禮百王禮樂之宗于時
punctuated: 圜丘于鍾山之陽、方丘于鍾山之陰，每歲分祀天地。行之數年，雨暘未若，洪應衍忒。休乃斷自宸衷，定爲合祀之制。以十二年春，肇行于大祀殿。其夕，天宇澄霽，星緯昭煥，祥飈慶雲，光彩燁煜，若有鑾荅。於是親製樂歌，以著明貺焉。夫天地並祀，有合食之親，無分抗之迹，得其順矣；首春上辛，先庶事而舉，又三陽之月，地天交泰，得其時矣；六宗、山川、羣神各爲壇以從祀，合乎有虞肆類之典矣；立兆國陽，爲屋而祭，蓋兼用周家泰壇、明堂之制，而不盡拘《司樂》之文矣。於卓哉！精當明備，丕天之大律也。列聖祗循，行之百六十餘年，上帝鑒歆，萬靈嘉饗，休徵具歛，祉福叢臻，有由然哉！迨我世宗肅皇帝中興建極，禮百王禮樂之宗。于時
translation_en: … the Circular Mound Altar (Huanqiu) on the southern slope of Mount Zhong (Zhongshan) and the Square Mound Altar (Fangqiu) on the northern slope of Mount Zhong, sacrificing separately to Heaven and Earth each year. After this was practiced for several years, rain and sunshine were not seasonable, and the great responses showed anomalies. Happily [?], deciding from His Imperial mind, He established the system of joint sacrifice. In the spring of the twelfth year [of Hongwu, 1379], it was performed for the first time in the Hall of Great Sacrifices (Dasi dian). That evening, the firmament was clear and bright, the stars and planets shone brilliantly, auspicious breezes and felicitous clouds gleamed with resplendent radiance, as if an imperial carriage were answering [? 鑾荅, for 響荅]. Thereupon He personally composed musical songs to make manifest the luminous favor. Now, sacrificing to Heaven and Earth together embodies the intimacy of dining together without the trace of division and rivalry—thus attaining proper harmony. Performing it on the first xin day of the first month of spring, prior to all other affairs, and in the month of the three yang when Earth and Heaven交泰 (interpenetrate in peace)—thus attaining the proper season. Setting up separate altars for the Six Honored Ones (Liuzong), mountains and rivers, and the myriad spirits to receive ancillary sacrifices conforms to the canon of the "sacrifice to the Supreme Ruler and the Six Honored Ones" (silie) of the Lord of Yu [Shun]. Establishing the sacred precinct in the southern suburb of the capital and building a roofed structure in which to sacrifice combines the Zhou dynasty systems of the Great Altar (Taitan) and the Hall of Light (Mingtang), without being wholly bound by the literal text of the Director of Music (Siyue) [in the Rites of Zhou]. Oh, how magnificent! Precise, fitting, luminous, and complete—it is the great statute under vast Heaven! Successive sacred emperors reverently followed it, practicing it for over one hundred and sixty years. The Lord on High looked down with favor and accepted the offerings, the myriad spirits delighted in the sacrifices, auspicious verifications were all gathered, and blessings and felicity arrived in abundance—truly there was a reason for this! Coming down to our Emperor Shizong Su [the Jiajing Emperor], who revived the dynasty and established the supreme standard, honoring [? 禮] the traditions of rites and music of the hundred kings—at that time…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
世宗雖建立
二郊而中世以後第行
祈穀
大饗于
內殿
圓方之祭竟不親舉豈非
聖心亦有所未安俟
後聖之更定者耶至于尊祖配天之禮古有以
始祖配者周之后稷是也有以受命之君
===
配者漢之高祖是也夫配天以功德而功
德孰大于開剏者則周之祀稷固明德光
靈之遠也而漢之祀高祖非以崛起在位
爲帝者首乎有天帝各配者周以稷配郊
又以文王配明堂漢以高祖配郊又以光
武配明堂是也有祖宗竝配者唐垂拱開
元以高祖太宗配昊天宋至道以太祖太
宗配圓丘是也夫廟壓于祖昭穆對向非
嫌也郊壓于天祖宗序列非嫌也然則天
punctuated: 世宗雖建立二郊，而中世以後，第行祈穀、大饗于內殿，圓方之祭，竟不親舉，豈非聖心亦有所未安，俟後聖之更定者耶？至于尊祖配天之禮，古有以始祖配者，周之后稷是也；有以受命之君配者，漢之高祖是也。夫配天以功德，而功德孰大于開剏者？則周之祀稷，固明德光靈之遠也；而漢之祀高祖，非以崛起在位，爲帝者首乎？有天帝各配者，周以稷配郊，又以文王配明堂；漢以高祖配郊，又以光武配明堂是也。有祖宗竝配者，唐垂拱、開元以高祖、太宗配昊天；宋至道以太祖、太宗配圓丘是也。夫廟壓于祖，昭穆對向非嫌也；郊壓于天，祖宗序列非嫌也。然則天…
translation_en: Although Shizong (the Jiajing Emperor) established the Two Suburban Altars, from the middle years of his reign onward, he merely performed the Prayer for Grain and the Great Sacrifice in the Inner Palace, and the sacrifices at the Round Mound and Square Altar were ultimately never conducted by him in person. Could it not be that the Sacred Mind also felt some unease in this, awaiting a later sage to revise and settle it? As for the rite of honoring the ancestors as coadjutors to Heaven: in antiquity there was the practice of making the Progenitor the coadjutor, such as Hou Ji in the Zhou dynasty; and there was the practice of making the sovereign who received the Mandate the coadjutor, such as Gaozu in the Han dynasty. Now, being associated with Heaven rests upon meritorious achievement and virtue, and what meritorious achievement and virtue are greater than those of founding a dynasty? Thus the Zhou sacrifice to Ji indeed reflected the far-reaching brilliance of his luminous virtue and divine spirit; and as for the Han sacrifice to Gaozu, was it not because he rose rapidly to the throne to become the first among the emperors? There was also the practice of assigning separate coadjutors to Heaven and the Supreme Lord (Di): the Zhou made Ji the coadjutor at the suburban sacrifice and further made King Wen the coadjutor in the Hall of Light (Mingtang), while the Han made Gaozu the coadjutor at the suburban sacrifice and further made Guangwu the coadjutor in the Hall of Light. And there was the practice of making both the dynastic founder (Zu) and exemplar (Zong) joint coadjutors: in the Chuigong and Kaiyuan eras of the Tang, Gaozu and Taizong were made joint coadjutors to Vast Heaven (Haotian), and in the Zhidao era of the Song, Taizu and Taizong were made joint coadjutors at the Round Mound. Now, in the ancestral temple all are subordinated to the First Ancestor, so the zhao and mu generations facing one another is no cause for scruple; at the suburban altar all are subordinated to Heaven, so the founder and exemplar being arrayed in sequence is no cause for scruple. This being so, assigning separate coadjutors to Heaven…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
帝各配者固章別之道也而祖宗竝配亦
何可以連袵䕫席議其非禮乎我
太祖之始建
郊以
仁祖配是周祀后稷溯本祥源意也而
成祖以
太祖配則如漢奉高祖崇功德之特起矣
仁宗時以
二祖配是唐宋所已行稱情而合禮者也
===
世宗乃獨奉
太祖配
南北郊其
祈穀之祭以
成祖同配尋亦不行蓋始猶稍采郊祀宗祀之
遺而終竟以父子相竝爲嫌矣夫
成祖再造區夏
奠鼎燕京
駿德豐功實同肇刱而推舉未至非褒敭
punctuated: 帝各配者，固章別之道也；而祖宗竝配，亦何可以連袵䕫席議其非禮乎？我太祖之始建郊，以仁祖配，是周祀后稷、溯本祥源意也；而成祖以太祖配，則如漢奉高祖、崇功德之特起矣。仁宗時以二祖配，是唐、宋所已行，稱情而合禮者也。世宗乃獨奉太祖配南北郊，其祈穀之祭以成祖同配，尋亦不行。蓋始猶稍采郊祀、宗祀之遺，而終竟以父子相竝爲嫌矣。夫成祖再造區夏，奠鼎燕京，駿德豐功，實同肇刱。而推舉未至，非褒敭
translation_en:
… separately associating an ancestor with Heaven and with the Lord on High is indeed the way to manifest distinction; yet as for jointly associating both founding ancestors, how could one criticize it as contrary to ritual on the grounds that their robes touch and their mats adjoin? When our Grand Progenitor (Taizu 太祖) first established the suburban sacrifice, he associated the Benevolent Progenitor (Renzu 仁祖) with Heaven; this followed the meaning of the Zhou sacrificing to Houji, tracing back to the root and the auspicious source. Then when the Accomplished Progenitor (Chengzu 成祖) associated the Grand Progenitor with Heaven, it was like the Han venerating Gaozu, exalting the extraordinary rise of his merit and virtue. In the time of the Benevolent Ancestor (Renzong 仁宗), both Progenitors were jointly associated in the sacrifice; this was what the Tang and Song had already practiced, corresponding to human feelings and conforming to ritual.

The Epochal Ancestor (Shizong 世宗), however, solely venerated the Grand Progenitor as the associate at the northern and southern suburban altars. For the sacrifice of Prayer for Grain (Qigu 祈穀), he had the Accomplished Progenitor jointly associated, but before long this too was discontinued. Thus at first he still somewhat adopted the legacy of the suburban sacrifice and the Bright Hall ancestral sacrifice, yet in the end he ultimately regarded the placing of father and son side by side as an impropriety to be avoided. Now, the Accomplished Progenitor recreated the realm of China and established the dynastic tripods at Yanjing (Beijing); his great virtue and abundant merit were truly equal to those of a dynastic founder. Yet to fail to reach the utmost in elevating and honoring him is not the ritual for praising and exalting …

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
前烈之禮也
配享百餘年一朝而罷之非孔安是若之義也
且今
祈穀之祭釐正已久而
郊丘配位未復非闕典甚者哉善乎輔臣之
獻議曰歲一舉
合祀而奉
二祖並配尊
太祖更定之制率
列聖世守之規體
世宗未安之情協時宜順人心合禮典應經義
上固已虛懷嘉納久矣惟需然下
明詔諭中外博忝之輿論而昭告之
靈祇不過一潤色恢定間而可以迓
睠顧之休隆繼述之績闡帝王之緒垂宇宙之
摹甚大美也何疑而不爲乎抑愚猶有
獻焉蓋聞議禮者當覈其文秉禮者貴探其
本夫莫尊于天地而合祀之誠父天母地
punctuated: 前烈之禮也。配享百餘年，一朝而罷之，非孔安是若之義也。且今祈穀之祭釐正已久，而郊丘配位未復，非闕典甚者哉？善乎輔臣之獻議曰：「歲一舉合祀，而奉二祖並配，尊太祖更定之制，率列聖世守之規，體世宗未安之情，協時宜，順人心，合禮典，應經義。」上固已虛懷嘉納久矣。惟需然下明詔諭中外，博忝之輿論，而昭告之靈祇，不過一潤色恢定間，而可以迓睠顧之休，隆繼述之績，闡帝王之緒，垂宇宙之摹，甚大美也！何疑而不爲乎？抑愚猶有獻焉。蓋聞議禮者當覈其文，秉禮者貴探其本。夫莫尊于天地，而合祀之，誠父天母地
translation_en:
… the ritual propriety for praising the illustrious achievements of our predecessors. Having been associated as coadjutor in the sacrifices for more than a hundred years, to abolish this status in a single morning is not in accordance with the principle of following what is thoroughly secure and proper. Moreover, at present the Sacrifice of Prayer for Grain has long since been rectified, yet the coadjutor tablet at the Suburban Altar has not been restored—is this not an extreme deficiency in our state rituals? How admirable is the proposal submitted by the Grand Secretaries, which states: “To perform the Joint Sacrifice once a year and revere the Two Ancestors together as coadjutors honors the institution revised and established by Taizu, follows the regulations guarded through the generations by the successive Sacred Emperors, embodies the uneasy sentiments of Shizong, harmonizes with what is timely and fitting, accords with human feelings, conforms to the ritual canons, and corresponds to the meaning of the Classics.” His Majesty has indeed long accepted this favorably with an open mind. It requires only sending down a clear edict in timely fashion to instruct the court and the provinces, consulting broadly [?] with public opinion, and announcing it brightly to the numinous spirits of Heaven and Earth. In no more than the space of a single act of refinement and grand settlement, one may welcome the blessings of Heaven’s loving regard, exalt the achievements of continuing and transmitting ancestral undertakings, illuminate the line of the Emperors and Kings, and hand down a model for the universe—this is a supreme beauty! Why hesitate and not carry it out?

Yet this humble one still has something to offer. For I have heard that those who deliberate on ritual ought to verify its outward forms, while those who uphold ritual value probing its fundamental root. Now, nothing is more revered than Heaven and Earth; to sacrifice to them jointly is truly to treat Heaven as father and Earth as mother …

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
而致親之極也莫親于祖宗而並配之郊
誠天其祖宗而致尊之極也故曰事天如
事親至仁也事親如事天至孝也仁不在
乎合祀之文昊天曰明及爾出王昊天曰
旦及爾游衍精神思慮渾乎孚通之不隔
者親之之實也孝不在乎崇配之文食則
見于羹坐則見于墻陟降上下懍乎保明
之不怠者尊之之實也斯道也
上聖性已得之益加之
===
聖心焉而憲
天法
祖之本立矣執其本以賁飾其文所謂建中和
之極兼總條貫金聲而玉振之煌煌乎萬
世之基不繇今其永垂哉
第二問
石崑玉
同考試官訓導李　批〔曆法甚關治具古今未有劃一之論是對究極天人理數之奧歷歷可稽宜有俾於璣衡者故錄〕
punctuated:
而致親之極也；莫親于祖宗，而並配之郊，誠天其祖宗而致尊之極也。故曰：「事天如事親，至仁也；事親如事天，至孝也。」仁不在乎合祀之文。「昊天曰明，及爾出王；昊天曰旦，及爾游衍。」精神思慮，渾乎孚通之不隔者，親之之實也。孝不在乎崇配之文。食則見于羹，坐則見于墻，陟降上下，懍乎保明之不怠者，尊之之實也。斯道也，上聖性已得之，益加之聖心焉，而憲天法祖之本立矣。執其本以賁飾其文，所謂建中和之極，兼總條貫，金聲而玉振之，煌煌乎萬世之基，不繇今其永垂哉！

第二問
石崑玉
同考試官訓導李　批〔曆法甚關治具，古今未有劃一之論。是對究極天人理數之奧，歷歷可稽，宜有俾於璣衡者，故錄。〕
translation_en:
… and expressing the utmost closeness; nothing is closer than the Imperial Ancestors, and to associate them together as coadjutors in the suburban sacrifice truly treats one's ancestors as Heaven, expressing the utmost reverence. Therefore it is said: "To serve Heaven as one serves one's parents is the highest benevolence; to serve one's parents as one serves Heaven is the highest filial piety." Benevolence does not lie merely in the ritual form of joint sacrifice. "Great Heaven is intelligent, and is with you in all your goings; Great Heaven is clear-seeing, and is with you in your wanderings and indulgences." When spirit and thought are in complete, unobstructed communion with it, that is the substance of closeness toward it. Filial piety does not lie merely in the ritual form of exalted coadjutorship. When eating, to see them in the broth; when sitting, to see them on the wall; ascending and descending, above and below, standing in awe and untiringly preserving and manifesting their virtue—that is the substance of reverence toward them. This Way, His Majesty has already grasped through his sagely nature; if he applies his sagely mind to it all the more, the foundation for modeling himself on Heaven and emulating the Ancestors will be established. Holding fast to this foundation in order to adorn its ritual forms—what is called establishing the ultimate standard of equilibrium and harmony, comprehensively gathering all threads in order, beginning with the sound of bronze bells and concluding with the sound of jade chimes—how brilliantly shall the foundation for ten thousand generations be handed down forever from this day forth!

Second Question
Shi Kunyu 石崑玉
Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Li 李 comments: 〔Calendrical astronomy is of great importance to the instruments of governance, yet from antiquity to the present there has never been a uniform theory. This reply thoroughly investigates the profound principles and numerical regularities of Heaven and humanity, with every detail verifiable. It should be of aid to those in charge of the astronomical instruments, and is therefore selected for inclusion.〕

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭程　批〔讀古今曆法甚悉而於訛之由〕
〔延訪之論尤中肯綮蓋嘗闚象數而有得者〕
同考試官教諭宋　批〔曆法差忒由星官失職所致此〕
〔作辨訛訂舛考據甚悉足見心天文之學者宜録之俾治曆者觀焉〕
同考試官教諭向　批〔曆法深渺難言獨此策考據辨〕
〔析至極分秒尤足爲占天迎日者準故録〕
考試官侍讀羅　批〔曆法甚玄關繫最大是策考據歷代得失〕
〔折衷以虞招賢精考校修舉星官之職足知政所先者録之不徒以文也〕
考試官右中允高　批〔今司天鮮究其術往往推策多失經紀見〕
===
〔是作能不悚然〕
曆法之難言也尚矣書曰在璿璣玉衡以
齊七政易曰澤火革君子以治曆明時夫
七政之運盈縮疎密逆順進退至雜揉靡
定也而奚以使之齊曆象之法考古校今
積算推步宜有術可操也而奚以取諸革
蓋起數於微渺測驗於星躔其運行者有
常而其員機者不滞至一也而至不一也
三才之妙管是矣夫惟沉幾熟慮經緯化
punctuated:
同考試官教諭程　批〔讀古今曆法甚悉，而於訛之由、延訪之論，尤中肯綮，蓋嘗闚象數而有得者。〕
同考試官教諭宋　批〔曆法差忒，由星官失職所致。此作辨訛訂舛，考據甚悉，足見心天文之學者。宜録之，俾治曆者觀焉。〕
同考試官教諭向　批〔曆法深渺難言，獨此策考據辨析，至極分秒，尤足爲占天迎日者準，故録。〕
考試官侍讀羅　批〔曆法甚玄，關繫最大。是策考據歷代得失，折衷以虞，招賢精考校，修舉星官之職，足知政所先者。録之，不徒以文也。〕
考試官右中允高　批〔今司天鮮究其術，往往推策多失經紀。見是作，能不悚然！〕

曆法之難言也，尚矣。《書》曰：「在璿璣玉衡，以齊七政。」《易》曰：「澤火革，君子以治曆明時。」夫七政之運，盈縮疎密、逆順進退，至雜揉靡定也，而奚以使之齊？曆象之法，考古校今，積算推步，宜有術可操也，而奚以取諸「革」？蓋起數於微渺，測驗於星躔，其運行者有常，而其員機者不滞，至一也，而至不一也，三才之妙管是矣。夫惟沉幾熟慮，經緯化…
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Instructor Cheng comments: [He has read up on ancient and modern calendrical methods in great detail, and his discussions on the origins of errors and on seeking out experts especially hit the mark. Clearly he is someone who has looked into the images and numbers of the heavens and gained real insight.]
Associate Examiner Instructor Song comments: [Discrepancies in calendrical computation result from astronomical officials neglecting their duties. This essay distinguishes errors and corrects mistakes with thoroughly detailed evidence, amply demonstrating a scholar who has devoted his mind to astronomy. It should be recorded so that those who regulate the calendar may examine it.]
Associate Examiner Instructor Xiang comments: [Calendrical science is profound, abstruse, and difficult to discuss, yet this policy essay alone researches and analyzes the evidence down to the finest fractions of a second. It is especially worthy to serve as a standard for those who observe the heavens and calculate the progression of the sun; therefore it is recorded.]
Examiner Academician Reader-in-Waiting Luo comments: [Calendrical science is exceedingly abstruse and of the greatest consequence. This policy essay examines the successes and failures of successive dynasties, weighs them with careful judgment [?], and proposes recruiting worthy talents to refine examinations and verifications and to revive the duties of the astronomical officials—sufficiently showing an understanding of the priorities of governance. We record it not merely for its literary merit.]
Examiner Right Companion to the Heir Apparent Gao comments: [Nowadays those in charge of the Directorate of Astronomy rarely master their art, and in their calculations they frequently lose the regular principles. Seeing this piece, how could they not be struck with awe!]

That calendrical methods are difficult to speak of has been true since antiquity. The Book of Documents says: "Examine the pearl-adorned turning sphere and the jade transverse tube in order to align the Seven Regulators." The Book of Changes says: "Lake and Fire form Revolution (Ge); the noble man thereby regulates the calendar and clarifies the seasons." Now, the movements of the Seven Regulators—their waxing and waning, their looseness and density, their retrograde and prograde motions, their advances and retreats—are utmost in their complexity and lack of fixity; how then can they be brought into alignment? And the methods of calendrical astronomy—examining antiquity and verifying the present, accumulating calculations and pacing the heavens—ought to have a fixed technique that can be grasped; why then take their image from "Revolution"? It is because calculations begin in the infinitesimal and observations are tested against the courses of the stars; their movements have constancy, yet their revolving mechanism never stagnates. They are at once supremely unified and supremely varied—the subtlety of the Three Powers is governed right here. Only when one exercises deep foresight and mature deliberation, weaving and tailoring the transformations…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
裁兩戒之外無微不窺四游之內靡神不
洽乃可以與於此然則司其事者詎不甚
重乎哉在昔顓頊氏有重黎唐虞有羲和
夏有昆吾商有巫咸周有萇弘各司其官
以資調燮故晦朔弦望適其節分至啓閉
協其期欽若敬授之化終將賴焉嗣是而
秦漢之間史官喪紀疇人失業故其詳不
可得聞一時言曆象者舉溺其職矣張蒼
本五勝而詘於論著公孫卿射姓輩議造
漢曆而不諳算法張盛景防等署弦望月
食而不通曆元持衡相仗推算依違太常
奉詔雜議迄無所据太史明知錯謬而不
能更撂乾者憂之乃始不愛祿爵廣延宣
問挾技殫慮之士輻湊竝進而自獻於前
雜候鉤校則張壽王徐禹各呈其效先大
先小則編訢衛崇各闘其捷太初四分之
用則亶誦張衡各恣其辨得失更迭劇於
聚訟雖紛呶莫決而爲說寖詳歷代以還
punctuated: 裁，兩戒之外無微不窺，四游之內靡神不洽，乃可以與於此。然則司其事者，詎不甚重乎哉！在昔顓頊氏有重黎，唐、虞有羲、和，夏有昆吾，商有巫咸，周有萇弘，各司其官，以資調燮。故晦朔弦望適其節，分至啓閉協其期，欽若敬授之化，終將賴焉。嗣是而秦、漢之間，史官喪紀，疇人失業，故其詳不可得聞，一時言曆象者舉溺其職矣。張蒼本五勝而詘於論著，公孫卿、射姓輩議造漢曆而不諳算法，張盛、景防等署弦望月食而不通曆元。持衡相仗，推算依違。太常奉詔雜議，迄無所据；太史明知錯謬，而不能更。撂乾者憂之，乃始不愛祿爵，廣延宣問，挾技殫慮之士輻湊竝進，而自獻於前。雜候鉤校，則張壽王、徐禹各呈其效；先大先小，則編訢、衛崇各闘其捷；《太初》、《四分》之用，則亶誦、張衡各恣其辨。得失更迭，劇於聚訟，雖紛呶莫決，而爲說寖詳。歷代以還，
translation_en: … and tailoring its transformations, peering into every subtlety beyond the Two Boundaries (liangjie) and attuning every spirit within the Four Excursions (siyou), can one take part in this. That being so, how could those in charge of this matter not carry the utmost weight! In antiquity, Zhuanxu had Chong and Li, Tang and Yu had Xi and He, the Xia had Kunwu, the Shang had Wu Xian, and the Zhou had Chang Hong; each presided over his office to aid in harmonizing the cosmos. Thus, the dark of the moon, the new moon, the quarter moons, and the full moon met their proper intervals, while the equinoxes, solstices, and beginnings of the seasons accorded with their appointed times; the transformative governance of reverently following Heaven and respectfully bestowing the seasons ultimately depended on this. Thereafter, during the Qin and Han, thecourt historians lost their records and the hereditary astronomers lost their profession, so that the details could no longer be heard, and those of the age who spoke of calendrical astronomy all failed in their duties. Zhang Cang 張蒼 based himself on the conquest cycle of the Five Phases yet fell short in his treatises; Gongsun Qing 公孫卿, She Xing 射姓, and their ilk deliberated on creating the Han calendar without understanding mathematical methods; Zhang Sheng 張盛, Jing Fang 景防, and others registered the quarter moons, full moons, and lunar eclipses without comprehending the calendrical epoch. Holding the balance in mutual reliance, their calculations were hesitant and inconsistent. The Minister of Ceremonies obeyed imperial decrees to hold joint deliberations, yet ultimately had nothing to rely upon; the Grand Scribe clearly knew of the errors and fallacies, yet was unable to reform them. Those who wielded imperial authority [?] were troubled by this, and only then began without grudging emoluments and noble ranks to issue broad invitations and open inquiries, whereupon scholars who possessed technical skills and exhausted their thoughts converged like spokes at a hub, advancing together to present themselves before the throne. In observing diverse phenomena and cross-checking calculations, Zhang Shouwang 張壽王 and Xu Yu 徐禹 each displayed their results; over whether to begin with a long month or a short month, Bian Xin 編訢 and Wei Chong 衛崇 each vied in their ingenuity; over the use of the Taichu (Grand Inception) and Sifen (Quarter-Remainder) calendars, Dan Song 亶誦 and Zhang Heng 張衡 each gave free rein to their arguments. Successes and failures alternated, more fiercely than in a courtroom dispute; and though the clamorous debate remained undecided, their theories grew progressively more detailed. Down through successive dynasties, …

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
法制斯備或起於鍾律或起於著策或起
於晷景此推驗之法以漸而變矣劉洪悟
月行有遲疾劉倬悟日行有盈縮何承天
悟測景以定氣序姜岌悟以月行所衝之
宿爲日所在之度祖冲之始悟歲差張子
信悟月行有交道表裏五星有見伏向背
李淳風悟定朔之制并氣朔閏餘皆同一
術此推驗之法以漸而精矣惟勝國之授
時曆出於許衡郭守敬所定參别同異酌
取中數積日積年之算悉屛不用以之攷
古則增歲餘而損歲差以之推來則增歲
差而損歲餘當時稱其法者謂能發順天
求合之徵證前人附會之失自古及今未
有能逮者也我
太祖高皇帝
太統曆稍采授時之舊設官則幷合華夏占候
則參綜古今儀式精詳神機妙運卽使大
撓執役隸首布算奚足以方焉以故用之
punctuated: 法制斯備：或起於鍾律，或起於著策，或起於晷景，此推驗之法以漸而變矣。劉洪悟月行有遲疾，劉倬悟日行有盈縮，何承天悟測景以定氣序，姜岌悟以月行所衝之宿爲日所在之度，祖冲之始悟歲差，張子信悟月行有交道表裏、五星有見伏向背，李淳風悟定朔之制，并氣朔閏餘皆同一術，此推驗之法以漸而精矣。惟勝國之《授時曆》出於許衡、郭守敬所定，參别同異，酌取中數，積日積年之算悉屛不用；以之攷古，則增歲餘而損歲差，以之推來，則增歲差而損歲餘。當時稱其法者，謂能發順天求合之徵，證前人附會之失，自古及今，未有能逮者也。我太祖高皇帝《太統曆》稍采《授時》之舊，設官則幷合華夏，占候則參綜古今，儀式精詳，神機妙運，卽使大撓執役、隸首布算，奚足以方焉！以故用之
translation_en:
… institutional systems thus became complete: some originated from pitch-pipes and musical temperament, some from yarrow-stalk divination [? 著策 for 蓍策], and some from gnomon shadow measurements. In this way, the methods of calculation and verification gradually changed. Liu Hong 劉洪 realized that the moon's motion has retardation and acceleration; Liu Zhuo 劉倬 realized that the sun's motion has expansion and contraction (equation of center); He Chengtian 何承天 realized how to measure gnomon shadows to determine the sequence of solar terms; Jiang Ji 姜岌 realized how to take the lunar lodge directly opposite the eclipsed moon's path as the degree of the sun's position; Zu Chongzhi 祖冲之 was the first to realize the precession of the equinoxes; Zhang Zixin 張子信 realized that the moon's path falls inside and outside the ecliptic nodes and that the Five Planets have appearances, disappearances, and direct and retrograde motions; and Li Chunfeng 李淳風 realized the system of true syzygy (dingshuo 定朔) and unified solar terms, syzygies, and intercalary remainders under a single computational technique. In this way, the methods of calculation and verification gradually grew more precise.

Yet the Season-Granting Calendar (Shoushi li 授時曆) of the vanquished [Yuan] dynasty, established by Xu Heng 許衡 and Guo Shoujing 郭守敬, compared and distinguished similarities and differences, judiciously adopted mean values, and completely discarded the computation of accumulated days and accumulated years from a superior epoch. When using it to investigate antiquity, one increases the tropical year fraction and reduces the precession of the equinoxes; when using it to project the future, one increases the precession of the equinoxes and reduces the tropical year fraction. Those of that time who praised its method said that it was able to reveal the evidence of following the heavens to seek agreement and prove the errors of earlier scholars' forced correlations—from antiquity to the present, none had been able to equal it.

The Grand Concordance Calendar (Datong li 大統曆 [written 太統曆]) of our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (Taizu Gao Huangdi 太祖高皇帝), largely adopted the old system of the Season-Granting Calendar. In establishing offices, it combined Chinese and foreign [Muslim] bureaus; in observational astronomy, it synthesized ancient and modern practices. Its regulations and formulas are precise and detailed, its marvelous mechanisms operate with subtlety—even if Da Nao 大撓 were to perform the service and Li Shou 隸首 were to lay out the counting rods, how could they suffice to compare with it! title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
至今晝一靡爽視彼漢唐以後未數歲而
輒差者其精密固已相懸即正嘉間之交
食時刻分秒起復方位稍與推驗不協然
比之永平永元之際先後背馳日月乖異
者又奚啻徑庭哉繇斯以譚雖俟諸萬世
無敝可也乃頃者星官失職乖舛昜常遠
邇傳聞以爲駭異夫數出於秒忽以成毫
釐毫釐積累遂成分寸初行生分積分成
度此於法至玄矣乃若躔度儀式粲然可
===
覩即卜祝能辯之而輒已違舛若玆曲算
旁占安所復望萬一閏餘失次交食靡驗
有能如楊岑之先識宗紺之獻言者乎宜
乎廑執事之問也愚生管窺蠡測何足與
知顧嘗竊聞之前人曰天道無端惟理可
以推其幾天道至妙因數可以窮其理理
緣數顯數從理出故班孟堅言治曆之所
當急者三謂專門之裔明理之儒精算之
士均之不可缺一也昔元封間下詔徵募
punctuated:
至今，晝一靡爽。視彼漢、唐以後，未數歲而輒差者，其精密固已相懸。即正、嘉間之交食，時刻、分秒、起復、方位稍與推驗不協，然比之永平、永元之際，先後背馳、日月乖異者，又奚啻徑庭哉！繇斯以譚，雖俟諸萬世無敝可也。

乃頃者星官失職，乖舛昜常，遠邇傳聞，以爲駭異。夫數出於秒忽，以成毫釐，毫釐積累，遂成分寸；初行生分，積分成度，此於法至玄矣。乃若躔度儀式，粲然可覩，即卜祝能辯之，而輒已違舛若玆，曲算旁占，安所復望？萬一閏餘失次，交食靡驗，有能如楊岑之先識、宗紺之獻言者乎？宜乎廑執事之問也。

愚生管窺蠡測，何足與知？顧嘗竊聞之前人曰：「天道無端，惟理可以推其幾；天道至妙，因數可以窮其理。」理緣數顯，數從理出。故班孟堅言治曆之所當急者三，謂專門之裔、明理之儒、精算之士，均之不可缺一也。昔元封間，下詔徵募，

…down to the present day, it has remained uniform and without error. Compared to those calendars after the Han and Tang dynasties that fell into discrepancy within just a few years, its precision is already worlds apart. Even though during the Zhengde (1506–1521) and Jiajing (1522–1566) eras, the hours, quarters, minutes, and seconds of solar and lunar eclipses, as well as the directions of their onset and restoration, did not slightly accord with calculations and observations, yet when compared to the Yongping (58–75) and Yongyuan (89–105) eras of the Han—when predictions and actualities ran counter to one another and the sun and moon were out of step—how could the difference be merely that of a courtyard and a path! Speaking from this perspective, even if we expect it to last for ten thousand generations without defect, it is possible.

Yet recently, the astronomical officials have been derelict in their duties, and anomalies and errors have altered the norm [? 昜常, for 易常]; as reports spread far and near, people regard it with astonishment. Now, numbers arise from seconds and microscopic fractions (miaohu) to form hairs and thousandths (haoli), and as hairs and thousandths accumulate, they consequently form tenths and inches (fencun); the initial movement generates fractions, and accumulated fractions form degrees—in terms of method, this is most profound. Yet when it comes to the ceremonial formats of celestial motions and degrees, which are brilliantly clear to see—such that even diviners and invocators can discern them—if they have already fallen into such error as this, what hope is left for intricate calculations and collateral prognostications? Should the intercalary remainder lose its sequence and eclipses fail to be verified, would there be anyone capable of foresight like Yang Cen 楊岑 or of offering counsel like Zong Gan 宗紺? It is fitting indeed that this has aroused the concern of the examiners' question.

With my narrow view through a tube and measurement with a gourd, how am I worthy of participating in such knowledge? Yet I have ventured to hear from predecessors: "The Way of Heaven has no beginning or end; only through principle (li) can one deduce its subtle incipient tendencies. The Way of Heaven is supremely wondrous; through numbers (shu) one can exhaustively fathom its principle." Principle becomes manifest through numbers, and numbers issue from principle. title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄

text:
聖明在上百度惟貞攝提順紀
曆數得序固無庸輕有所修改以滋悯擾之端
唯是二三疇人僅挾一技史所謂陰陽家
耳顧欽若敬授之鉅典悉揭而畀之其事
則重其學則末此歐陽修氏所慨嘆也且
其訛舛相襲漫無校證昔人謂獨非莫知
獨是莫曉其旨正與此類彼又何所憚而
不覈且弛耶故先臣大學士丘濬請詔求
天下通星曆者以任考驗之責盡講究之
===
方禮部主事鄭善夫請擇海內儒術中有
究心天人之學使得盡觀秘書加以歲月
俾上按往古下訂來今而疇人金鍾慨司
候之弛業亦請歲會月試甄別去留大計
之期茲嚴黜陟事有似緩而實急者此類
是也今誠倣此意行之自世業子弟至於
草澤布衣愽加延訪論定後官如漢人署
職課候覈其中否以為上下又如魏人命
高堂隆楊偉輩推校天文更相劾奏俟其
punctuated: 聖明在上，百度惟貞，攝提順紀，曆數得序，固無庸輕有所修改，以滋悯擾之端。唯是二三疇人，僅挾一技，史所謂陰陽家耳，顧欽若敬授之鉅典，悉揭而畀之，其事則重，其學則末，此歐陽修氏所慨嘆也。且其訛舛相襲，漫無校證，昔人謂獨非莫知，獨是莫曉，其旨正與此類，彼又何所憚而不覈且弛耶？故先臣大學士丘濬請詔求天下通星曆者，以任考驗之責，盡講究之方；禮部主事鄭善夫請擇海內儒術中有究心天人之學，使得盡觀秘書，加以歲月，俾上按往古，下訂來今；而疇人金鍾慨司候之弛業，亦請歲會月試，甄別去留，大計之期，茲嚴黜陟。事有似緩而實急者，此類是也。今誠倣此意行之，自世業子弟至於草澤布衣，愽加延訪，論定後官，如漢人署職課候，覈其中否以為上下；又如魏人命高堂隆、楊偉輩推校天文，更相劾奏，俟其
translation_en: … With the Sage and Enlightened Emperor above, all institutions are upright; the celestial cycle follows its regular order, and the calendrical calculations are in proper sequence. Certainly there is no need to lightly make modifications that would only give rise to confusion and disturbance [? 悯擾]. Yet those few hereditary astronomers possess only a single technical skill—what the histories call the School of Yin and Yang—and still the great canon of reverently following Heaven and respectfully granting the seasons is wholly lifted up and entrusted to them. Their responsibility is weighty, yet their learning is superficial; this is what Ouyang Xiu 歐陽修 lamented with a sigh. Moreover, their errors and discrepancies are passed down from one to another without any collation or verification. When men of the past said, "Even if they alone are wrong, no one knows; even if they alone are right, no one understands," the point applied precisely to cases like this. What then do they have to fear that would keep them from being unverified and lax in their duties? Therefore, the former official and Grand Secretary Qiu Jun 丘濬 requested that an imperial decree be issued to seek out throughout the realm those conversant with astrology and calendrical science, so as to charge them with the responsibility of testing and verification and to exhaust all methods of thorough investigation. Secretary in the Ministry of Rites Zheng Shanfu 鄭善夫 requested that from among the Confucian scholars within the seas, those who had devoted their minds to the study of Heaven and Man be selected and permitted to read all the secret archives, granting them years and months so that they might examine deep antiquity above and establish rules for the present and future below. And the hereditary astronomer Jin Zhong 金鍾, lamenting that the observers had grown lax in their profession, likewise requested annual evaluations and monthly tests to screen and determine who should be dismissed or retained, and that at the time of the Great Evaluation, demotions and promotions be strictly enforced. Among affairs that appear unhurried yet are in reality urgent, such cases are prime examples. If today we truly imitate the intent of these proposals and put them into practice—broadly extending inquiries to invite everyone from the sons and younger brothers of hereditary astronomical families down to commoners in the countryside, appointing them to office only after their merits have been assessed, just as the men of Han assigned posts to test astronomical observations and verified their accuracy to determine higher or lower rank; and again, just as the men of Wei commanded Gaotang Long 高堂隆, Yang Wei 楊偉, and others to calculate and collate celestial phenomena, impeaching and memorializing against one another in turn, and waiting until their…

When men of old said, "Where they alone are wrong, no one knows it; where they alone are right, no one understands it," their meaning applied precisely to cases such as this. What then do those men have to fear that would keep them from growing negligent and lax? Therefore, the former official and Grand Secretary Qiu Jun 丘濬 requested that an edict be issued to seek out throughout the realm those conversant with astrology and calendrical science, to charge them with the responsibility of testing and verification so as to exhaust every method of thorough investigation; the Secretary in the Ministry of Rites Zheng Shanfu 鄭善夫 requested that from among the Confucian scholars within the seas, those who had devoted their minds to the study of Heaven and Man be selected and permitted to read all the secret palace books, granting them years and months so that they might examine deep antiquity above and establish corrections for the present and future below; and the hereditary astronomer Jin Zhong 金鍾, lamenting that the observers had grown lax in their profession, likewise requested annual evaluations and monthly tests to distinguish who should be dismissed and who retained, and that at the time of the Great Reckoning promotions and demotions be strictly enforced. title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
聖明在上百度惟貞攜提順紀
曆數得序固無庸輕有所修改以滋憪擾之端
唯是二三疇人僅挾一技史所謂陰陽家
耳顧欽若敬授之鉅典悉揭而畀之其事
則重其學則末此歐陽修氏所慨嘆也且
其訛舛相襲漫無校證昔人謂獨非莫知
獨是莫曉其旨正與此類彼又何所憚而
不黜且弛耶故先臣大學士丘濬請詔求
天下通星曆者以任考驗之責盡講究之
方禮部主事鄭善夫請擇海內儒術中有
究心天人之學使得盡觀秘書加以歲月
俾上按往古下訂來今而疇人金鍾慨司
===
候之弛業亦請歲會月試甄別去留大計
之期並嚴黜陟事有似緩而實急者此類
是也今誠倣此意行之自世業子弟至於
草澤布衣博加延訪論定後官如漢人署
職課候覈其中否以爲上下又如魏人命
高堂隆楊偉輩推校天文更相劾奏使其
punctuated: 聖明在上，百度惟貞，攜提順紀，曆數得序，固無庸輕有所修改，以滋憪擾之端。唯是二三疇人，僅挾一技，史所謂陰陽家耳；顧欽若敬授之鉅典，悉揭而畀之，其事則重，其學則末，此歐陽修氏所慨嘆也。且其訛舛相襲，漫無校證，昔人謂「獨非莫知，獨是莫曉」，其旨正與此類，彼又何所憚而不黜且弛耶？故先臣大學士丘濬，請詔求天下通星曆者，以任考驗之責，盡講究之方；禮部主事鄭善夫，請擇海內儒術中有究心天人之學，使得盡觀秘書，加以歲月，俾上按往古，下訂來今；而疇人金鍾，慨司候之弛業，亦請歲會月試，甄別去留，大計之期，並嚴黜陟。事有似緩而實急者，此類是也。今誠倣此意行之，自世業子弟，至於草澤布衣，博加延訪，論定後官：如漢人署職課候，覈其中否以爲上下；又如魏人命高堂隆、楊偉輩推校天文，更相劾奏。使其
translation_en:
…With His Sacred Majesty above, all measures are upright; he guides and upholds the regular cycles in harmony, and the calendrical calculations are in proper order. Truly there is no need lightly to make revisions and alterations that would only give rise to confusion and disturbance. Yet those two or three hereditary astronomers possess merely a single technical skill—what the histories call the Yin-Yang school, nothing more. Nevertheless, the grand state canon of "reverently following High Heaven and respectfully bestowing the seasons" is handed over to them in its entirety. Their responsibility is weighty, yet their learning is superficial—this is what Ouyang Xiu 歐陽修 lamented. Moreover, as they pass down errors and discrepancies from one to another without any verification or correction, it is just as a writer of the past said: "When they alone are wrong, no one knows it; when they alone are right, no one understands it." The point applies to just such cases as this—what then do they have to fear that would keep them from being faulty [?] and remiss?

Therefore, the late Grand Secretary Qiu Jun 丘濬 requested that an imperial edict be issued to seek out throughout the realm those conversant with astrology and calendrical science, to entrust them with the responsibility of testing and verification and to exhaust every method of thorough investigation. And the hereditary astronomer Jin Zhong 金鍾, lamenting that the observers of the astronomical signs were neglecting their profession, likewise requested that there be annual assessments and monthly tests to screen who should be dismissed and who retained, and that at the time of the Great Triennial Evaluation, demotions and promotions be strictly enforced. Among matters that appear unhurried on the surface yet are in reality urgent, such cases are prime examples.

If today we truly emulate this intent and put it into practice—broadly seeking out and inviting candidates ranging from the sons and younger brothers of hereditary astronomical families to commoners in the countryside, evaluating and settling upon their capabilities before appointing them to office; just as the men of Han assigned posts to test astronomical observations and verified their accuracy or inaccuracy to determine higher or lower rank; and just as the men of Wei commanded the likes of Gaotang Long 高堂隆 and Yang Wei 楊偉 to calculate and verify celestial phenomena, impeaching and memorializing against one another—and if we allow those who…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
積有勞勩卽顯陟隨之則術業寖興人心
競奮庶幾有深明曆理如楊雄善立差法
如邵雍沉潛智巧如許衡郭守敬者以應
當宁之求而于敬天勤民之務未必無少補矣
若謂中和位育無關於器數此迂儒之闊
論非明問意也愚何敢贅陳焉
第三問
甯瑞鯉
同考試官訓導郭　批〔以聖賢之與葩漢魏之英〕
===
可誦可傳
同考試官訓導張　批〔古聖賢兼善獨善是能立德立業者茲作羞其發其蘊且務調諸詞句在秦漢之上其立言者與敬錄〕
同考試官教諭范　批〔獨善兼善之旨發揮明盡且敘〕
事斷制種種臻妙始非灸辭以後文字可以傳矣
考試官侍讀羅　批〔善無窮蓋此聖學也是策品隲精確發揮〕
明盡必有養之士宜錄以式
考試官右中允高　批〔此一策道術人心所關乃辨析幾微論〕
議激切非具卓識者不能宜錄
punctuated:
積有勞勩，卽顯陟隨之。則術業寖興，人心競奮，庶幾有深明曆理如楊雄，善立差法如邵雍，沉潛智巧如許衡、郭守敬者，以應當宁之求，而于敬天勤民之務，未必無少補矣。若謂中和位育無關於器數，此迂儒之闊論，非明問意也，愚何敢贅陳焉。

第三問
甯瑞鯉
同考試官訓導郭　批：〔以聖賢之與，葩漢魏之英，〕可誦可傳。
同考試官訓導張　批：〔古聖賢兼善獨善，是能立德立業者。茲作羞其發其蘊，且務調諸詞句，在秦漢之上，其立言者與？敬錄。〕
同考試官教諭范　批：〔獨善兼善之旨，發揮明盡。且敘〕事斷制，種種臻妙，始非灸辭以後文字，可以傳矣。
考試官侍讀羅　批：〔善無窮，蓋此聖學也。是策品隲精確，發揮〕明盡，必有養之士，宜錄以式。
考試官右中允高　批：〔此一策，道術人心所關，乃辨析幾微，論〕議激切，非具卓識者不能，宜錄。
translation_en:
… Once they have accumulated meritorious service and toil, prominent promotions should immediately follow. Then the technical arts will gradually flourish and men's minds will vie in exertion. Perhaps there will emerge those who deeply understand the principles of the calendar like Yang Xiong 楊雄, who excel at establishing the method of precession like Shao Yong 邵雍, or who possess profound reflection and ingenious skill like Xu Heng 許衡 and Guo Shoujing 郭守敬, so as to answer the sovereign's quest; and for the task of revering Heaven and being diligent toward the people, this will not necessarily be without some small benefit. As for claiming that equilibrium, harmony, Heaven and Earth keeping their proper places, and all things flourishing have nothing to do with instruments and mathematical calculations—this is the impractical talk of pedantic scholars and is not the intent of your perceptive question; how would I dare to state it superfluously?

Question Three
Ning Ruili 甯瑞鯉
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Guo 郭 comments: 〔Combining the depth [?] of the sages and worthies with the literary brilliance of the Han and Wei—〕 worthy of recitation and transmission.
Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Zhang 張 comments: 〔When the ancient sages and worthies perfected the empire together with others or perfected themselves in solitude, they were able to establish virtue and great enterprise. This essay nearly [?] brings forth their profound essence, and moreover strives to harmonize its phrasing and diction, placing it above the Qin and Han. Is he not one who establishes enduring words? Respectfully recorded.〕
Associate Examiner and Instructor Fan 范 comments: 〔The purport of perfecting oneself in solitude and perfecting the empire together with others is expounded with complete clarity. Moreover, in narrating〕 events and making decisive judgments, every aspect reaches perfection. Truly this is not the sort of writing produced after the ornate rhetoric of later ages [?]; it deserves to be transmitted!
Examiner and Academician Reader-in-Waiting Luo 羅 comments: 〔Goodness is inexhaustible—such is the learning of the sages. This policy essay evaluates with precision and expounds〕 with complete clarity. He must be a scholar of cultivated attainment; it should be recorded as a model.
Examiner and Right Companion to the Heir Apparent Gao 高 comments: 〔This policy question concerns moral learning and the human mind; yet he analyzes the subtlest nuances and argues〕 with ardent urgency. None withoutoutstanding insight could achieve this; it should be recorded.

萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
汲汲於兼善也然誦詩讀書以樂堯舜之
道其修爲爲於有莘者果何物哉彼得成湯
爲之後先故行而益遠矣而善非有加也
孟氏稱其聖之任諒矣顏子簞食瓢飲終
身陋巷而不改其樂謂之獨善誰曰不宜
乃問仁問爲邦内聖外王之學宛然天下
爲度也彼方進德於夫子之門故潛而未
見耳而善非有損也孟氏稱其賢與禹稷
竝其知顏子哉夫伊尹顏子其次者也伯
===
夷矯節於首陽而風之激也至廉頑起懦
百世師清焉柳下惠蒙耻於三黜而風之
淳也至敦薄銷鄙百世師和焉夫曰師百
世則當時可推矣二子之不遇也如此而
善之及人也如彼謂窮之必獨善可乎直
其心固曰不善足以浼我吾拒之云耳不
善不足以浼我吾玩之云耳而猶不免於
形骸爾我之隔故孟氏謂其隘與不恭而
不由也夫夷下惠又其次者也逌後楊朱
punctuated: 汲汲於兼善也。然誦詩讀書，以樂堯、舜之道，其修爲爲於有莘者，果何物哉？彼得成湯爲之後先，故行而益遠矣，而善非有加也。孟氏稱其「聖之任」，諒矣！顏子簞食瓢飲，終身陋巷而不改其樂，謂之獨善，誰曰不宜？乃問仁、問爲邦，内聖外王之學，宛然天下爲度也。彼方進德於夫子之門，故潛而未見耳，而善非有損也。孟氏稱其賢與禹、稷竝，其知顏子哉！夫伊尹、顏子，其次者也。伯夷矯節於首陽，而風之激也，至廉頑起懦，百世師清焉；柳下惠蒙耻於三黜，而風之淳也，至敦薄銷鄙，百世師和焉。夫曰師百世，則當時可推矣。二子之不遇也如此，而善之及人也如彼，謂窮之必獨善，可乎？直其心固曰：「不善足以浼我，吾拒之」云耳；「不善不足以浼我，吾玩之」云耳，而猶不免於形骸爾我之隔，故孟氏謂其「隘」與「不恭」而不由也。夫夷、下惠，又其次者也。逌後楊朱
translation_en:
…anxious about perfecting the whole empire together. Yet when he chanted the Odes and read the Documents to delight in the Way of Yao and Shun, what indeed was the cultivation he practiced in the fields of Youshen? Because he found Cheng Tang to assist him before and after, his Way was put into practice and reached ever farther—yet his goodness itself had nothing added to it. When Mencius called him "the sage who took on responsibility," how true that was!

Master Yan [Yan Hui] had a bamboo dish of rice and a gourd of drink, dwelling all his life in a mean alley without altering his joy; if one called this perfecting himself alone, who would say it is unfitting? Yet he asked about humaneness and asked about governing a state; his learning of inner sageliness and outer kingliness clearly took the whole empire as its measure. He was just then advancing in virtue at the gate of the Master [Confucius], and so remained hidden and not yet manifest—yet his goodness itself suffered no diminution. When Mencius declared his worthiness equal to that of Yu and Ji, how well he understood Master Yan! Now Yi Yin and Master Yan represent the next tier.

Bo Yi upheld his lofty integrity on Mount Shouyang, and the stirring force of his moral example was such that it made the corrupt pure and the timid resolute, becoming a teacher of purity for a hundred generations. Liuxia Hui endured the disgrace of being dismissed three times, and the simple warmth of his moral example was such that it made the ungenerous kind and the mean-spirited broad-minded, becoming a teacher of harmony for a hundred generations. Now if they are called teachers for a hundred generations, their influence in their own time can be inferred. Such was the ill fortune of these two men in not meeting their proper time, yet such was the reach of their goodness to others—how could one say that in obscurity one necessarily perfects only oneself? It is just that in their hearts the one stubbornly said, "What is not good is enough to defile me, so I reject it," while the other said, "What is not good is not enough to defile me, so I treat it lightly." Thus they still could not avoid a barrier between physical selves, between "you" and "me." Therefore Mencius called them "narrow" and "lacking in respect" and declined to follow their path. Now Bo Yi and Liuxia Hui represent the tier after that. Coming later, Yang Zhu…
