translation_en:
…eagerly striving to share their goodness with all the world. Yet when he chanted the Odes and read the Documents, delighting in the Way of Yao and Shun, what indeed was that cultivation which he practiced in the fields of Youshen? Because he found Cheng Tang to support him before and after, his Way was put into practice and reached ever further—yet nothing was added to his goodness itself. Truly, when Mencius (Mengshi 孟氏) praised him as "the sage who took responsibility upon himself," he was right! Master Yan (Yanzi 顏子) had a single bamboo dish of rice and a gourd of drink, living all his life in a mean alley without letting it affect his joy; if one called this perfecting himself in solitude, who would say it is unfitting? Yet he asked about benevolence and asked about governing a state; his learning of inward sageliness and outward kingliness clearly took the whole empire as its measure. Because he was just then advancing in virtue at the gate of the Master, he remained hidden and unmanifested—yet nothing was detracted from his goodness. When Mencius praised his worthiness as equal to that of Yu and Hou Ji, how well he understood Master Yan! Now Yi Yin and Master Yan represent the next tier.

Bo Yi (伯夷) maintained his lofty integrity on Mount Shouyang, and the rousing force of his moral example was such that it made the corrupt pure and the timid resolute, so that for a hundred generations men took his purity as their teacher. Liuxia Hui (栁下惠) endured the disgrace of being dismissed three times, and the unspoiled warmth of his moral example was such that it made the ungenerous kind and the narrow-minded broad [? 鎖鄙, for 銷鄙], so that for a hundred generations men took his harmony as their teacher. Now if they are called teachers for a hundred generations, their influence on their own times can well be inferred! Such was the misfortune of these two men in not meeting their time, and yet such was the reach of their goodness to others—how then can one say that in obscurity a man necessarily perfects only himself? It is simply that in their hearts the one insisted, "What is not good is enough to defile me, so I reject it, and that is all," while the other insisted, "What is not good is not enough to defile me, so I treat it lightly, and that is all." Thus they still could not avoid a barrier between physical forms, between "you" and "me"; therefore Mencius called them "narrow" and "lacking in respect" and declined to follow either of them. Now Bo Yi and Liuxia Hui represent the tier after that. Later on, Yang Zhu (楊朱)…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
老莊公孫則略不道矣不此之少攻而唯
彼之深闢何也蓋吾夫子惡似是而非彼
公孫龍之誕妄郎鄒衍已勝之矣老莊蔑
棄仁義掊擊聖王說若高虛而易聽亦激
於一時憤世之言而未必行事之實也至
申商之刑名蘇張之功利大抵皆枉尋直
尺希世取寵之事在鄉黨自好者猶羞稱
之矣惟楊氏爲我似獨善而實非獨善墨
氏兼愛似兼善而實非兼善吾窮而鼓其喙
===
猶足以陷人心妨政事使達而行其教其
不胥天下而無父無君不止矣故孟氏至
比其害於洪水夷狄猛獸而猶曰能言距
楊墨者聖人之徒也蓋至是而孟氏兼善
之志見矣繇斯以譚洪鍾之在簴小叩小
鳴大叩大鳴聲出於叩而不在叩也寶劍
之在匣陸斷犀兕水斷蛟龍利出於斷而
不在斷也聖人之於窮達猶鍾劍之於叩
斷耳而其本則在吾心矣聖人之心何心
punctuated: 老、莊、公孫，則略不道矣。不此之少攻，而唯彼之深闢，何也？蓋吾夫子惡似是而非。彼公孫龍之誕妄，郎鄒衍已勝之矣。老、莊蔑棄仁義，掊擊聖王，說若高虛而易聽，亦激於一時憤世之言，而未必行事之實也。至申、商之刑名，蘇、張之功利，大抵皆枉尋直尺、希世取寵之事，在鄉黨自好者猶羞稱之矣。惟楊氏「爲我」，似獨善而實非獨善；墨氏「兼愛」，似兼善而實非兼善。吾窮而鼓其喙，猶足以陷人心、妨政事；使達而行其教，其不胥天下而無父無君不止矣。故孟氏至比其害於洪水、夷狄、猛獸，而猶曰：「能言距楊、墨者，聖人之徒也。」蓋至是而孟氏兼善之志見矣。繇斯以譚，洪鍾之在簴，小叩小鳴，大叩大鳴，聲出於叩而不在叩也；寶劍之在匣，陸斷犀兕，水斷蛟龍，利出於斷而不在斷也。聖人之於窮達，猶鍾、劍之於叩斷耳，而其本則在吾心矣。聖人之心，何心
translation_en: …as for Laozi, Zhuangzi, and Gongsun Long, he barely mentioned them at all. Why did he not attack these even slightly, while deeply refuting only those others [Yang Zhu and Mo Di]? It is because our Master hated that which seems right but is actually wrong. As for the absurdities of Gongsun Long, even Zou Yan had already overcome them. Although Laozi and Zhuangzi cast aside benevolence and righteousness and attacked the sage kings, and though their doctrines seemed lofty, empty, and appealing to the ear, they were merely words provoked by a momentary indignation against the world, and not necessarily matters put into actual practice. As for the Legalist doctrines of forms and names of Shen Buhai and Shang Yang, and the utilitarianism of Su Qin and Zhang Yi, on the whole they were all affairs of bending eight feet to straighten one foot, flattering the age to curry favor—things that even a person of modest self-respect in a village community would be ashamed to speak of. Only Yang Zhu's doctrine of "each for himself" resembles cultivating oneself in obscurity, yet in reality is not true self-cultivation in obscurity; and Mo Di's doctrine of "universal love" resembles bringing goodness to the whole world, yet in reality is not truly bringing goodness to the whole world. Even when they are in obscurity and merely wagging their tongues, they are still enough to ensnare people's minds and harm governance; if they were to attain high station and put their teachings into practice, they would not stop until they had led the entire world into acknowledging neither father nor ruler. Therefore Mencius went so far as to compare their harm to that of floodwaters, barbarian tribes, and fierce beasts, and yet also said: "Whoever is able to oppose Yang and Mo with words is a disciple of the sages." Thus, at this point, Mencius's aspiration to bring goodness to the whole world was made manifest. Speaking from this perspective, when a great bell hangs on its stand, struck lightly it rings softly, and struck hard it rings loudly; the sound emerges from the striking, yet does not reside in the striking itself. When a precious sword rests in its scabbard, on land it can slice through rhinoceroses and wild buffaloes, and in water it can sever flood-dragons; its sharpness emerges in the severing, yet does not reside in the severing itself. The sage's relation to poverty and high station is just like the bell's and the sword's relation to striking and severing, while the root lies within one's own mind. As for the mind of the sage, what kind of mind…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
也無窮達無人我無可無不可渾然萬物
一體者也果其爲一體萬物之心雖窮如
孔顏且不得以獨善名之而况進此者乎
少有私一己之心雖聖如夷惠且以隘與
不恭病之而况異此者乎蓋惟聖人以天
下爲一身故精神血脉流暢而無滯而不
爲遺世者之忍以吾身視天下故貴賤小
大較然其有辨而不爲尚同者之愚夫如
是則烏覩乎吾身之爲小而天下之爲大
===
耶又烏覩乎兼善之爲達而獨善之爲窮
耶借曰必達而後爲兼善則孔子不足大
顏淵不足仁夷惠不足師而墨氏之說滋
矣窮而即爲獨善則虞舜不必聞於側陋
伊尹不必樂於莘野而楊氏之說横矣然
則學聖人者宜何如舜與夫子尚矣其次
則顏子伊尹乎顏子學在克己復禮而極
其効於天下歸仁之遠吾窮取之以善吾
身而莫非兼也伊尹志在堯舜君民而植
punctuated: 也？無窮達，無人我，無可無不可，渾然萬物一體者也。果其爲一體萬物之心，雖窮如孔、顏，且不得以獨善名之，而况進此者乎？少有私一己之心，雖聖如夷、惠，且以隘與不恭病之，而况異此者乎？蓋惟聖人以天下爲一身，故精神血脉流暢而無滯，而不爲遺世者之忍；以吾身視天下，故貴賤小大較然其有辨，而不爲尚同者之愚。夫如是，則烏覩乎吾身之爲小，而天下之爲大耶？又烏覩乎兼善之爲達，而獨善之爲窮耶？借曰必達而後爲兼善，則孔子不足大，顏淵不足仁，夷、惠不足師，而墨氏之說滋矣；窮而即爲獨善，則虞舜不必聞於側陋，伊尹不必樂於莘野，而楊氏之說横矣。然則學聖人者宜何如？舜與夫子尚矣，其次則顏子、伊尹乎！顏子學在克己復禮，而極其効於天下歸仁之遠，吾窮取之以善吾身，而莫非兼也；伊尹志在堯、舜君民，而植…
translation_en: …is it? Knowing neither adversity nor prominence, neither self nor other, neither preordained permissibility nor impermissibility, it is one that seamlessly forms a single body with the myriad things. If indeed one possesses this mind that forms a single body with the myriad things, then even in adversity like that of Confucius (孔) and Yan Hui (顏), one still cannot be labeled as merely cultivating oneself in solitude—how much less those who advance beyond this? Yet if there is the slightest selfishness of mind, then even sages like Boyi (夷) and Liuxia Hui (惠) are faulted for narrowness or lack of respect—how much more those who diverge from them? For only the sage regards the world as a single body; therefore, his vital spirit and lifeblood flow smoothly without obstruction, and he does not fall into the callousness of those who abandon the world. And because he views the world through the measure of his own person, noble and base, great and small are clearly distinguished, and he does not fall into the folly of those who exalt uniformity. This being so, how could one view one's own person as small and the world as great? And how could one view benefiting the world together as prominence, and cultivating oneself in solitude as adversity? Suppose one were to say that one must achieve prominence before one can benefit the world together; then Confucius would not be worthy of being called great, Yan Yuan (顏淵) would not be worthy of being called humane, Boyi and Liuxia Hui would not be worthy of being taken as teachers, and the doctrines of Mozi (墨氏) would proliferate. And if being in adversity meant merely cultivating oneself in solitude, then Yu Shun (虞舜) need not have become renowned from humble obscurity, Yi Yin (伊尹) need not have delighted in the fields of莘 (Shen), and the doctrines of Yang Zhu (楊氏) would run rampant. Well then, how ought one who learns from the sages to proceed? Shun and the Master are supreme; next after them would be Master Yan (顏子) and Yi Yin! Master Yan's learning lay in overcoming the self and returning to propriety, yet its ultimate efficacy reached as far as the whole world turning to humanity; in adversity, I draw upon him to cultivate my own person, and yet there is nothing in it that is not also benefiting all together. Yi Yin's ambition lay in making his ruler and people like those of Yao (堯) and Shun, yet he planted…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
其節於一介取予之嚴吾達取之以善乎
天下而莫非獨也要使吾萬物一體之心
盎然充乎中而溢乎外如元氣之周於一
身而耳聽目視手持足行無入而不自得
然後無忝於聖人之學而聖人之心在我
矣彼異端者吾烏乎攻之
第四問
史懋文
同考試官推官舒　批〔論治者先吏將今每以之才爲諸蓋選任之未盡也子援古証今切中時弊而末復歸重守令之選尤〕
===
知時務之要者錄之
考試官侍讀羅　批〔吏備將良盛世事也而本諸課取得其本矣兼以雄偉之文推古今之變足見博通文武者錄之〕
考試官右中允高　批〔選賢吏將乃安攘要務子以采實立說篇末尤歸本得民益通達治體者〕
聖王所以安內攘外分猷共理者非吏與
將哉然未得其人則擇之不可不精也既
得其人則任之不可不至也蓋以天下之
punctuated:
其節於一介取予之嚴，吾達取之以善乎天下，而莫非獨也。要使吾萬物一體之心，盎然充乎中而溢乎外，如元氣之周於一身，而耳聽、目視、手持、足行，無入而不自得，然後無忝於聖人之學，而聖人之心在我矣。彼異端者，吾烏乎攻之？

第四問

史懋文
同考試官推官舒　批〔論治者先吏、將。今每以之才爲諸，蓋選任之未盡也。子援古証今，切中時弊，而末復歸重守、令之選，尤〕知時務之要者，錄之。
考試官侍讀羅　批〔吏備將良，盛世事也，而本諸課取，得其本矣。兼以雄偉之文，推古今之變，足見博通文武者，錄之。〕
考試官右中允高　批〔選賢吏、將，乃安攘要務。子以采實立說，篇末尤歸本得民，益通達治體者。〕

聖王所以安內攘外、分猷共理者，非吏與將哉？然未得其人，則擇之不可不精也；既得其人，則任之不可不至也。蓋以天下之
translation_en:
…his moral integrity in strictness over taking or giving even a single trifle; when I attain high office, I draw upon him to do good for the whole world, yet none of it is anything other than solitary self-cultivation. The essential thing is to cause my mind that forms one body with all things to abundantly fill the interior and overflow to the exterior, like primordial vitality circulating throughout the entire body, so that in the ears' hearing, the eyes' seeing, the hands' grasping, and the feet's walking, there is no situation one enters without being at ease with oneself. Only then will one bring no shame to the learning of the sages, and the mind of the sages will reside within me. As for those heterodox teachings, why would I even need to attack them?

Fourth Policy Question

Shi Maowen 史懋文
Comment by Associate Examiner and Prefectural Judge Shu 舒: [Those who discuss governance put civil officials and military commanders first. Nowadays people often make excuses about a lack of talent [?], which is really because selection and appointment have not been carried out to the fullest. You cite antiquity to verify the present, hitting squarely upon contemporary ills, and at the end you return to emphasizing the selection of Prefects and Magistrates. Especially] as one who understands the essentials of current affairs, we record his essay for publication.
Comment by Examiner and Academician Reader-in-Waiting Luo 羅: [Having complete civil officials and capable military commanders is the business of a flourishing age, and by grounding this in evaluation and selection, you have grasped the root of the matter. Combined with vigorous and magnificent prose that traces the changes from antiquity to the present, this is sufficient to show one who is broadly conversant in both civil and military affairs; we record it for publication.]
Comment by Examiner and Right Companion to the Heir Apparent Gao 高: [Selecting worthy civil officials and military commanders is the essential task for pacifying the interior and repelling external threats. You establish your argument on gathering substantive realities, and at the end of the piece you especially return to the root of winning the people—truly one who thoroughly understands the principles of governance.]

Are not those by whom the sage kings pacify the interior and repel external threats, sharing plans and jointly governing, the civil officials and military commanders? Yet before one has obtained the right men, their selection cannot but be meticulous; and once one has obtained the right men, their entrustment with responsibility cannot but be complete. For given the…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
大非盡乏才也譬之杞幹梧栢隨地而生
必大匠操繩引以求之而後可收以充梁
柱夫擇人者亦猶是矣人才之出非盡無
適於用也譬之御騄駬之馬者非驅策之
有方必不得使之服銜勒而至千里夫任
人者亦猶是矣擇之精則所得者皆良任
之至則所用者畢効由是以之安内以之
攘外而帝王順治威嚴之績不可坐而致
哉蓋聞之昔人云守令者民之本言吏重
===
也乃史遷之傳循吏必取經術潤飾吏事
者何耶蓋吏不尚夫能而尚夫循彼藝識
趫敏懼或流於詐弁稜跡厲懼或入於暴
修姱廉隅懼或失於矯訶擿伏匿懼或傷
於譎籍令一能吏足辦之矣惟用經術者
乃有以鏡作牧之理而弘學道之用然後
悶悶於政事泯泯於聲聞其質惇也寧爲
保障不爲繭絲寧爲鸞鳳不爲鷹鸇其惠
流也循行阡陌與民興利敎之以孝弟禮
punctuated:
大，非盡乏才也。譬之杞幹梧栢，隨地而生，必大匠操繩引以求之，而後可收以充梁柱，夫擇人者亦猶是矣。人才之出，非盡無適於用也。譬之御騄駬之馬者，非驅策之有方，必不得使之服銜勒而至千里，夫任人者亦猶是矣。擇之精，則所得者皆良；任之至，則所用者畢効。由是以之安内，以之攘外，而帝王順治威嚴之績，不可坐而致哉？

蓋聞之昔人云：「守令者，民之本。」言吏重也。乃史遷之傳循吏，必取經術潤飾吏事者，何耶？蓋吏不尚夫能，而尚夫循。彼藝識趫敏，懼或流於詐；弁稜跡厲，懼或入於暴；修姱廉隅，懼或失於矯；訶擿伏匿，懼或傷於譎。籍令一能吏，足辦之矣。惟用經術者，乃有以鏡作牧之理，而弘學道之用。然後悶悶於政事，泯泯於聲聞，其質惇也；寧爲保障，不爲繭絲，寧爲鸞鳳，不爲鷹鸇，其惠流也；循行阡陌，與民興利，敎之以孝弟禮…
translation_en:
… vastness, it is not utterly devoid of talent. It is like willow trunks, parasol trees, and cypresses, which grow everywhere, yet only when a master carpenter holds his marking-line to seek them out can they be gathered to serve as beams and pillars—selecting men is just like this. When men of talent emerge, it is not that none of them are suited for use. It is like driving a fine Lu'er steed: unless one has the proper method for urging it on, one certainly cannot make it submit to the bit and bridle and cover a thousand li—employing men in office is just like this. When selection is discriminating, all those obtained are worthy; when trust and delegation are complete, all those employed exert themselves to the utmost. Using them on this basis to pacify the interior and to repel outside threats, could the achievements of the emperors and kings in bringing about orderly rule and awe-inspiring majesty not be attained effortlessly?

Indeed, I have heard that the ancients said: "Prefects and magistrates are the foundation of the people." This speaks to the importance of civil officials. Yet when Sima Qian (Shi Qian 史遷) wrote his biographies of Upright Officials (Xunli 循吏), why did he invariably choose those who adorned their administrative affairs with classical scholarship? It is because in civil officials, what is valued is not mere capability, but upright adherence to principle. Those whose technical skills and perception are nimble and quick, one fears may lapse into deceit; those whose demeanor is sharp-edged and whose conduct is fierce [?], one fears may cross into cruelty; those who cultivate ostentatious integrity, one fears may err through affectation; those who ferret out and expose hidden matters, one fears may do harm through guile. Any merely capable official would suffice to handle such things. Only those who employ classical scholarship have the means to mirror the principles of shepherding the people and expand the practical application of learning the Way. Only then are they unpretentious in governance and unconcerned with reputation—such is the genuineness of their substance; they would rather act as protective bulwarks than as silk-reelers extracting the last thread, and rather be phoenixes than hawks and falcons—such is the flowing of their benevolence; they tour the field paths, promote what is beneficial for the people, and instruct them in their innate nature of filial piety, fraternal submission, ritual…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
義之性其澤究也夫此則非循吏不能也
史遷其知言哉又云將者國之輔言將重
也乃晉人之謀元帥必取說禮樂而敦詩
書者何耶蓋將不以才勝而以賢勝彼鴟
張虎視不足逞其雄鷹搏猿射不足程其
技六化四廂不足藏其智三書八符不足
況其幾藉令一才將足勝之矣惟習詩禮
者乃有以審公私之分而軌德義之途然
後受命忘家援枹鼓忘身以節殉也泰山
崩而不變麋鹿興而不瞬以氣定也戰如
守守如戰有功如幸以志懾也夫此則非
賢將不能也晉人殆聞道哉愚嘗俯仰今
昔吏之稱良者惟漢世為盛夷考其人通
春秋而守成都者非文翁乎修學宮以造
士蜀地比齊魯之風舉明經而守渤海者
非龔遂乎散盜賊以歸農齊民易刀劒之
俗卓茂以習禮聞為密令而視民如子詔
有名冠天下之褒魯恭以習詩著宰中牟
banxin: 鄉試錄 卷 八十六
punctuated:
義之性，其澤究也。夫此則非循吏不能也，史遷其知言哉！又云：「將者，國之輔。」言將重也。乃晉人之謀元帥，必取說禮樂而敦詩書者，何耶？蓋將不以才勝，而以賢勝。彼鴟張虎視，不足逞其雄；鷹搏猿射，不足程其技；六化四廂，不足藏其智；三書八符，不足況其幾。藉令一才將，足勝之矣。惟習詩禮者，乃有以審公私之分，而軌德義之途。然後受命忘家，援枹鼓忘身，以節殉也；泰山崩而不變，麋鹿興而不瞬，以氣定也；戰如守，守如戰，有功如幸，以志懾也。夫此則非賢將不能也，晉人殆聞道哉！
愚嘗俯仰今昔，吏之稱良者，惟漢世為盛。夷考其人：通《春秋》而守成都者，非文翁乎？修學宮以造士，蜀地比齊、魯之風。舉明經而守渤海者，非龔遂乎？散盜賊以歸農，齊民易刀劒之俗。卓茂以習《禮》聞，為密令而視民如子，詔有「名冠天下」之褒；魯恭以習《詩》著，宰中牟
translation_en:
… the nature of [filial piety, brotherly respect, ritual,] and righteousness—thus their beneficence reaches its utmost. Now, this is something that none but an upright official could achieve. How well Sima Qian 司馬遷 understood words! It is also said: "A general is the bulwark of the state," which speaks to the importance of the general. Yet when the men of Jin deliberated over a supreme commander, why did they insist on choosing one who delighted in ritual and music and was devoted to the Odes (Shi) and Documents (Shu)? It is because a general triumphs not through mere talent, but through worthiness. Those who puff themselves up like owls and glare like tigers are not enough to display true heroism; those who strike like falcons and shoot like gibbons are not enough to measure true skill; the Six Transformations and Four Wings are not enough to encompass true wisdom; the Three Books and Eight Tallies are not enough to fathom true subtleties. Even a merely talented general would suffice to master such things. Only one well-versed in the Odes and Rites has the means to discern the distinction between public and private and to follow the path of virtue and righteousness. Only then, upon receiving his commission, does he forget his family, and upon taking up the drumstick, forget his own person—sacrificing himself through integrity; though Mount Tai collapse before him he does not blench, and though elk dart out beside him he does not blink—steadfast through vital spirit; he attacks as cautiously as he defends, defends as vigorously as he attacks, and regards achievement as mere good fortune—awed in mind. Now, this is something that none but a worthy general could achieve. The men of Jin had surely heard the Way!
I have reflected on past and present: among officials praised as virtuous, only the Han era was truly flourishing. Let us examine these men: Was not the one who mastered the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) and governed Chengdu Wen Weng 文翁? He built school buildings to cultivate scholars, so that the land of Shu came to rival the customs of Qi and Lu. Was not the one recommended for 明經 (Mingjing, Classicist) who governed Bohai Gong Sui 龔遂? He dispersed bandits and returned them to farming, so that the common people exchanged their habits of swords and blades. Zhuo Mao 卓茂 was renowned for his study of the Rites (Li); serving as Magistrate of Mi, he regarded the people as his own children, and an imperial edict praised him as "foremost in renown throughout the realm." Lu Gong 魯恭 was distinguished for his study of the Odes (Shi); governing Zhongmou…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
而用德爲理掾有三異還白之狀所謂經
術潤飾者玆非極選與不然何以純任敎
化如此也若乃鍩〔管用〕投書趙廣漢之在潁
川非不流威名也然專厲〔逢螽〕氣卒以此賈
敗矣虎穴揍獄尹賞之在長安非不入高
等也然率務殘賊卒以此坐免矣吾姑取
其能可耳而經術則何知焉將之稱良者
亦惟漢世爲盛夷考其人陳湯好書博達
甞副西域都護因矯制徵兵遂斬郅支之
首馮奉世涉春秋大義甞送大宛諸客因
持節傳諭竟誅莎車之王號大樹將軍者
則通左氏之馮異也時赤眉煽亂乃奮翼
破之於澠池稱北道主人者則尚經學之
耿弇也時劇虜猖狂乃振旅降之於淄水
所謂敦說禮樂詩書者玆非流亞與不然
何以義急國事如此也若乃韓信登於亡
卒而名成垓下功烈非不偉也獨以勇略
震主而於謀身亦旣疎矣衛青起於人奴
punctuated: 而用德爲理，掾有三異還白之狀。所謂經術潤飾者，玆非極選與？不然，何以純任敎化如此也？若乃鍩〔管用〕投書，趙廣漢之在潁川，非不流威名也，然專厲〔逢螽〕氣，卒以此賈敗矣；虎穴揍獄，尹賞之在長安，非不入高等也，然率務殘賊，卒以此坐免矣。吾姑取其能可耳，而經術則何知焉？將之稱良者，亦惟漢世爲盛。夷考其人：陳湯好書博達，甞副西域都護，因矯制徵兵，遂斬郅支之首；馮奉世涉《春秋》大義，甞送大宛諸客，因持節傳諭，竟誅莎車之王；號大樹將軍者，則通《左氏》之馮異也，時赤眉煽亂，乃奮翼破之於澠池；稱北道主人者，則尚經學之耿弇也，時劇虜猖狂，乃振旅降之於淄水。所謂敦說禮樂詩書者，玆非流亞與？不然，何以義急國事如此也？若乃韓信登於亡卒而名成垓下，功烈非不偉也，獨以勇略震主，而於謀身亦旣疎矣；衛青起於人奴
translation_en:
… and employed virtue as his principle of administration, so that the investigating clerk returned and reported the three marvels of his rule. Those who are described as adorning their governance with classical scholarship—are these men not the finest selections? Otherwise, how could they have relied purely on moral instruction and transformation like this? As for using a bamboo receptacle [transcription has 鍩〔管用〕 for 筩] to receive anonymous letters, when Zhao Guanghan 趙廣漢 was in Yingchuan 潁川, it is not that he failed to spread a fearsome reputation; yet he devoted himself exclusively to sharpening a waspish [transcription has 〔逢螽〕 for 鋒] temper, and in the end brought ruin upon himself by this means. And in making a "tiger's den" pit to imprison offenders [transcription has 揍獄], when Yin Shang 尹賞 was in Chang'an 長安, it is not that he failed to be ranked in the highest grade; yet he generally occupied himself with cruelty and ruthlessness, and in the end was dismissed for this offense [?]. We may provisionally take note of their competence, but what did they know of classical scholarship?

Among generals who were praised as good, it was likewise in the Han era that they were most numerous. Let us examine these men: Chen Tang 陳湯 loved books and had broad understanding; while serving as Assistant Protector-General of the Western Regions (Xiyu duhu 西域都護), he forged an imperial decree to levy troops and consequently severed the head of Zhizhi 郅支. Feng Fengshi 馮奉世 was versed in the great principles of the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu 春秋); while escorting the foreign envoys from Dayuan 大宛, he held his staff of authority to proclaim the imperial command to the states and ultimately executed the King of Yarkand (Shache 莎車). He who was called the "Big Tree General" (Dashu jiangjun 大樹將軍) was Feng Yi 馮異, who was thoroughly conversant with the Zuo Commentary (Zuoshi 左氏); when the Red Eyebrows (Chimei 赤眉) fanned rebellion, he spread his wings at Huichi 澠池 (Mianchi) and crushed them there. He who was referred to as the "Host of the Northern Road" (Beidao zhuren 北道主人) was Geng Yan 耿弇, who esteemed classical learning; when formidable rebels ran rampant, he marshaled his legions and forced their surrender at the Zi River (Zishui 淄水). Those who are described as earnestly delighting in the Rites, Music, Odes, and Documents—are these men not of that same peerless class? Otherwise, how could they have hurried to the emergencies of the state out of righteousness like this? As for Han Xin 韓信, who rose from a deserting soldier and achieved fame at Gaixia 垓下, it is not that his meritorious deeds were not grand; yet solely because his bravery and strategic prowess made his ruler tremble, he was altogether remiss in planning for his own preservation. And Wei Qing 衛青, who rose from a household slave…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
而威振狼胥勳伐非不茂也獨以和柔媚
上而於天下固無稱矣吾第取其才可耳
而詩書則何觀焉夫論績效之遲速則德
禮之化或謝於武健之操第恐法令滋章
者終不若絃頌入人之尤深矣論扞禦之
勇怯則文墨之士或殿於介冑之夫第恐
一劒爲任者終不若樽俎折衝之尤易矣
然則議置吏將者雖不必拘之以方問之
以類而誠得經明之士於民社封疆不尚
===
有利哉我
國家以六合元元之命係于守令於是除之
於科目拔之於鄉貢循資以注銓量材以
授職諸不在執經之列者必弗與其選焉
蓋庶幾哉烝烝之治矣顧今臧否渾殽習
緣隨窳其能者不自激發而徒興乎約結
之嘆不能者益以怠廢而自甘于闒茸之
歸吏而能揚其職者或尠其人也又以三
軍存亡之道係於將帥於是進之以武舉
punctuated:
而威振狼胥，勳伐非不茂也，獨以和柔媚上，而於天下固無稱矣。吾第取其才可耳，而詩書則何觀焉？夫論績效之遲速，則德禮之化或謝於武健之操，第恐法令滋章者，終不若絃頌入人之尤深矣；論扞禦之勇怯，則文墨之士或殿於介冑之夫，第恐一劒爲任者，終不若樽俎折衝之尤易矣。然則議置吏將者，雖不必拘之以方、問之以類，而誠得經明之士，於民社封疆，不尚有利哉！
我國家以六合元元之命係于守令，於是除之於科目，拔之於鄉貢，循資以注銓，量材以授職，諸不在執經之列者，必弗與其選焉，蓋庶幾哉烝烝之治矣。顧今臧否渾殽，習緣隨窳，其能者不自激發，而徒興乎約結之嘆；不能者益以怠廢，而自甘于闒茸之歸，吏而能揚其職者，或尠其人也。又以三軍存亡之道係於將帥，於是進之以武舉，
translation_en:
…yet his awe shook Mount Langju. His meritorious achievements were certainly not inconsiderable, yet solely because he flattered his superior with compliant gentleness, he went unpraised by the empire. One may simply employ them for their talents; what is there to look for in them regarding the Odes and Documents?

Now, if we discuss the speed of achieving results, transformation through virtue and ritual might yield to tough and vigorous measures; yet I fear that multiplying laws and ordinances is ultimately not as effective as the music of strings and hymns in penetrating deeply into people's hearts. If we discuss bravery and cowardice in defense, men of letters and ink might lag behind men in armor and helmets; yet I fear that relying on a single sword is ultimately not as easy as repelling the enemy amid goblets and ritual stands at the diplomatic table. This being so, when deliberating on the appointment of civil officials and military commanders, although one need not restrict them by fixed methods or interrogate them according to categories, if we truly obtain scholars who understand the Classics, would that not still be advantageous for the people, the altars of the soil, and the frontiers?

Our Dynasty considers that the lives of the common people throughout the realm depend upon Prefects and Magistrates. Therefore, it appoints them through the civil service examination categories and selects them from the local tribute students, registering them for selection according to seniority and bestowing offices according to talent. Anyone not in the ranks of those who study the Classics is never allowed to participate in this selection—thus coming close indeed to a flourishing and progressive governance! Yet nowadays, good and bad are muddled together, and customs have grown corrupt and negligent along with established routines. Those who are capable do not rouse themselves, merely sighing over being bound and constrained; those who are incapable grow ever more lazy and neglectful, willingly resigning themselves to the ranks of the base and mediocre. Among civil officials, those who can distinguish themselves in their duties are perhaps few indeed. Furthermore, considering that the survival or ruin of the armies depends upon the generals and commanders, the state advances them through the Military Examinations,…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
試之以騎射購方略之伎而攬智勇之英
卽不皆治經之儒亦豈無博習古今者焉
蓋庶幾哉桓桓之武矣顧今柄置乖刺競
攫梁肥以弓馬得者不過挽强引重矜尚
蹶張之能以策試中者亦循塵飯塗羹無
當韜鈐之用將而克稱其舉者亦鮮乎聞
也夫賢人志士欲有所樹立以著不朽於
後世者甚於人君之求才茲求之者非不
勤而應之者亦非不至乃一當緩急則無
===
異試割於鉛刀求濟於土櫬者此何故也
患在名實之相冒而已有名而實不副則
飾名之術益工有實而名不彰則敦實之
志不固故今吏與將之所務皆名也騖遠
以自旌托之乎卓異株守以累日托之乎
循理藻績以博譽托之乎恢張詘附以弭
謗托之乎謹畏甚至溼薪操下愁疾閭閻
漁獵取盈殫空杼柚而亦得以善狀聞焉
幸有矯俗者欲修破觚斲琱之意則其形
punctuated: 試之以騎射，購方略之伎，而攬智勇之英。卽不皆治經之儒，亦豈無博習古今者焉？蓋庶幾哉桓桓之武矣！顧今柄置乖刺，競攫梁肥。以弓馬得者，不過挽强引重，矜尚蹶張之能；以策試中者，亦循塵飯塗羹，無當韜鈐之用。將而克稱其舉者，亦鮮乎聞也。夫賢人志士欲有所樹立，以著不朽於後世者，甚於人君之求才。茲求之者非不勤，而應之者亦非不至，乃一當緩急，則無異試割於鉛刀、求濟於土櫬者，此何故也？患在名實之相冒而已。有名而實不副，則飾名之術益工；有實而名不彰，則敦實之志不固。故今吏與將之所務，皆名也。騖遠以自旌，托之乎卓異；株守以累日，托之乎循理；藻績以博譽，托之乎恢張；詘附以弭謗，托之乎謹畏。甚至溼薪操下，愁疾閭閻；漁獵取盈，殫空杼柚，而亦得以善狀聞焉。幸有矯俗者，欲修破觚斲琱之意，則其形
translation_en: … tested them in horsemanship and archery, sought out their skills in strategic planning, and gathered the finest men of wisdom and courage. Even if they are not all scholars who have mastered the Classics, how could there not be among them those broadly versed in antiquity and the present? One might hope this would bring about martial prowess! Yet today the allocation of authority is perverse, and men compete to seize rich and lucrative posts. Those who succeed through bow and horse do no more than draw stiff bows and lift heavy weights, boasting of their ability to cock crossbows with their feet; those who pass through the policy questions merely follow after meals of dust and soups of mud, having nothing that suits the practical use of military strategy. Among generals, those truly worthy of their elevation are likewise rarely heard of. Now, worthy men and gentlemen of ambition desire to establish achievements so as to make an imperishable name for themselves in later generations even more eagerly than a ruler seeks talent. At present, those who seek them are not lacking in diligence, and those who respond are not failing to come forward; yet once an emergency arises, it is no different from trying to cut with a lead knife or seeking to cross a river in a clay coffin [reading 櫬 for 9/泝?]. Why is this? The trouble lies simply in name and reality being confused with one another. When there is a name without the corresponding reality, the art of embellishing one's reputation grows ever more ingenious; when there is reality but the name is not made manifest, the resolve to cultivate substance does not remain firm. Therefore, what civil officials and generals devote themselves to today is nothing but reputation. Those who chase after distant goals to distinguish themselves pass it off as extraordinary excellence; those who cling to routine to accumulate seniority pass it off as abiding by principle; those who embellish their achievements to win praise pass it off as grand expansion; those who bend and curry favor to forestall criticism pass it off as cautious reverence. It even goes so far that they bind their subordinates like wet firewood, bringing grief and distress to the common people in the villages, or fish and hunt for full quotas until the looms are completely emptied—and yet they still manage to be reported to the throne with favorable evaluations. If by some good fortune there is someone who wishes to correct vulgar customs and revive the spirit of breaking octagons into circles and carving away ornaments for simplicity, then his outward appearance …

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
無足以飾目聲無足以飾耳且曹起而議
其無能將不久而去之矣此吏之所以日
靡於名也攘腕而先登見謂猛以敢閑壘
而自固見謂安以重馳突而颷舉見謂疾
以速虛聲而遮邀見謂威以備甚至牧馬
屯牛鞠爲椎剽啇夫樵婦罄作俘囚而亦
得以中律稱焉幸有伉節者欲厲死綏任
咎之志則其肘爲之所掣足爲之所維且
從中而疑其專制將觀釁而危之矣此將
===
之所以日靡於名也然則欲挽今日之弊
奚繇哉亦惟知人善任而責以實焉可也
夫卽墨以積毀受封而王戉以僞增賜爵
則課吏難也必也嚴綜核之法愼會計之
典行業勤修下璽書以示勸功庸竟緒增
爵秩以致褒治有異等之蹟雖超遷而不
爲驟民有服習之美寧久任而不爲淹如
是則吏修實效卽芔棠之詠不足多矣寧
文翁諸人可道哉夫趙括撓敗於知書而
punctuated: 無足以飾目，聲無足以飾耳，且曹起而議其無能，將不久而去之矣。此吏之所以日靡於名也。攘腕而先登，見謂猛以敢；閑壘而自固，見謂安以重；馳突而颷舉，見謂疾以速；虛聲而遮邀，見謂威以備。甚至牧馬屯牛，鞠爲椎剽；啇夫樵婦，罄作俘囚，而亦得以中律稱焉。幸有伉節者，欲厲死綏任咎之志，則其肘爲之所掣，足爲之所維，且從中而疑其專制，將觀釁而危之矣。此將之所以日靡於名也。然則欲挽今日之弊，奚繇哉？亦惟知人善任，而責以實焉可也。夫卽墨以積毀受封，而王戉以僞增賜爵，則課吏難也。必也嚴綜核之法，愼會計之典：行業勤修，下璽書以示勸；功庸竟緒，增爵秩以致褒。治有異等之蹟，雖超遷而不爲驟；民有服習之美，寧久任而不爲淹。如是則吏修實效，卽《芔棠》之詠不足多矣，寧文翁諸人可道哉！夫趙括撓敗於知書，而
translation_en:
…appearance is insufficient to dazzle the eye, and his reputation is insufficient to flatter the ear. Moreover, the crowd rises up to criticize him as incompetent, and before long he will be dismissed. This is why civil officials daily decline into the pursuit of mere reputation.

As for rolling up one's sleeves and being first to scale the walls, it is regarded as fierce and daring; keeping quietly to the ramparts to secure one's defense is regarded as calm and prudent; charging forth like a rising gale is regarded as swift and rapid; making empty boasts to intercept the enemy is regarded as awe-inspiring and well-prepared. It goes so far that pastured horses and garrison cattle are entirely plundered, and traveling merchants and wood-gathering women are all taken as captives and prisoners, yet even this can be praised as acting in accordance with military discipline. Should there fortunately be a man of upright integrity who wishes to rouse the resolve to die in battle when retreating or to take blame upon himself, his elbows are held back by others and his feet are tied down; moreover, from within the court he is suspected of acting arbitrarily, and people will watch for a fault to imperil him. This is why military commanders daily decline into the pursuit of mere reputation.

If so, then if we wish to reverse the abuses of today, by what means can it be done? Only by knowing men, employing them well, and holding them accountable for realities. Now, the Daifu of Jimo (卽墨) received an enfeoffment despite accumulated slander, whereas Wang Cheng (王戉 [王成]) was bestowed a noble rank because of falsified increases in population registers—thus evaluating civil officials is difficult! We must strictly enforce the laws of comprehensive verification and be circumspect with the statutes of administrative accounting: when conduct and achievements are diligently cultivated, send down an imperial letter under the玺 seal to show encouragement; when meritorious service is brought to full completion, increase noble rank and salary grade to bestow praise. When governance shows accomplishments of an extraordinary grade, even a rapid promotion beyond normal sequence is not too sudden; when the people show the beauty of being accustomed to and compliant with an official, it is better to keep him long in office without considering it stagnation. In this way, civil officials will cultivate tangible results; even the ode of the Sweet Pear ("Gantang" 芔棠 [甘棠]) will not be enough to marvel at—how could the likes of Wen Weng (文翁) and others even be worth mentioning! Now, Zhao Kuo (趙括) suffered rout and defeat despite knowing the military books, whereas…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
閻士選
同考試官教諭曾　批〔從來治河無奇策此作獨能熟數往迹之利害備舉善後之長誠非通方之士越拘攣之見者不能經〕
濟才也
考試官侍讀羅　批〔河難治也亦難言也是策洞晰源委較計失得要歸之預防善後其知言哉而勁筆雄詞混混百折不迴之勢有〕
學有識士也録之允宜
考試官右中允高　批〔策治河獨主塞是濟變之論而善後諸議俱極□□可行取之〕
執事以河防策諸士夫河大患也治河大
事也議事以制患大計也敢不一抒愚臆
以復盖聞河之害中國所從來久矣自昔
君臣相與蒿目嘔心未聞有稱善治者河
也以治之之者誠難也河源自星宿逾崑
崙已折而趨積石乃會雍浮汴以達于淮
夫以萬里奔騰之勢無重岡巨磵以闌之
故常衝決而不可禁此一難也河有出有
過有逕有合有分有屈有注有入何多變
punctuated:
閻士選
同考試官教諭曾　批〔從來治河無奇策，此作獨能熟數往迹之利害，備舉善後之長，誠非通方之士、越拘攣之見者不能。經〕濟才也。
考試官侍讀羅　批〔河難治也，亦難言也。是策洞晰源委，較計失得，要歸之預防善後，其知言哉！而勁筆雄詞，混混百折不迴之勢，有〕學有識士也，録之允宜。
考試官右中允高　批〔策治河獨主塞，是濟變之論，而善後諸議俱極□□可行，取之。〕
執事以河防策諸士。夫河，大患也；治河，大事也；議事以制患，大計也。敢不一抒愚臆以復？盖聞河之害中國，所從來久矣。自昔君臣相與蒿目嘔心，未聞有稱善治者，河也；以治之之者誠難也。河源自星宿，逾崑崙，已折而趨積石，乃會雍、浮汴，以達于淮。夫以萬里奔騰之勢，無重岡巨磵以闌之，故常衝決而不可禁，此一難也。河有出、有過、有逕、有合、有分、有屈、有注、有入，何多變
translation_en:
Yan Shixuan 閻士選
Associate Examiner and Instructor Zeng 曾 comments: 〔From past to present, there has never been a miraculous strategy for controlling the Yellow River. This essay alone is able to thoroughly recount the pros and cons of past precedents and comprehensively set forth the strengths of rehabilitation measures. Truly, no one could achieve this who is not a scholar of broad understanding transcending narrow, pedantic views. He is a〕 talent in statecraft.
Examiner and Reader-in-waiting Luo 羅 comments: 〔The Yellow River is difficult to control, and also difficult to speak about. This policy essay thoroughly understands the origins and course of the matter, weighs the losses and gains, and ultimately brings the argument back to precautionary and rehabilitation measures—how well he understands words! Moreover, with its vigorous brush and majestic phrasing, rolling on with the momentum of a hundred turns without turning back, he is〕 a scholar of both learning and insight; recording this for publication is truly fitting.
Examiner and Right Companion to the Heir Apparent Gao 高 comments: 〔In discussing Yellow River control, this policy essay uniquely advocates blocking the breaches, which is an argument suited to meeting emergencies, while its various proposals for rehabilitation are all extremely [?] and practicable. Selected.〕
Your Excellency has posed a policy question to the scholars regarding Yellow River defense. Now, the Yellow River is a great disaster; controlling the Yellow River is a great undertaking; and deliberating on this undertaking to curb the disaster is a great plan of state. How could I dare not pour forth my humble thoughts in reply? Indeed, I have heard that the harm caused to China by the Yellow River is of long standing. Since antiquity, rulers and ministers have gazed out in anxious concern and poured out their hearts together, yet we have never heard of anyone praised as skillful at controlling it—such is the Yellow River, because controlling it is truly difficult. The Yellow River originates at Xingxiu 星宿, crosses Kunlun 崑崙, then bends and hastens toward Jishi 積石, before converging in Yong 雍 [province], floating past Bian 汴, and reaching the Huai 淮 River. Now, with the momentum of rushing and surging across ten thousand li, and without layered ridges or great ravines to hold it back, it constantly bursts its banks and cannot be restrained—this is the first difficulty. The Yellow River has points where it emerges, passes through, skirts by, converges, divides, bends, pours in, and enters—how numerous are its changes…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
也乃其行則至悍猛而不安爲順豈緩急
能釃其流而殺其怒此二難也河之性善
下斯得其平而不爭今亘齊梁之野曠衍
如砥而以洪濤洄洑于其間卒有方數千
里之水欲其建瓴於地中也得乎此三難
也河雜灉沙游泥非有迅流常滌之則勢
必益墊而其身反鬱起而高於岸夫堆出
于岸流自湍之況霖潦百川復爲之灌集
與此四難也夫誠難其治也而遂委之于
===
不治則非也治之已難也而使不得其所
治之道則尤難也蓋上世惟陶唐時鴻水
沸出民人升降移徙崎嶇而不安禹起而
治之乃行山表木灑沈澹菑故道河自積
石下砥柱歷盟津雒汭至于大伾乃廝爲
二渠過洚水至大陸又播爲九河夫由大
伾以上地形高而水峻急易瀉合乎其所
不得不合也由大伾以下地形卑而土輕
脆善潰分乎其所不得不分也故曰禹之
punctuated: 也！乃其行則至悍猛而不安爲順，豈緩急能釃其流而殺其怒？此二難也。河之性善下，斯得其平而不爭。今亘齊、梁之野，曠衍如砥，而以洪濤洄洑于其間，卒有方數千里之水，欲其建瓴於地中也，得乎？此三難也。河雜灉沙游泥，非有迅流常滌之，則勢必益墊，而其身反鬱起而高於岸。夫堆出于岸，流自湍之，況霖潦百川復爲之灌集與？此四難也。夫誠難其治也，而遂委之于不治，則非也；治之已難也，而使不得其所治之道，則尤難也。蓋上世惟陶唐時鴻水沸出，民人升降移徙，崎嶇而不安。禹起而治之，乃行山表木，灑沈澹菑，故道河自積石下砥柱，歷盟津、雒汭，至于大伾，乃廝爲二渠；過洚水至大陸，又播爲九河。夫由大伾以上，地形高而水峻急易瀉，合乎其所不得不合也；由大伾以下，地形卑而土輕脆善潰，分乎其所不得不分也。故曰「禹之
translation_en:
…is it! Moreover, in its course it is exceedingly fierce and violent and does not rest content in flowing smoothly; how could one, through measured adjustments of pace, divide its current and abate its fury? This is the second difficulty. The nature of the Yellow River favors low ground, whereby it attains equilibrium and does not contend. Yet now, stretching across the plains of Qi and Liang, the land is vast and flat as a whetstone, and when surging billows eddy and swirl across it, if suddenly there gathers water from an area of several thousand square li, could one possibly make it pour swiftly downward within the earth like water tipped from a roof tile? This is the third difficulty. The River is mixed with turbid sand and shifting silt; unless a swift current constantly scours it, the channel will inevitably become ever more silted up, until the riverbed itself mounds upward and rises higher than its banks. When the bed mounds above the banks, the current naturally rushes violently from it—how much more so when torrential rains and the hundred streams again pour and gather into it? This is the fourth difficulty.

Now, although it is truly difficult to control, to therefore abandon it to non-control is wrong; yet since controlling it is already difficult, if one fails to grasp the proper way of controlling it, it becomes harder still. In high antiquity, during the time of Tao Tang [Yao], the floodwaters boiled forth, and the people climbed up and down and migrated about, living in hardship and without peace. Yu arose to control them: he traversed the mountains and placed wooden markers, dispersing the sunken waters and calming the calamity. Thus he guided the River from Jishi down past Dizhu, passing Mengjin and the confluence of the Luo, as far as Dapi, where he split it into two channels; passing the Jiang Waters and reaching Dalu, he further distributed it into the Nine Rivers. Now, above Dapi, the terrain is high and the water is steep, swift, and easily discharged, so he united it where it could not but be united; below Dapi, the terrain is low and the soil is light, friable, and prone to collapse, so he divided it where it could not but be divided. Therefore it is said, "Yu's…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
治水水之道也此禹所以通其法也嗣後
殫石畫之思者發盈庭之論逞奇譎之慮
者競作舍之謀故有欲以人力勝者則曰
塞之便愚以爲是鄣之也有惟諉于天事
勝者則曰不塞便愚以爲是循滋蔓也何
也水氣之導也過爲防壅終必盈溢焉能
築垣而久居水乎然蟻孔之變禍且不測
而欲徐觀其所自定又惡可得也眉山氏
曰不塞氾濫不止塞之則水未必聽是塞
===
與不塞皆非所以永持至安之長策也夫
使其決也而幸不至戕毒可且勿塞脫或
溢皐汨陸將有闊殫爲河之患固莫若隨
決隨塞卽不能保其勿壞尚足支數十載
寬近憂歐陽氏曰治水本無奇策相地勢
謹隄防而已是塞也者猶爲猝可倚救敗
術也胡不引漢事觀之乎蓋自周定王時
河徙砰礫禹之故道無可求者故迄於西
京而其爲害益綿綿而不絶孝文時嘗決
punctuated: 治水，水之道也。」此禹所以通其法也。嗣後，殫石畫之思者發盈庭之論，逞奇譎之慮者競作舍之謀。故有欲以人力勝者，則曰：「塞之便。」愚以爲是鄣之也。有惟諉于天事勝者，則曰：「不塞便。」愚以爲是循滋蔓也。何也？水氣之導也，過爲防壅，終必盈溢，焉能築垣而久居水乎？然蟻孔之變，禍且不測，而欲徐觀其所自定，又惡可得也？眉山氏曰：「不塞，氾濫不止；塞之，則水未必聽。」是塞與不塞，皆非所以永持至安之長策也。夫使其決也而幸不至戕毒，可且勿塞；脫或溢皐汨陸，將有闊殫爲河之患，固莫若隨決隨塞，卽不能保其勿壞，尚足支數十載，寬近憂。歐陽氏曰：「治水本無奇策，相地勢、謹隄防而已。」是塞也者，猶爲猝可倚救敗術也。胡不引漢事觀之乎？蓋自周定王時，河徙砰礫，禹之故道無可求者，故迄於西京，而其爲害益綿綿而不絶。孝文時，嘗決
translation_en: … method of controlling the waters was to follow the way of the waters themselves.” This was how Yu adapted his methods to the circumstances. Thereafter, those who exhausted their thoughts on rock-solid plans filled the court with arguments, while those who indulged in strange and ingenious schemes vied with one another like builders consulting passersby on a house by the roadside. Thus, there were those who wished to prevail through human effort, saying, “It is expedient to dam it.” I humbly consider this to be merely blocking it up. And there were those who sought only to shift responsibility onto the work of Heaven, saying, “It is expedient not to dam it.” I humbly consider this to be letting the trouble spread and grow. Why is this? Water is a vital force that must be guided; if one excessively dikes and blocks it, in the end it will surely brim over and flood—how can one build walls and keep water confined within them for long? Yet a breach starting from an ant-hole can lead to unpredictable disaster; if one wishes to watch unhurriedly and wait for the water to settle by itself, how could that ever be achieved? Master Meishan (Su Shi 蘇軾) said, “If you do not dam it, the flooding will not stop; if you dam it, the water will not necessarily obey.” Thus, neither damming nor not damming is a long-term strategy for permanently maintaining supreme peace and security. Now, supposing a breach occurs and by good fortune does not cause destructive harm, one may temporarily refrain from damming it. But if perchance it overflows the marshes and submerges the dry land, threatening to turn the whole broad expanse entirely into a river, then nothing is better than damming each breach as soon as it occurs. Even if one cannot guarantee that it will never break again, it will still suffice to hold out for several decades and relieve immediate anxieties. Master Ouyang (Ouyang Xiu 歐陽修) said, “In controlling the waters there is fundamentally no miraculous strategy; it is simply a matter of examining the configuration of the land and carefully maintaining the dikes.” Thus, damming remains an expedient art for rescuing a failing situation that can be relied upon in an emergency. Why not cite the events of the Han dynasty to observe this? Ever since the time of King Ding of Zhou 周定王, when the Yellow River shifted its course at Pengli [礫溪/宿胥口?], the old channels of Yu could no longer be traced; therefore, down to the Western Capital (Western Han), the harm it caused continued endlessly without cease. In the time of Emperor Xiaowen 孝文, it once breached its banks at…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
酸棗矣乃大興東郡卒塞之故金隄之潰
旋復而白馬之波不揚終帝之世瀕河民
不識濡足之患孝武時再決瓠子矣乃自
臨河湛璧馬扈從將軍已下皆負薪使二
卿將卒寘決口已而築宮宣防侈其盛由
是而觀用塞之效可覩已夫孝文海內富
庶非不足修禹之業而計卒出于塞且僅
再傳而復決武以雄才大略猶然長歌悲
感旣徼靈于河祇窮數年之力而始塞蓋
===
即一塞且不易如此甚矣河之難治也我
朝歲漕淮取濟黃流宋之疏汴元之引汶皆
所倚爲用焉利盡東南半天下之賦由此
以進若人之咽喉然繫至重矣然惟南行
則利漕或東決則害漕今之言治者正利
害相持之際也乃欲盡去其害而獨資其
利則難之難矣蓋嘗槩水患而測之河非
汴不得合于淮故漕之憂常在汴猶之內
關之疾也假令汴可無憂矣則虞其轉而
punctuated:
酸棗矣，乃大興東郡卒塞之，故金隄之潰旋復，而白馬之波不揚，終帝之世，瀕河民不識濡足之患。孝武時再決瓠子矣，乃自臨河，湛璧馬，扈從將軍已下皆負薪，使二卿將卒寘決口，已而築宮宣防，侈其盛。由是而觀，用塞之效可覩已。夫孝文海內富庶，非不足修禹之業，而計卒出于塞，且僅再傳而復決；武以雄才大略，猶然長歌悲感，旣徼靈于河祇，窮數年之力而始塞。蓋即一塞且不易如此，甚矣河之難治也！
我朝歲漕淮，取濟黃流，宋之疏汴、元之引汶，皆所倚爲用焉。利盡東南，半天下之賦由此以進，若人之咽喉然，繫至重矣。然惟南行則利漕，或東決則害漕，今之言治者，正利害相持之際也。乃欲盡去其害而獨資其利，則難之難矣。蓋嘗槩水患而測之：河非汴不得合于淮，故漕之憂常在汴，猶之內關之疾也；假令汴可無憂矣，則虞其轉而
translation_en:
… at Suanzao. He then mobilized the troops of Dong Commandery on a large scale to plug it. Consequently, the breach at the Golden Dike (Jindi) was quickly repaired, the waves at Baima did not rise, and throughout the rest of the emperor's reign, the people living along the Yellow River knew nothing of the calamity of getting their feet wet. In the time of Emperor Xiaowu, it breached again at Huzi. The emperor personally went to the river, sank jade bi-disks and a horse as sacrifices, and ordered his retinue from the Generals downward all to carry firewood on their backs, while dispatching two Chamberlain-level officials to lead soldiers to fill in the breach; afterward, he built the Xuanfang Palace to celebrate the grand achievement. Viewed from this perspective, the effectiveness of plugging breaches can be clearly seen. Now, under Emperor Xiaowen, the realm within the seas was wealthy and populous—not lacking the resources to restore the enterprise of Yu the Great—yet his plan ultimately resorted to plugging the breach, and after merely two reigns it burst again. Even Emperor Wu, with his heroic talent and grand strategy, still chanted a long song in sorrowful emotion, praying for the blessing of the River Spirit and exhausting several years of effort before it was finally plugged. Thus, even merely plugging a breach is as difficult as this—how extreme indeed is the difficulty of controlling the Yellow River!

Our Dynasty annually transports grain via the Huai River, drawing aid from the flow of the Yellow River; the dredging of the Bian River under the Song and the diverting of the Wen River under the Yuan are both relied upon for our use. It captures all the wealth of the southeast, and half the tax grain of the empire is brought forward by this route; like a person's throat, its importance is paramount. Yet only when the Yellow River flows south does it benefit the grain transport; if it breaches to the east, it harms the grain transport. Those who discuss river control today stand precisely at the juncture where benefit and harm hang in the balance. To wish to completely eliminate its harm while solely drawing upon its benefit is the most difficult of difficulties. I have tried to survey the flood disasters as a whole and fathom them: without the Bian channel, the Yellow River cannot join the Huai, and therefore the anxiety over the grain transport always lies with the Bian, much like an illness of blockage within the body; yet supposing the Bian could be free of worry, one would then fear that the river might turn and…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
治遥隄又非圖上請行之遺謀乎蓋昔人
焦心銷志殫數百年錯出之奇顧卒崇空
語者而盡施行于
今日此曠世之業也乃議者猶謂河有故道
宜及時恢圖興復茲過計也河流既久走
沙漸淤水沉滯難行自不得不棄而他徙
茲欲奪新河之所必趨强幹而回注于已
滅難明之故道非所以察形也往者孫渡
之役不有覆轍耶或又謂當别開一河以
備運道藉阻茲又過計也遠圖不可倖致
将糈糒偹作必倚辦縣官勞費且什伯卒
未有能濟而乃設不必然之慮以徼難竟
之功非所以軌事也近日膠泇之役不苦
跋盭耶揆今之計亦曰慎預防之術規善
後之宜而已是故長隄遠護非不可約攔
水勢然東强西傷之語未必妄也則畚鍤
之工可弗常飭與隆崇塡閼非不可抑遏
浚流然止啼塞口之喻未必誣也則栅落
punctuated: 治遥隄，又非圖上請行之遺謀乎？蓋昔人焦心銷志，殫數百年錯出之奇，顧卒崇空語者，而盡施行于今日，此曠世之業也。乃議者猶謂河有故道，宜及時恢圖興復，茲過計也。河流既久，走沙漸淤，水沉滯難行，自不得不棄而他徙。茲欲奪新河之所必趨，强幹而回注于已滅難明之故道，非所以察形也。往者孫渡之役，不有覆轍耶？或又謂當别開一河，以備運道藉阻，茲又過計也。遠圖不可倖致，将糈糒偹作，必倚辦縣官，勞費且什伯，卒未有能濟；而乃設不必然之慮，以徼難竟之功，非所以軌事也。近日膠泇之役，不苦跋盭耶？揆今之計，亦曰慎預防之術，規善後之宜而已。是故長隄遠護，非不可約攔水勢，然「東强西傷」之語未必妄也，則畚鍤之工，可弗常飭與？隆崇塡閼，非不可抑遏浚流，然「止啼塞口」之喻未必誣也，則栅落
translation_en:
…and constructing distant dikes—are these not also legacy plans that were mapped out and presented with requests for implementation? Indeed, those ingenious schemes that emerged in various forms over hundreds of years as people of the past racked their brains and exhausted their wills, yet ultimately remained exalted only as empty words, have all been carried into effect today; this is an achievement unmatched across the ages.

Yet commentators still argue that the Yellow River has its old course, and that we should seize the moment to plan on a grand scale for its restoration. This is an overreaching calculation. When a river flows for a long time, shifting sands gradually silt it up, and the water becomes sluggish and difficult to move, so that naturally it cannot help but abandon its bed and shift elsewhere. Now, to seek to wrest the river from the new course toward which it must inevitably rush, and forcibly turn and pour it back into an old channel that has already vanished and is hard to discern—this is no way to observe the topography. Did not the past project at Sundu 孫渡 leave behind the tracks of an overturned cart?

Others argue that a separate canal should be excavated to prepare against the grain transport route being obstructed. This too is an overreaching calculation. Far-reaching schemes cannot be achieved by mere luck; provisions, rations, and construction preparations must all rely on the state treasury, entailing ten- or a hundred-fold labor and expense, and in the end none have succeeded. Yet to entertain worries about what will not necessarily happen in order to angle for an achievement that is difficult to complete—this is no way to keep affairs on their proper track. Did not the recent projects on the Jiao 膠 and Jia 泇 rivers suffer from frustrating intractability?

Weighing the plans for today, it is simply a matter of being cautious in the techniques of precaution and planning what is appropriate for ongoing maintenance. Therefore, protecting from afar with long dikes is not incapable of restraining the force of the waters, yet the saying "strengthening the east injures the west" is not necessarily false; how then can the work of baskets and spades not be constantly kept in readiness? Building high barriers to block and dam the channel is not incapable of checking and holding back a deep and rapid current, yet the metaphor of "stuffing the mouth to stop a child's crying" is not necessarily groundless; how then can the materials for fascines and palisades…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
之具可弗時集與歲當夏秋信水旣漲而
忽有非時之客水乘之則其潰也必暴故
平準之候人宜議選也地居河壖寸壤方
齧而卽數百丈之息壤因之則其陷也必
廣故巡視之番卒宜議補也上流不暢斯
騰涌而爲災水之由泗入者不可漸以濬
之乎下流不疾斯羨漫而爲害水之由徐
入者不可漸以疏之乎而又于青兗冀豫
可田之處各正溝洫以引水之漑而披其
===
勢則治田亦以治河也衞博徐邳經漕之
所多開月河以伺水之橫而折其猛則漕
通亦河之通也夫飭畚鍤而集栅落則成
業保矣選候人而補番卒則警備嚴矣上
流濬而下流疏則原委道矣溝洫正而月
河開則水利廣矣所謂預防而善後者或
以斯乎昔管子論備害之道首請置水官
故其要尤在以擇官爲本謂宜妙簡經明
禹貢之士俾領河隄而又博求習水者分
punctuated: 之具可弗時集與？歲當夏秋，信水旣漲，而忽有非時之客水乘之，則其潰也必暴，故平準之候人宜議選也。地居河壖，寸壤方齧，而卽數百丈之息壤因之，則其陷也必廣，故巡視之番卒宜議補也。上流不暢，斯騰涌而爲災，水之由泗入者，不可漸以濬之乎？下流不疾，斯羨漫而爲害，水之由徐入者，不可漸以疏之乎？而又于青、兗、冀、豫可田之處，各正溝洫，以引水之漑而披其勢，則治田亦以治河也；衞、博、徐、邳經漕之所，多開月河，以伺水之橫而折其猛，則漕通亦河之通也。夫飭畚鍤而集栅落，則成業保矣；選候人而補番卒，則警備嚴矣；上流濬而下流疏，則原委道矣；溝洫正而月河開，則水利廣矣。所謂預防而善後者，或以斯乎？昔管子論備害之道，首請置水官。故其要尤在以擇官爲本。謂宜妙簡經明《禹貢》之士，俾領河隄，而又博求習水者，分
translation_en: … [can the fascines and] gabions not be regularly stockpiled? When the season reaches summer and autumn, the seasonal floods have already risen, and if unexpected tributary waters suddenly ride atop them, the breaches are bound to be violent; therefore, we should deliberate on selecting scouts to gauge water levels. Where land lies along the riverbanks, no sooner is an inch of soil eroded than hundreds of zhang of built-up earth give way because of it, and the collapse is bound to be widespread; therefore, we should deliberate on filling the ranks of patrolling soldiers on rotation. When the upper reaches do not flow freely, the waters surge up and cause disaster—can the waters entering from Sizhou not be gradually dredged? When the lower reaches do not flow swiftly, the waters overflow and cause harm—can the waters entering from Xuzhou not be gradually channeled? Furthermore, in the arable areas of Qingzhou, Yanzhou, Jizhou, and Yuzhou, if we rectify the irrigation ditches and channels in each place so as to draw water for irrigation and divide its momentum, then managing the farmlands is also a way of managing the River. And in the places through which the Grand Canal passes—such as Weihui,Bozhou, Xuzhou, and Pizhou—if we open many crescent-shaped bypass canals to watch for when the water runs wild and break its ferocity, then keeping the Grand Canal clear is also keeping the River clear. Indeed, if we ready baskets and spades and stockpile stakes and gabions, existing achievements will be preserved; if we select water-gauging scouts and fill the ranks of patrolling soldiers, our vigilance and preparedness will be strict; if the upper reaches are dredged and the lower reaches channeled, the source and course will be guided; if irrigation ditches are rectified and crescent bypasses opened, water benefits will be extended. What I meant by taking precautions beforehand and planning for long-term maintenance afterward—perhaps it lies in this? In antiquity, when Master Guan (Guanzi) discussed the way to guard against calamities, he first requested the establishment of Water Officials. Thus, the essential point lies above all in taking the selection of officials as the foundation. I would say we ought to carefully select scholars thoroughly versed in the Classic—specifically the "Tribute of Yu" (Yu gong)—and have them take charge of the river dikes, while also broadly seeking out men experienced with water to divide…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
置其屬使之共行視圖方略得便宜經理
則職任專而事功自立嘗聞江河在天地
間猶脈絡在人身中然則河之爲患非卽
脈絡之病乎而擇官之說則良醫之求也
由前數說則鍼砭湯熨之法也誠采而行
之河之患庶其有瘳乎語云智則謀不肖
則頓愚之爲此言者不過勦曲士迂談而
私畫以爲時事之可行者無便於此若夫
洞利害之故究名數之分以謀萬載之大
===
計則非愚生所可及也
alt_text:
1. 置其屬使之共行視圖方略得便宜經理
2. 則職任專而事功自立嘗聞江河在天地
3. 間猶脈絡在人身中然則河之為患非即
4. 脈絡之病乎而擇官之說則良醫之求也
5. 由前數說則鍼砭湯熨之法也誠采而行
6. 之河之患庶其有瘳乎語云智則謀不肖
7. 則頓愚之為此言者不過剿曲士迂談而
8. 私畫以為時事之可行者無便於此若夫
9. 洞利害之故究名數之分以謀萬載之大
10. 計則非愚生所可及也
置其屬使之共行視圖方略得便宜經理
則職任專而事功自立嘗聞江河在天地
間猶脈絡在人身中然則河之為患非即
脈絡之病乎而擇官之說則良醫之求也
由前數說則鍼砭湯熨之法也誠采而行
之河之患庶其有瘳乎語云智則謀不肖
則頓愚之為此言者不過剿曲士迂談而
私畫以為時事之可行者無便於此若夫
洞利害之故究名數之分以謀萬載之大
計則非愚生所可及也
punctuated: 置其屬，使之共行視圖方略，得便宜經理，則職任專而事功自立。嘗聞江河在天地間，猶脈絡在人身中。然則河之爲患，非卽脈絡之病乎？而擇官之說，則良醫之求也；由前數說，則鍼砭湯熨之法也。誠采而行之，河之患庶其有瘳乎！語云：「智則謀，不肖則頓。」愚之爲此言者，不過勦曲士迂談，而私畫以爲時事之可行者無便於此。若夫洞利害之故，究名數之分，以謀萬載之大計，則非愚生所可及也。
translation_en: …assign them as subordinates, having them jointly inspect and devise strategies, and granting them authority to manage affairs as circumstances require; then responsibilities will be focused and achievements naturally established. I have heard that the Yangtze and the Yellow River exist between Heaven and Earth just as the vessels and meridians exist within the human body. If that is so, is the trouble caused by the Yellow River not precisely an illness of the vessels and meridians? The proposal to select the right officials is thus the search for a skilled physician, while the several proposals discussed earlier are the methods of acupuncture, stone probes, decoctions, and hot compresses. If these are genuinely adopted and put into practice, the affliction of the Yellow River may perhaps be cured! As the saying goes, "The wise devise plans; the unworthy falter." In offering these words, I in my ignorance have done no more than borrow the pedantic talk of parochial scholars, privately reckoning that nothing is more expedient than this for what is practicable in current affairs. As for penetrating the causes of benefit and harm and thoroughly investigating the distinctions of names and numbers so as to plan a grand strategy for ten thousand generations, that is beyond what this ignorant student can reach.

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
應天府鄉試錄後序
臣萬化常稽古虞周之盛道
德隆洽治教休明維時九德
宅俊之士敬應而出者皆足
以翊賛帝業黼黻王猷詩書
蓋不勝載焉此微獨聖作物
覩稱千載曠遇巳也良繇古
===
人學爲實學用爲實用故出
入不悖如此我
國家設科取士專尚經術夫亦
欲士務實學以爲世用庶幾
帝臣王佐出其間耳二百年
来士繇斯軌以佐太平者史
不絕書斌斌盛矣暨我
punctuated:
應天府鄉試錄後序
臣萬化常稽古虞、周之盛，道德隆洽，治教休明。維時九德宅俊之士，敬應而出者，皆足以翊賛帝業，黼黻王猷，《詩》、《書》蓋不勝載焉。此微獨聖作物覩，稱千載曠遇巳也，良繇古人學爲實學，用爲實用，故出入不悖如此。我國家設科取士，專尚經術，夫亦欲士務實學以爲世用，庶幾帝臣王佐出其間耳。二百年来，士繇斯軌以佐太平者，史不絕書，斌斌盛矣。暨我
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination

Your servant [Shao] Wanhua (萬化) has often examined the flourishing eras of ancient Yu [Shun] and Zhou, when morality was lofty and harmonious, and governance and instruction were auspicious and bright. At those times, scholars possessing the nine virtues who held offices for men of outstanding talent came forth in reverent response; all were capable of assisting the imperial enterprise and adorning the royal plans—indeed, the Book of Odes (Shi) and the Book of Documents (Shu) contain more accounts of them than can be fully recorded. This was not merely because when a sage arises all creatures behold him, making it a rare encounter of a thousand years; it was truly because the ancients pursued learning as practical learning and applied it to practical use, so that their conduct in retirement and in office never contradicted one another.

Our Dynasty established the examination system to select scholars with an exclusive emphasis on classical scholarship; in doing so, it likewise desired that scholars devote themselves to practical learning so as to be of use to the world, in the hope that imperial ministers and royal coadjutors would emerge from among them. For two hundred years, scholars who have followed this path to assist the Grand Peace have been recorded without interruption in the histories, flourishing in refined abundance. Coming now to our…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
皇上以冲聖御極懋學右文廣厲
官師益崇雅道誠
虞周載覩而士敬應之時也廼
南都才藪爲
聖世鎬京涵濡景曜最先郡國而
諸挾策遊成均者又四方所
稱英俊之儔誠以彼才具而
遇若此有不純然雅化遵道
德之途循仁義之軌者耶臣
萬化猥以凡庸被
命偕中允臣啓愚典試事獲與觀
文才之盛而竊附於以人事
君之義臣幸厚矣然臣甞論之士
之致用者學也而所爲學者
punctuated: 皇上以冲聖御極，懋學右文，廣厲官師，益崇雅道。誠虞、周載覩，而士敬應之時也。廼南都才藪，爲聖世鎬京，涵濡景曜，最先郡國；而諸挾策遊成均者，又四方所稱英俊之儔。誠以彼才具而遇若此，有不純然雅化，遵道德之途，循仁義之軌者耶？臣萬化猥以凡庸，被命偕中允臣啓愚典試事，獲與觀文才之盛，而竊附於以人事君之義，臣幸厚矣。然臣甞論之：士之致用者，學也；而所爲學者，
translation_en: … His Majesty ascended the throne in youthful sagehood, striving in learning and esteeming civil culture, broadly encouraging officials and teachers, and ever more exalting the refined Way. Truly this is a time when the ages of Yu [Shun] and Zhou are seen once again, and scholars reverently respond to it. Now the Southern Capital is a reservoir of talent, serving as the Haojing of our sagely age, steeped in brilliant radiance ahead of all other commanderies and principalities; and those who carry their texts to study at the Imperial University are furthermore the peers of the finest talents acclaimed throughout the four quarters. Truly, possessing such endowments of talent and meeting with an occasion such as this, how could there be any who are not purely transformed in refinement, following the path of morality and virtue and keeping to the track of benevolence and righteousness? Your servant [Dai] Wanhua 戴萬化, despite his mediocrity, received the imperial command to join Companion for the Heir Apparent (zhongyun) your servant [Gao] Qiyu 高啓愚 in taking charge of the examination affairs. Having been privileged to witness the flourishing of literary talent and to humbly attach myself to the principle of serving the ruler by recommending men, my good fortune is profound indeed. Yet your servant has常 discussed the matter: that by which a scholar achieves practical service is learning, and the purpose for which one pursues learning…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
以適用也學不在詞章之末
技用不在揮霍之虛聲處則
析義窮理以慎厥修出則肩
鉅謀大以楨王國夫然故士
重上亦重士而於世道有攸
賴已今士所屈首受業者非
六經孔孟乎易言時書言事
===
詩言志禮樂言和敬春秋言
名分孔孟言仁義士童而習
居而求此物此志也至其抒
而爲文章建而爲功業亦此
物此志也豈其空取聖賢之
訓誦讀之入耳而出口以希
世取寵不其然矣夫學而不
punctuated: 以適用也。學不在詞章之末技，用不在揮霍之虛聲。處則析義窮理以慎厥修，出則肩鉅謀大以楨王國。夫然，故士重，上亦重士，而於世道有攸賴已。今士所屈首受業者，非六經、孔、孟乎？《易》言時，《書》言事，《詩》言志，《禮》、《樂》言和敬，《春秋》言名分，孔、孟言仁義。士童而習，居而求，此物此志也；至其抒而爲文章，建而爲功業，亦此物此志也。豈其空取聖賢之訓誦讀之，入耳而出口，以希世取寵？不其然矣。夫學而不
translation_en:
…is in order to be suited for practical service. Learning does not lie in the minor skill of literary embellishment, nor does practical service lie in the empty reputation of flamboyant display. When living in retirement, a scholar analyzes righteousness and exhausts principle so as to be careful in his self-cultivation; when going forth into office, he shoulders heavy burdens and plans great undertakings so as to serve as a pillar of the royal state. Because this is so, scholars carry weight, the ruler likewise attaches weight to scholars, and the way of the world has something upon which to rely.

Now, that to which scholars bow their heads and receive instruction—is it not the Six Classics, Confucius, and Mencius? The Book of Changes (Yi) speaks of timeliness; the Book of Documents (Shu) speaks of affairs; the Book of Odes (Shi) speaks of intent; the Record of Rites (Li) and the Classic of Music (Yue) speak of harmony and reverence; the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) speaks of titles and duties; and Confucius and Mencius speak of benevolence and righteousness. What a scholar practices in youth and seeks while dwelling at home is this very substance and this very aspiration; and when he expresses it as literature and establishes it as meritorious achievement, it is likewise this very substance and this very aspiration. Could it be that one merely takes the teachings of the sages and worthies in vain and recites them—letting them enter the ear and exit the mouth—so as to flatter the age and curry favor? Surely it is not so! Now, to study and yet not…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
適於用是飾韥也用而遂舍
所學是委弁也飾韥者不可
與行遠委弁者不可與守貞
斯二者非所望於
聖世之士亦非士所以自待也故
臣玆校多士無徒櫛字比句
顓顓於繁縟崛奇之求也第
===
其詞平正通達氣渾厚爾雅
遠之不詭於先民之程近之
能詳乎當世之務而器識之
宏遠心術之端亮曉然若可
望而知者輒亟收之蓋曰因
文徵學因學徵用即未敢謂
拔十得十亦庶幾氣求神遇
punctuated: 適於用，是飾韥也；用而遂舍所學，是委弁也。飾韥者不可與行遠，委弁者不可與守貞。斯二者，非所望於聖世之士，亦非士所以自待也。故臣玆校多士，無徒櫛字比句，顓顓於繁縟崛奇之求也。第其詞平正通達，氣渾厚爾雅，遠之不詭於先民之程，近之能詳乎當世之務，而器識之宏遠，心術之端亮，曉然若可望而知者，輒亟收之。蓋曰因文徵學，因學徵用，即未敢謂拔十得十，亦庶幾氣求神遇，
translation_en: …be suited to practical application is merely adorning the casket; to be employed in office and thereupon abandon what one has learned is casting aside one's cap. With one who merely adorns the casket, one cannot travel far; with one who casts aside his cap, one cannot uphold constancy. Neither of these two is what is hoped for in scholars of a sacred age, nor is it how scholars ought to regard themselves. Therefore, in examining the many scholars on this occasion, your servant did not merely comb through characters and compare phrases, single-mindedly seeking ornate elaboration or striking novelty. Rather, whenever their diction was balanced, lucid, and penetrating, their vital breath deep, substantial, and refined, in distant matters not deviating from the standards of the ancients, and in immediate matters able to speak in detail on the affairs of the present age—while the breadth and farsightedness of their capacity and insight, as well as the uprightness and clarity of their intentions, were so manifest that they could be known at a glance—I promptly selected them. The idea was to verify learning through composition, and to verify practical utility through learning; even if I dare not claim to have selected ten out of ten, perhaps through a resonance of spirit and mind…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
可籍手報萬分一耳然此豈
臣之明能遠必哉異日諸士
果學易者誠知變化學書者
誠審因革學詩者誠敦溫厚
學禮樂者誠會中和學春秋
者誠嚴法戒佩服孔孟體仁
集義肫肫然棄華修實與九
德宅俊之士相後先焉乃可
謂體用一原之學不負
===
虞周之時矣脫一有不售是靜言
庸違而無所容於
聖世者也詎惟多士喪厥重即臣
且蒙不任之罰可弗戒耶夫
期千里者慎跬步累層臺者
punctuated: 可籍手報萬分一耳。然此豈臣之明能遠必哉？異日諸士，果學《易》者誠知變化，學《書》者誠審因革，學《詩》者誠敦溫厚，學《禮》《樂》者誠會中和，學《春秋》者誠嚴法戒，佩服孔孟，體仁集義，肫肫然棄華修實，與九德宅俊之士相後先焉，乃可謂體用一原之學，不負虞、周之時矣。脫一有不售，是靜言庸違，而無所容於聖世者也。詎惟多士喪厥重，即臣且蒙不任之罰，可弗戒耶？夫期千里者慎跬步，累層臺者
translation_en: … wherewith I may have something in hand to repay even one ten-thousandth of the imperial grace. Yet how could my own discernment possibly guarantee this far into the future? In days to come, if these scholars—those who study the Book of Changes (Yi) truly understanding change and transformation, those who study the Book of Documents (Shu) truly discerning continuity and reform, those who study the Book of Odes (Shi) truly cultivating gentleness and generosity, those who study the Record of Rites (Li) and Music (Yue) truly grasping centrality and harmony, and those who study the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) truly upholding strict standards and warnings—take to heart the teachings of Confucius and Mencius, embody benevolence and accumulate righteousness, earnestly cast aside華 [flashy ornament] to cultivate substance, and vie with men of the Nine Virtues and the Three Eminences, then theirs may indeed be called learning in which substance and function share a single source, worthy of an age like those of Yu [Shun] and the Zhou. Should even one among them fail to live up to what he professes, that would be to speak smoothly when tranquil yet act perversely when employed, for which there is no place in this sacred age. Not only would the many scholars lose their standing, but I too would incur the punishment for incompetence—how could we not be on our guard? Now, he who aims for a thousand li is careful with each half-step; he who builds a tiered terrace…

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
text:
先正基多士往矣行且隨牒
詣
闕下駸駸乎嚮用期矣詩曰京邑
翼翼四方之極又曰彼都人
士萬民之望其立極四方也
唯爾多士固始今日其鉠萬
民之望也唯爾多士亦始今
日臣重言之矣尚相與重圖
===
之其往可哉
翰林院侍讀羅萬化謹序
punctuated:
先正基。多士往矣，行且隨牒詣闕下，駸駸乎嚮用期矣。《詩》曰：「京邑翼翼，四方之極。」又曰：「彼都人士，萬民之望。」其立極四方也，唯爾多士，固始今日；其鉠萬民之望也，唯爾多士，亦始今日。臣重言之矣，尚相與重圖之，其往可哉！
翰林院侍讀羅萬化謹序。
translation_en:
…first make right the foundation. Go forth, then, you many scholars! Soon you will follow the official rosters to present yourselves beneath the Palace Gates, rapidly approaching the time when you will be employed in service. The Book of Odes (Shi) says: "The capital city is well-ordered; it is the standard for the four quarters." And again it says: "Those gentlemen of the capital are looked up to by the myriad people." As for establishing the standard for the four quarters, it rests with you many scholars, and truly begins today; as for disappointing [?; 鉠, likely a print error for 缺] the expectations of the myriad people, that too rests with you many scholars, and likewise begins today. Your servant has spoken of this with great gravity; may you together plan for it with equal gravity. With that, you may go forth!
Respectfully written as a postface by Luo Wanhua 羅萬化, Expositor-in-Waiting in the Hanlin Academy.

title: 萬曆柒年應天府鄉試錄
